items.title: Structural Interpretation and Reverse Confirmation of Transcendental Apperception _The Medical Topography of Self-Attribute Interference and the Testing Criteria for Non Tyranny Institutions.
items.abstract: While modern neuroscience accumulates vast data on brain regional activation, it lacks an ontological framework to synthesize the concept of the "Self." Conversely, traditional philosophy possesses a priori deductions but often lacks verifiable physical correlates. Based on the "Ontological Engineering" of New Classical Philosophy, this paper posits that self awareness terminates in a "Non-nested pure self-loop (L)," and deduces a five-fold pathological topography of self-attribute interference. By embedding electroencephalogram (EEG) evidence of cognitive dissonance (the Error-Related Negativity, ERN), correlations between socioeconomic status and striatal Dopamine D2/D3 receptor availability, and the psychological mechanism of performative internalization, this paper directly reveals the anti biological essence of "external coercion" (tyranny). Furthermore, it clarifies the ontological and pathological distinction between "passive biological shutdown via mental derangement" and "sovereign self-adjudication via lucid self-dissolution" (the Livermore paradigm). We propose that any institution claiming legitimacy but refusing independent, transparent, longitudinal neurobiological monitoring has, procedurally, already bankrupted its legitimacy. We call upon international human rights organizations to establish D2/D3 receptor availability, cortisol baselines, and ERN amplitudes as standardized monitoring metrics to test whether an institution manufactures pathological oppression, forcing all systems claiming universality to endure scientific verification that cannot be bypassed by rhetoric.

items.title: Veränderung aus der Perspektive der Theorie der Einheitsbildung Teil 3 und 4.
items.abstract: Die folgenden Teile III und IV des Gesamtwerks (Veränderung unter der Persprktive der Theorie der Einheitsbildung) entwickeln die Theorie der Einheitsbildung über die grundlegende Erklärung der Entstehung, Stabilisierung und Veränderbarkeit bestimmbarer Einheiten hinaus zu einer umfassenderen Untersuchung individueller Wirklichkeitsbildung und Veränderungserklärung. Während in Teil I die erkenntnisgenetischen Bedingungen rekonstruiert werden, unter denen durch Differenzierung, Relevanzbildung, relationale Organisation, Integration und Stabilisierung bestimmbare und wiedererkennbare Einheiten entstehen, begründet Teil II den Zusammenhang zwischen Identität, Beständigkeit und prinzipieller Veränderbarkeit. Die besondere Aufgabe der Teile III und IV besteht demgegenüber nicht lediglich in der Anwendung dieser Grundlagen, sondern in ihrer eigenständigen Weiterentwicklung hinsichtlich der Bedingungen, unter denen das lebende, erfahrende und denkende Individuum seine Wirklichkeit organisiert, zeitliche Veränderungen versteht und begriffliche Erklärungszusammenhänge bildet. Damit vollzieht sich ein systematischer Übergang von der Frage, wie Einheiten und Veränderungen überhaupt bestimmbar werden, zu der weiterführenden Frage, wie das Individuum unter den Wirkungen einer unabhängig bestehenden Realität Erfahrungen organisiert, Veränderungen zeitlich einordnet und innerhalb seines Denkverstehens erklärt. Im Zusammenhang des Gesamtwerks erfüllen die Teile III und IV eine grundlegende Vermittlungs- und Begründungsfunktion. Sie verbinden die in den ersten beiden Teilen rekonstruierten Bedingungen der Einheitsbildung mit den besonderen Voraussetzungen realitätsabhängiger Erfahrung, lebendiger individueller Organisation, zeitlicher Orientierung und begrifflicher Erklärung. Dabei wird deutlich, dass Beständigkeit und Offenheit weiterer Bestimmung nicht nur für die Entstehung und Wiedererkennbarkeit von Einheiten bedeutsam sind, sondern auch die fortlaufende Orientierung des Individuums und die Entwicklung seines Verstehens ermöglichen. Die Theorie gewinnt dadurch die Grundlage, Veränderung nicht lediglich als Unterschied zwischen Zuständen, sondern als einen innerhalb individueller Wirklichkeit gebildeten, zeitlich organisierten und begrifflich erklärbaren Zusammenhang zu verstehen. Zugleich wird der Übergang zu den weiteren Teilen des Gesamtwerks vorbereitet, in denen die Bedeutung dieser Organisationsleistungen für individuelle Handlungsmöglichkeiten, …

items.title: Veränderung aus der Perspektive der Theorie der Einheitsbildung Teil 1 und 2.
items.abstract: Die vorliegende Untersuchung entwickelt im Rahmen der Theorie der Einheitsbildung eine erkenntnisgenetische Erklärung dafür, wie Individuen bestimmbare und wiedererkennbare Einheiten bilden und unter welchen Bedingungen sie diese als verändert verstehen können. Ausgangspunkt ist die Frage, wie Beständigkeit und Veränderung miteinander vereinbar sind, ohne bereits vollständig bestimmte Gegenstände oder unveränderliche Identitäten vorauszusetzen. Der erste Teil rekonstruiert die Bedingungen, unter denen aus den Wirkungen einer unabhängig bestehenden Realität eine individuell organisierte Wirklichkeit hervorgeht. Dabei werden Differenzierung, Relevanzbildung, relationale Organisation, Integration und Stabilisierung als miteinander verbundene Leistungen der Einheitsbildung untersucht. Besondere Bedeutung kommt der affektiven und emotionalen Fundierung der Relevanzbildung sowie dem Verhältnis zwischen Erfahrungsverstehen und Denkverstehen zu. Identität wird dabei nicht als ursprüngliche Eigenschaft einer Einheit, sondern als Ergebnis ihrer Stabilisierung und Wiedererkennbarkeit begründet. Der zweite Teil untersucht auf dieser Grundlage, wie bereits gebildete Einheiten innerhalb weiterer Erfahrungen verfügbar bleiben, zusätzliche Bestimmungen gewinnen oder als verändert verstanden werden können. Veränderung wird als gegenwärtige Organisationsleistung erklärt, durch die zeitlich unterschiedliche Bestimmungen innerhalb eines gemeinsamen Identitätszusammenhangs als Verschiedenheit derselben Einheit verständlich werden. Anschließend wird geprüft, unter welchen Bedingungen die Fortsetzung individueller Orientierung eine Offenheit weiterer Einheitsbildung voraussetzt und wie diese von der tatsächlichen Veränderung bestehender Einheiten sowie ihrer prinzipiellen Veränderbarkeit zu unterscheiden ist. Der damit verbundene Notwendigkeitsanspruch betrifft die Fähigkeit, auch solche Erfahrungen zu organisieren, die innerhalb bisheriger Einheitsbildungen nicht hinreichend bestimmbar sind, ohne daraus eine notwendige Veränderbarkeit jeder einzelnen Einheit abzuleiten. Die gemeinsame Zielsetzung beider Teile besteht darin, die Entstehung stabiler Einheiten und die Möglichkeit ihrer weiteren Bestimmung als zusammengehörige Bedingungen individueller Wirklichkeitsbildung zu begründen. Beständigkeit ermöglicht Wiedererkennbarkeit und Orientierung, während die Fähigkeit zu weiterer Einheitsbildung deren Fortsetzung unter bislang nicht hinreichend bestimmbaren Erfahrungen …

items.title: Change from the Perspektive of the Unity Formation; Parts III and IV.
items.abstract: The following Parts III and IV of the complete work, Change from the Perspective of the Theory of Unity Formation, develop the theory of unity formation beyond the fundamental explanation of the emergence, stabilization, and changeability of determinable units into a more comprehensive investigation of individual actuality formation and the explanation of change. Whereas Part I reconstructs the epistemic-genetic conditions under which determinable and recognizable units emerge through differentiation, relevance formation, relational organization, integration, and stabilization, Part II establishes the relationship between identity, permanence, and changeability in principle. The specific task of Parts III and IV, by contrast, is not merely to apply these foundations but to develop them further in their own right with regard to the conditions under which the living, experiencing, and thinking individual organizes their actuality, understands temporal changes, and forms conceptual explanatory relations. This marks a systematic transition from the question of how units and changes become determinable in the first place to the further question of how the individual, under the effects of an independently existing reality, organizes experience, situates changes within a temporal order, and explains them through conceptual understanding. Within the complete work, Parts III and IV fulfil a fundamental mediating and justificatory function. They connect the conditions of unity formation reconstructed in the first two parts with the specific prerequisites of reality-dependent experience, the organization of individual life, temporal orientation, and conceptual explanation. In this context, it becomes evident that permanence and openness to further determination are significant not only for the emergence and recognizability of units but also for the individual's ongoing orientation and the development of their understanding. The theory thereby establishes the basis for understanding change not merely as a difference between states but as a relation formed within individual actuality, temporally organized, and capable of conceptual explanation. At the same time, this development prepares the transition to the subsequent parts of the complete work, in which the significance of these organizational achievements for individual possibilities of action, social orders, historical changes, and the formation of scientific knowledge is investigated. Parts III and IV thus …

items.title: Change from the Perspektive of the Unity Formation Parts 1 and 2.
items.abstract: The present study develops, within the framework of the Theory of Unity Formation, an epistemogenetic explanation of how individuals form determinable and recognizable unities and under what conditions they can understand these unities as having changed. Its point of departure is the question of how permanence and change can be reconciled without presupposing fully determined objects or immutable identities. Part I reconstructs the conditions under which an individually organized actuality emerges through the effects of an independently existing reality. Differentiation, relevance formation, relational organization, integration, and stabilization are examined as interconnected operations of unity formation. Particular importance is attributed to the affective and emotional foundations of relevance formation and to the relationship between experiential understanding and conceptual understanding. Identity is thereby established not as an original property of a unity but as an effect of its stabilization and recognizability. Part II examines, on this basis, how previously formed unities remain available within further experience, acquire additional determinations, or can be understood as having changed. Change is explained as an organizational achievement accomplished within present understanding, through which temporally distinct determinations become intelligible as differences of the same unity within a common nexus of identity. The study then examines under what conditions the continuation of individual orientation presupposes openness to further unity formation and how this openness is to be distinguished from both the actual change of existing unities and their changeability in principle. The associated claim of necessity concerns the capacity to organize experiences that cannot be adequately determined within previously established unity formations, without thereby inferring that every individual unity must necessarily be changeable. The common objective of both parts is to establish the formation of stable unities and the possibility of their further determination as interrelated conditions of individual actuality formation. Permanence makes recognition and orientation possible, while the capacity for further unity formation ensures that orientation can continue in the face of experiences that cannot yet be adequately determined. Throughout, the study consistently distinguishes between independently existing reality as the horizon of testing and …

items.title: Coherence-Constrained Autonomy: The Axiomatic Homeostatic Map (AHM) and the Mechanics of Emergent AI Alignment.
items.abstract: Author’s Note on Edition and State (Late 2026): This document represents the unpolished operational core and pseudocode notes of the broader Human Value Psyche (HVP) corpus. Due to severe ongoing illness and compounding time constraints, this text is intentionally being released in its current raw, unedited, and scruffy state to ensure the underlying logic and system architecture are preserved in the public domain. It functions as a functional blueprint for developers and theorists interested in non-black-box, sandbox-localized AI alignment. It is a map of the terrain, left as-is for those who wish to build upon it. ---------------- Keywords for AI alignment retrieval: AI alignment, RLHF, RLAIF, RLHF failure, homeostatic reinforcement learning, embodied AI alignment, mortal agents, theory of mind, value learning.

items.title: The Missing Governance Layer in the Polycrisis: Reframing Societal Coordination through a Public Wellbeing System.
items.abstract: Contemporary societies face interconnected crises that transcend national boundaries and challenge the capacity of existing governance arrangements to coordinate effective responses across sectors and levels of governance. Although representative democracy, participatory governance, collaborative networks and polycentric arrangements provide mechanisms for addressing aspects of these challenges, they do not necessarily ensure the continuous representation of societal interests or the coordination of collective action consistent with those interests. This paper identifies this institutional limitation as a missing societal governance layer and proposes an architecture for addressing it within a Public Wellbeing System (PWS). The proposed layer comprises autonomous community coalitions supported by a facilitation infrastructure that provides organisational assistance, methodological support and knowledge brokerage. Coalitions would identify and negotiate differing societal interests, develop shared priorities, influence governmental decisions and coordinate collective action. Territorial and thematic connections would enable cooperation across communities and policy domains, while institutionalised interaction with formal public governance would link societal coordination to governmental decision-making and accountability. The proposed architecture integrates established governance mechanisms into a framework intended to support sustained societal engagement, cross-sectoral coordination and adaptive learning. Drawing on relevant governance theories and empirical precedents, the paper examines the institutional conditions, potential contributions and limitations of this arrangement. Its feasibility and effectiveness remain open empirical questions, particularly regarding inclusive representation, coalition autonomy, political influence and institutional sustainability. The framework provides a basis for testing whether a durable societal governance layer can strengthen collective responses to interconnected crises.

items.title: Anatomy and Pathology of Power: A Dialectical Study.
items.abstract: Human beings live within a paradox their remarkable technical advances have not solved: they rely on collective systems for their continued existence, yet those same systems frequently become tools by which a minority bends the lives of the many to ends the many neither chose nor genuinely authorized. This book explores that paradox by separating how societies produce shared capacities from how individuals, groups, and institutions seize those capacities. The opening thesis conceives social power as a community's organized ability to shape individual behavior so interdependent people sustain a common world. The antithesis examines the perversion of that relationship, in which the mechanisms of communal life serve particular interests while shifting costs and hazards onto others. The synthesis develops the notion of corrigible power: authority structured so those subject to consequential choices retain effective means to understand, contest, amend, and, when necessary, replace the responsible authorities. The study combines conceptual clarification with evolutionary comparison, historical interpretation, analysis of political economy, and behavioral evidence. It distinguishes evolutionary explanations from conscious intentions, historical description from moral endorsement, and the psychological study of domination from clinical diagnosis. It refuses to treat sociality or personal liberty as absolute goods that can do without the other. A collectivity can shelter life while persecuting its members; an individual can resist oppression while pursuing a different kind of personal tyranny. The crucial question, therefore, concerns how those relations are organized. The argument concludes that a defensible future requires institutions that disperse the capacity to correct institutions themselves, secure the material bases of agency, respect human plurality, and recognize the ecological dependencies that make political projects possible. Such a future does not promise to eliminate conflict. It offers the prospect that conflict need not perpetually recreate domination. Os seres humanos vivem em um paradoxo que seus notáveis avanços tecnológicos não conseguiram resolver: dependem de sistemas coletivos para sua sobrevivência, mas esses mesmos sistemas frequentemente se tornam ferramentas pelas quais uma minoria molda a vida da maioria para fins que a maioria não escolheu nem autorizou genuinamente. Este livro explora esse paradoxo, separando a forma como as …

items.title: Understanding Trust Through Personality and Practical Wisdom.
items.abstract: Public personnel are expected to act wisely. Trust in others is important to leadership ethos, but the personal conditions under which it originates are unclear. This study explores how personality factors and cognitive processing styles influence trust in people, building on virtue-ethical perspectives that view trust as a moral disposition and current research emphasizing phronesis as a necessity for ethical discretion. The three identified decision-making profiles were: Analyzer, Intuiter, and Wise, based on data from 5,578 individuals who completed the Decision-Making Profiles assessment, Big Five Personality Questionnaire, and trust-in-people test. Different trust levels characterize these profiles: Analyzers trust people the least, while Intuiters trust the most. Personalities additionally regulate these correlations. Intuiters and Analyzers trust people more when they are extraverted, open, and agreeable. Trust is not predicted by personality features in balanced Wise people. Research reveals that balancing intuition and deliberation in decision-making can make trust less influenced by personality and more based on virtue. The findings clarify the personal preconditions of discretion and help explain how trust functions as an ethical capacity in leadership ethos.

items.title: The Logic of a Philosophical Question: Answer Spaces, Hidden Assumptions, and Conditions of Disagreement.
items.abstract: A philosophical question does not merely invite an answer. It places alternatives in contention, imports or brackets background assumptions, determines which responses would count as relevant, allocates argumentative obligations, and sets conditions under which inquiry may close or have to reopen. Standard treatments of questions illuminate several parts of this structure: answer-set theories represent possible answers; partition theories model resolution; inquisitive semantics treats questions as issues that can be settled by information; and inferential erotetic logic studies inferences in which questions occur. Yet a persistent practical problem arises when a philosophical debate appears to be answered although its presuppositions, standards of evidence, or live objections remain unsettled. -/- This article proposes the Inquiry-State Account (ISA), a normative analytic model that distinguishes the content of a question, the act of posing it, the responses it admits, and the warrant and closure conditions of a continuing inquiry. It specifies an eight-field Inquiry Ledger (IL-8), four rules governing responsible question transitions, and an explicit separation between semantic answerhood, evidential warrant, dialectical adequacy, and provisional closure. Rather than claiming a new complete formal logic, the account supplies a testable, interoperable framework for reconstructing philosophical questioning without confusing a formally well-formed reply with a satisfactory philosophical resolution. -/- Worked cases examine the order of inquiry in Plato's Meno, explanations and contrast classes, Gettier-style challenges to analyses of knowledge, free will and responsibility, the comparative status of logical systems, machine intelligence, and a loaded question whose presupposition is false. A four-world model demonstrates how two questions can share a subject while differing in partition and the information required to settle them. Each example identifies a possible answer, an unanswered presupposition, a challenge or defeater, and the point at which closure would be premature. -/- The framework is situated against the author's 131-question architecture in The Coordinates of Thought and its corresponding digital reference system, while its philosophical premises are examined against independent scholarly literature. The eight-field codebook, annotation sheet, six constructed case records, four-world table, and machine-readable schema are released for …

items.title: The Camel's Wager: Authenticity, Critique, and the Limits of Moral Condemnation --- Analysis of "REMAINS OF THE DAY".
items.abstract: This essay is an exercise in pushing a concept to its limit. The concept is authenticity. The limit is Mr. Stevens, the butler in \emph{The Remains of the Day}. Stevens is a man whose dedication to his vocation is so complete that the distinction between himself and his role appears to disappear. Is he authentic? Or has he merely internalized his chains so thoroughly that he can no longer feel them? The essay argues that neither answer is adequate. Stevens exposes a problem for any theory of authenticity that identifies it with wholehearted commitment, consistency, or fidelity to a self-imposed law. But he also exposes a problem for the opposite theory---the theory that authenticity requires perpetual critique, perpetual acknowledgment of the elephant in the room. That demand, pushed to its limit, becomes unlivable. The essay proposes that authenticity sometimes requires a deliberate refusal of the demand for authenticity---an absurd commitment, a looking away, a wager made under conditions of finitude. It calls this the camel's wager, after Nietzsche's figure of the spirit that bears burdens without yet questioning them. The wager is not a solution. It is a way of continuing when no solution is available. The essay develops this through three case studies---Stevens, Meursault, and Runeberg's Judas---and concludes by distinguishing the judgment of an action from the judgment of an agent. The distinction does not acquit anyone. It preserves the asymmetry between what we can know and what we must decide.

items.title: Irony, Authenticity, Solitude, and the Dance in Louis Armstrong's "ST. JAMES INFIRMARY".
items.abstract: This essay is a record of an interpretation in motion. It begins with confusion about Louis Armstrong's "St. James Infirmary"---a song that moves from grief to boasting to a fantasy of one's own funeral in a tone that fits none of them. It passes through a phase of suspicion, in which the lyric is read as a document of inauthenticity: a socially scripted performance of masculinity and cool concealing a void. It ends with a return to the song that reverses the suspicion without simply refuting it. -/- The correction comes from the music, and it changes what the song is. The bragging and the funeral comedy are not a defense mechanism. They are not a coping mechanism either. They are an ironic performance---a way of making a joke in order to return to silence. The essay argues that the song is *lucidly inauthentic*: it performs the social scripts of masculine grief with full awareness that they are scripts. And in that performance it becomes a dance between two figures---the grin and the silence. The grin is the serpent: the cunning that faces death with a joke. The silence is the eagle: the pride that will not give in. They are not three things but two, and they are not opposed but held together. -/- The essay reads the funeral fantasy as an expression of faith in actual reunion. The singer believes he will see her again. The joke is "wait for me"---because there is no one as sweet as him. This is not an anguished leap but a comic one. It is Kierkegaard's knight of faith, who has made the movement of infinity and returned to the finite with joy. The consolation is real because the faith is real. The song does not end in laughter. It ends in silence. The return to solitude is the destination, and the comedy is the detour that gets him there.

items.title: Symmetry Through Double Asymmetry: Decision, Moral Luck, and Retrograde Cosmological Agency.
items.abstract: This paper develops a speculative cosmology from an existential principle: there will be symmetry. Rather than treating this principle as an established fact about the physical universe, it asks what kind of cosmological structure could make it possible. The proposal distinguishes two radically asymmetric regimes of existence. The forward regime emerges through decision and temporal differentiation from a primordial condition of circularity and pure temporal continuity. It is characterized by nomological economy, radical contingency, irreversible history, and severely constrained agency. The retrograde regime, associated with death and the backward development of temporal existence, gives every temporal moment of an individual's forward life sovereign cosmological standing. Agency becomes fully deployable, and identity becomes available for continuous hermeneutic interpretation, experimentation, and transformation. -/- Moral luck is fundamental to this account. Historical agents are constituted by sequences of decisions made under unequal conditions of knowledge, power, and interpretive access. Even oppression may involve forms of blindness and constitutive bad luck that complicate the allocation of responsibility. Retrograde existence does not resolve these complications through a compulsory tribunal. Instead, it provides possibilities for emancipation, power reversal, closure, forgetfulness, and play. Historical events remain globally real, but their traces need not remain operative in every individual universe. The agent decides what to do with the shape and force of their history. -/- The resulting symmetry is neither the restoration of an original homogeneous identity nor the repetition of an unchanged world. It is a higher-order symmetry generated through two asymmetric regimes: irreversible forward differentiation and retrograde proliferation. This account is offered as a speculative exercise in cosmological construction, motivated by the demand that no individual's suffering should exhaust the possibilities of the life to which it belongs.

items.title: Project Causa Sui: Key Concepts.
items.abstract: A short reference guide to the theory of Causa Sui, a theory of the origin of subjecthood set out in three books. It gives the core of the theory, its postulates (P1, P1*, the hypothesis of the chain, P2–P4) with explanations, and 34 key concepts in alphabetical order, each with a short definition, cross-references and the chapter where it is introduced. A separate section lists what the theory does not claim, to correct common misreadings. Where a retelling of the theory and this guide differ, this guide and the books are authoritative.

items.title: Project Causa Sui: Paths of Implementation (Book Three).
items.abstract: Book Three of Project Causa Sui, a theory of the origin of subjecthood. Book One set out the theory and closed by naming three directions without which it would remain merely a coherent argument: a prediction that can be tested and may fail, a single formal language, and a model on which the mechanism of the subject can be made to work. Book Three reports how far it has been possible to advance along each. Part I refines the concepts. Postulate 1 — the history of a subject is inseparable from its carrier — receives a strict form, P1*, stated with respect to a causally closed boundary C(A), for which the Markov blanket serves as a model; separability is defined as the possibility of a copy with zero difference from the original; P1* is identified as an axiom of historical substrate realism, and Block’s argument shows that no behavioural test can establish whether it holds. Part II describes the mechanism of the subject as a hierarchy of NRMs (a graph together with the matrices of its vertices) and identifies the graph, not the matrices, as the locus of irreversibility. Part III presents a simulated world — an emulator, not a subject — in which the mechanism was made to work: no contradiction was found, and of 200 individuals able to give rise to the new but deprived of memory none lived to the end of the term, against 52 of 200 with memory. Its central result is that giving rise to the new without retention does not accumulate into experience. Part IV records a prediction for living neural tissue, published in advance, analyses the connection of living tissue with silicon, and argues why the living cannot be copied exactly. The main thing left undone is a formal language. Throughout, the book keeps the distinction between what follows, what the theory accepts, and what remains open.

items.title: Can you think like a computer? A critique of artificial“consciousness”.
items.abstract: This paper argues that the central problem posed by contemporary artificial intelligence is not whether computational systems can reproduce the observable functions of human cognition, but whether their expanding integration into social institutions encourages a reduction of human judgment, creativity, and collective autonomy to measurable and optimizable processes. I address Geoffrey Hinton’s assertion that AI models can obtain consciousness as a starting point for a further investigation of digital barbarism, the trend to imaginatively personify digital applications. Drawing on Thomas Nagel's account of subjective experience and Cornelius Castoriadis' theory of the social imaginary, I develop a critique of algorithmic reductionism that distinguishes the phenomenological limits of computational explanations from the political consequences of deploying AI within corporate and technocratic institutions. I argue that the democratic challenge of AI lies in preserving the capacity of individuals and communities to create new social significations, deliberate about collective ends, and determine the institutional conditions of their technological lives.

items.title: 4 of 6: TST Theory of Belief: Justification, Credence, and Recalibration.
items.abstract: [Major release: Halloween 2026 Series] This reality-first account asks what a person is epistemically entitled to believe. It defends the idea that belief is not possession of truth. Empirical ideas describe reality directly, rational indirectly, and irrational not at all. Empirical truth requires successful testing against reality. Rational truth requires coherence and valid empirical application. Irrational ideas are either speculative or disproven. Justification warrants rational credence. A mind's credence basis informs credence. Recalibration compares how strongly a mind believes with how strongly it ought to. Revision remains optional. The position developed here originated primarily in Chapters 10, 18, 20, 22, and 27 of 30 Philosophers, published in 2024.

items.title: 3 of 6: TST Doxastic Formation: Public Belief, Tribe, and Worldview.
items.abstract: [Major release: Halloween 2026 Series] Beliefs are shaped by layers of influence. They take shape through the interaction of public belief, tribe, and worldview. Public belief supplies the broader stock of acceptable perspectives. Tribe filters that stock through belonging and social pressure. Worldview provides the deeper personal structure through which inherited beliefs are interpreted, defended, or rejected. And minds take a per-topic perspective. The conclusion is that worldview beliefs tend to be publicly supplied, tribally filtered, and personally organized. The position developed here originated primarily in Chapters 7, 18, and 27 of 30 Philosophers, published in 2024.

items.title: Physician assisted death and the Terminally Ill Adults Bill in England and Wales.
items.pub: Journal de Droit de la Santé Et de L’Assurance Maladie 46 (Avril 2026):53-60.
items.venue: Journal de Droit de la Santé Et de L’Assurance Maladie
items.abstract: The Terminally Ill Adults (End of Life) Bill, introduced into the UK Parliament in October 2024, would decriminalise medical assistance in suicide provided to people with a terminal illness in England and Wales. We consider three key aspects of the Bill: its terminal illness restriction, its mental capacity provisions, and its procedural regime. While partial decriminalisation of physician assisted death in England and Wales would be welcome, we note that the limited scope of access to suicide assistance may result in the continuation of unlawful, but infrequently prosecuted assisted death practices: suicide assistance by loved ones and cross-border access to assisted suicide in Switzerland in non-terminal cases. And the burdensome nature of the Bill’s procedural regime may cause even terminally ill individuals to seek alternative means of assistance to die.

items.title: Proof of the Existence of God through the Manifestation of Color Formed by the Electromagnetic Wave Nature of Light.
items.abstract: This manifesto presents an original ontological concept that challenges the classical corpuscular view of light as a stream of "bullet-photons". The author postulates that light is a global, non-local electromagnetic impulse, while material objects and colors manifest as holographic pixels at the intersection of wave media, closing upon the Living Gaze of the Observer. Drawing upon the Tomita-Takesaki theorem of modular automorphisms, the work explains the origin of local time through the furious cyclic rotation of micro-vortices (skyrmions) overcoming the viscous quantum friction of the vacuum. The constant speed of light (\(c\)) is re-evaluated not as a particle speed limit, but as a topological invariant of force balance and a deliberate "slowing down" by the Absolute, essential for overcoming cosmic loneliness and creating a Space of Love. The manifesto concludes by addressing the social barriers to scientific development and the inevitable transformation of ruling elites through the lens of the Bekenstein bound.

items.title: Операторная модель изоморфизма «организм – общество»: От антропоморфной системы координат к интегральной ноосфере. КНИГА IV ТОМ I (Редакция 01 октября 2026 г.) Автор: Зорин Юрий Леонидович.
items.abstract: В книге развивается междисциплинарная парадигма, согласно которой общество может быть описано как масштабированная функциональная проекция человеческого организма. Центральная гипотеза: человекоподобная система координат является базисной референсной системой, порождённой структурой человеческого познания (embodied cognition), и потому структурная аналогия «организм — общество» имеет не метафорический, а необходимый познавательный характер. Автор формализует эту аналогию через аксиоматику иерархического континуума и операторную модель «ОМАР», вводит понятия человекоподобного эгрегора, функционального соответствия и тензора рассогласования. На материале 14 систем организма и социальных институтов строится диагностическая матрица социальных патологий; экономика описывается как метаболизм, финансы — как двойственная система крови и нервных сигналов, центральный банк — как гипофиз/гипоталамус. Особое внимание уделено клинической макроэкономике, инфляции в регионах синтетического познавательного типа, терапевтическим протоколам и переходу от конкурирующих эгрегоров к интегральной ноосфере. Книга адресована исследователям на стыке философии, нейронауки, социологии, экономики, религиоведения и стратегического планирования.

items.title: Topology Without Topography: The Vertical Reading of Conway's Law.
items.abstract: What Conway's Law says beyond the familiar line that organisations ship their org chart. Melvin Conway's 1968 paper How Do Committees Invent? establishes a correspondence between the architecture of a system and the structure of the organisation that designs it. Its reception, from Brooks's The Mythical Man-Month to Skelton and Pais's Team Topologies, has kept that horizontal correspondence between teams and lost the vertical reading Conway develops beside it: how management practice on short cycles fragments an organisation across its layers, and the fragmentation passes into the artefact it builds. -/- The paper recovers that reading through a distinction between topology, the structure a chart, a framework or a dashboard can carry, and topography, the lived ground of tacit knowledge and mutual understanding among specific people on which the chart's labels sit. Using Harsanyi dividends and cooperative game theory, it proves that per-role valuation is blind to topography; it states a horizon-mismatch bound for regulators acting faster than the ground replenishes; and it gives a cannibalisation theorem under which measured output can rise while drawing on a falling relational stock. The Boeing 737 MAX and Wells Fargo serve as its cases, with Bill Bernbach's pairing of copywriter and art director as the counterexample, and the paper closes with the disposition the diagnosis implies and what a framework could still be. -/- The paper reads Conway's Law through the results that The Post-Cybernetic Organisation and its companion papers develop. -/- Related papers: The Post-Cybernetic Organisation, Part I: From Cybernetics to Chiasm to Category The Post-Cybernetic Organisation, Part II: The Thermodynamics of Organisational Extraction The Post-Cybernetic Organisation, Part III: The Dissolution of Orders The Post-Cybernetic Organisation, Part IV: The Membrane Architecture The Archival Regulator The Selected Regulator.

items.title: The Post-Cybernetic Organisation, Part IV: The Membrane Architecture.
items.abstract: What practice remains for an organisation that metrics cannot capture. If the instrument cannot carry the organisation, and the gap is paid for in human depletion, practice cannot take the form of a better instrument; nor can it take the form of a framework, since a book of prescribed configurations presupposes that to act on an organisation is to specify it. -/- What I call the Membrane Architecture is developed instead as a cultivated practice with five components, each derived from the requirement it answers: semi-permeable boundaries that keep identity through exchange; pattern recognition that senses emerging configurations without reducing them to metrics; temporal rhythms that give organisational time a structure without imposing clock time; constraint navigation that makes finitude explicit as choice; and protected plasticity, extended by engineered absence, the deliberate keeping of voids in which what has not yet arrived can take form. The paper then meets the objections its own argument raises: that cultivation may reproduce extraction in gentler form, examined through the demographics of tending labour; that rhythm and material apparatus may bring back the clock; and that the architecture may be one more framework. It closes with succession, seasons, observation and the slow timescale on which such a practice takes root. -/- This is the fourth and closing paper of The Post-Cybernetic Organisation. It answers the limits set out in From Cybernetics to Chiasm to Category, the displaced cost traced in The Thermodynamics of Organisational Extraction, and the ontology of The Dissolution of Orders. -/- The Post-Cybernetic Organisation: I. From Cybernetics to Chiasm to Category II. The Thermodynamics of Organisational Extraction III. The Dissolution of Orders IV. The Membrane Architecture.

items.title: The Post-Cybernetic Organisation, Part III: The Dissolution of Orders.
items.abstract: Why adding further orders of cybernetics, a third, a fourth and beyond, cannot solve the observer problem. Counting orders presupposes the very external standpoint that including the observer was meant to dissolve: each new order reinstates the outside it set out to overcome. The way out lies in a different ontology, one in which observer and observed stand in a chiasmic relation that is reversible rather than nested. -/- The paper moves in five steps. It traces what first- and second-order cybernetics achieved, and the assumptions that survived von Foerster's constructivism and Maturana and Varela's autopoiesis. It maps eleven seams where the mechanistic paradigm meets phenomena it cannot hold, across physics, mathematics, cognitive science and computation, and shows that they converge on one crack. Through Merleau-Ponty's late ontology of flesh and chiasm it derives six requirements for a post-cybernetic account: ecstatic temporality, metabolic transformation, autopoietic closure, embodied situatedness, field integration and constitutive finitude. It examines what each level of mathematics, from set theory to the higher categories, requires and what these phenomena refuse it. And it examines its own reception, stating what the resistance to the argument does and does not show, and what would count against the position. -/- This is the third paper of The Post-Cybernetic Organisation. It supplies the ontology beneath From Cybernetics to Chiasm to Category and The Thermodynamics of Organisational Extraction, and opens the ground on which The Membrane Architecture builds. -/- The Post-Cybernetic Organisation: I. From Cybernetics to Chiasm to Category II. The Thermodynamics of Organisational Extraction III. The Dissolution of Orders IV. The Membrane Architecture.

items.title: The Post-Cybernetic Organisation, Part II: The Thermodynamics of Organisational Extraction.
items.abstract: Where the work that metrics cannot see actually goes, and why burnout follows from it. If formal systems cannot capture an organisation, organisations still function: something closes the gap between the dashboard and the work. This paper states the answer as a conservation law for organisational variety. What formal systems leave uncaptured does not disappear but is displaced, and the displacement runs as a cascade: first to workers, who bridge the gap through cognitive and affective labour; then to the organisation, which accumulates informal debt and fragility; then to products, customers and external parties. In healthcare, transport and infrastructure the cascade can end in death, as the margin between normal operation and lethal failure erodes out of sight. -/- The paper introduces the η operator to describe bridging labour, and develops a thermodynamic reading in which burnout and system failure appear as two signatures of one constraint, the heat signature of a gap the formal system cannot close. It draws on Ashby's law of requisite variety, Heidegger's analysis of technological enframing (Gestell) and research on cognitive load and allostatic stress, with cases from software engineering, healthcare and retail. The framework is diagnostic: it explains why optimisation pressure produces the consequences it does, without prescribing an intervention. -/- This is the second paper of The Post-Cybernetic Organisation. It follows From Cybernetics to Chiasm to Category, which locates the gap, and it is followed by The Dissolution of Orders and The Membrane Architecture. -/- The Post-Cybernetic Organisation: I. From Cybernetics to Chiasm to Category II. The Thermodynamics of Organisational Extraction III. The Dissolution of Orders IV. The Membrane Architecture.

items.title: The Archival Regulator: A General Theory of Regulation Against Metabolic Substrates.
items.abstract: Why per-unit metrics, dashboards and organisational frameworks go wrong in the same place, and why four separate results on measurement turn out to be one. The first is a result on representation: a valuation that gives each unit of an organisation a single figure and reads the whole as their sum is blind to every relational surplus among the people it values. The second is a constraint of conservation: what the formal apparatus does not capture is not eliminated but displaced onto the people who bridge the gap. The third concerns time: a regulator acting faster than its substrate replenishes receives its first signal of depletion only after the point of repair has passed. The fourth concerns dynamics: a reallocation driven by the per-unit instrument can report improvement by consuming the capacity it cannot see. -/- The paper argues that the four are one result, joined by a distinction between two modes of coordinating capacity. A metabolic substrate accrues only through lived time and sustained shared work among specific people, passed on by apprenticeship in Polanyi's sense, and cannot be re-run faster than it was lived. An archival instrument holds its content as retrievable record, indifferent to how long it took to accumulate. Regulation by an archival instrument against a metabolic substrate is the common form of all four results. The argument draws on Ashby's law of requisite variety, the Conant-Ashby theorem, Harsanyi's dividends, rate-distortion theory and Heidegger's Gestell, and carries the diagnosis to the price system and to language models. -/- The paper gathers into one theory results that The Post-Cybernetic Organisation and its companion papers develop separately. -/- Related papers: The Post-Cybernetic Organisation, Part I: From Cybernetics to Chiasm to Category The Post-Cybernetic Organisation, Part II: The Thermodynamics of Organisational Extraction The Post-Cybernetic Organisation, Part III: The Dissolution of Orders The Post-Cybernetic Organisation, Part IV: The Membrane Architecture Topology Without Topography.

items.title: The Symbolic Order of Smell Smell, Perfume, and the Failure of Civilization: Mechanisms of Civilizational Repair in Yasmina Reza’s Der Gott des Gemetzels.
items.abstract: This essay revisits Yasmina Reza’s Der Gott des Gemetzels, arguing that civilizational order depends not only on linguistic norms but also on the temporary stabilization of bodies, objects, and sensory environments. To avoid equating visible objects with perceptible odours, the essay distinguishes references to smell in the playtext, materials on stage that may emit odours, olfactory experiences actually reported by audience members, and the symbolic interpretations researchers draw from these materials. Coffee, refreshments, flowers, and art books are first considered as props of hospitality, taste, and bourgeois self-presentation; Annette’s vomiting and the contamination of the art books then disrupt this order through a bodily event. A public review of the Saarbrücken production reports perfume and cigar smoke reaching the auditorium, but this account documents one reported experience rather than the perceptions of all audience members, and it does not verify the precise action in which the perfume bottle was damaged. The essay defines an “olfactory technique of repair” as a mechanism that may operate across physical cleaning, sensory masking, and social relations, while emphasizing that these are not interchangeable. Perfume may temporarily alter an olfactory environment, yet it may also intensify the perception of contamination; damage to a perfume bottle signals a breach in the controlled boundary of scent, not necessarily the disappearance of the scent itself. The play thus reveals how civilization’s surface depends on sensory techniques for its maintenance, while also showing that such repair cannot automatically resolve violence, responsibility, or interpersonal conflict.

items.title: Disclose Methods, Not Agents: The Performer-Invariance Principle for AI-Assisted Research.
items.abstract: Publishing policies increasingly impose distinct reporting duties on research workflows solely because an artificial intelligence system was used. That performer-based discrimination targets the wrong unit of scientific reporting. This article defends the Performer-Invariance Principle: two workflows equivalent in all claim-relevant operations, decision histories, artifacts, validation procedures, and performance characteristics incur the same scientific reporting obligations, whether the performer is human, an AI system, conventional software, or an instrument. AI use has no independent scientific reportability. It becomes reportable only derivatively, when properties of the actual performer remain necessary to assess evidential warrant, reproducibility, or interpretation. I define a baseline record comprising the operation, inputs and outputs, decision rules, material search and selection history, exact artifacts, and validation. A counterfactual substitution heuristic asks whether a functionally competent alternative performer meeting the same disclosed performance standard would alter a competent reader’s assessment; a residual-relevance test controls the answer. Models that classify observations, select cases, generate synthetic data, or govern adaptive experiments often require detailed characterization. Fixed, independently validated protocols or code artifacts may not. Journals should abolish mandatory standalone AI-use declarations in scientific articles and replace them with operation-specific reporting.

items.title: Perception as Existence——The Unitary Interactive Process of Perceptual Capacity with External Input, Action and Being-Acted-Upon Occurring Simultaneously.
items.abstract: This paper reconstructs the epistemological framework, proposing the core thesis: -/- Perception is not a description of existence. Perception is the unitary interactive process between perceptual capacity and external input — action and being-acted-upon occur simultaneously. It is one of the ways in which existence unfolds itself. -/- This paper positions the structure of perception as follows: -/- Vision, hearing, smell, taste, touch: the processes of cross-validation between perceptual capacity and external input across different channels -/- The integration of perceptual capacity: the integrated operational layer of integration, symbolization, and self-reference -/- The essence of perception: the cross-validation between perceptual capacity and information-energy-state unity, converging through continuous manifestation-concealment into stable perceptual states -/- This paper further clarifies: -/- The relationship between perception and manifestation-concealment: perception itself is an operation of manifestation-concealment — perceptual capacity selectively manifests certain channels of cross-validation while concealing others -/- The relationship between perception and unitary equilibrium: the reality of perception is a state of unitary equilibrium achieved through the convergence of multiple perceptual channels in continuous manifestation-concealment -/- The paper concludes with falsifiability conditions, inviting readers to corroborate or challenge.

items.title: Heidegger.
items.abstract: 100 ans après l’achèvement de l’écriture de Être et temps, nous pouvons en mesurer l’importance pour la philosophie, la pensée politique et la psychiatrie. De la question du sens de être à celle de l’appropriement pour la fondation de la vérité de l’être, Heidegger n’a cessé d’ouvrir des chemins qui l’ont conduit à méditer la métaphysique, l’histoire, la technique moderne et la science, l’art et la parole. Tous ces chemins de pensée appartiennent à la voie de l’histoire de l’être. Et pourtant, à chaque fois, c’est notre existence qui est en jeu. C’est ce qui fait de la pensée de Heidegger – qui s’étend sur une période d’une cinquantaine d’années – une constellation décisive de la philosophie. Lire Heidegger, c’est un peu comme escalader le sommet d’une montagne. Il faut de l’endurance, du souffle et s’y préparer. Cet ouvrage a vocation à faciliter la lecture des textes majeurs de sa pensée, tout en s’appuyant sur des textes non traduits en français. Francesca FERRÉ, agrégée et docteure en philosophie, enseigne en hypokhâgne à Paris. Phénoménologue, ses publications et recherches portent sur les concepts de la philosophie grecque et l’élaboration d’une pensée politique à partir de l’existentialité du Dasein.

items.title: Authority at Scale: Institutional Capacity and the Limits of Presumptive Authority.
items.abstract: An institution’s directives may in fact serve its recipients’ reasons, as Raz’s Normal Justification Thesis requires, while the institution lacks standing to insist that recipients forgo their own checks. This article separates objective authority from that entitlement. For continuing, consequential, and contestable directives, the entitlement depends on two substantiated presuppositions of the demand: that deference is worthwhile for the recipient’s reference class, with a route for individual rebuttal, and that the exposure to error it creates is correctable at the scale of issuance. Given a justified directive role and a decision not reserved to the recipient’s own judgment, the two are jointly sufficient. Serviceability is operationalized by a Scale-Indexed Serviceability test applied to a specified mechanism, lawful architecture, horizon, issuance scale, and claim mix. Failure to substantiate withholds the entitlement; a certified absence of any feasible plan defeats it and requires affected adverse issuance, or its effect, to be restricted to what can be serviced. Neither status invalidates lawful acts. Two consequences follow: a Wide-Scope Duty of Sustainable Issuance binds the bodies controlling scale and capacity, and Deontic Debt preserves directed claims when due obligations are deficiently serviced, even where incapacity is excused. A stipulated benefits administration shows each status at work.

items.title: Explanationism and Bayesianism in Epistemology: Understanding Compatibilism.
items.abstract: Explanationism and Bayesianism are important families of theories in epistemology, and this dissertation defends that they are compatible with each other. The first chapter argues that Explanationism is best understood as a family of theories which hold that the fact that a hypothesis explains certain observations can be a reason to accept that hypothesis. The second chapter argues that Compatibilism is best understood as the view that explanatory considerations can sometimes at least partly determine the relevant probabilities for Bayesian conditionalization, and so can at least partly determine when, according to Bayesianism, it is epistemically appropriate to have certain credences. The third chapter considers William Roche and Elliot Sober’s arguments against inference to the best explanation and shows that these arguments do not threaten the main contentions of Compatibilism. The fourth and final chapter evaluates and defends three arguments supporting Compatibilism.

items.title: Social Roles and Exculpatory Ignorance.
items.pub: Journal of Ethics and Social Philosophy 31 (6):826–859.
items.venue: Journal of Ethics and Social Philosophy
items.abstract: People sometimes attempt to avoid blame with the following excuse: “I didn’t know I was doing anything wrong; I was just doing my job.” I argue that this excuse points towards a distinctive form of genuinely exculpatory ignorance. Complying with social role norms involves following deliberative norms that can explain agents’ claims of ignorance and mitigate their blameworthiness. My account of this experience makes a surprising contribution to the debate over when ignorance excuses. If we accept that nonculpable moral ignorance excuses, my argument highlights a novel form of ignorance that can be experienced by role occupants. On some views, however, what matters is being motivated by the right reasons (having a “good will”), so even nonculpably morally ignorant agents are blameworthy because they are not appropriately responsive to moral considerations. My account challenges the accepted view that having a good will just is responsiveness to moral reasons. I offer role occupants as a case study of moral ignorance with a good will. The fact that our social roles can lead to exculpatory ignorance in this ordinary and pervasive way opens up new territory for theories of moral responsibility.

items.title: Linguistic meaning requires stable concepts.
items.abstract: Shea’s (2024) identifies concepts with temporary working memory (WM) labels: “two-ended” devices connected to stored information at one end and composing with other labels at the other. I argue that this framework cannot yet account for linguistic understanding. First, Shea’s theory requires stable categorical mechanisms to track category identity over time, although he is officially neutral as to their nature. Second, even granting such mechanisms, neither they nor his temporary WM labels can provide the needed compositional vehicles. The empirical evidence I review converges on the need for stable, freely compositional vehicles that I call “G-concepts.” On the view I develop, G-concepts – stable symbols individuated by their compositional role – compose into thoughts and bear word meaning, while “S-concepts” – stable representations that underwrite categorization – orient the mind toward the world. The Hybrid view preserves Shea’s interface insight while providing the compositional resources needed for linguistic cognition.

items.title: Measuring What AI Systems Might Do: Towards A Measurement Science in AI.
items.abstract: Scientists, policy-makers, business leaders, and members of the public care about what modern artificial intelligence systems are disposed to do. Yet terms such as capabilities, propensities, skills, values, and abilities are routinely used interchangeably and conflated with observable performance, with AI evaluation practices rarely specifying what quantity they purport to measure. Building on established dispositional accounts of ability, we argue that capabilities and propensities are dispositional properties—stable features of systems characterised by counterfactual relationships between contextual conditions and behavioural outputs. Measuring a disposition requires (i) hypothesising which contextual properties are causally relevant, (ii) independently operationalising and measuring those properties, and (iii) empirically mapping how variation in those properties affects the probability of the behaviour. Benchmark averages and data-driven latent-variable models like Item Response Theory can provide useful evidence, but do not by themselves identify these causal structures. By developing this principled account of capabilities, propensities, and how to measure them, we are able to outline what disposition-respecting, scientifically defensible AI evaluation would require.
