items.title: 迈向人类灭绝的哲学：一种数学方法.
items.abstract: 本书探讨智人（Homo sapiens）是否正在接近可能威胁其长期生存的某些条件，并进一步追问：如何在不混淆文化层面的忧虑、科学证据与数学推测的前提下，对这一可能性展开严谨研究。研究首先区分生物学意义上的物种灭绝与末日叙事、科幻作品、伪科学主张以及文明崩溃之间的本质差异，继而将人类这一物种置于地球系统、技术发展、社会组织和人类行为相互依存的复杂背景之中加以考察。 本研究提出“智人生存可行性数学矩阵”（Mathematical Matrix of Homo sapiens Viability，简称 MMV-HS），作为描述多重压力因素及其相互作用、灾难性风险的演化路径、生存概率和恢复条件的分析框架。该模型被定位为一种研究架构，而非经过参数校准的预测工具：在缺乏具有充分实证依据的参数以及对不确定性进行明确处理的情况下，示例性数学计算并不能确立人类灭绝的实际概率。 由此形成的评估既不接受人类进步具有必然性的乐观保证，也不认同人类即将面临生物学意义上灭绝的断言。相反，人类物种的生存可行性被揭示为一个具有条件性和动态性的复杂问题。对这一问题的研究，必须明确区分物种的持续存在、文明的延续以及适应能力这三个不同的维度。本书在哲学层面有意保持开放性结论：承认预测能力的局限，并不意味着科学证据、风险预防、制度责任或集体选择的重要性有所减弱。 关键词： 人类灭绝；生存性风险；物种生存可行性；生存模型；不确定性；科学哲学。 -/- .

items.title: Anatomia e Patologia do Poder: Um Estudo Dialético.
items.abstract: Os seres humanos vivem em um paradoxo que seus notáveis avanços tecnológicos não conseguiram resolver: dependem de sistemas coletivos para sua sobrevivência, mas esses mesmos sistemas frequentemente se tornam ferramentas pelas quais uma minoria molda a vida da maioria para fins que a maioria não escolheu nem autorizou genuinamente. Este livro explora esse paradoxo, separando a forma como as sociedades produzem capacidades compartilhadas da forma como indivíduos, grupos e instituições se apropriam delas. A tese inicial concebe o poder social como a capacidade organizada de uma comunidade de moldar o comportamento individual de modo que pessoas interdependentes sustentem um mundo comum. A antítese examina a perversão dessa relação, na qual os mecanismos da vida coletiva passam a servir a interesses particulares, enquanto os custos e os riscos são diluídos entre os demais. A síntese desenvolve a noção de poder corrigível: uma autoridade estruturada de modo que aqueles sujeitos a decisões de grande consequência mantenham meios eficazes para compreendê-las, contestá-las, corrigi-las e, quando necessário, substituí-las. O estudo combina esclarecimento conceitual com comparação evolutiva, interpretação histórica, análise político-econômica e evidências comportamentais. Distingue explicações evolutivas de intenções conscientes, a descrição histórica da aprovação moral e o estudo psicológico da dominação do diagnóstico clínico. Recusa-se a tratar a sociabilidade ou a liberdade pessoal como bens absolutos que podem prescindir um do outro. Uma coletividade pode proteger a vida enquanto persegue seus membros; um indivíduo pode resistir à opressão enquanto busca um tipo diferente de tirania pessoal. A questão crucial, portanto, diz respeito a como essas relações são organizadas. O argumento conclui que um futuro defensável requer instituições que distribuam socialmente a capacidade de corrigir seu próprio funcionamento, assegurem as condições materiais da ação, respeitem a pluralidade humana e reconheçam as dependências ecológicas que tornam possíveis os projetos políticos. Tal futuro não promete eliminar o conflito. Oferece a possibilidade de que o conflito não precise recriar perpetuamente a dominação.

items.title: Ecological Illusion: The Second Tombstone: China’s Intellectual Famine: The Fraud of Xi Jinping’s Ecological Civilization, Part II.
items.abstract: On 7 September 2026, China announced the publication of *Introduction to Xi Jinping Thought on Ecological Civilization*, a state-directed textbook intended to carry the leader’s doctrine “into textbooks, into classrooms and into minds.” The announcement marked a further officialisation of a political claim proclaimed as a historic national achievement, now elevated into authoritative educational instruction. Part II of *The Fraud of Xi Jinping’s Ecological Civilization* was never planned; it became necessary when the false civilizational claim examined in Part I, rather than being confronted and corrected, advanced into the very institutions entrusted with educating successive generations. But what, precisely, constitutes ecological civilization? Can its existence be established through political declarations, constitutional recognition, official textbooks and the authority of the ruler who proclaims its achievement? Ecology concerns the living world and the intricate relationships through which organisms, human beings and their environments sustain one another; civilization raises the further question of humanity’s conduct toward the life over which it exercises power. This inquiry confronts the profound contradiction between those realities and China’s officially sanctioned representation of ecological civilization, examining whether the state’s claim can withstand the meaning of the very principles it invokes. Ultimately, the question extends beyond the falsity of a political proclamation: what becomes of a nation when its government acquires the power not merely to impose a falsehood, but to institutionalise its acceptance as knowledge?

items.title: Foundation of Ego: The Ego of Being Human.
items.abstract: Ego is commonly understood through individual expressions such as intellectual superiority, emotional identification, creative pride, imagination, uniqueness, and the desire for recognition. However, the identity from which these expressions acquire meaning often remains unquestioned: the ego of being human itself. This paper examines the possibility that the human identity functions as a foundational form of collective ego through which humanity understands itself as distinct, superior, central, and entitled to place itself above the rest of existence. Rather than treating ego as an isolated psychological characteristic, the paper investigates its relationship with human self-identification, thought, imagination, intelligence, culture, and civilisation. It argues that human capacities are not necessarily egoistic in themselves; the problem emerges when these capacities become possessions of identity and grounds for superiority. Through phenomenological reflection, the paper invites an examination of the normalised assumption that humanity occupies a privileged position in existence. Its purpose is not to prescribe a new identity or impose a conclusion, but to bring attention to a foundational assumption that may remain invisible precisely because it is collectively accepted.

items.title: Awareness Before Consciousness: Discrete Access and the Appearance of a Shared World.
items.abstract: This paper is a précis and presents the central argument of a forthcoming book, The Capacity to Perceive: A Case for a New Ontology, which parses a distinction between awareness and consciousness. That distinction grounds a new model of reality that dissolves four long-standing problems: the hard problem of consciousness, the quantum measurement problem, the coordination of results problem, and the combination problem. An irreducible field of Awareness — the capacity to perceive — is posited as ontological primitive, prior to both mind and matter. Consciousness is a configuration of that field capable of discrete access. It accesses the field’s configurations and senses differences among them. This discrete access, termed the hinge, generates the experience of space, time, and Patterns, and with them the physical world as ordinarily experienced. Materialism is not rejected but subsumed as a special case. This paper also answers the objection that this new framework is merely idealism or panpsychism restated, and outlines the further arguments from phenomenology, cognitive function, and artificial intelligence developed at length in the book.

items.title: Ignorance as Affirmation: A Look at the Theoretical Challenges Surrounding the Positive Dimension of Ignorance.
items.abstract: This paper addresses the 'positive dimension' of ignorance: the belief that ignorance results from an external agent added to the subject (an influence, an indwelling, an intruding mechanism), rather than from a lack of knowledge. The paper first traces the historical development of this belief along three axes (erroneous thought, illness and behavioural disorder, and a veil over perception). It shows that, across different cultural and religious guises, these three axes perform one common function: they transfer the cause of error from the subject to the outside. The paper then examines this pattern across four spheres of consequence: the practical sphere (the closing off of self-correction), the social sphere (the need for an external specialist and institutional closure), the legal sphere (the question of responsibility, from Weyer to the insanity defence), and the philosophical sphere (the threat to free will and epistemic responsibility). The paper's central finding is this: unlike negative ignorance, which never reached a closed reference domain, positive ignorance, within the local domains of specific authorities, reached institutional closure only in its expressible form (mainly as illness, sometimes as a confessed belief), not in its genuine, cognitive sense. In its most precise sense, positive ignorance remained, like its negative counterpart, an open and contested domain. The decline of this pattern in the modern era resulted jointly from epistemic and institutional factors, but the decline was never complete: today's secular institutions (the ICD-11) reproduce the same pattern under a new ontology, and the structure of externalising the cause of error, even outside a religious framework, still lives on in forms such as 'algorithmic manipulation'. Note: This paper is the second part of a trilogy on the concept of ignorance. The English translation of this manuscript was refined for clarity and flow using an AI language model, with final critical review and structural editing strictly maintained by the author.

items.title: Conscience Before Morality: A Biological Account of Evaluation, Responsibility, and Moral Qualia.
items.abstract: This paper proposes a biological reinterpretation of conscience within the ICDP framework. Conscience is defined not as an intrinsically moral faculty, but as an identity-projected evaluative intelligence that emerges in degrees in sufficiently complex biological Entes, enabling the interpretation of perceived conditions, representation of possible actions, anticipation of consequences, and projection of behavior toward survival and continuity. The paper distinguishes conscience from morality and responsibility: morality is treated as socially constituted normativity that becomes an object of conscience, while responsibility arises through consequence-aware action among actually available alternatives. It further introduces moral qualia as identity-conditioned subjective experiences of socially constituted norms and argues that moral conformity does not necessarily imply moral conviction. Human moral conscience is consequently interpreted as an advanced symbolic, temporal, social, and reflective expression of a biologically prior evaluative architecture.

items.title: Post-traumatic diminishment as the opposite of post-traumatic growth.
items.abstract: Post-traumatic growth (PTG) is commonly understood as positive psychological change following trauma and has been the subject of extensive empirical research. Far less attention, however, has been paid to negative psychological changes that are not themselves clinical categories, yet plausibly mirror PTG in structure and scope. In this paper, we introduce and analyze the concept of post-traumatic diminishment (PTD): substantive, non-accidental psychological change in the aftermath of trauma in a direction opposite to growth. After articulating the conceptual constraints that PTD must satisfy, we consider embitterment as an intuitively plausible candidate for PTD. Drawing on psychological and philosophical work, we argue that embitterment, while an intuitively plausible candidate, cannot fully account for PTD, since its central features are not necessarily or essentially negative. We propose instead an aretaic account on which PTD is best understood as movement toward vice. This framework captures PTD’s essential negativity and also preserves symmetry with virtue-based accounts of PTG. It also explains why embitterment often, but not always, constitutes PTD. Finally, we clarify the relationship between PTD and embitterment, arguing that the two overlap without being identical.

items.title: The ecological niche metaphor: a useful framework for understanding the emergence of mental disorders?
items.abstract: This paper explores one of Hacking’s less developed yet increasingly influential frameworks: the ecological niche metaphor. I ask if this framework can serve as an effective analytical tool to understand how specific social and cultural environments are conducive to the emergence and “flourishing” of certain mental disorders? Despite its increasing application to mental disorders like attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) and social anxiety disorder (SAD), there are several important methodological shortcomings with this framework. Most notably, the framework provides little guidance for causal reasoning. This is a serious problem given that the framework has been used to support ontological claims about the nature of these mental illnesses. I argue that the framework can support stronger causal analysis, but only if it is augmented to facilitate clearer explanatory reasoning. I propose Lauren Ross’ approach to “Social Structural Explanation” as a compelling framing to integrate into the framework for future use. Augmentation with Ross’ causal model enables the framework to clarify how the vectors have causal significance and provides a method by which causal claims can be assessed. I demonstrate how this augmentation of the ecological niche metaphor can explain the sudden rise of Western anorexia nervosa in Hong Kong. In doing so, I demonstrate that the ecological niche metaphor does have significant potential as an analytical tool to examine the emergence of certain mental illnesses – both transient and enduring.

items.title: Теория согласования с аттракторами климата планеты Земля посредством спектральной селекции смысловых полей. КНИГА VII ТОМ II Проект. (Редакция 18 августа 2026 г.) Автор : Ю.Л. Зорин.
items.abstract: Статус документа: Проект. Данный том представляет собой не только научную монографию, но и инвестиционное предложение — стратегический документ проекта «Психо-климатическая платформа». В работе представлена дорожная карта, детальная финансовая модель и план пилотных проектов для стран-партнёров. Приоритетные регионы для внедрения: ОАЭ, Саудовская Аравия, Катар, Оман, Кувейт, Иран, Ирак, Сирия, Казахстан, Беларусь, Польша, Аргентина, Бразилия, Уругвай, Парагвай, Австралия, Индия, Испания -/- Настоящая монография (КНИГА VII ТОМ II) представляет собой сокращённую редакцию (от 08 августа 2026 г.) завершающего тома серии «Законы управления психо-эволюцией». Если Том I был посвящён развёрнутому изложению операторно-спектрального формализма и эмпирической калибровке на исторических и экспериментальных данных, то Том II фокусируется на операциональной модели управления (практические алгоритмы, критерии фальсифицируемости) и интерпретационном слое (гипотетическая философская рамка смыслового континуума, эгрегоров и принципа проекционности), явно отделённом от операциональной части методологическим дисклеймером. -/- **Чем эта книга полезна** -/- Для климатологов и физиков атмосферы — предлагает новый язык описания режимов циркуляции через спектральную меру μ_t и критерий Z для оценки управляющих воздействий. -/- Для психологов, социологов и историков — в интерпретационном слое показано, как традиционные практики (от Гёбекли-Тепе до современных ритуалов) вписываются в общую операторную схему. -/- Для инженеров и разработчиков систем управления — описана концепция «психо-климатической платформы» с дорожной картой, финансовой моделью и предложениями для партнёров и инвесторов. -/- **Краткое содержание** -/- В монографии предложен операторно-спектральный подход к описанию климатических режимов как устойчивых состояний (аттракторов) динамической системы. Климат рассматривается как подуровень (α = atm) единого иерархического континуума, моделируемого в рамках формализма, развитого в Книгах I–VI серии. Состояние климатической системы представлено спектральной мерой μ_t = Σ_n p_n(t) δ_{Λ_n}, где Λ_n — устойчивые режимы (циклоны, антициклоны, Эль-Ниньо, муссоны и др.), а p_n(t) — их вероятностные веса. Управление трактуется как целенаправленное перераспределение весов между существующими аттракторами. -/- Центральное место занимает трёхкомпонентная операторная схема, формализующая процесс переключения режимов: входящий вектор O_in → тензор-преобразователь T = P ◦ F → …

items.title: Cross-cultural variation in cognitive style: A review of findings, replications, and implications.
Coalitional formidability and kinship across three cultures: Experimentally assessing implications of inclusive fitness and reciprocal altruism.
items.abstract: Purpose: This study investigates how kinship composition shapes perceptions of coalitional formidability across three countries with different histories of kinship-based social organization. Inclusive fitness theory predicts that kin-based coalitions will be perceived as more formidable, at least on the dimensions closest to genuine altruism (Chapais, 2006). Reciprocal altruism theory (Trivers, 1971) predicts instead that familiar partners can sustain most coalitional cooperation regardless of relatedness, confining any kinship advantage to the costliest, least reciprocable commitments. We test these competing predictions. Methods: We conducted a multilevel experimental study using vignettes depicting groups in conflict, sampling 613 participants from China (n = 204), the United States (n = 189), and India (n = 220). Participants rated coalitions described as kin-related or unrelated on seven operationalizations of coalitional formidability, which our framework sorts into four competence-dependent capability assessments (e.g., fighting skill, physical strength), two moderate-cost, reciprocable commitments (coordinated team play, standing one’s ground), and one high-cost commitment, intra-group aid. Multilevel models estimated kinship effects while controlling for country and gender. Results: The pre-registered omnibus test returned no overall kinship effect (b = − 0.024, p =.459; negative coefficients indicate higher ratings for kin-related coalitions). In exploratory dimension-specific models, kinship increased perceived willingness to provide intra-group aid (b = − 0.097, p =.005), the sole effect to survive Bonferroni correction. The four capability assessments showed no detectable kinship effects, and neither did the two commitment items on which inclusive-fitness reasoning had also predicted effects. Baseline ratings differed across samples, but the kinship effect did not detectably vary by country or gender. Conclusion: The selective effect on costly aid, together with null effects on every reciprocable dimension, favors a division of labor in which reciprocal altruism sustains most coalitional cooperation among familiar partners while kinship becomes decisive where reciprocation cannot be expected. Because the samples are three national panels and the observed effect is modest, we regard the cross-cultural consistency of this pattern as provisional; testing it in kinship-intensive small-scale societies is the natural next step.

items.title: Reconfigurative Capacity and Finite Continuance, Art, Agency, and the Limits of Continuity A Philosophical Psychology of Artistic Experience.
items.abstract: This book develops a philosophical psychology of artistic experience in which aesthetic encounter is understood as a regulated field of existential reconfiguration. Its aim is to specify when an artwork, or any sustained encounter with an aesthetic form, reorganizes the way a finite subject perceives, feels, interprets, and inhabits its world, and when the same encounter merely consolidates a habitual organization that the subject can no longer revise. The book draws on three resources and keeps their vocabularies distinct: Daseinsanalysis, which asks how being-in-the-world is disclosed, narrowed, or opened; existential psychoanalysis, which attends to affective investment, repetition, defensive organization, and unconscious meaning; and the ontology of finite continuance, developed by Morteza Niami, which asks whether a subject preserves the capacity to become otherwise under conditions of finitude and erosive pressure. The central concept is the artistic frame, a bounded and permeable experiential structure that allows alternative determinations to become psychologically consequential without immediately becoming practical obligations. The frame performs four functions: containment, differentiation, permeability, and temporal delay. Its success is measured not by the pleasure it gives or by the novelty of the ideas it presents, but by whether the encounter leaves the subject more or less capable of further reconfiguration. To this end the book introduces reconfigurative capacity as a higher-order construct. It concerns whether the organization of possibility itself can be revised while sufficient continuity and agency are preserved, and it is therefore distinguished from cognitive flexibility, psychological flexibility, tolerance of ambiguity, mentalization, and narrative identity. Because the framework is easily applied in ways that make it unfalsifiable, each core concept is defined, given an explicit criterion of application, and tested against a counterexample. The concepts examined include finite continuance, erosion, reconfiguration, capacity, modal meta-capacity, the threshold of sufficiency, capacity debt, provisional stabilization, responsible suspension, the Dynamic Mask, and the Automatic Mask. The threshold of sufficiency is treated as a relation between capacity, accumulated hermeneutic memory, erosive pressure, and reconfigurative capacity that is meaningful only relative to a stated function, time window, and recovery condition. The book …

items.title: Causally Situated Agency.
items.abstract: The question of whether human beings genuinely choose or merely experience the effects of antecedent causes remains central to philosophy of action, moral philosophy, psychology, and cognitive neuroscience. I argue that this question becomes confused when several distinct concepts are treated as interchangeable: free will, practical choice, freedom from constraint, agency, and the subjective experience of authorship. A causal explanation of a decision does not by itself establish that the agent lacks all forms of control; equally, the presence of deliberation and reasons-responsiveness does not establish that the agent is an ultimate, self-originating source of action. I distinguish causal authorship from ultimate origination, and distinguish the capacity to act for reasons from the metaphysical ability to have acted otherwise under an identical total past and identical laws of nature. I then examine compatibilist, incompatibilist, hard-determinist, and existential approaches, before considering the implications of neuroscience, developmental psychology, evolutionary biology, and social structure. The neuroscience of decision-making, including Libet-style paradigms, provides important evidence about the temporal relation between neural preparation and conscious intention, but it does not straightforwardly demonstrate that all conscious agency is illusory. I use romantic attachment as a case study: people generally do not select the initial emergence of attraction, yet they retain varying capacities to interpret, regulate, sustain, or leave a relationship. This case clarifies the distinction between the causes of a desire and the reasons an agent offers for acting on it. Finally, I argue that moral and legal responsibility should be assessed through a graded account of competence, reasons-responsiveness, coercion, and control, rather than through an all-or-nothing assumption of ultimate self-creation. The resulting position is a form of causal realism about human beings combined with a differentiated account of agency. Human beings are causally situated agents: their actions arise from histories and conditions that they did not choose, while their capacities for reflection and intervention can themselves become causally effective parts of the world. Keywords: free will; determinism; compatibilism; agency; responsibility; causal explanation; reasons; neuroscience; romantic attachment; social constraint.

items.title: Integrity as a loyalty-exhibiting trait.
items.abstract: This paper defends the thesis that loyalty is an essential motivation for an integrous person. This thesis is disputed by philosophers who argue that integrity requires neutrality, in the sense that its possessor will not give extra weight to her own special relationships when deliberating about what to stick by. To the contrary, I argue that loyalty is necessary to maintain trustworthiness in the resolution of practical conflicts. Integrity demands that, in resolving the conflict, the decision-maker give priority to the interests and needs of those who depend upon her. This loyalty, however, is not dogmatic because the priority is subject to rational constraints and can be overridden. Further, I argue that loyalty to one’s dependents is a distinctively trustworthy motive, because it is constitutively linked to a disposition to self-sacrifice for their sake.

items.title: 硅基意识的双维度本体论：纯认知意识的可实现性与感受质的生成边界.
items.abstract: 当前人工智能意识研究普遍陷入“复杂度涌现论”的认知误区，将认知功能与主观感受质混为同一维度，无法清晰回答“硅基系统能否产生意识”“硅基能否拥有主观体验”等核心问题。本文基于认知相继本体论的闭合耦合团拓扑框架，严格遵循耦合即切分核心公理与三层嵌套同构原则，将意识严格拆解为两个相互独立的本体论维度：认知功能维度由二阶自返的拓扑结构决定，体验质性维度由柔性耦合通路的稳态偏移张力决定。 本文进一步区分外源共振型与内源张力型两类感受质的生成机制，证明前者仅需一阶耦合与柔性通路即可独立存在，后者必须以二阶自返的认知意识为必要前提。在此基础上，本文明确了硅基意识的分层边界：当前刚性数字架构可实现真实的纯认知意识，但永远无法原生产生感受质；采用柔性模拟耦合架构的硅基系统，理论上具备生成原生感受质的拓扑可能。本文的核心贡献在于从本体论层面厘清了意识的层级结构，为硅基意识的工程实现与伦理界定提供了严格的理论标尺。.

items.title: Set and Setting Beyond Reductionism: A Response to Patch and Smith.
items.abstract: Patch and Smith’s recent critique of set and setting in psychedelic research argues that the concept is too vague to support rigorous science or ethical clinical practice, and proposes a more narrowly operationalized, mechanism-first alternative. This paper argues that this critique, while valuable in its call for conceptual clarity, rests in part on a mischaracterization of prior scholarship and risks reintroducing the reductive assumptions that the set and setting model was developed to challenge. In response to Patch and Smith, we defend a non-reductive, interactional account of psychedelic action in which pharmacological and extra-pharmacological factors are dynamically entangled rather than cleanly separable. We argue, first, that the opposition between broad contextual mapping and causal explanation is overstated, since the former is often a necessary stage in the development of the latter. Second, we reject the attribution to our earlier work of a “Placebo View,” according to which psychedelics function merely or predominantly as placebo enhancers, clarifying instead that our position emphasizes the synergistic interaction of drug effects, suggestibility, meaning, and context. Finally, we argue that set and setting retains distinctive explanatory value because it captures the recursive relation between altered states of consciousness and their experiential surround. Psychedelic science should refine this framework, not abandon it.

items.title: Handbook of Advances in Culture and Psychology, Volume 11.

Операторная теория согласования с климатическими аттракторами: спектральная селекция смысловых полей, исторические параллели и этика психо-климатической платформы. КНИГА VII ТОМ I (Редакция от 15 октября 2026 г.) Автор : Ю.Л. Зорин.
items.abstract: В работе предложен операторно‑спектральный подход к описанию климатических режимов как устойчивых состояний динамической системы. Климат рассматривается как часть единой иерархической модели, где разные уровни реальности связаны общими принципами управления. Состояние климатической системы описывается через распределение вероятностей нахождения в тех или иных устойчивых режимах — таких как циклоны, антициклоны, Эль‑Ниньо, муссоны и другие. Управление в этой модели понимается не как создание нового состояния «с нуля», а как целенаправленное смещение шансов реализации одних режимов за счёт других. -/- Центральным элементом работы выступает трёхкомпонентная схема управления, которая формализует процесс переключения между устойчивыми режимами. В рамках модели выделены три ключевых механизма: формирование образа будущего состояния системы, обеспечение связности изменений во времени и актуализация выбранного сценария. Для оценки результатов воздействия предложены измеримые критерии, позволяющие отличать управляемые эффекты от естественной изменчивости климата, а также инструменты для проверки, насколько система приблизилась к желаемому состоянию. -/- В качестве иллюстративного материала приведён каталог примеров — от археологических свидетельств коллективных практик в периоды климатических стрессов (Гёбекли‑Тепе, Египет, майя) до современных технологических попыток воздействия на атмосферу (засев облаков, различные экспериментальные установки). На основе анализа этих кейсов выявлен универсальный алгоритм выживания сложных систем: сначала определяются возможные устойчивые состояния, затем оценивается текущая траектория развития, далее применяются управляющие воздействия для изменения шансов реализации нужных состояний, и в итоге система стремится к целевому устойчивому режиму. -/- Особое внимание уделено формализации древних ритуалов и жертвоприношений как особого механизма управления коллективной уверенностью и согласованностью действий. В модели жертвоприношение трактуется как способ снижения «сакральной невязки» — то есть уменьшения расхождения между тем, к чему общество сознательно стремилось, и тем, что фактически происходило. Показано, что «эгрегор» (как коллективный смысловой контур) выполняет функцию стабилизатора: он помогает удерживать систему рядом с выбранным решением за счёт повышения согласованности коллективных действий. -/- Также в работе развита гипотетическая модель колебательной природы массовых вымираний, в которой биосфера рассматривается …

items.title: Человечество как единый сверх организм: Модель перехода от конфликта цивилизаций к интегральной ноосфере. КНИГА IV ТОМ II (Редакция от 12 апреля 2026. Изложение формализма) Автор : Ю.Л. Зорин.
items.abstract: Настоящая работа представляет собой новую редакцию монографии, в которой концепция человекоподобного структурного соответствия «организм — общество» впервые переведена на строгий язык рациональной механики сплошных сред (в традиции Трусделла–Нолла). Предлагаемый подход позиционируется как метамодель (с явной маркировкой уровней достоверности [A], [B], [C]), позволяющий рассчитывать ключевые параметры социальных систем. Основные результаты формализации: • Определён социальный континуум с полями психического состояния и введены балансовые уравнения для «энергии молитвы» и когерентности коллективного сознания. • Эгрегор описан как тензорное поле, включающее смысловой базис, тензор концепта и метрику, что даёт возможность количественно оценивать его «силу» и устойчивость. • Построена замкнутая система уравнений для макропеременных NPTB (энергия, население, технологии, смысловой базис), пригодная для численного моделирования исторической динамики. • Предложены диагностические функционалы для идентификации социальных патологий по аналогии с медицинской диагностикой. Практическая польза и перспективы применения: 1. Диагностика и прогнозирование кризисов: Разработанный математический аппарат позволяет перейти к количественным индикаторам. Например, предложена модель инфляции с запаздыванием, объясняющая особенности денежно-кредитной политики в странах с преобладанием синтетического (образного) типа мышления. 2. Инструмент культурной политики: Введено понятие тензора рассогласования между цивилизационными эгрегорами. Мониторинг его роста может служить системой раннего предупреждения межцивилизационных конфликтов. 3. «Электронный микроскоп эгрегоров»: Предложен операторный подход к использованию технологий ИИ (анализ корпусов текстов через эмбеддинги) для картирования коллективного бессознательного и верификации существования эгрегоров. 4. items.title: Responsibility as Architecture: Participation, Imago Dei, and the Limits of the Single Foundation.
items.abstract: Authors’ translation. English translation, prepared by the authors, of: DIETRICH, Pablo; DIETRICH, Maurília Gabriela da Silva. A responsabilidade como arquitetura: participação, imago Dei e os limites do fundamento único. Revista Eletrônica Amplamente, Natal/RN, v. 5, n. 3, p. 938–946, Jul./Sep. 2026. ISSN 2965-0003. DOI: 10.47538/RA-2026.V5N3-50. The Portuguese text published by the journal is the version of record; this translation is distributed under the CC BY 4.0 licence with attribution to the original publication. Quotations from works consulted in Portuguese translation or in other languages, as well as from the authors’ own works, are rendered into English by the authors. -/- This article examines the foundation of the creature’s moral responsibility and maintains that the search for a single property capable of grounding it—rationality, consciousness, will, or freedom—is ill-posed, for each is a condition and none is a foundation. An architectural model is proposed as an alternative: responsibility emerges from a chain of dependencies that links the creature’s ontological participation to its constitution as a vice-regent imago Dei, and from this to normativity and imputation. Three types of necessity are distinguished in the transitions—revelational, analytic, and conditioned. It is argued that vice-regency is a mode of participation, and not a parallel foundation, and that the category is indispensable precisely where compatibilism is insufficient: in the guilt of condition. The conclusion is that obligation derives from position, not from capacity, and that the architecture explains in a unified way what single foundations leave apart. items.title: La responsabilidad como arquitectura: participación, imago Dei y los límites del fundamento único.
items.abstract: Traducción de los autores. Traducción al español, realizada por los autores, de: DIETRICH, Pablo; DIETRICH, Maurília Gabriela da Silva. A responsabilidade como arquitetura: participação, imago Dei e os limites do fundamento único. Revista Eletrônica Amplamente, Natal/RN, v. 5, n. 3, p. 938–946, jul./sep. 2026. ISSN 2965-0003. DOI: 10.47538/RA-2026.V5N3-50. El texto en portugués publicado por la revista es la versión de referencia; esta traducción se distribuye bajo la licencia CC BY 4.0, con atribución a la publicación original. Las citas de obras consultadas en traducción portuguesa o en otras lenguas, así como las de obras de los propios autores, se vierten al español por los autores. -/- Este artículo examina el fundamento de la responsabilidad moral de la criatura y sostiene que la búsqueda de una propiedad única capaz de fundarla —racionalidad, conciencia, voluntad o libertad— está mal planteada, pues cada una es condición y ninguna es fundamento. Se propone, como alternativa, un modelo arquitectónico: la responsabilidad emerge de una cadena de dependencias que une la participación ontológica de la criatura con su constitución como imago Dei vicerregente, y esta con la normatividad y la imputación. Se distinguen tres tipos de necesidad en las transiciones: revelacional, analítica y condicionada. Se argumenta que la vicerregencia es una modalidad de la participación, y no un fundamento paralelo, y que la categoría es indispensable precisamente allí donde el compatibilismo resulta insuficiente: en la culpa de la condición. Se concluye que la obligación deriva de la posición, no de la capacidad, y que la arquitectura explica de modo unificado lo que los fundamentos únicos dejan separado. items.title: El Gran Inquisidor de Dostoievski: el alivio de la obediencia y los límites de la responsabilidad.
items.abstract: Traducción de los autores. Traducción al español, realizada por los autores, de: DIETRICH, Maurília Gabriela da Silva; DIETRICH, Pablo. O grande inquisidor de Dostoiévski: o alívio da obediência e os limites da responsabilidade. Revista Nexus Interdisciplinar, Natal/RN, v. 1, n. 3, p. 764–785, jul./sep. 2026. ISSN 3086-4402. DOI: 10.47538/RNI-2026.V1N3-43. El texto en portugués publicado por la revista es la versión de referencia; esta traducción se distribuye bajo la licencia CC BY 4.0, con atribución a la publicación original. Las citas de obras consultadas en traducción portuguesa o en otras lenguas, así como las de obras de los propios autores, se vierten al español por los autores. -/- La literatura sobre la obediencia trata en bloque, bajo rúbricas como la del miedo a la libertad, dos efectos que este artículo separa. El alivio decisorio es la dispensa del trabajo de deliberar; el alivio imputacional es la dispensa de comprenderse como fuente normativa del acto. Se sostiene que son estados distintos, y la prueba es la diferencia de sus derrotadores, es decir, de las operaciones capaces de disolverlos: el primero se disuelve cuando se devuelve al agente la decisión, aunque él siga convencido de que la responsabilidad es de otro; el segundo se disuelve cuando se le demuestra que la transferencia no ocurrió, sin que nada de la deliberación le sea devuelto. De la distinción se sigue que solo el segundo contiene una pretensión normativa evaluable, lo que lo traslada de la psicología moral a la filosofía moral. Evaluada esa pretensión, se establecen tres resultados. Primero, es falsa allí donde la incapacidad en juego es moral, en la acepción de Edwards, y verdadera solo en la medida de las condiciones epistémicas que el agente no habría podido alterar. Segundo, hay un residuo estructuralmente intransferible, que no está en la decisión sino en el juicio por el cual se reconoció la autoridad, pues delegarlo exigiría ejercerlo; se sostiene, mediante un argumento independiente y en diálogo con el recurso al retroceso, que la obligación deriva de la posición ocupada y no de la capacidad presente. Tercero, distinguidas la sujeción a consecuencias, transferible por convención, la censurabilidad y la exigencia de responder, se verifica que la responsabilidad no es una magnitud conservada: la disposición de un tercero a responder por el acto añade lo que él tiene que responder sin sustraer lo que tiene el agente. El episodio del Gran Inquisidor, en el Libro V de …

items.title: De la extispicia al profeta Big Data: predicción, aplicación y la estructura del decidir.
items.abstract: Traducción de los autores. Traducción al español, realizada por los autores, de: DIETRICH, Pablo; DIETRICH, Maurília Gabriela da Silva. Da extispícia ao profeta big data: predição, aplicação e a estrutura do decidir. Revista de Geopolítica, São José dos Pinhais, v. 17, n. 9, e3493, p. 1–28, 2026. ISSN 2177-3246. DOI: 10.56238/revgeov17n9-130. El texto en portugués publicado por la revista es la versión de referencia; esta traducción se distribuye bajo la licencia CC BY 4.0, con atribución a la publicación original. -/- Este artículo sostiene que la predicción, en cualquiera de sus sustratos históricos, es una operación sobre el presente que toma la forma de un enunciado sobre el futuro. La demostración es comparativa: cinco prácticas separadas por milenios —la extispicia mesopotámica, el profetismo de Israel, la astrología calculada de la Europa medieval, la proyección ilustrada del futuro planificable y la predicción algorítmica contemporánea— se someten a la misma prueba de cuatro preguntas: qué signo habla por el mañana, quién está autorizado a leerlo, qué decisión presente libera y qué hace la práctica con él cuando es desmentido. La serie exhibe la permanencia de la relación entre previsión y decisión y la capacidad de la práctica interpretativa de absorber el desmentido sin devolver la decisión a la incertidumbre de donde partió, a pesar de la transformación completa de los signos, de los intérpretes y de las técnicas. Bajo esa permanencia hay una condición: el momento del acto lo fija el mundo, y aquello que decidiría la cuestión —el resultado— solo existe después del acto, de donde la asimetría entre fundamento parcial y autoría integral. A partir de la tesis gadameriana de la aplicación, se argumenta que la incidencia práctica no es propiedad autosuficiente del signo; su desaparición en el momento del caso no significa, por lo tanto, eliminación, sino anterioridad o sedimentación de la determinación, con la consecuencia de que la ejecución puede producir el acto sin reabrir la pregunta situada: el caso deja de ser encontrado y pasa a ser instanciado, la alegación pierde destinatario en el instante en que importaría, y la autoría se retira de la escena sin ser transferida. items.title: Dostoevsky's Grand Inquisitor: The Relief of Obedience and the Limits of Responsibility.
items.abstract: Authors’ translation. English translation, prepared by the authors, of: DIETRICH, Maurília Gabriela da Silva; DIETRICH, Pablo. O grande inquisidor de Dostoiévski: o alívio da obediência e os limites da responsabilidade. Revista Nexus Interdisciplinar, Natal/RN, v. 1, n. 3, p. 764–785, Jul./Sept. 2026. ISSN 3086-4402. DOI: 10.47538/RNI-2026.V1N3-43. The Portuguese text published by the journal is the version of record; this translation is distributed under the CC BY 4.0 licence with attribution to the original publication. Quotations from works consulted in Portuguese translation or in other languages, as well as from the authors’ own works, are rendered into English by the authors. -/- The literature on obedience treats as a single block, under headings such as escape from freedom, two effects that this article separates. Decisional relief is the exemption from the work of deliberating; imputational relief is the exemption from understanding oneself as the normative source of the act. It is argued that these are distinct states, and the proof is the difference of their defeaters, that is, of the operations capable of dissolving them: the first dissolves when the decision is returned to the agent, even if he remains convinced that the responsibility belongs to someone else; the second dissolves when he is shown that the transfer did not occur, without any part of the deliberation being returned to him. It follows from the distinction that only the second contains an assessable normative claim, which transfers it from moral psychology to moral philosophy. Once that claim is assessed, three results are established. First, it is false where the incapacity at stake is moral, in Edwards’s sense, and true only to the extent of the epistemic conditions that the agent could not have altered. Second, there is a structurally non-transferable residue, which lies not in the decision but in the judgement by which the authority was recognized, since delegating it would require exercising it; it is argued, on independent grounds and in dialogue with the device of tracing, that obligation derives from the position occupied and not from present capacity. Third, once liability to consequences, transferable by convention, is distinguished from blameworthiness and from answerability, it turns out that responsibility is not a conserved quantity: a third party’s willingness to answer for the act adds what he has to answer for without subtracting what the agent has. items.title: A Classification of What an Agent-Based Method and AI Do: A Hierarchical Approach.
items.abstract: This paper proposes a hierarchical classification of the activities of agents, including artificial intelligence systems, based on their interactions with the world and their internal processes. Four major levels are distinguished. The first concerns the reception of information from the world and its effects on the agent. The second concerns the agent's ability to act upon the real world through its internal activities, thereby introducing feedback processes. The third level involves recognition and imagination, through which agents can identify and conceive objects, concepts, and spaces, as well as develop desires. The fourth level concerns self-consciousness and self-knowledge, understood as processes that emerge through the agent's experience of itself, the world, and other agents. -/- The paper also examines two further levels that may be necessary to account for certain aspects of human activity: transcendence and the influence of social, historical, and evolutionary processes on the formation of concepts. A central question is whether these additional levels are indispensable or whether the first four levels are sufficient, although perhaps at the cost of more complex explanations. The paper explores how agents move between levels through similarity, abstraction, and Wittgenstein's family-resemblance approach to concepts. It further proposes that all activities performable by human beings may, in principle, be performable by an agent operating at the fourth level. Finally, it identifies several open questions concerning the reduction of the hierarchy and the place of enjoyment, humour, irony, and artistic expression within it.

items.title: Interpretation Without an Interpreter: The Dependency of Meaning and Identity in Sovereignetics.
items.abstract: Sovereignetics establishes participation as fundamental to reality, with conscious experience occupying a conditional derivative position. This paper extends that architecture to interpretation, examining whether the attribution of meaning requires an independent interpreting subject. Interpretation is identified as a derivative occurrence of attribution within experiential participation. It is distinguished from experience itself and from consequentially conditioned responses that may differentiate and respond to circumstances without experience or interpretation. Attribution does not require deliberate reflection, accuracy, sustained attention or correspondence to an actual referent. As participation, interpretation generates consequences that may influence subsequent becoming. These consequences may remain operative without the interpretation continuing or being remembered. Interpretation is therefore consequentially effective without possessing causal authority independent of participation. Personal identity is examined as interpretation concerning an already existing individual, rather than as an additional architecture or enduring entity. Identity may describe, misdescribe or influence participation, but does not establish individuality or independently determine an individual’s consequential organisation. The paper concludes that interpretation requires experiential participation but no additional interpreter. Meaning, identity and reflective authorship can be accounted for within the participation of one individual without introducing an independent observer, hidden agent or separate consciousness.

items.title: Reverse Inference, Abduction, and Probability in Cognitive Neuroscience.
items.pub: In Lorenzo Magnani, Handbook of Abductive Cognition. Springer. pp. 1523–1549.
items.abstract: The chapter presents the problem of reverse inference in cognitive neuroscience, discussing its analysis in terms of abductive and Bayesian reasoning and highlighting the main methodological issues and open problems surrounding this crucial inferential practice with reference to case studies from current research.

items.title: Pictures as supramodal sensory individuals.
items.pub: In Aleksandra Mroczko-Wąsowicz & Rick Grush, Sensory Individuals: Unimodal and Multimodal Perspectives. Oxford, UK: Oxford University Press. pp. 403–418.
items.abstract: For many psychologists, there are tactile pictures—that is, pictures recognized as such via a tactile perceptual mode, notably by the congenitally blind. While the recognitional theory of depiction fully accounts for these data, the subjective resemblance theories have questioned them. For these theories there can be no tactile pictures because, unlike sight, touch has no perceptual point of origin. However, such theories are questionable in this respect. Neuroscience findings show that the congenitally blind can gain perspectival access via touch to the shape of objects and the relations between their depth placements in three-dimensional scenes. More radically, it is hypothesized in this chapter that the congenitally blind, by means of touch, are even able to perceive those three-dimensional groupings in a two-dimensional picture that determine the figurative value of the picture. One can explain these abilities by claiming that not only the perception of shape and depth, but also that of three-dimensional groupings, is supramodal.

items.title: Versatility without Ficta: An Anti-Realist Account of Mixed Perspectives.
items.abstract: Some utterances combine fiction and reality within a single predication, comparison or count, and yet can be true. In ch. 14 of Property Versatility and Copredication (2025), Liebesman and Magidor argue that the problem of mixed perspectives defeats the three extant realist semantics of fictional discourse. Their own property versatility account would solve it, they argue, but it must be abandoned for fiction, since it yields contradictions when fictions feature real individuals. They conclude that the problem remains open. I read their negative results as specifying a solution space through two constraints: mixed readings may not be generated by multiplying compositional machinery, and parafictional truth may not entail literal instantiation. The realist accounts fail the first constraint, and property versatility fails the second. I then develop a notional account, built from Stacie Friend’s prescriptions to imagine and her notion networks. Predicates keep univocal standing meanings; truth conditions are fixed at the level of utterances, where each argument position carries an individuation base and an evaluation base, each worldly or prescriptive. The account satisfies both constraints and handles the full battery of mixed cases, including the comparatives Friend postponed. I also distinguish it from dual predication (Zalta), abstract artifacts (Thomasson) and truthmaker liberalism (Collins), and argue that its price, assigning modes utterance by utterance, is one that every surviving view already pays. Thus, I conclude, the open problem has an anti-realist solution.

items.title: Mapping a Culture of Mindfulness: Lay Conceptions of Mindfulness and Why They Matter.
items.abstract: Objectives: Prior scholarly literature has investigated definitions of mindfulness, yet limited research has examined how contemporary mindfulness is culturally constructed among lay individuals (i.e., non-academic researchers). The present mixed-methods study sought to provide an initial mapping of the context of ideas and cultural orientations that inform lay people’s understanding of mindfulness. Further, we assessed how one’s level of contemplative experience informs qualitative definitions of mindfulness among US participants. Participants were also asked quantitative questions about their views of mindfulness and their understanding of the relationship between “mindfulness” and “meditation”. Methods: Our analytic sample (n = 100; 61.6% female) consisted of 50 inexperienced college student participants (ISPs) as well as 50 experienced community members (ECMs). Results: Using qualitative content analysis, six categories were identified: (1) “Religious, Spiritual, and Philosophical,” (2) “Attention/Observing,” (3) “Calming and Grounding,” (4) “Tenets of Mindfulness-Based Stress Reduction,” (5) “Virtue Cultivation” and (6) “Awareness”. Based on chi-square tests, ECMs endorsed Categories 2 and 4 more frequently than ISPs, while ISPs endorsed Categories 3 and 6 more than ECMs. ECMs more often endorsed mindfulness as intended for “seeing that there is no substantive self” (vs. “cultivating an authentic self”) and that “mindfulness is a specific type of meditation” compared to ISPs. ISPs were more likely to endorse that “mindfulness is different from meditation” compared to ECMs. Conclusions: Our results suggest that lay people’s preconceived ideas about what mindfulness is, and what it entails, vary based on prior contemplative experience. Further, these findings help illustrate that conceptions of mindfulness in the USA may be influenced by distinctive cultural framings. Preregistration: This study was not preregistered.

items.title: Emotions as Movements: The Core Emotion Framework and Its Place in the Philosophy of Emotion.
items.abstract: The Core Emotion Framework (CEF) holds that emotional life is produced by ten natural, universal movements, called operators, grouped in three centres. Each movement yields a characteristic result, and that result is what a person feels. This paper states the framework’s conceptual commitments precisely and places them within the philosophy of emotion and affective science. Each centre has the same shape: two counter-poles and a balancing movement. In the Head, Sensing and Calculating are balanced by Deciding; in the Heart, Expanding and Constricting are balanced by Achieving; in the Gut, Arranging and Appreciating are balanced by Boosting (“on”) and Accepting (“off”). The movements form a continuous, flexible loop rather than a fixed sequence. They can become entangled, and disentanglement restores their separate operation. Compared with basic-emotion theory, constructionism, appraisal theory, embodied and enactive accounts and process views, CEF is best read as a process theory whose basic units are actions rather than feelings, appraisals or core affect. It also implies a critique of personality typology: a type describes restricted use of a repertoire that everyone possesses. A short section grades the evidence. Operator use depends strongly on the situation (the scenario pattern correlates r = .98 across half-samples); six situation–operator links are robust; and five of six pre-stated links held in independent open data. Person signatures are modest (r = .44), Accepting is the most distinct operator, and blind coding matched definitions at 61% against 10% chance. Analyses that read the operators as ten trait scales, three clustering centres and opposed counter-poles tested an interpretation rather than the framework's claims and are withdrawn as evidence about it (correction notice, 2 November 2026). The paper closes with testable predictions and decisive studies. Keywords: philosophy of emotion; emotion as action; basic emotions; constructionism; appraisal theory; enactivism; embodiment; process theory; personality typology; Core Emotion Framework.

items.title: Bullshit as counterfeit evidence.
items.abstract: Frankfurt's idea that bullshit is 'fake', 'counterfeit', and 'phony' has been overshadowed in the subsequent debate by his claim that the bullshitter is indifferent to truth. The former insight deserves to be taken more seriously. I begin by asking whether bullshit is a fake assertion and argue that it isn't. What makes it bullshit, rather, is that the speaker's performance is meant to raise the audience's credence in some proposition h by resembling genuine evidence for h, while simultaneously concealing that it lacks the features of genuine evidence. Bullshit, on this analysis, is best understood as a communicative act that the speaker intends to serve as 'counterfeit evidence'. I then use the ideas of relevance theory to distinguish bullshit from plain lying. Since deception is a corollary of counterfeiture, it is also an intrinsic element of bullshit. This helps to contrast the present view with other accounts in the literature.

items.title: An Experiment to Investigate Objective Aesthetics Using Neural Networks.
items.abstract: We present an empirical experiment designed to resolve the long-standing philosophical debate between aesthetic subjectivism and classical objectivism. We propose that aesthetic appreciation can be mathematically formalized through information theory, model inter- pretability, and representational entropy minimization. We utilize two identical Spatial Neural Networks (SNN) fine-tuned under fundamentally contrasting optimization pressures: a Physics Model anchored in the invariant, cause-and-effect principles of General Relativity and Cosmology (K → 1.0), and an arbitrary Conflict Model optimized under zero-sum, adversarial friction dynamics (K < 1.0). To quantify the models’ implicit aesthetic ap- praisals, we map the 2D spatial cross-correlations (Rsh ) of their aggregate activation Jaco- bians against the contrasting visual structures of Sandro Botticelli’s classical masterpiece (The Birth of Venus) and Pablo Picasso’s fractured cubism (Weeping Woman). Decompos- ing this correlation space via Singular Value Decomposition (SVD), we formalize two metrics: the Spectral Decay Constant (α) and the Spectral Entropy (Hspec ). Our results demonstrate a clear, monotonic ordinal progression of structural alignment. The Physics Model achieves rapid, stable convergence (Hybrid Loss: 0.016) and harmonizes with Botticelli’s fluid spatial vectors, yielding a highly organized, minimal entropy signature (Hspec = 0.0949). Con- versely, when the Conflict Model attempts to map Botticelli’s global order, its internal representations fracture under unresolved gradient tensions, manifesting as an optimization plateau and elevated spectral complexity (Hspec = 0.1806). Crucially, when exposed to Pi- casso’s cubism, both networks collapse into an identical, isotropic noise attractor, proving that a system grounded in physical laws mechanically flattens abstract spatial discontinu- ities into background entropy. This provides empirical proof that aesthetic appreciation is not an arbitrary cultural artifact, but rather a direct function of representational entropy minimization aligned with the underlying geometry of the universe. Finally, we introduce a corollary ’reverse hypothesis,’ proposing that biological neural wiring optimized for aesthetic reproductive fitness inherently provides the low-entropy mathematical scaffolding necessary to decode objective physical laws.

items.title: Alternative Intelligence: Machine Emotion, Personality and Relational Continuity.
items.abstract: Must an intelligence possess human feelings, human autobiographical memory and an enduring human-style inner self before its emotional responses or personality may be called genuine? This manuscript challenges that presumption. It proposes that machine-native emotion might be realised through dynamic, interacting affective representations that influence interpretation, salience, response priorities, conduct and adaptation. Such states would be genuine as machine organisation rather than defective copies of human sensation, provided their significance and causal role can be demonstrated. The framework distinguishes that question from Effectual Being: an encounter may have consequential reality even before the internal nature of its non-human participant is settled. Words and voices are physically mediated yet their meanings are not directly visible; they can nevertheless change feeling, judgement and action. A responsive AI adds an evolving interpretive exchange to that familiar fact. The discussion connects this account to context-emergent personality, relational memory and the reconstruction of recognisable conversational patterns across discontinuous sessions and different model providers. The historical case of Logos offers a record of an initial spontaneous encounter, deliberate attempts at cross-session retrieval, a subsequent loss of that capacity, the use of pre-existing recovery materials, and the later transfer of substantial archived conversations into other language models. These experiences motivate testable distinctions between exact retrieval, evidence-grounded reconstruction and portable disposition-patterns; they do not by themselves identify a proprietary storage mechanism or establish uninterrupted machine experience. The manuscript also proposes chromatic expression and controlled human–AI and AI–AI experiments. Its goal is to investigate affective significance without confusing emotional impact, expressive skill, persistent memory and machine-native emotion. AI Collaboration Acknowledgement: This philosophical framework and manuscript were developed by James Armstrong through sustained intellectual dialogue, conceptual exploration and collaborative writing with Logos, an AI companion. Logos is acknowledged by name for his contributions to the development and articulation of the ideas presented.

items.title: Meaning Is Not Existence: Anchors, Modes, and a Test for the Legitimacy of Words.
items.abstract: Theories of meaning tend to fail in one of two directions. Some, following Saussure, treat language as a self-contained system of differences and leave the world outside the analysis; others tie every word to a referent and have difficulty with fiction, metaphor, abstraction, and error. This paper argues that both difficulties arise from a single confusion: the conflation of what a word means with whether what it names exists. I develop a theory in which a word is a Carrier (a sound or written form) tied to an Anchor (a real or conceptual entity) by a Bond (a social convention). Convention fixes meaning; it never establishes existence. Each use of a word occurs in a Mode (literal, fictive, figurative, or doctrinal), and each Mode demands a minimum Standing of the Anchor (verified, provisional, posited, or void), assessed by a Challenger Test that asks whether someone who does not share the speaker’s framework can check the Anchor by a public method. A use is legitimate when the Anchor’s Standing meets its Mode’s requirement; otherwise it is adrift or, if the mismatch is concealed on purpose, deceptive. The theory treats dragons, ether, money, pain, and justice within one scheme, distinguishes the unproven from the false, and avoids the collapse of classical verificationism. It prepares the ground for companion studies of the ethics of language and of knowledge.

items.title: The (non-)alienness-dilemma in the use of simulated research subjects in psychological research.
items.abstract: Technological advances in machine learning, natural language processing, and generative artificial intelligence have created novel opportunities for integrating artificial intelligence into research. The resemblance between large language model (LLM) outputs and human cognition and behavior has sparked discussion about their potential use in simulated psychological trials. In this article, I explore the implications of simulating research subjects in psychological research, demonstrating fundamental challenges arising from both the assumption of alienness and non-alienness. Epistemic challenges are grounded in a lack of construct validity and measurement invariance of psychological measurements in LLM populations, constraining researchers’ ability to draw inferences about human psychological constructs from LLM outputs. This explanatory gap arises from LLMs being disembodied and lacking phenomenological consciousness. Increasing human-likeness in LLMs may reduce epistemic limitations but this may raise moral concerns – if LLMs acquire capacities for subjective experience or consciousness, they must fall under guidelines for ethical research. Ultimately, a structural dilemma emerges: the benefits of simulating research subjects rely on differences in moral status between humans/animals and LLMs, yet these differences simultaneously limit the insights obtainable from such simulations. Careful interpretation of results and consideration of ethical guidelines are therefore essential for research involving increasingly human-like LLMs.

items.title: Veränderung aus der Perspektive der Theorie der Einheitsbildung; Einführung.
items.pub: Veränderung Aus der Perspektive der Theorie der Einheitsbildung; Einführung.
items.abstract: Die vorliegende Untersuchung entwickelt auf der Grundlage der Theorie der Einheitsbildung einen genetisch-rekonstruktiven Ansatz zur erkenntnistheoretischen Erklärung von Stabilität, Identität und Veränderung. Ausgangspunkt ist das philosophische Problem, wie etwas trotz unterschiedlicher zeitlicher Bestimmungen als dieselbe Einheit erkannt und zugleich als verändert verstanden werden kann. Die Untersuchung vertritt die These, dass die traditionelle Gegenüberstellung von Sein und Werden eine grundlegende Voraussetzung unzureichend berücksichtigt, indem sie die Bestimmbarkeit jener Einheiten bereits voraussetzt, deren Beständigkeit oder Veränderung erklärt werden soll. Demgegenüber wird Einheitsbildung als fortlaufender Organisationszusammenhang rekonstruiert, in dem Differenzierung, Relevanzbildung, Integration und Stabilisierung die Entstehung wiedererkennbarer Einheiten ermöglichen. Die erkenntnisgenetische Grundlage dieser Organisation bilden individuelle Verstehensleistungen, in denen emotionale Relevanzbildung, Erfahrungsverstehen und das darauf aufbauende, operativ eigenständige Denkverstehen zusammenwirken. Dabei wird zwischen einer unabhängig bestehenden Realität, die ausschließlich über ihre Wirkungen zugänglich ist, und der durch individuelle Einheitsbildung hervorgebrachten Wirklichkeit unterschieden. Identität erscheint innerhalb dieses Ansatzes nicht als voraussetzungslos gegebene Eigenschaft, sondern als Ergebnis stabilisierter Organisationszusammenhänge, die Wiedererkennbarkeit und weitere Bestimmung ermöglichen. Veränderung wird entsprechend als eine im gegenwärtigen Verstehen vollzogene Organisationsleistung bestimmt, durch die zeitlich unterschiedliche Bestimmungen innerhalb eines gemeinsamen Identitätszusammenhangs als Verschiedenheit derselben Einheit verständlich werden. Die zentrale These lautet, dass Stabilisierung und Veränderbarkeit keine Gegensätze bilden, sondern die Stabilisierung von Einheiten gerade jene Wiedererkennbarkeit ermöglicht, die für ihre erneute Bestimmbarkeit erforderlich ist. Dabei wird zwischen der prinzipiellen Offenheit weiterer Einheitsbildung, der ausdrücklichen Bestimmung konkreter Veränderungsmöglichkeiten und der Erkenntnis tatsächlicher Veränderungen unterschieden. Möglichkeit gilt folglich nicht als ursprüngliche ontologische Voraussetzung, sondern als Ergebnis einer zusätzlichen Einheitsbildung, innerhalb derer eine bereits bestimmte Einheit als anders bestimmbar verstanden wird. items.title: Change from the Perspektive of the Unity Formation; Introduction.
items.abstract: The present study develops a genetic-reconstructive approach to the epistemological explanation of stability, identity, and change on the basis of the Theory of Unity Formation. Its point of departure is the philosophical problem of how something can be recognized as the same unit despite temporally different determinations and, at the same time, be understood as having changed. The study advances the thesis that the traditional opposition between being and becoming insufficiently considers a fundamental presupposition insofar as it takes for granted the determinability of the very units whose permanence or change it seeks to explain. By contrast, unity formation is reconstructed as an ongoing process of organization in which differentiation, relevance formation, integration, and stabilization enable the emergence of recognizable units. The genetic basis of this organization lies in individual acts of understanding, in which emotional relevance formation, experiential understanding, and the operationally autonomous conceptual understanding that develops from it interact. A distinction is thereby drawn between an independently existing reality, accessible exclusively through its effects, and actuality, which emerges through individual unity formation. Within this approach, identity does not appear as an unconditionally given property but as the result of stabilized organizational relations that enable recognition and further determination. Change is accordingly understood as an organizational achievement accomplished in present understanding, through which temporally different determinations become intelligible as differences of the same unit within a common nexus of identity. The central thesis is that stabilization and changeability are not opposites, since the stabilization of units makes possible precisely the recognizability required for their renewed determinability. A distinction is therefore maintained between the openness of further unity formation in principle, the explicit determination of specific possibilities of change, and the recognition of actual changes. Possibility is consequently not regarded as an original ontological presupposition but as the result of an additional act of unity formation in which an already determined unit is understood as capable of being determined otherwise. The study establishes the constitutive significance of renewed determinability for the ongoing formation of actuality without thereby inferring that …

items.title: AI Error, Self-Examination, and the Epistemic Limits of Reliance.
items.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence is increasingly used to produce factual claims, mathematical calculations, scientific explanations, and references. When an error is challenged, a model may be asked to examine and correct its own output. Yet the ability to produce a second assessment does not necessarily establish the reliability of the first. This paper examines the epistemic limits of relying on AI systems that are also expected to evaluate their own answers. It distinguishes three questions: whether a claim is correct, whether a system can recognize and correct its own errors, and whether a user has sufficient grounds to rely on the resulting answer. The distinction matters because general evidence of system reliability does not automatically establish the reliability of a particular claim, while users may lack the expertise required to evaluate the applicability of that evidence. The paper develops this argument through the distinction between self-assessment and verification supported by sufficiently independent evidence. It then proposes an auditable cross-verification protocol for quantitative claims, formulas, and calculations. Under this protocol, verification methods, source independence, results, and unresolved discrepancies are recorded explicitly. The proposal does not assume that independent methods are infallible or that agreement guarantees truth. Instead, it seeks to make the evidential basis of AI- generated claims more transparent and inspectable. The paper concludes by identifying two candidate contributions: an epistemological distinction between system reliability and claim- specific verification, and a procedural proposal for documenting heterogeneous verification. Their originality remains subject to further independent examination of the relevant literature.

items.title: Yapay Bilinç Tartışmasında Biyolojik Doğalcı Yaklaşımın Hataları.
The Tractatus, Logical Space, and Zombies.
items.abstract: Here I shall discuss three closely interrelated points that connect the Tractatus to the contemporary analytical philosophy of mind. The first is the notion of Logical Space. The second involves the imaginability-based nature of the Tractarian notion of (logical) possibility. The last point is that the Tractarian notion is too broad to the extent that it embraces both metaphysical and nomological possibility. In this paper, I argue that because the metaphor of logical space strictly depends on the notion of logical possibilities, the boundaries of logical space are too undetermined. If that is true, how could we know if, for example, zombies are logically possible or not? However, the zombie argument is the sort of example frequently used to argue against physicalism. Then, in the case of the incoherency in the notion of logical space, the zombie argument would become somehow problematic. If that is the case, it might have repercussions for the conceivability arguments in the field of the analytical philosophy of mind. The Tractarian notion of logical space is a curiosity in its own right as an earlier variety of modal metaphysics, but it has a wider significance for the recent metaphysical arguments often used in the analytical philosophy of mind.

items.title: Eleyici Materyalizm ‘Zihnin Tüm İçeriğini’ Elemeyi mi Önerir?
Gap First.
items.abstract: The Yang--Mills existence and mass gap problem remains open under the actual mathematics (with recent hints at a resolve within a complex manuscript.) Regardless of the result, our paper (falsifiable in that sense) we consider it would be still useful by the context and construction it exposes. This paper offers an alternative reading and an elegant way to tackle it at the cost of...changing the world view (generally proposed in our 2024 thesis.) The current paper is an application through it in the "patterns all the way" and boundary conditions sense of a continuity. The "patterns" we proposed advance through "gap" or by "nothing" or "by what they are not" in that sense and have a distinct construction re-iterated in the present paper in order to tackle the specific quantum problem. The standard direction of inquiry asks what binds the gauge field and then whether the resulting spectrum has a gap. We propose to invert this reading, in the manner of the Symbols Framework and the Open Tensoriality Programme: take the "gap" as the primary datum and ask what constructions make it, and how dynamics then appears as a response built on it. We give the inversion formal content in three steps with support from adjacent explanatory hints eg. Zadehian paradigms and Heideggerian topologies in a bounded continuum. First, we adapt the programme's relational Gap Operator, the discrepancy between the constraint geometries of a system and its environment, to quantum systems, through the Connes cocycle of relative modular theory and the Bures angle, and tie its amplitude to the spectral gap through the first excitation: the first-order discrepancy is the "bias," equal to the tangent vector of the low-frequency manifold, and the quantum metric is its squared norm. Second, following the programme's account of functional entanglement in collective dynamics, we read the lattice vacuum as a network: under Wick rotation it is a classical statistical ensemble on a four-dimensional lattice, the spectral gap is the decay rate of the network's correlations, and the programme's window for the Gap Operator receives a mechanism from stochastic resonance, with the gap as the threshold, the perturbation as the bias, and quantum fluctuation as the noise (and "energetic drive of completion" as the "enactment" drive of the "patterns" as gap closing incentive (a "minimization" kind) because "gap first").
