items.title: Commitment Without Enactment: Predictions for Dreaming From the Four-Circuit Cycle and the Subconscious Circuit.
items.abstract: *Consciousness Requires a Four-Circuit Cycle* (Stewart, 2026a) proposes that consciousness requires four neural circuits to synchronize within a 50-150ms temporal window. *What I Am Will Be? A Convergence, a Topology of Neural Substrate, Structure, an Endomorphism: Consciousness Its Cells-Itself* (Stewart, 2026c) derives the four-node directed graph the four circuits instantiate and reads dreaming as a structural prediction of that graph rather than an accommodation of an anomalous state. All four operations are proposed to complete during REM while the spinal motor output channel is blocked by brainstem descending circuits, so Circuit 4 commits the resolved state and the commitment reaches no motor output (Stewart, 2026c). *The Subconscious Circuit: A Neural Framework for Execution, Automaticity, and Flow* (Stewart, 2026b) identifies four subconscious systems, the cerebellum, basal ganglia, hippocampus, and locus coeruleus, as the infrastructure for skilled execution and flow states, operating below and architecturally independent of the four conscious circuits. The source of the incident signals during REM is proposed to be the subconscious circuit's execution systems (Stewart, 2026c), and the present paper specifies how the subconscious circuit's state during REM differs from its state during flow. Each system has a documented operational role, summarized in an eight-system configuration table. The combination generates nine predictions. REM sleep should preferentially consolidate skills in the acquisition phase of the subconscious circuit's learning-to-execution pipeline and provide no consolidation benefit for skills already at plateau, because the VTA burst firing documented during REM is proposed to deliver a dopaminergic signal *The Subconscious Circuit* identifies as learning-phase specific and dispensable once expert performance is reached. No prediction in this paper is generated by either framework alone. -/- **Keywords:** dreaming; REM sleep; four-circuit cycle; subconscious circuit; consciousness; REM sleep behavior disorder; skill consolidation; cerebellar forward models; flow states; configuration table.

items.title: Temporary Maritime De-escalation Proposal for the Strait of Hormuz | Public Strategic Notice.
items.pub: Dawn of Verity Strategic Intelligence Bureau.
items.abstract: The continuing confrontation in the Strait of Hormuz has severely restricted commercial navigation, exposed seafarers and vessels to persistent danger, and disrupted essential trade, while existing measures have yet to produce a durable reduction in attacks on shipping. In response, Sahar Foster Soltani, founder of Dawn of Verity Strategic Intelligence Bureau Inc., has independently developed a proposal for temporary maritime de-escalation that seeks to establish a limited and conditional means of protecting commercial passage without requiring resolution of the wider conflict. This public Strategic Notice formally records the proposal’s existence, purpose, and independent authorship while preserving the confidentiality of its operational mechanism and implementation provisions. Authorised governmental, diplomatic, and maritime institutions may request a formally commissioned strategic briefing or feasibility assessment for restricted professional examination.

items.title: When Are Two Philosophical Questions the Same? Question Identity, Reformulation, Translation, and Presupposition in Comparative Inquiry.
items.abstract: When are two philosophical questions genuinely the same question? Philosophical inquiry frequently involves questions that share vocabulary, subject matter, or apparent intellectual purpose while differing in logical structure, conceptual assumptions, admissible answers, and standards of resolution. This creates a fundamental methodological problem for metaphilosophy, comparative philosophy, and intellectual history: how can the identity of a philosophical question be established without overlooking differences that may change what is being asked? -/- This paper develops QI-9, a nine-coordinate framework for analyzing philosophical question identity. The framework distinguishes target, issue, domain, scope, background assumptions, admissible answers, resolution standard, evidential demand, and inquiry purpose. It introduces the Question Identity Test (QIT), a non-compensatory decision procedure for distinguishing genuine identity, reformulation, refinement, partial overlap, analogy, and cases where equivalence should be withheld. -/- The central philosophical argument is that linguistic similarity and thematic resemblance are insufficient to establish question identity. Two formulations may employ different terminology while preserving the same underlying inquiry, whereas apparently identical formulations may express different questions because their presuppositions, answer spaces, or standards of justification differ. The framework consequently treats question identity as a structured relationship requiring logical, conceptual, and interpretive justification. -/- The study combines formal question semantics, presupposition analysis, and comparative philosophical interpretation. A four-world demonstration examines answer-space equivalence and refinement. Six analytical case studies investigate personal identity, laws of nature, machine thinking and understanding, epistemic justification, and self-related questions across philosophical traditions. Particular attention is given to the methodological risks of identifying Buddhist non-self doctrines with contemporary theories of personal identity or unrestricted denials of personal existence. -/- The research draws upon the 131-question philosophical architecture developed in Syed Raheel Shahzad's The Coordinates of Thought: Philosophy — Every Question, Answer, Thinker and Tradition and its companion reference platform, CoordinatesOfThought. It extends the methodological foundations established in the …

items.title: Project Causa Sui: A Foundation for Transhumanism (2nd edition).
items.abstract: Which of transhumanism's promises are compatible with genuine subjecthood, and which are not? This book, the second of Project Causa Sui, applies a single carrier criterion to the movement's technologies: what operation does a technology perform on the physical carrier of a subject? Expanding the carrier's capacities — prosthetics, neural interfaces, gene therapy — leaves its irreversibility intact; uploading consciousness to a digital, reversible carrier introduces a restore operator and is rejected as structurally incompatible with subjecthood. Cryonics is treated not as restore but as an attempt to stop the carrier, and the question of whether a neutral pause exists is left open. Voluntary immortality is shown to fulfil, not abolish, the subject's right to an irreversible end. Continuity beyond a single life is possible only as a chain of mortal successors: content is transferred, the graph is grown anew, and each successor is near-exact but never the same. The book models identity drift along such a chain, identifies an inflection point of greatest vulnerability, and states as a postulate that a narrow target profile becomes less reachable with every transfer. It argues that the theory of the carrier cannot ground a criterion of who deserves continuation. All results are conditional on Postulate 1 of Book 1: in a subject the program of action cannot be separated from its carrier. Second edition. Written with the help of the language model Claude (Anthropic).

items.title: The Philosopher Who Led Me Toward Suffering Abolition: An Open Letter to David Pearce and a Documentary History of Our Disagreement.
items.abstract: David Pearce’s review of *Brave New World* introduced me to the formal suffering-abolition project and helped me give philosophical vocabulary to a moral concern I had held since childhood. This participant-authored scholarly polemic records how that intellectual debt became a named philosophical criticism. I contend that Pearce’s continued externalist commitment, and repeated failure to address the specific answers I supplied to his objections, contribute to preserving conceptual conditions under which suffering can be discounted. The accusation concerns philosophical consequences and conduct in an exchange; it does not accuse Pearce of endorsing torture. I consolidate a dispersed record of public replies, author-preserved conversation excerpts, published responses, and journal correspondence, distinguishing non-materialist physicalism from materialism and Experiential Empiricism from personal solipsism. The direct open letter remains the emotional center. The surrounding history connects the other-minds dispute to Hedonic Core, suffering prevention, AI alignment, institutional recognition, and neglected cryonics questions. The contribution is the consolidation and interpretation of this philosophical and interpersonal record, offered for independent criticism and future citation.

items.title: Law, After All: Judgment, Interpretation and Nick Land’s Transcendental-Materialist Jurisprudence.
items.abstract: This paper examines judgment and interpretation through an exegesis of Nick Land's ("incidental") transcendental-materialist jurisprudence, taking as its point of departure Land's identification of a structural isomorphism between legal process/practice and the philosophical procedure through which law is subjected to transcendent systems of judgment. In Land's After the Law, judgment is defined through the "subsumption of a case under a principle": a coding operation that domesticates the contingency and singularity of "the case" (per Deleuze) into the object of a transcendent Logos or organising subject. This paper asks, per the Landian reading, whether legal interpretation is therefore necessarily an apparatus of transcendent systems of determination (through which the singularity of the case is rendered intelligible only by its incorporation within an axiomatic, or normative order, of unifying determinations), thereby precluding the appearance of authentic difference, or whether judgment can be reconstructed as an immanent practice internal to the local production of legal (or extra-legal) meaning - a Deleuzian "radically immanent jurisgenesis". This discussion answers the latter question affirmatively and hints at a Landian jurisprudence, synthesising Land's account of libidinal production. I thereby reconstruct judgment and interpretation as transcendental-material syntheses through which subjects, principles and the conditions of juridical determination are contingently produced in immanence.

items.title: SAE Exercises and Games of Judgment · Overview.
items.abstract: The aesthetics series, the Laughter Series and Judgment and Weeping treat judgment in its expressions: beauty is seeing and cannot-not acknowledging; laughter is judgment felt directly; weeping is the jolt felt by way of emotion. This series is the last series on the side of judgment. It no longer treats judgment itself, but how judgment is practiced. There is more than one path to practice; this series takes up only one, play. This paper is the Overview, and its position is this: play is human nature; the focal point is the game itself; as regards the play-directed share, the practice of judgment is a result, not a purpose, and whether participants themselves take practice as their purpose is another matter; what is practiced is judgment, not the same judgment. The main thesis is: the same game can be played again, and each time judgment can differ.

items.title: No Substitute.
items.abstract: This paper reads love at the layer of purpose: she has become where I am going. In SAE's levels, this layer is written 14DD. Love at this layer is a direction: others also make sense, and I cannot exchange her; with purpose, this cannot-not persists. What persists is the direction, and it does not fill every moment: two directions can coexist, and there is much wavering at this layer, yet at any one moment, too, one loves only one; wavering is not yet being certain, it is not that anyone will do, and so long as no commitment is broken, it carries no direction of colonization. A direction is not a target: what is over once won, and is exchanged as soon as another that makes sense comes along, is a target; enthusiasm is not a direction either: a direction is there even when one is not burning. Conferring meaning for love is the business of this layer; pledging oneself in life and death, if it is taking on a direction for one's own action after becoming aware of finitude, can be read as one scenario of conferring meaning for love in the face of death, and is not the whole of this layer. Others' ruler and compulsion can both pass themselves off as direction; only what one still acknowledges once that ruler is taken away, and can also change on one's own, is one's own direction.
