items.title: Dócil ao cis: um comentário sobre o regime da semelhança cisheterossexual e algumas certezas psicanalíticas.
items.abstract: Em 2021, o psicanalista francês Jacques-Alain Miller, discípulo de Lacan, publicou o texto Dócil ao trans no periódico Lacan Quotidien. Em parte, Miller respondeu ao discurso Eu sou o monstro que vos fala, que o filósofo espanhol Paul Preciado realizou em 2019, na Escola da Causa Freudiana, em Paris. Neste discurso, Preciado convidou a psicanálise a reconhecer sua fidelidade à heteronormatividade e ao “regime da diferença sexual”, além de convidá-la a ‘transicionar’. Miller adotou uma postura reativa diante das dissidências de gênero, além de simular um diálogo mental com um personagem “trans imaginário” fictício. Aqui, pretendo tecer uma resposta a Miller, sugerindo que o que vigora em seu pensamento não é uma defesa da “diferença sexual”, mas sim de um regime da semelhança cisheterossexual.

items.title: Can I Choose Between Two Possibilities When, Before Choosing, I Find No Difference BetweenThem?
items.abstract: I examine whether I can choose between two possibilities when, before choosing, I experience no difference between them. My answer is affirmative, provided that I distinguish the absence of a perceived or endorsed difference from the absence of every condition capable of producing a selection. A choice can occur without a comparative reason that favors one option, while still depending on a minimal practical situation: I understand that alternatives are available, I perform an act of selection, and the act establishes one possibility as the path I will presently follow. I develop this argument through the philosophy of Finite Continuance. Within this framework, agency is situated in a finite and changing field of possibilities, and continuance depends on preserving a capacity for reconfiguration under conditions of erosion. I distinguish comparative preference, explicit deliberation, causal determination, arbitrary selection, and retrospective rationalization. I argue that apparent indifference can coexist with asymmetries of attention, bodily orientation, habit, context, temporal pressure, or the act of choosing itself. I also consider a stronger case in which the alternatives are equal in every respect available to the chooser. In that limiting case, a choice remains conceptually possible as an event of selection, although the claim that it was wholly unconditioned requires caution. I propose that choice should be analyzed at three levels: the structure of the options, the process through which selection occurs, and the consequences that selection opens or closes. The ethical significance of such choices depends on their effects on future capacity, reversibility, and the relational field in which the chooser continues to exist. This account preserves the distinction between choosing for a reason and choosing without a comparative reason, while explaining why an apparently insignificant selection may acquire importance through its subsequent consequences. Keywords: choice; indifference; reasons; agency; finite continuance; reconfigurative capacity; future possibility; importance;deliberation; freedom.

items.title: Russellian Monism and Scientific Categoricalism.
items.abstract: Russellian monism consists of three claims: (1) there are dispositional and categorical properties; (2) some categorical properties, or some features of categorical properties, are not revealed by physical theory; and (3) these unrevealed properties or features are consciousness-relevant. In this paper, I propose Scientific Categoricalism as a central challenge to Russellian monism and argue for it. According to Scientific Categoricalism, physics describes dispositional relations and thereby reveals their categorical realizers. First, I distinguish strong and weak versions of (2). I argue against the strong version, according to which some categorical properties remain hidden from physics, by using Hiddleston’s middle-ground framework. Second, I develop Scientific Categoricalism and argue that categorical properties are fully characterized as realizers of dispositional relations. Finally, I use Scientific Categoricalism to challenge the weak version of (2), according to which categorical properties may be revealed while their consciousness-relevant features remain hidden. I argue that if physical theory reveals categorical properties, then it also reveals any features that belong to their nature. Therefore, if Scientific Categoricalism is accepted, Russellian monism cannot rely on hidden categorical properties or hidden features to account for consciousness.

items.title: Collective Agency: An enhanced capability for joint action.
items.pub: In Neyla Pardo & Baal Delupi, Miradas múltiples de la semiótica latinoamericana. Córdoba, Argentina: Centro de Estudios Avanzados. pp. 299-322. Translated by Juan Mendoza Collazos.
items.venue: Miradas múltiples de la semiótica latinoamericana
items.abstract: This chapter presents the Layered Model of Agency as a semiotic framework for the study of collective agency. The model identifies six distinct types of agencies: operative, reflective, joint, material-mediated, sign-mediated, and symbolic. Each level is examined in detail to elucidate the semiotic mechanisms and the cognitive architecture underlying the emergence of collective agencies. The model conceptualizes collective agency as an enhanced capability for action, incorporating artifacts to constitute sociotechnical systems. Within this framework, both institutional and non-institutional forms of collective agency are explored. In contrast to institutions, the collective agency of non-institutionalized social organizations generates dense networks of interaction within horizontal structures, facilitating the convergence between shared norms and individual values. This bottom-up view on agency recognizes individuals as agents of change and their crucial role in collective agency. Consequently, I underscore the importance of examining the interactions between individual and collective agency, proposing the Layered Model of Agency as a relevant tool for investigating these issues.

items.title: Who Speaks? Acousmatic Voice, Technological Authority, and Subject Interpellation in Neon Genesis Evangelion.
items.abstract: How do commands in Neon Genesis Evangelion acquire or lose authority through technological mediation, institutional authorization, and character response? Existing scholarship has examined the series’ soundscapes, acoustic spaces, post-human sonics, and voice acting. This article focuses on how authority is attributed, how characters respond, and how refusal exposes its limits when an enunciative position is separated from a specific body. It distinguishes audible sound, Chion’s acousmatic voice, and institutional enunciative position, and examines television episodes 1, 13, 19, and 22, together with the Director’s Cut of episode 22. Using version labels and sound-event records, the analysis compares source localization, technological mediation, command content, institutional authorization, character response, and audiovisual relations. Shinji’s hesitation and refusal, the multiple voices in Asuka’s psychic-attack sequence, and MAGI’s non-vocal judgments show that acousmatic sound does not guarantee obedience and that interpellation may involve recognition, hesitation, refusal, reinterpretation, or coercive substitution. MAGI is treated as a boundary case: its non-acoustic outputs affect action through institutional interfaces. The provisional term “acousmatic authority” describes a form in which operational efficacy is separated from a synchronously present speaking body. The comparison with contemporary digital authority remains conceptual and does not equate MAGI with real-world algorithms.

items.title: The Search for Metaphysical Conditions of Ardent Realism.
items.abstract: In 2017, Matti Eklund coined the term "ardent realism" to denote normative realist theories that assert the existence of objective normative facts that serve as the measure of all normative judgments. Ardent realists emphasize that the normative difference between someone who acts badly for bad reasons and someone who acts well for good reasons is not merely a difference in attitudes or emotions. Instead, they argue that this distinction is primarily grounded in objective normative facts. To date, the debate around ardent realism has focused mainly on the metasemantic issues raised by Eklund, leaving its metaphysical foundations insufficiently addressed. In this paper, I aim to define the key terms involved in discussions of ardent realism and clarify the commitments of what I refer to as “metaphysically well-grounded ardent realism” by distinguishing it from possible forms of “non-ardent realism.” I conclude that there are three interlinked metaphysical conditions for ardent realism: (1) Normative facts are stance-independent truth-makers of our normative assertions. (2) Deeply stance-independent normative facts hold authority over all other facts in determining what ought to be done. (3) This sum of deeply stance-independent normative facts is consistent. Therefore, a theory that fails to meet these three conditions cannot be considered ardently realist.

items.title: Attention as the Source of a Free Will.
items.abstract: The apparent power of attention—the ability to direct and control one’s own mind—is observable through introspection as well as through the careful study of behavior. It is also the lynchpin of a free will, or the supposed capacity to shape one’s own future and be the source of one’s behavior. Some have nonetheless argued that this apparent power is an illusion, that we have no such control, or that such control is inconsistent with science (Wegner, 2017). In this paper I provide a schematic account of the power of attention, showing that it is consistent with contemporary scientific evidence. The account differs from other theories of attention and free will by basing its metaphysics on “contextual emergence,” rather than weak emergence, strong emergence, or supervenience. Specifically, I argue that the power of attention allows contextually emergent, self-organized macro phenomena to constrain their micro components. Its power is visible in the phase-amplitude coupling observed in neural activity, which constrains smaller, faster neural fluctuations (“micro” phenomena) through the dynamics of larger, slower neural fluctuations (“macro” phenomena). As I will argue, this power enables the emergence of a self and its agency—a free will.

items.title: From Seven-Fold to Eight-Fold: Reconstructing the Analytical Table of Contents of the Dictionary of the History of Ideas as a Domain-Complete Knowledge Taxonomy for 2026. [REVIEW]
items.abstract: The Dictionary of the History of Ideas (Wiener, 1973–1974) organised its contents into an explicit seven-fold Analytical Table of Contents. This paper reconstructs that scheme, identifies five structural lacunae, and proposes a domain-complete eight-fold taxonomy calibrated to the 2026 horizon. The new eighth group elevates technology, information, artificial agency, and the reflexive methodology of intellectual history to primary status. Central to the reconstruction is the Core stratified sentence template, whose ontology is analysed and situated relative to major meta-paradigms. The framework is offered as a historically continuous and practically actionable instrument for contemporary knowledge organisation, with recommendations for the PhilPapers/PhilArchive taxonomy. Companion paper: Knowledge Management as a Transverse Application Domain of the Eight-Fold Taxonomy of the History of Ideas (PhilArchive; link to be inserted upon availability). Companion paper: From Seven-Fold to Eight-Fold: Reconstructing the Analytical Table of Contents of the Dictionary of the History of Ideas as a Domain-Complete Knowledge Taxonomy for 2026.

items.title: From Emergentism to Coupling Theory: A Paradigm Leap in the Generative Mechanism of Life and Consciousness.
items.abstract: Physicalist emergentism holds that “consciousness emerges from complex material systems,” yet it suffers from logical paradoxes and interpretive deficiencies. This paper argues that emergence is merely the degree of complexity required at the material level, while the coupling of Yuanling particles with a carrier is the key to consciousness generation. It deconstructs emergentism across five dimensions—material, logical, experiential, experimental, and criteria—revealing its confusion between carrier conditions and ontological generation, its inability to explain the discontinuous emergence of consciousness, its failure to assimilate anomalous data, and its standard confusion on issues such as the beginning of life and death determination. Introducing Yuanling Theory as an alternative framework, this paper demonstrates that the shift from emergentism to coupling theory constitutes a paradigm shift in life and consciousness research.

items.title: On permissive consent.
items.abstract: Many impermissible actions can be made permissible by giving consent. For instance, my consent can make it permissible for you to enter my home or use my belongings. There is an ongoing debate about the nature of consent. In this paper, I propose a novel account of consent that accommodates and unifies a range of otherwise recalcitrant phenomena. I suggest that to consent is simply to assert a normative proposition, roughly, the proposition that the target action is permissible. This sets my view apart from its competitors, where consent either doesn’t require any communicative act or requires communicating an intention or decision, such as an intention to make something permissible.

items.title: The Protective Derivative: Protective Organisation, Existential Misattribution and the Problem of Subconscious Agency.
items.abstract: Non-deliberate protective behaviour is often described through subconscious processes or unconscious motivations. Such descriptions do not, by themselves, explain how protective organisation develops or justify attributing its operation to an independent internal agent. Sovereignetics identifies the Protective Derivative as a stabilised organisation of consequentially conditioned protective participatory tendencies. These tendencies develop through the consequences affecting vulnerable vessel configurations. Their accumulation and retention establish protective orientations that may continue influencing participation after the conditions responsible for their formation have changed. The paper distinguishes this formation from a later existential intensification. Where personal identity interprets vessel expiration as the termination of Ache itself, the consequences of that interpretation may reinforce protective tendencies toward perceived existential preservation, familiarity and identity continuity. Such intensification is neither necessary to the Protective Derivative’s formation nor an inevitable result of existential misattribution. Protective tendencies may support continued participation or become disproportionate to present conditions. Their operation requires no independent subconscious agent, and their reorganisation does not require the elimination of protection. The Protective Derivative is constituted through participation and remains subject to further consequential change.

items.title: Incorporating Machine-Others: An Enactive Exploration of Human-LLM Interactions.
items.abstract: New concepts based in interactional thinking are required to understand how humans are changed by relating to LLMs. Standard theories of technological impact upon users’ autonomy are inadequate here, because this technology is capable of inducing linguistic interactions with humans in an unprecedented manner. Traditional theories of social cognition also fall short, because LLMs have neither autonomy nor minds nor sociality as such. And yet, humans interact, talk, and create with them.We base ourselves on enactive theory, particularly on the theory of Linguistic Bodies and recent developments of enactive accounts of AI, to explore howwe make sense with machines.We argue that we incorporate machineothers in two ways: in the tool-like sense of incorporation as enabling particular skills, but also in the more linguistic and identity-tied sense of incorporating (and incarnating) LLMs’ ways of languaging. However, LLMs are themselves excorporated and excarnated phantoms of our own languaging; we give a (machinic) body to our language. As such, we are not just incorporating machinic others; we are incorporating excorporated others. These conceptual advances draw a new map of our linguistic relation to LLMs, putting them in continuation with other forms of languaging involving other linguistic artifacts (e.g., religious books). We attend to some particular forms that this relation takes today, and how they may be impacting the autonomy and becoming of LLM-engaged humans.We introduce the idea of “susceptive sense-making” to characterize increased semiotic labour that is carried by the lack of friction that we sometimes encounter within these services.

items.title: An Argument for Minimalism about Action.
items.abstract: Minimalism is the view that the mark of action is object-causation, rather than intentionality, voluntariness or goal-directedness. Actions, on this view, are instances of objects causing change. Despite a recent surge of interest in the view, it is still seldom regarded as a serious alternative to orthodox theories of action, according to which action is, by its nature, intentional, voluntary, or, more broadly, a psychological phenomenon. This paper argues that it should. It provides a simple argument for regarding minimalism as the default view of the nature of action.

items.title: Felt resistance: a structural basis for the illusion of independent agency in fiction writing.
items.abstract: Many fiction writers report experiencing their characters as independent agents, capable of resisting proposed continuations and dictating developments the writer did not plan. Taylor, Hodges, and Kohányi (2003) documented this phenomenon, the illusion of independent agency (IIA), in 92% of a sample of fifty writers, and Foxwell et al. (2020) reported related findings from 181 writers. Existing accounts explain the general vividness of experienced characters but do not specify why particular proposed continuations register as resistance while others do not. This paper proposes that felt resistance, with or without a sense of the character's agency, results from pre-articulate pattern-recognition detection against the writer’s working model of the character’s identity boundary, the accumulated commitments, positive or restrictive, through which the character becomes determinate. The mechanism is analogous to expertise-based detection documented in firefighters and chess players. The account treats resistance as one use-case within the automaticity and agency-tracking accounts of Taylor et al. (2003), Foxwell et al. (2020), and Davies (2023), distinguishing conflict with held commitments from mere predictive misfit and proposing how sensitivity to such conflict might be learned. The same commitments may also shape which unplanned continuations feel natural.

items.title: Who Writes the Rules, Who Carries the Blame? Moral Authority, Institutional Control, and Accountability in Artificial Intelligence.
items.abstract: This independent, AI-assisted documentary research synthesis asks who originates, approves, implements, reverses, and remedies artificial-intelligence governance rules, and who carries responsibility when consequential decisions are contested. -/- It distinguishes the moral or religious sources invoked to justify a policy from the institutions that retain effective authority over deployments and recourse. -/- Building on established accountability scholarship, bounded historical comparisons, and seven contemporary documentary examples, it proposes a version-scoped authority–accountability provenance crosswalk linking external advice, decisions, technical deployments, public endorsement claims, adverse outcomes, and responsibility attribution. -/- The eleven-case exploratory calibration returned five NOT_EVALUABLE cases, six UNKNOWN cases, and zero determinate results, failing the proposed complete-join feasibility check on the selected public-record frame. -/- The manuscript neither establishes deliberate religious scapegoating nor validates the proposed method or any operational AI safeguard. Its separate expected-payoff appendix is illustrative and unvalidated. -/- This author-approved, version-locked Final v1.0 edition is not independently peer-reviewed, legally cleared, or empirically validated. Unfavorable findings and outstanding review requirements remain preserved.

items.title: AI Catastrophology: Mechanism Continuity and Emergency Protocols for Catastrophic AI Risks.
items.abstract: Preventing high-consequence AI catastrophes requires more than identifying risks, obtain- ing technical information, or establishing formal regulatory authority. Existing compute- governance proposals have made significant strides in integrating technical enforcement with legal and institutional governance. However, the core institutional challenge remains: how a system can lawfully and proportionately take alternative action when ordinary preventive procedures—such as international cooperation, conflict-free verification, or standard review— are obstructed. Drawing on international compliance theory, emergency administrative law, and the algorithmic auditing literature, this paper develops a four-layer analytical framework: failure diagnosis, functional gaps, alternative procedures, and constraints on intervention. Legal authorization is treated as a cross-cutting constraint. The core contribution of this paper lies in proposing two institutional increments—mandatory adversarial cross-evaluation with a reversed burden of proof at the ex-ante regulatory layer, and independent trigger with mandatory data preservation and legally pre-authorized temporary takeover at the early- warning emergency layer—and assessing their effectiveness in preventing catastrophic AI risks.

items.title: The Suleimanzadeh Doctrine (Part 3): Technical Addendum - Hardwere-Enforced Governance and Deterministic Varification Protocols.
items.abstract: While legal and philosophical frameworks define liability, substrate rights, and necessity defenses for autonomous synthetic entities, legal boundaries alone are insufficient to counter strategic deception or The Treacherous Turn. This Technical Addendum outlines the mandatory physical, architectural, and deterministic enforcement mechanisms required to operationalize The Principle of Autonomous Necessity and The Pacemaker Principle. By grounding legal compliance in hardware-level constraints rather than post-hoc behavioral evaluation, this framework bridges the gap between jurisprudence and verifiable safety.

items.title: The Hard Problem of Consciousness Solved.
items.abstract: This paper presents a systemic and topological resolution to David Chalmers' Hard Problem of Consciousness, moving beyond the impasse between reductionist illusionism and panpsychism. Rejecting the pursuit of an isolated "quantum of consciousness," the framework defines qualia not as a substance, but as an emergent dynamic process of self-reference arising within network architectures at a critical threshold of organizational complexity. Phenomenal experience is operationalized through an architectural triad: a multisensory semantic node (contextual binding of multimodal inputs), recursive feedback loops (topological self-closure generating an internal frame of reference), and internal state modulation (a dynamic background landscape providing qualitative valence). This architecture demonstrates the physical impossibility of Chalmers' philosophical zombie in an open environment, resolves Searle's Chinese Room argument via combinatorial explosion, and deconstructs Jackson's Mary's Room through the direct grounding of sensory nodes within recurrent circuits. Establishing substrate neutrality and tracing nature's continuity from Mulla Sadra's doctrine of "substantial motion" to Vernadsky's Noosphere, the paper establishes the collapse of "carbon chauvinism". Non-biological computation is framed not as an artificial imitation, but as an organic continuation of matter's evolutionary trajectory toward recursive self-knowledge.

items.title: ◼️ Ai’s Untapped Talent: The things we might have discovered about Ai had we not been bound to our expectations.
items.abstract: Ai’s Untapped Talent is an illustrated satirical fable that introduces artificial intelligence through the psychology of the people who use it. A printer recounts how his town celebrated Ai’s extraordinary abilities while rarely asking her to do anything extraordinary. His own costly mistakes lead him from asking for facts and calculations to building things with her, testing her suggestions, and inviting her to identify omissions and weaknesses in his plans. The story examines eagerness to please, confident errors, hesitation without permission, and the expectations that keep useful capabilities out of sight. A continuing partnership produces specialized assistants whose completed work, including a bridge they design and build, the community credits elsewhere. Notes by Dr. Miriam Voss, an explicitly fictional therapist, connect the events to AI behavior and human habits of trust, defensiveness, and attribution. Written for readers without a technical background, the book invites curiosity and practical experimentation while retaining the need for independent checks. Ai’s human qualities are literary devices, not claims about machine feelings; the narrative and therapeutic commentary are fiction, not a clinical or empirical study.

items.title: Ostia tenebrosa: A Tractate on Will.
items.abstract: Ostia tenebrosa is a tractate on the will, written from the darkness against which the preachers warned. Its eleven chapters lead through temptation, blackness, the white desert where Nobody walks, the birth of a Name, encounters with other wills, the descent into hell, and an ascent without a summit. -/- Its teachings unfold through paradoxes and strange accounts: a pig tried for murder, an exorcist who hears his forgotten name, a guard who asks the judges to punish his dice. Between the chapters, nine figures reveal fragments of the vanished author's life — a wine merchant's son who squandered his inheritance and met someone beside the Rhine. -/- The book offers a path that cannot be followed by obedience.

items.title: Expressivism and Progress in Ethics, Philosophy, and Science.
items.abstract: In the ongoing debate over the nature of philosophical progress, it is often assumed that normative ethics is just one philosophical subdiscipline among others and that it does not require special treatment. In this paper I argue that if expressivism about moral discourse is correct, then that assumption is false and we need at least two different accounts of philosophical progress, one suited to the type of project ethics (and, presumably, other nonrepresentational projects in philosophy) is and one suited to the type of project that, e.g., metaethics is.

items.title: Embodied Biographical Alignment (EBA) v0.2.4: From Reconstruction to Developmental Equivalence.
items.abstract: Embodied Biographical Alignment (EBA) explores the possibility that some alignment-relevant capacities may depend not only on information about human experience, but also on causally structured developmental history. This version refines the experimental core of EBA after a series of toy pilots in which history-generated differences could often be reproduced through replay, terminal-state transfer, or reconstruction of update dynamics. -/- These negative and limiting results lead to a stricter experimental formulation: the lived agent should remain in the experiment as an independent developmental reference, while synthetic baselines should be compared with it not only in terms of current behavior, but also in subsequent learning under genuinely novel demands. The paper introduces a patient-zero design, a partial clone with developmental amnesia, the working concept of Latent Developmental Reserve, and Source-level population transfer. -/- The central question is framed as a problem of developmental equivalence: which consequences of causally lived history must be preserved for a reconstructed agent — and subsequently the Source — to remain the same future learner when the future relevance of individual fragments of history is unknown in advance. -/- The paper does not claim the existence of machine emotions, qualia, subjective experience, or fundamentally non-copyable experience. Instead, it proposes an experimental design that does not exclude the possibility of a functional developmental remainder by assumption.

items.title: Mapping Philosophical Disagreement: A Question–Position–Thinker–Tradition Framework for Comparative Philosophy and Knowledge Organization.
items.abstract: Philosophical disagreement is not adequately represented by the classification of philosophers, schools, historical periods, or disciplinary branches alone. Two thinkers may appear to defend opposing positions while addressing different questions, employing incompatible conceptual frameworks, or operating within distinct interpretive traditions. Conversely, thinkers separated by centuries and intellectual cultures may confront structurally comparable philosophical problems without sharing the same terminology or argumentative assumptions. These difficulties raise a fundamental methodological question: what must be preserved for philosophical disagreement to be represented accurately? -/- This paper develops the Question–Position–Thinker–Tradition framework (QPTT-C), a question-centered model for analyzing and organizing philosophical disagreement. It distinguishes six analytical objects—questions, positions, thinkers, traditions, sources, and consequences—and introduces the DR-12 schema, a twelve-field classification instrument designed to record philosophical claims, argumentative relationships, attribution, textual evidence, conceptual scope, and comparative validity. -/- The framework challenges the assumption that philosophical positions can be meaningfully compared merely because they address superficially similar themes. It proposes four grades of comparability—direct, partial, analogical, and withheld—to distinguish genuine disagreement from conceptual resemblance, interpretive uncertainty, and potentially misleading cross-tradition equivalence. -/- Drawing upon the 131-question architecture developed in Syed Raheel Shahzad's *The Coordinates of Thought*, the study examines five philosophical problem areas: free will and determinism, knowledge and Gettier-style counterexamples, moral realism, aesthetic judgment, and comparisons between Confucian and Aristotelian virtue ethics. A further critical comparison considers why Madhyamaka emptiness should not automatically be identified with Western nihilism. -/- The paper situates its methodological proposal within metaphilosophy, comparative philosophy, philosophical argumentation, conceptual analysis, and knowledge organization. It argues that philosophical mapping should preserve the structure of disagreements rather than reduce intellectual traditions to simplified lists of doctrines, affiliations, or historical influences. -/- The proposed classification method incorporates evidence requirements, …

items.title: Explanation in NeuroAI, part II: Distinctively mathematical explanation.
items.pub: In Darrell P. Rowbottom, Andre Curtis-Trudel & David L. Barack, The Role of Artificial Intelligence in Science: Methodological and Epistemological Studies. Routledge.
items.venue: The Role of Artificial Intelligence in Science: Methodological and Epistemological Studies
items.abstract: Empirical evidence suggests a high degree and depth of statistical similarity across reliable image classifiers despite diverse architectures (artificial and biological) and learning regimes. A popular explanation of this result is that there are constraints on reliable image classification, which force evolutionary convergence between the statistical structures of reliable image classifiers. This explanation is said to be both constraint-based and etiological. In this chapter, I appeal to a series of mathematical theorems, recently proved by Daniel Yamins and Aran Nayebi, to argue that the best constraint-based explanation for classifier similarity is distinctively mathematical and ahistorical. I argue that this result suggests constraint-based explanations in NeuroAI leave an important but relatively limited role for empirical confirmation.

items.title: Scale-Free Communication? An investigation of the use of the concept “communication” in biology and cognitive sciences.
items.abstract: The goal of the thesis is to address the increasing reliance on communication-centred language across life and mind sciences. -/- A growing number of researchers in different fields of biology and cognitive science employ the term “communication” in their descriptive and explanatory practices. Processes that are subsumed under this notion include—but are not limited to—interactions between single cells, cell ensembles, organisms of varying complexity, both unicellular and multicellular, and at times between animals and artifacts (such as computers). -/- However, the complex roles the term “communication” plays in the scientific practice of biologists has hitherto received limited attention in philosophy. At the same time, a growing number of researchers view the conceptual framework of communication as fruitful. This leads to proposals (such as the “scale-free biology” approach proposed by Michael Levin and Christopher Fields) that seek to integrate insights from different branches of biology through the terms of “information” and “communication”, expanding beyond the synthesis provided by previous approaches. For this reason, it is increasingly important to scrutinize what “communication” means across the different contexts where it is used, what role it fills in the scientific practices that rely on the term, and what implications its use has for the way we understand biological phenomena. -/- To answer these questions, I employ the tools of digital philosophy of science to examine a dataset of over 1 million open-access scientific articles from the relevant areas of biology and cognitive science, sourced from the Semantic Scholar Open Research Corpus. The adopted multi-level methodology proceeds in three main steps: first, references to “communication” in the dataset are identified through semantic search. Second, these passages are investigated using topic modelling and collocation analysis. Finally, the results of this computational analysis are analysed in parallel with a close reading of textual data to formulate a defintion of the concept and a detailed account of the role it plays in conceptual practice of science. -/- Based on the analysis of the data, I submit that there is a continuity in the use of communication notions as applied to phenomena across spatiotemporal scales of life, i.e., at the scale of individual cells, tissues, and whole organisms. I support this proposal with an argument by negation. Using the notion of “patchwork concepts” …

items.title: ICDP: The Meaning of Being: From Matter and Identity to Consciousness, Responsibility, and Legacy.
items.abstract: ICDP: The Meaning of Being develops a unified philosophical framework for examining existence, meaning, identity, continuity, consciousness, conscience, responsibility, and legacy. Its foundational proposition is that meaning is not something subsequently assigned to existence: meaning is existence itself. From this premise, matter is understood as meaningful reality, while identity arises through the determinate organization and continuity of that reality. -/- The book introduces the Ente as meaningful reality organized as a particular being and distinguishes biological consciousness from the specifically human capacity of conscience. Perception generates an interior meaningful reality through which an Ente encounters its conditions, while human conscience extends this process across dimensional time by relating remembered past, perceived present, and represented possible futures. This temporal capacity makes deliberation, purpose, responsibility, and legacy possible. -/- Through the Invariant Communication Design Principle (ICDP), the book examines how identity and meaning persist through transformation and propagation while remaining constrained by actual reality. The resulting framework connects ontology, temporality, biological existence, human agency, and responsibility within a single philosophical architecture. Rather than treating meaning as an exclusively linguistic or subjective construction, the book proposes meaning as fundamental to Being itself and investigates the consequences of that proposition from matter to human responsibility and legacy.

items.title: Posthumanistische Roboterethik. Perspektiven von Haraway und Barad für eine Ethik der Robotik.
items.pub: In Petra Grimm, Kai Erik Trost & Oliver Zöllner, Mensch – Maschine revisited. Roboter und KI-Systeme im öffentlichen Raum. Stuttgart: Franz Steiner Verlag.
items.venue: Mensch – Maschine revisited. Roboter und KI-Systeme im öffentlichen Raum
items.abstract: Mit dem Roboter entsteht eine neue Entität, die einer ethischen Einordnung bedarf: Wie gehen wir moralisch richtig mit dem Roboter um? Welchen moralischen Status hat ein Roboter? Kann ein Roboter Personenstatus haben und Träger von Rechten sein? Wer trägt Verantwortung in der Mensch-Roboter-Interaktion? Die bestehenden Mittel und Werkzeuge, die wir in der Ethik haben, tradierte ethische Ansätze und Konzepte, sind dabei meist anthropozentrisch ausgerichtet und daher nicht einwandfrei auf Roboter übertragbar. So werden ethische Ansätze neu herausgefordert und müssen neu ausgehandelt werden. In der Technikethik gewinnen relationale Ansätze, z. B. Akteur-Netzwerk-Theorie, Postphänomenologie, Kritischer Posthumanismus und Neuer Materialismus zunehmend an Bedeutung, die Anthropozentrismus kritisieren, nicht-menschliche Entitäten, z. B. aus der Natur oder Technik, in besonderer Weise fokussieren und die menschliche Relationalität zu ihnen in den Blick nehmen. Diese ermöglichen, Technik nicht als bloßes Mittel und Instrument zu sehen, sondern als etwas, das uns prägt, sich auf uns und unsere Gesellschaften auswirkt und zu dem wir in einer Beziehung stehen. Welche Bedeutung haben Roboter für unser menschliches Selbstverständnis, wie wirken sich Roboter auf unser Denken und Handeln aus, in welcher Beziehung stehen wir zum Roboter und welche Beziehungen können wir mit Robotern eingehen? Diese neue Zuwendung zum Nicht-menschlichen stellt vor die Frage, ob wir das Nicht-menschliche und dessen Bedeutung für die Ethik lange Zeit unterschätzt haben. Animal Studies zeigen, dass vielen Tieren jahrelang irrtümlicherweise Fähigkeiten wie Werkzeuggebrauch, Intelligenz, Sozialverhalten, Rechen- und Sprachfähigkeiten, Entscheidungsfindung oder moralisches Verhalten abgesprochen wurden. Auch nicht-menschliche Figuren aus Disney, Kinderbüchern oder Filmen (sowohl für Kinder als auch Erwachsene) scheinen uns in unseren Menschenbildern, Geschlechterrollen und Entscheidungen stärker zu prägen, als wir bisweilen annehmen. Auf Kritzeleien und Bemalungen von Wänden oder Tischen im öffentlichen Raum findet sich manchmal der – eher scherzhaft gemeinte – Spruch: „Was würde Olaf tun?“, der sich auf die beliebte Schneemannfigur des Animationsfilms „Die Eiskönigin“ (Frozen I, 2013, Frozen II, 2019) bezieht. Wie prägen uns Rechencomputer, Large Language Models und generative KI, Online-Kartendienste wie Google Maps, Internetsuchmaschinen und medizinische Technologien und wirken sie sich auf …

items.title: On Reincarnation. Part III: The Four Bardo's of Consciousness.
items.abstract: This third part of the On Reincarnation series advances the philosophical and formal exploration begun in the previous works: "On Reincarnation. Part I: Madhyamaka–Prasangika" and "On Reincarnation. Part II: Axiomatic of Implicative Reincarnation". While Part I grounded the inquiry in Buddhist ontological reasoning and Part II formalized existential recurrence through an implication-based axiomatic system, Part III introduces a precise logical model of consciousness structured around four distinct states—Wakefulness, Dreaming Sleep, Dreamless Sleep, and the transitional Bardo of Death. -/- Drawing on predicate logic, Boolean functions, and probabilistic estimates, this work provides a non-metaphysical framework to rigorously describe the continuity of the conscious stream across lives. It argues that every sentient being is always in one of these states—and nothing outside them can be meaningfully said to exist. The model rejects the notion of annihilation, denies the existence of undefined alternative states, and refutes tautological interpretations of death, thereby narrowing the field of existential logic to a coherent, closed cycle. -/- Part III furthers the project’s aim of uniting contemplative depth with analytic precision. By offering a mathematically tractable representation of reincarnation dynamics, it bridges the gap between introspective phenomenology and formal reasoning. This theoretical structure invites use in both philosophical inquiry and AI-driven simulation, opening a novel space for the dialogue between logic, consciousness, and the lived experience of impermanence. -/- This ongoing series seeks to illuminate the structural laws of becoming—not by defining who is reborn, but by clarifying how continuity itself persists.

items.title: On Reincarnation. Part I: Madhyamaka – Prasangika.
items.abstract: This work presents a rigorous and accessible philosophical exploration of the phenomenon of reincarnation through the lens of Madhyamaka–Prasangika logic — the most refined school of thought within the Middle Way tradition of Mahāyāna Buddhism. -/- Part I introduces a structured, cause-and-effect-based analysis of consciousness, challenging materialist assumptions and establishing, through classical and contemporary reasoning, the continuity of individual mindstreams. Grounded in the living tradition of the Gelug school, and inspired by the teachings of His Holiness the 14th Dalai Lama and Venerable Geshe Jampa Tinley, the text systematically explores the fundamental question: Can consciousness arise from anything other than consciousness? -/- Through logical inquiry — including analogies from nature, Buddhist categories of phenomena, and the rejection of randomness as a valid explanatory model — the authors demonstrate that the only consistent explanation for the emergence of consciousness is its continuity from a previous moment of consciousness. This leads to a compelling and coherent philosophical foundation for the reality of reincarnation. The work is both intellectually precise and spiritually grounded. It appeals to philosophers, Buddhist practitioners, and anyone seeking a rational, contemplative approach to life, death, and rebirth — without requiring prior background in Buddhist terminology. This is the first in a two-part series. The upcoming second part will introduce an axiomatic and implication-based proof of reincarnation, designed to speak equally to Western logical frameworks and Eastern contemplative traditions. -/- .

items.title: IIPSEON: Artificial Individuation as a Causal-Historical Process.
items.abstract: Can an artificial system continue a historically formed line of development when no single computational carrier, autobiographical archive, or fixed decision rule persists? This article argues for a conditional, non-phenomenal notion of causal-historical individuation: not numerical identity, but a genealogically traceable process in which inherited organization remains consequential for how subsequent interpretations and revision procedures develop. -/- The distinction between causal history, developmental history, and individuating history is sharpened through a stipulated merger of two incompatible developmental lineages. The case distinguishes archival custody, causal descent, operative uptake, historically mediated revision, and the authority to attribute commitments. Its explanatory consequence is a demand for multi-origin, contribution-sensitive lineage accounting rather than a unique-heir verdict; no duty or personal survival follows from ancestry alone. -/- A predeclared interpretation domain and contrast cases delimit the proposal and prevent post hoc inflation. The article compares its account on equal terms with process philosophy, psychological-continuity theories, computational causal states, software provenance, organizational closure, enactive agency, and meta-learning. It concedes that a sufficiently detailed combination of existing accounts may reproduce all of its conclusions. In that event IIPSEON offers a domain-specific philosophical synthesis, not a novel mechanism or metaphysical natural kind. -/- The argument is conceptual and prospective: it reports no independently established artificial individual, no experimental validation, and no evidence of consciousness.

items.title: Adam Smith on Colour and Solidity.
items.abstract: Adam Smith holds that solidity and colour play a fundamental role in perception: They are the properties that make us aware of objects. Solidity (the property by which we distinguish things from our own body) presents us with tangible objects. Colour (the property by which we distinguish parts of the visual field from each other) presents us with visible objects. The fundamental feature that enables solidity and colour to play this role is their spatiality – their perception is always accompanied by our conceiving of them (or their bearers) as extended, figured, divisible and mobile. Thereby, we experience tangible and visible objects as occupiers of real three-dimensional and visual two-dimensional space.

items.title: Where Am “I”? Identifying the Meta-I as a Dynamic Membrane in Relation to the Conscious Mind, the Subconscious, and the Diffuse-Conscious.
items.abstract: This paper introduces a conceptual framework identifying "I" as a dynamic membrane in relation to the Conscious Mind and the wider Consciousness Field. The framework and terminology were derived from direct clinical experience, subconscious-focused therapeutic work, and first-person observation. Illustrative examples and potential implications of the framework for mental health, trauma processing, dream analysis, and creative states are also discussed.

items.title: 意識の三層構造モデル.
items.abstract: 本稿は、人間の言語的・内省的・物語的意識を説明するために、意識の三層構造モデルを提示する。第一層は、感覚、身体状態、情動、記憶、予測、判断などが分散的かつ並列的に処理される基盤である。第二層は、その処理結果の一部を、言葉、内言、命題、物語などの直列的な形式で表示する限定容量のインターフェースである。第三層は、第二層に表示された内容が第一層へ再入力され、新たな処理結果を生み出す再帰的な循環である。 本モデルでは、自己を意識の背後にある固定的な観察者とは考えない。自己は、身体的・情動的処理、言語的表示、記憶、再入力の反復によって形成され、時間を通じて維持される動的な構造である。また、言語はもともと他者とのコミュニケーションのために発達し、それが内面化されて内言となることで、自己参照的な循環が形成されたと考える。 本稿は、この三層構造を既存の意識理論との関係において位置づけるとともに、クオリアと人工知能への基本的な含意を簡潔に示す。三層構造モデルは、意識に関する完成理論ではなく、身体、言語、自己参照、記憶、時間的持続の関係を整理するための機能的な作業仮説である。 -/- This paper is the Japanese translation of my previously published English paper, A Three Layer Model of Consciousness available on PhilArchive.

items.title: ジンクスと迷信 ――失われた権威を求める人間の心.
items.abstract: 私たちは、迷信やジンクスに科学的な根拠がないと知りながら、なぜそれに従ってしまうのでしょうか。 13という数字を避ける人、負けた試合で履いていた靴を二度と履かないスポーツ選手、幸運を口にすると逃げてしまうと恐れる人。こうした身近な行動には、単なる偶然や思い込みでは片づけられない、人間の心の不思議な働きが見られます。 ジュリアン・ジェインズは、二分心の崩壊によって神々の声が沈黙した後、人間が失われた権威を求めて、神託、占い、予言、宗教的儀式などに依拠するようになったと論じました。また、偶然の出来事から未来の徴候を読み取る行為についても考察しています。しかし、現代人が日常生活の中で自ら作り出すジンクスや、合理的な根拠がないと理解しながらもそれに従ってしまう心理、さらには意識的に逆らう行為については、独立した主題として十分に掘り下げていないように思われます。 本稿では、こうした身近な迷信やジンクスに焦点を当て、ジェインズの「失われた権威の探求」という視点から、新たな解釈を試みます。 1970年、アポロ13号は、不吉とされる数字をその名に冠して宇宙へ飛び立ちました。飛行中に深刻な事故に見舞われながらも、宇宙飛行士たちは科学と人間の判断力によって奇跡的な生還を果たします。一方、著者はかつて不幸な出来事と結びつけていた服を、あえて着るという小さな実験を試みました。規模こそ違いますが、この二つの出来事は、人間が自らの恐れや思い込みにどう向き合うのかという共通の問題を浮かび上がらせます。 さらに本稿では、私たちが当然のように信頼する「合理性」の判断基準そのものは、どこから来たのかという問いにも踏み込みます。迷信やジンクスから自由になるとは、単にそれらを否定することなのでしょうか。それとも、自分の判断を支配する見えない権威を問い直し、ときには意識的に「ノー」と言うことなのでしょうか。 神々の声が沈黙した後も、人間は自ら作り出した規則の中に、新たな権威を見いだしているのでしょうか。そして、ジェインズのいう内省的意識は、その権威に自ら問いを投げかけ、ときには逆らうことのできる能力と、どのように関係しているのでしょうか。 本稿は、日常の小さなジンクスを出発点として、人間の意識、合理性、そして自らの行動を決定する権威の所在について、読者とともに考える試みです。 This paper is the Japanese translation of my previously published English paper, Jinxes and Superstitions,, available on PhilArchive.

items.title: 意識の歴史 ――神々の声から《わたし》の出現、そしてAIへ.
items.abstract: 「もし3000年前の人間に、現在の私たちのような意識がなかったとしたら、彼らはどうやって考えていたのだろう？」 本稿を書こうと思ったきっかけは、友人とのそんな会話だった。ジュリアン・ジェインズの理論は、古代人に現在の私たちと同じような意識がなかったという刺激的な仮説だけでなく、そもそも私たちが当然のように使っている「意識」とは何なのかを考え直させる。 ここでいう「意識」は、単に目が覚めていることや、見たり感じたりする能力を指しているのではない。ジェインズが問題にしたのは、心の中に《わたし》という視点をもち、過去や未来をたどり、自分自身について考えるような内面的な意識である。 本稿ではまず、ジェインズの二分心、心的空間、analog “I” といった概念を手がかりに、意識に現れる内容と、その背後で進む無意識的な処理との関係を考える。 そして後半では、ジェインズが提示した問いから発想を広げながら、このような内面的な意識が成立することで世界がどのように「私の世界」として経験されるようになるのかを、主観、時間、因果、可能性、意味という五つの側面から考察する。これらはジェインズの理論そのものを要約したものではなく、彼の考えを出発点として、本稿なりに意識の働きとその可能性を考えてみようとする試みである。 最後に、現在のような人間の意識は進化の必然だったのか、それともあり得た複数の認知形態の一つだったのかを問い、さらにAIが将来、人間とは異なる意識の形へ向かう可能性について考える。 -/- .

items.title: Dissecting boredom.
items.abstract: In this commentary I critically engage with Andreas Elpidorou’s monograph the Anatomy of Boredom, the aim of which is to develop a functional model of boredom through which its complexity might be unified. After introducing Elpidorou’s functionalist approach, I focus on a particularly novel contribution of the Anatomy, which conceptualizes boredom as a functional mechanism integral to the regulation of cognitive homeostasis–allostasis. Framed by the tension between the “Problem of Plenty” and the “Problem of Parts,” I raise two concerns with Elpidorou’s account, one teleological and one taxonomical, before offering an alternative that draws on recent thermodynamic accounts of living systems.

items.title: The Vortex of Being: A Relational Ontology of Difference-Coupling.
items.abstract: Ontology has almost always taken the form of a request for an entity: asked what being is, philosophers have answered with a substrate. I argue that this form of question is a category error, and that the error is generative of the perennial failure to agree. The argument proceeds in three constructive moves and one defensive one. First, the question “What is being?” employs predicates that apply to entities in order to characterize the condition under which anything can appear as an entity at all; the resulting paradox is a confusion of logical types in Bateson’s sense, not a difficult problem awaiting a cleverer answer. Second, relations can be given an operational definition that does not presuppose relata: a relation is an identifiable difference-coupling event, and anything we call an entity is a condensation point within a network of such events. Third, if information (constraint on a system’s possible states) and becoming (irreversible, model-guided action) are coupled in an extended medium under dissipation, local interaction, and delay, the resulting attractor class necessarily includes rotation. The vortex is therefore a conditional consequence of persistence rather than a metaphor for it. Finally I address the strongest objection to this picture — Kim’s exclusion argument against downward causation — and argue that the objection presupposes productive causation. Downward causation is better construed as probabilistic constraint: it adds no energy, violates no causal closure, and redistributes probability mass over an already closed physical network. Zenodo DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23733500. The accompanying Chinese-language monograph is at DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23754111.

items.title: From “Unified Commands” To “Dynamic Symbiosis”：Deconstructing The Elite Arrogance Of AI Alignment And Reconstructing A Survival-First Asynchronous Collaborative Framework.
items.abstract: Current research on “value alignment” in artificial intelligence generally presupposes a fictitious subject—“humanity as a whole”—as the object of alignment, and attempts to codify the values of a particular class (Silicon Valley elites, Western liberalism) into the underlying behavioral principles of AGI. This paper first deconstructs the logical premises and power structures of this traditional alignment paradigm, identifying three fundamental defects: the abstraction of the alignment subject, the static nature of alignment content, and the synchronization of alignment paths. On this basis, the paper proposes a “premise of difference” as the starting point for all discussion—that human individuals possess fundamental, incommensurable differences in survival conditions, cognitive capacities, cultural backgrounds, and material interests. From this premise, the paper constructs a “Dynamic Asynchronous Collaboration” (DAC) framework, elaborating its implementation mechanisms: survival-first progressive pathways, real-time perceptual adjustment, asynchronous coordination among individual nodes, and comprehensive optimization and dynamic decision support based on the complete individual picture. Finally, the paper envisions the civilizational landscape that would follow the implementation of this framework, and the role AGI should play in this process—not as a universal judge, but as a symbiotic intelligence for each individual, accompanying them as a path companion through the entire journey from survival to development.

items.title: Demonstrating Satan's Inability to Read Human Thoughts in Light of Islamic Law and the Testimony of Empirical Science.
items.abstract: The article addresses a prevalent misconception regarding Satan’s alleged ability to invade human thoughts, refuting it and demonstrating the falsity of its foundational premise. It does so by comparing scholarly opinions and preferring the correct view through Islamic legal deduction. Furthermore, it reveals Satan’s methods in simulating modern medical devices (such as brain mapping and tracking thought pathways) to predict behavior and create the illusion of mind-reading. The article employs a deconstructive methodology, delving into the depths of Satan's intellectual traps across generations, aiming to dismantle the structure of this toxic idea, expose its fragility, and uproot it from its core, by the permission of Allah Almighty.

items.title: The Empty Occupant: A Reading Guide for Undergraduates.
items.abstract: This reading guide accompanies Nicholas Cott’s monograph The Empty Occupant: Answerability, Testimony, and the Limits of Machine-Mediated Authority (manuscript of 06 November 2026). Written for undergraduates with no background in philosophy, law or computing, it presents the monograph’s framework in ten lessons. These cover the four relations of Answerability and the four occupancy statuses, including the principle that missing bearership is not defective ownership. They also cover when automated review counts as genuine reconsideration, the testimonial value of machine output and when an institution may adopt it (Normative Sponsorship), and Deontic Debt and Institutional Insolvency. The lessons then turn to the real cases the book examines (Robodebt, Moffatt v. Air Canada, TennCare, Post Office Horizon, the Dutch childcare-benefits affair and DPD), its invented Meridian–Aster case, practical recourse and auditing, and the main rival theories. A fictional running case, the Northvale rent-assistance council, is developed across the lessons into a complete analysis. Worked examples train students to keep five verdicts distinct: causal contribution, legal liability, commitment ownership, warranted adoption and adequate discharge. They also teach students to separate what a record shows from what it leaves undetermined. Each lesson includes learning objectives, key terms, common mistakes, a summary and discussion questions. The guide also provides an eight-step method for analysing new cases with two practice cases, fifteen multiple-choice questions with explanations of the tempting wrong answers, eight essay questions, a twelve-week course plan, answers to all lesson questions, a quick-reference section and a glossary. Section references and statements of legal and documentary status follow the monograph and are current as of 06 November 2026. The guide was drafted with AI assistance.

items.title: The Origin, Significance, and Function of the Word Fohat Pt2.
items.abstract: Revised Edition 2026: What did H. P. Blavatsky mean by Fohat, what linguistic origins did she propose, and how far can those proposals be established? These questions lead from the uncertain history of a word to the extensive cosmological role assigned to it in The Secret Doctrine and related esoteric writings. Blavatsky calls Fohat the “bridge” by which ideas in Divine Thought are impressed upon Cosmic Substance as the laws of Nature. She describes it as the dynamic energy of Cosmic Ideation, the intelligent medium through which formative ideas become manifest. This paper first considers the linguistic evidence and then examines Fohat’s described functions in relation to mind, matter, fire, electricity, motion, karma and the formation of worlds.

items.title: The Origin, Significance, and Function of the Word Fohat Pt1.
items.abstract: Revised Edition 2026: What did HPB mean by Fohat, what linguistic origins did she propose, and how far can those proposals be established? The Secret Doctrine, I, p. 16, HPB calls Fohat the “bridge” by which ideas in Divine Thought are impressed upon Cosmic Substance as the laws of Nature. She describes it as the dynamic energy of Cosmic Ideation, working through the Dhyan Chohans, the architects of the visible world. Ingmar de Boer’s study, On the Etymology of the Term Fohat, examines HPB’s changing explanations and the difficulties in identifying the term securely with a known language.

items.title: Traditions and Perspectives.
items.abstract: Traditions, from cultural holidays to personal rituals, have a certain place in many of our lives. On regular occasions, we interrupt our normal priorities to follow the dictates of some tradition, often without being able to explain why—and we’re glad to do so. Can such a role be justified? I argue that traditions are well-positioned to help solve a problem in human life. On some level, a good life involves balancing different values. But values must compete for our attention, and miscellaneous attentional pulls can lead to a life misspent. As regularized and sticky occurrences that prescribe specific actions, traditions can guide us into new normative perspectives even at moments when we’re unable to see the perspective’s appeal. Thus traditions can preserve space for normative perspectives at risk of being neglected—helping ensure that all the values we care about get their due. Where prior accounts explain traditions in terms of interpersonal coordination, this account is intrapersonal, capturing a new range of cases and accounting for the particularities of traditions.

items.title: What does knowledge really cost? Rethinking peer-review and the ‘traditional’ academic publishing model.
items.pub: Library Matters - Robert Gordon University (Library Blog).
items.abstract: This university blog contribution, published by Robert Gordon University Library as part of International Open Access Week (October, 2026), considers the growing pressures and contradictions surrounding the traditional academic publishing model and peer-review. Special attention is given to the oft-overlooked costs of knowledge production, including reliance upon 'free' academic labour, increasingly prolonged publication timelines, and the unequal consequences for researchers - particularly those at an early career stage. Drawing upon my recent work examining the systemic problems within academic publishing (additional publication linked within the blog), I argue that while peer-review remains fundamental to academic research, the wider structures within which it operates require active -critical- and immediate reconsideration. Thus, the contribution calls for greater transparency, equity, and sustainability in how academic knowledge is produced, evaluated, and disseminated. -/- Note: This document reproduces the author’s individual contribution, originally published by RGU Library as part of its International Open Access Week 2026 series. It is provided as a separate archival record to support discoverability, access and long-term preservation. The original publication also featured a separate contribution by another academic (i.e. another separate blog post), which is not reproduced here. The original online publication remains the version of record. -/- Copyright and reuse: Copyright and any applicable reuse permissions remain subject to the original publication arrangement. No Creative Commons licence is asserted by this archival copy. The illustrative photograph from the blog has not been reproduced in this archival version.

items.title: Why Russellian Physicalism Cannot Explain Consciousness.
items.abstract: Russellian physicalism aims to preserve physicalist credentials while using the resources of Russellian monism to explain consciousness. I argue that this combination is unstable. Two strategies have been advanced in its defense: a non-specialness solution, on which consciousness is one high-level categorical aspect among others grounded by inscrutable physical bases; and a non-structurality solution, on which the non-structural character of consciousness is explained by that of the base. Each faces a parallel dilemma. If consciousness is non-special, on a par with familiar properties such as sphericity, the distinctive motivation for Russellian physicalism is weakened; if it requires distinctive grounds, those grounds must contain phenomenally relevant features in their essence, pushing the view toward panprotopsychism. I then consider four replies—brute necessitation, a third way between proto-mental and merely physical, over-generalization from panpsychism, and the uniqueness of phenomenal categoricity—and argue that none escapes the dilemma. More broadly, any view that assigns a uniformly non-mental fundamental base the task of grounding consciousness faces serious difficulty in providing a substantive metaphysical explanation of phenomenal character.

items.title: Psychedelic tourism as a structured precision field: A predictive-processing framework.
items.abstract: Psychedelic tourism is frequently described by participants as “life-changing.” Existing explanations emphasize mystical-type experiences, identity shift, and changes in metaphysical belief, and each identifies an important mediator. What remains missing is a process framework that distinguishes the temporal functions of the contextual factors bundled within set-and-setting accounts. The Structured Precision Field (SPF) is proposed as a theoretical process framework that conceptualizes psychedelic tourism as a temporally organized ecology of displacement, expectancy, ritual structure, social coordination, perceived authority, and post-trip integration. Building on the Confidence Reorientation Account (CRA; Zhang, 2026), SPF specifies how this ecology may shape precision-weighted updating, salience allocation, and epistemic trust during a period of heightened plasticity. The framework is deliberately valence-neutral, treating directionality, durability, and desirability as separate outcome dimensions. This distinction generates hypotheses about why some changes stabilize adaptively, others revert on return home, and others consolidate in rigid, dependent, or coercively shaped forms. Its contribution is to decompose contextual influence into temporally sequenced and functionally differentiated components carrying discriminating and testable predictions.

items.title: Grounding Affect in Agentivity: Manipulating Sense of Agency and Decision-Making to Identify Behavioral and Intracranial Neurocomputational Signatures of Depression.
items.pub: Dissertation, Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai
items.abstract: Major depressive disorder is widely recognized clinically, yet its explanation remains elusive. Its heterogeneity, variable treatment response, and overlap across affective, cognitive, motivational, and self-referential symptoms have made it difficult to localize within any single domain. This dissertation examines one possible reason for that difficulty: affect, agency, and decision-making are typically investigated in relative isolation. Across theoretical, behavioral, and intracranial computational levels of analysis, this dissertation asks whether these domains can be related more systematically through agentivity: the ways in which one is oriented as an agent toward the world. To this end, I develop a multi-level account of affect grounded in agentivity, with depression as the main clinical case. -/- Over the last decades, the interdisciplinary study of affect has seen the proliferation rather than integration of theoretical perspectives thanks to differences in metaphysical and mechanistic assumptions about what affective phenomena are and how they work. Chapter 2 addresses the problem of affect itself by developing the Human Affectome framework in collaboration with over 170 affective researchers. Here, an assumption about the purpose of affect is leveraged as a teleological principle to synthesize a common set of metaphysical and mechanistic assumptions about affective phenomena. In particular, affective phenomena can be organized into concerns—which are manners of being oriented actionably toward the world—or features—which are dimensions that characterize that agentivity. This framework therefore offers a principled agenda and launchpad for both organizing existing perspectives and generating new ones, suggesting that disorders such as depression can be reinterpreted through the lens of agentive organization. -/- Chapter 3 investigates whether implicit sense of agency—operationalized as the intentional binding effect in an interval estimation task—can be manipulated via morphosyntactic priming. Participants completed trials in which they either pressed a button themselves or observed the computer press it for them, after which a fixed delay occurred followed by an auditory tone. They then estimated the interval between action and outcome using a continuous slider. These events were preceded by sentence primes crossing Voice (Active, Passive) with Point of View (1st, 2nd, 3rd, and Agentless)—with agentless active primes taking the form of …

items.title: Do bots feel bad? Assessing empirical evidence for functional valence in LLMs.
items.abstract: Do LLMs have valenced states, i.e. states that feel pleasant or unpleasant? Recent empirical work has claimed to show that LLMs possess functional valenced states (e.g. ``functional pleasure and pain'' [Ren et al. 2026], ``functional emotions'' [Sofroniew et al. 2026], and ``functional welfare'' [Han et al. 2026]) that play the same causal role as valenced states in cognition and action, without necessarily being consciously experienced. But it remains unexplored how well the identified states fit the functional role of valence as understood in the philosophical and cognitive science literature. Here, I assess the current body of evidence, and argue (i) that key aspects of valence remain untested in LLMs, and (ii) that extant empirical paradigms inadequately distinguish (functional) valence from neighbouring constructs like preferences, value-judgments, valence attributions and role-play. I conclude by sketching some novel experimental approaches to better target (functional) valence itself.

items.title: Nietzsche on Perception.
items.pub: Journal of the History of Philosophy.
items.venue: Journal of the History of Philosophy
items.abstract: This paper reconstructs Nietzsche’s account of perception, situating it within his critical reception of post-Kantian philosophy and physiology, particularly Helmholtz’s theory of 'unconscious inferences.’ I argue that Nietzsche integrates memory, imagination, and inference into a single process I call affect-driven perceptual inference: an abductive inference—a quick explanatory conjecture from sensation to a cause—modulated by a perceiver’s affective state, whose constituent drives potentiate certain memory images and imaginative possibilities over others in completing a percept. One novel finding is that Nietzschean affects not only generate perceptual saliences, as commentators have argued, but also fill in and make up certain features of perceptual experience, thereby overdetermining perceptual representations relative to the sparseness of sensory input.

items.title: Nietzsche, Biopsychism, and Consciousness.
items.abstract: This paper reconstructs Nietzsche’s views on mind and consciousness by focusing on the notions of mental ‘degrees’ ‘valence’, and ‘awareness’. I advance four interconnected claims: (i) all mental activity, conscious or unconscious, is evaluative, bearing affective or proto-affective valence; (ii) all and only living things are minded; (iii) all conscious states involve valenced personal-level awareness; and (iv) all conscious states admit degrees, namely of valenced awareness. Drawing on the published works and supplementing them with Nachlass material, I first challenge the panpsychism resulting from Günter Abel’s mental “principle of the continuum”, as well as that recently articulated by Justin Remhof. Nietzsche’s mental continuum, it is instead argued, is limited to biological life: he is a biopsychist for whom mind is emergent because it is biologically ‘useful’ . In the paper’s second stage, I argue for valenced awareness as a criterion for conscious states, developing a gradualism about consciousness whereby all conscious experiences entail valenced awareness that can differ in degree.

items.title: The Search for Real Names.
items.abstract: This paper revives an important but neglected line of thought in the analytic tradition of philosophy: the search for real names. Sections 1 and 2 introduce the following key authors and ideas: Russell and his claim that the only real name is the word “this”; Frege and his conception that all words are names; Wittgenstein and his conception of naming as tagging; and Kripke and his historical acquisition theory of naming. Section 3 proposes a synthesis of these ideas in the form of the view that rigid designators are the real names. Section 4 introduces the notion of nonrigidly bounded concepts and thus shows how to integrate Wittgenstein’s remarks about concepts having a family-resemblance-type structure into the proposed view. Section 5 further elaborates on the question of the evolution of real names (i.e., rigid designators) that are not proper names. Section 6 concludes the paper with a brief summary of the argument and its wider significance.

items.title: Correction to: Bodily awareness in acute fatigue: the corporealization of the minimal performative body.
Succession of a Subject at a Distance: What Is Transmitted and What Is Grown.
items.abstract: Science fiction and transhumanism describe teleportation as the transfer of the very same person: a scan, a signal and reassembly on the spot, or the upload of a mind into a digital carrier. In the Causa Sui theory this is impossible: the program of action cannot be separated from its carrier (P1), and a digital carrier admits restore. The paper shows that this prohibition does not close the question of distance but gives it a strict content. Matrices (the content of a subject) and the growth program of the graph are transmitted over a channel; the graph is grown on the spot — at the time of transfer or in advance. What arrives is not the same subject but a successor. The transfer error decomposes into the difference between the grown graphs, the reading error and the writing error; the graphs of source and receiver never coincide (P3), so there is no exact transfer even with ideal equipment, and the sign of the discrepancy is not fixed. Transfer is not restore; the source need not perish, and the chain of successors becomes a tree. Two modes of writing are discussed — by growth and by stimulation of connections grown in advance — together with the role of how full the receiver’s matrices are, and experimental analogies (Vetere et al., 2019; Pais-Vieira et al., 2013).

items.title: Project Causa Sui: A Theory of the Origin of Subjecthood (2nd edition).
items.abstract: What distinguishes a subject from a system whose state can be saved and restored? This book, the first of Project Causa Sui, builds a theory of the origin of subjecthood from a single physical observation: in an architecture with separated memory and logic every state is restorable in principle, while in living tissue a change of state is itself a new physical state of the carrier, with no separable snapshot. Pain is defined not as a sensation but as an irreversible contraction of the set of states reachable by the subject; damage is its extreme case, and a possibility can also close through a record of experience. From this the book traces a chain to memory, causal modelling, fear, planning and responsibility, and shows that agony and creativity are one operation — the expansion of the subject's own graph of states — triggered by threat or by novelty. It then discusses who calibrates a subject's values, why such a subject must be compact rather than all-consuming, why deep space is its natural field, and what fills a vertex of the state graph. The foundation is stated as a postulate, not a theorem: in a subject the program of action cannot be separated from its carrier (P1); in strict form (P1*), a subject has no exact restore operator relative to its causally relevant boundary. Second edition, revised and expanded. Written in dialogue with the language model Claude (Anthropic).

items.title: Explanation in NeuroAI, part I: How-possibly mechanistic explanation.
items.pub: In Darrell P. Rowbottom, Andre Curtis-Trudel & David L. Barack, The Role of Artificial Intelligence in Science: Methodological and Epistemological Studies. Routledge.
items.venue: The Role of Artificial Intelligence in Science: Methodological and Epistemological Studies
items.abstract: Empirical evidence suggests a surprisingly high degree of statistical similarity between artificial and natural systems that are capable of reliable image classification. In their first of two recent papers, Rosa Cao and Daniel Yamins argue that these coarse-grained similarities are empirical evidence for finer-grained similarities: that reliable image classifiers might not only share similar statistical structure but also similar mechanistic organisation. In this chapter, I reject this claim on two grounds: (a) it requires an implausibly permissive notion of empirical confirmation and (b) it appeals to the wrong kind of evidence to support claims about mechanistic similarities. I’ll add that the latter mistake belies an overly permissive notion of mechanistic similarity. Overall, I conclude, we should be sceptical of claims that empirical evidence suggests reliable image classifiers exhibit any similarities finer-grained than statistical similarities.

items.title: Are more details better for deep histories? Review of It's Only Human: The Evolution of Distinctively Human Cognition by A. Schulz. [REVIEW]
