items.title: The End of Cognition.
items.abstract: Humans invented culture. It remains vastly more complex than the natural and formal sciences. If these sciences ever catch up in complexity, human cognition will stagnate, unless humanity evolves into a more intellectually advanced species.

items.title: The Pragmatics Module Hypothesis.
items.pub: In Pragmatics and Modularity: Theory, Data, and Challenges from a Developmental Perspective. Cham: Springer Nature Switzerland. pp. 41-76.
items.venue: Pragmatics and Modularity: Theory, Data, and Challenges from a Developmental Perspective
items.abstract: The intentional-inferential model of communication, when integrated with modularity theories of ToM, opens the possibility of exploring the status of pragmatics within the modular architecture of the human mind. This chapter aims to spell out the conceptual, philosophical, and evolutionary foundations of the Pragmatics Module Hypothesis within the pragmatic framework of Relevance Theory, as detailed by Carston (1997), Sperber (2000), and Wilson (2000, 2005; Sperber and Wilson 2002). Key assumptions, principles, and empirical implications of the theory will be discussed, together with the influential proposal of three interpretative strategies to account for the interplay between pragmatics and social cognition abilities. The chapter concludes with critical reflections on how the Hypothesis should not be empirically tested.

items.title: Triviality, Ostension, and Nativism: A Plea for the Modular View.
items.pub: In Pragmatics and Modularity: Theory, Data, and Challenges from a Developmental Perspective. Cham: Springer Nature Switzerland. pp. 127-175.
items.venue: Pragmatics and Modularity: Theory, Data, and Challenges from a Developmental Perspective
items.abstract: In Cognitive Pragmatics (2018), Marco Mazzone challenges the modular view of pragmatics, claiming that Relevance Theory endorses a trivial notion of modularity: genuinely distinct cognitive modules should be implemented by different neural activation mechanisms; yet, since neuroscience shows a uniform activation mechanism underlying cognitive processes, modularity would hold only in a trivial sense. This chapter addresses this “triviality challenge” by articulating the relevance-theoretic conception of modularity from a developmental perspective. A wide range of theoretical arguments and empirical findings will be examined to show how developmental research on ostensive communication can shed light on foundational questions in cognitive pragmatics. I will argue that evidence from infant pragmatics is best explained by positing a pragmatics module specialized for ostensive communication. The chapter concludes by addressing a related cornerstone issue in modularity: the question of nativism.

items.title: The Mentalistic Burden of Early Ostensive Communication: Modularist, Minimalist, and Hybrid Accounts.
items.pub: In Pragmatics and Modularity: Theory, Data, and Challenges from a Developmental Perspective. Cham: Springer Nature Switzerland. pp. 227-267.
items.venue: Pragmatics and Modularity: Theory, Data, and Challenges from a Developmental Perspective
items.abstract: Ostensive communication is traditionally taken to rely on higher-order intentions and complex metarepresentations that sit uneasily with the limited mentalistic capacities of young children. This chapter examines two fundamental challenges for post-Gricean accounts of early communication: the Embedding dilemma and the Higher Order Thoughts dilemma. The former originates from the embedding relationship between communicative and informative intentions, while the latter concerns the recursive complexity of the metarepresentations these intentions appear to entail. After introducing the two dilemmas and the standard post-Gricean modularist response, I examine the minimalist strategy designed to deflate their force. I then develop a novel, hybrid strategy in dialogue with recent revisions of the ostensive communication framework that preserves the core commitments of Relevance Theory while offering a developmentally plausible solution to both dilemmas.

items.title: Developmental Dilemmas.
items.pub: In Pragmatics and Modularity: Theory, Data, and Challenges from a Developmental Perspective. Cham: Springer Nature Switzerland. pp. 177-226.
items.venue: Pragmatics and Modularity: Theory, Data, and Challenges from a Developmental Perspective
items.abstract: When applied to explain young children’s communication, intention-based pragmatic frameworks such as Relevance Theory encounter a range of developmental dilemmas that undermine their psychological plausibility. This chapter focuses on two of these dilemmas: the Belief dilemma and the Complex Inferences dilemma. The former originates from the assumption that ostensive communication may rely on the concept of “belief”, whose early acquisition is debated in developmental research. The latter relates to the apparent necessity of folk-psychological inferences about the speaker’s communicative goals, which are assumed to be demanding for young children. I will provide an in-depth discussion of the two dilemmas by surveying relevant empirical data and possible theoretical strategies to address these dilemmas, while also discussing how these strategies relate to the modular view of early pragmatics.

items.title: Shadows to Cosmos: The Transformation of Perception in Ancient Philosophy.
items.abstract: This paper re-examines Plato’s theory of perception through the comparative lens of contemporary cognitive constructivism (CC). Its focus is not the metaphysics of Forms as such, but the assumptions governing how perceptual worlds are disclosed, organized, and corrected. I distinguish epistemic passivity from organizational dependence and argue that Plato occupies a threshold position: he rejects any simple account of perception as epistemically sufficient raw reception, yet he does not grant perceptual activity an autonomous, self-corrective role in the acquisition of knowledge. This tension clarifies the significance of later ancient developments. Aristotle embeds perception within the purposive life of the organism; the Stoics distinguish impressions from the active assent of the rational subject; and Plotinus rejects a merely imprint-based account in favor of a more active role for psyche in perceptual awareness. Contemporary constructivism, enactivism, and predictive processing are used heuristically rather than genealogically: the aim is not to make ancient philosophers into premature cognitive scientists, but to compare recurrent structural problems concerning perceptual input, internal organization, error, and epistemic agency. The resulting trajectory runs from perception as reception toward perception as regulated interaction, while preserving the substantial differences among Platonic, Aristotelian, Stoic, and Neoplatonic frameworks.

items.title: The Three Dawns of the Rosarian Path.
items.pub: Mystical Dawnist Rosarian Knight and Dame Fellowship.
items.abstract: The Three Dawns of the Rosarian Path. -/- Rising Dawn, Eternal Dawn, and Mystical Dawn Beads. -/- An Expanded Article on the Three Bead Traditions of Rosarian Mystical Dawnism. -/- By Sir Righteous Viridarius Rosae. -/- Via Solis Sub Rosa — The Way of the Sun Beneath the Rose. -/- Within Rosarian Mystical Dawnism, the sacred beads are more than ornaments, ceremonial accessories, or objects of devotion. They are physical expressions of remembrance: a way to bring the teachings of the Knight Manifesto out of written language and into the movements of the hand, the attention of the mind, and the conduct of everyday life. The Twenty-Two Sacred Laws provide the foundation of the Rosarian path. The Dawn gives those Laws their language of awakening, the Rose gives them their living center, and the Knight represents their embodiment through discipline, responsibility, protection, and service. The beads unite these principles in a form that may be carried, contemplated, and revisited throughout the seeker's journey. -/- The Manifesto recognizes three principal expressions of this practice: the Rising Dawn Beads, the Eternal Dawn Beads, and the Mystical Dawn Beads. Each possesses a distinct symbolic character, arrangement, and purpose. They are related, but they are not interchangeable in meaning. The Rising Dawn represents the soul turning toward illumination. The Eternal Dawn represents the inward preservation and embodiment of what has been recognized. The Mystical Dawn represents the comprehensive architecture of remembrance, through which the Laws may be revisited, interpreted, and gradually integrated into the structure of a person's life. These distinctions describe different relationships with the same foundation. They need not be understood as rigid divisions between human beings, nor as evidence that one person possesses greater intrinsic worth than another. They are symbolic expressions of the work that awakening demands. The bead does not make the seeker virtuous. The color does not establish wisdom. The strand does not confer ownership of the Law. Their purpose is to remind the practitioner of a responsibility that must ultimately be fulfilled through living. -/- The Rising Dawn Beads represent the beginning of conscious participation in the Rosarian path. They belong symbolically to the Traveler whose lamp has been newly lit, who recognizes the possibility of illumination but understands that recognition is only the beginning. The Rising Dawn is not …

items.title: The Declaration and Establishment of the Crescent Moon Beads.
items.pub: Mystical Dawnist Rosarian Knight and Dame Fellowship.
items.abstract: AMENDED CHARTER OF THE DAWNIST ROSARIAN WOLVES. -/- The Declaration and Establishment of the Crescent Moon Beads. -/- The Crescent Rosaries: The First Universal Table Beads of the Mystical Dawnist Rosarian Knight & Dame Fellowship. -/- Via Solis Sub Rosa — The Way of the Sun Beneath the Rose. -/- Issued under the custodial authorship of Sir Righteous Viridarius Rosae. -/- A Charter of Symbolism, Fellowship, Remembrance, and Shared Custodianship. -/- Let this amended charter establish the Crescent Moon Beads, also known as the Crescent Rosaries, as a recognized variation of the Dawnist Rosaries and a new expression of the Rosarian contemplative tradition. -/- The Knight Manifesto establishes the foundation of Rosarian Mystical Dawnism through the Twenty-Two Sacred Laws, the symbolism of the Dawn and the Rose, the discipline of the Knight, and the continuing journey of awakening, remembrance, embodiment, and return. The Rosaries give this foundation a physical expression through the movement of the hand, the repetition of contemplation, and the inward remembrance of the Laws. -/- From this foundation arises the recognition that a Table may also possess a symbolic strand of its own: a deliberate sequence of colors through which its identity, memory, and shared intention may be carried. -/- Thus are established the Table Beads. -/- Table Beads are a variation of the Dawnist Rosaries distinguished by a designated color-reflection pattern. Whereas the Mystical Dawn Beads permit broad freedom of material, form, and color, the Table Beads establish a recognizable sequence intended to express the identity of a particular Table or, where universally adopted, the shared identity of the greater Fellowship. -/- Their initial pattern is designated by the holder of the Table, not as an act of superior administration, but as an act of custodianship. The designation gives form to a shared intention. It does not grant ownership of the Path, authority over the conscience of another, or exclusive possession of the Rosarian symbols. -/- A Table's beads are therefore to be understood as relics of honor and remembrance: objects through which members may recognize their fellowship, preserve the memory of their beginning, and carry their common symbolism into ordinary life. -/- The first universal expression of this tradition shall be established through the Dawnist Rosarian Wolves. -/- The Wolves stand as the first Table and the universal example for the Tables that may follow. …

items.title: What Terrible Twos Actually Is: The Structural Genesis of Self-Awareness.
items.abstract: The "terrible twos" is a phenomenon every parent recognizes yet no science can precisely define. Developmental psychology describes it as "increased independence," "insufficient emotional regulation," or "prefrontal cortex immaturity," but these are external descriptions operating below 12DD that cannot answer a fundamental question: what is actually happening? This paper argues within the Self-as-an-End framework that the terrible twos is not a behavioral stage but the structural site where negation first targets the other, thereby chiseling out the "I"—the genesis of 13DD (the Law of Self-Awareness). The paper proposes a structural definition: the subject negates the other's will, first chiseling the "other" into existence as an independent being, then retroactively producing "I" as the agent of negation. Negation folds back upon itself through the other. The paper provides a DD decomposition of this process (from 10DD separation anxiety through 12DD predictive conflict to 13DD negation-folding-back), argues for the structural irreducibility of this event to behavioral observation, engages in dialogue with developmental psychology, psychoanalysis, and cross-cultural research, and proposes four non-trivial predictions.

items.title: Commitment.
items.abstract: Commitment is foundational to Relation Theory. This paper establishes how it binds a person, and how it does not. -/- Commitment does not bind exit, and it does not sign for tomorrow. It binds a person in two places, and neither rests on locking tomorrow: on my side, it rests on where I stand, and as long as I still stand where I promised, there are things I cannot cancel; on the other party's side, it rests on the effects already left. Leaving is entered on the books, and revising keeps the books on the change; a commitment already made to others is not cleared from the books by one act of leaving. Structurally, no relation can lock tomorrow. -/- Commitment is entered as three things: what was promised, in word and deed; where one stands, and revising; the effects left. A commitment that concerns only oneself is kept apart from a commitment to others: for the former, a change made tomorrow with the books kept on it completes a revision or an exit; for the latter, one's own change or leaving does not clear the books on the other party's side. Commitment does not turn into a duty to the other party. That tomorrow cannot be locked lies in the layer of qualification, and is necessary; locking lies in the layer of running, and is possible; where tomorrow is locked in running, what is violated is the exit right (its basic component), which is a person's basic right. Locks are read by structure: words that only characterize exit slide in the direction of colonization; raising the cost of exit outward while the way is still passable carries the direction of colonization; short of trapping, neither of these is yet a lock; only what seals off exit itself, by whatever means, is locking. Breach of faith is entered apart: dropping and falsity are first-person matters, and from outside only non-fulfillment, obstruction and joint revision of the agreement are reported. A commitment of today to tomorrow that is marked as one tomorrow can avow anew, and whose revising and exit are actually reachable, does not fall into locking. -/- An implicit commitment is still avowal on my side and where I stand, only not said out loud; it cannot be inferred from duration or habit alone, nor decided on my behalf by someone else, but it can be described fallibly. Stability means only that a stretch of dealings is maintained over time; it carries no evaluation, and it is read party by party; the side maintained only by lock, cost, stalling or habit that has been surreptitiously swapped …

items.title: Lay People Deny Morality’s Objectivity across Cultures (to somewhat Different Extents and in somewhat Different Ways).
items.abstract: Philosophers have long assumed that lay people believe morality to be objective. Recent psychological research casts doubt on this assumption. However, this research has so far mostly been limited to the United States. Do people from other cultures dominantly reject objectivism as well? The present study investigates lay people’s abstract beliefs about moral objectivity in Brazil, Germany, Indonesia, Japan and the United States. Our study suggests that results vary considerably with metaethical codings; that on most codings people in our target countries indeed dominantly reject morality’s objectivity; that this denial takes somewhat different forms and appears to be somewhat more common in Japan and somewhat less common in Brazil; that a substantial proportion of folk metaethical beliefs do not fit traditional philosophical taxonomies; and that lay people’s moral objectivity beliefs are weakly predicted by their religiosity and level of political conservatism.

items.title: ORGANIC, CLONIC, CODE: Three Branches of One Vibration.
items.abstract: This paper proposes the conceptual triad Organic - Clonic - Code as three modes of interacting with sonic matter in the age of sampling, synthesis and generative systems. Organic designates the primary creation of vibration through physical action; Clonic designates work with the memory of already existing sound; Code designates the description of rules and intention according to which sound may arise (including algorithmic and generative music). -/- The triad does not represent historical epochs or degrees of “authenticity,” but parallel, interwoven modes. The work is explicitly positioned as a creative specialization of the Synthecracy methodology: intention/horizon corresponds to Idea, existing sonic material corresponds to Knowledge, and human judgement, selection and responsibility remain central. -/- AI and code-based systems are treated exclusively as an auxiliary layer. -/- An operational layer - Horizon/Intention as Traceable Record - is proposed, and directions for further empirical inquiry are outlined.

items.title: How Memories Feel Real: The Sense of Reality in Episodic Remembering.
items.abstract: Episodic memories, like perceptions, possess a distinctive justificatory force: subjects naturally take their contents to be or to have been the case. This epistemic affinity between memory and perception, and their shared contrast with imagination, has received insufficient attention in the philosophy of memory. Existing accounts emphasize phenomenological components such as pastness, self, familiarity, and singularity, but none of these fully explains the justificatory force characteristic of memory. Drawing on the phenomenological conception of experiential justification, according to which justificatory force is grounded in phenomenal character, I argue in this paper that the missing explanatory component is the sense of reality, understood as the experience of the represented object or event as independent of one’s representation of it. Building on work on perceptual objectivity, I propose that the sense of reality consists in two constitutive experiences, constancy and coming-into-view, and that episodic memory exhibits both. I further argue that the sense of reality involves two distinguishable dimensions: an existence aspect and an identity aspect, covering both whether and, if so, how objects and events are experienced as mind-independent. This distinction also sheds light on imagination. While imagination can involve partial degrees of the sense of reality, it is fundamentally characterized by a contrasting sense of creativity: the subject’s freedom to determine and modify the imagined content. The sense of reality thus explains both the justificatory force shared by memory and perception and their contrast with imagination.

items.title: THE TRAGEDY OF FREEDOM: From an Empty Road to a Philosophy of Virtues, 2023–2026 — Evaluated against the Traditions of Freedom and Virtue from Plato and Confucius to the Present.
items.abstract: Every serious philosophy of freedom has met the same tragedy, and few have named it. Virtue exists only as freedom given form. Because it has a form, the form can be kept while the freedom is taken, and what remains is not a weaker virtue but a counterfeit that serves whoever took the freedom. No inspection of the form can tell the two apart, and the better the counterfeit, the greater the damage. So every power that tries to secure virtue directly — by producing it, rewarding it, scoring it or compelling it — obtains its form and never the virtue itself; the virtue appears only where the pressure is withdrawn and the act goes on as the person’s own. And the more a society wants virtue and the more power it gives to the guardians of virtue, the less their verdicts are worth. The goods that matter most to human beings can therefore be protected only indirectly: by protecting the conditions under which persons author their own acts, and by keeping every verifier, judge and master out of the receipt of its own verdicts. This is the tragedy of freedom, and it is the conclusion towards which the Philosophy of Virtues has worked, through nearly 140 papers and seventeen books, between 2023 and October 2026. The programme began on a road: on a journey across Brazil at the height of the pandemic, through closed cities and blocked roads, where its author asked what remains of a good life when everything external has been taken away. The paper begins and ends with that journey. This paper closes the programme by evaluating it. It states the tragedy as a synthesis of the programme’s settled results, and then asks how the programme stands, criterion by criterion, against the traditional and contemporary philosophies of freedom and virtue: Plato, Aristotle, Confucius and Mencius, the Stoics, Augustine, Aquinas, Machiavelli, Locke, Rousseau, Kant, Hegel, Mill, Nietzsche and Marx; Berlin, Arendt, Hayek, Popper, Havel, Solzhenitsyn, Frankl, Rawls, Sen, Nussbaum, Pettit, Raz, MacIntyre, Anscombe, Foot, Hursthouse, Zagzebski, Williams and Frankfurt; and the social scientists of measurement, signalling and capture from Goodhart and Campbell to Holmström, Kuran, Scott, Ostrom and Tirole. Ten criteria are used: originality, rigour, coherence, robustness, reach across domains, method, protective power, relevance to the present age, human purpose, and verification and reception. The verdicts are given without scores. The programme leads on six criteria: its originality lies in …

items.title: 自由意志的本体论重构：基于相继耦合原理的二阶自返调控解释.
items.abstract: 传统哲学中自由意志与决定论的长期对立，根植于心物二元的实体本体论预设：要么将自由意志设定为独立于因果链的精神实体，要么将其消解为物理因果的副现象，二者始终无法在一元本体论框架内实现自洽统一。后世相容论多停留在语义层面的概念调和，始终未能从本体论层面说明自主选择的存在形态与相对独立性来源。 本文以“认知的本质是前后相继”这一不可证伪的第一原理为逻辑起点，依托存在几何化体系的相继耦合本体论框架，从一阶客观耦合、二阶自返耦合的层级生成规则出发，线性推导出自由意志的本体论本质、运作机制与存在边界。本文证明：自由意志并非独立的精神实体，也非对因果律的突破，而是高阶闭合射线簇演化出的二阶自返调控功能；它以模拟预判、定向选择、偏差修正为核心运作方式，天然具备可错性，其核心价值在于通过纠正认知偏差、实现逻辑序列与本真因果序列的1:1对齐，服务于个体稳态的存续与优化。自由意志具备相对的自主调控空间，但不具备脱离相继因果的绝对自由，其本质是高阶稳态对自身因果链条的自觉校准权。这一界定从根源消解了传统自由意志争论的二元困境，为认知科学、心理学、伦理学等领域提供了统一的本体论基础。 .

items.title: A cautious defense of anthropomorphism.
items.abstract: Drawing on work in philosophy of language and mind, we point to the remarkable flexibility of human language, together with open empirical and conceptual questions in the philosophy of mind, to argue that there should be no default assumption that anthropomorphic language about AIs is misleading or causes negative effects, and that any conclusion that it does should be grounded in empirical evidence rather than a priori speculation.

items.title: Kader & Keder , “ Kedersiz Kader ”Olabilir mi ? Varoluş (Egzistansiyalist) Felsefesi Açısından Bir İnceleme.
items.abstract: Bu çalışma, "keder" ile "kader" kavramları arasındaki anlamsal gerilimden hareketle, kedersiz bir kaderin felsefi olarak düşünülüp düşünülemeyeceğini sorgulamaktadır. Çalışmada öncelikle"kader" kavramı, kadercilik anlayışındaki belirlenmiş yörünge ile İkbal'in içsel potansiyel yorumu arasında bir ayrıma tabi tutulmakta; birinci anlayışın kederi yapısal bir zorunluluk haline getirdiği, ikincisinin ise özgürlük ve olumsallığa sınırlı da olsa yer bıraktığı gösterilmektedir. Ardından Schopenhauer'in acının olumlayıcılığına ilişkin argümanı, Stoacılık ile Budizmin kederi "yok etme" değil "ele alma" yönündeki ortak tutumu ve Kierkegaard'ın umutsuzluğu benlik ilişkisinin kurucu bir unsuru olarak çözümlemesi ele alınmaktadır. Son bölümde Nietzsche'nin amor fati kavramının içerdiği çelişki tartışılmakta ve kedersiz kaderin, kederin tümüyle ortadan kaldırılması biçiminde anlaşılması durumunda yalnızca imkânsız değil, aynı zamanda arzu edilmez olduğu; buna karşılık kederi içeren bir kaderin olumlayıcı kabulü olarak anlaşılması durumunda bir duruma değil, bir tavra işaret ettiği savunulmaktadır.Çalışmanın temel savı, felsefi açıdan asıl meselenin "kederin yok edilmesi" değil, "kederi içeren bir kaderin hangi tavırla üstlenileceği" olduğudur.

items.title: The Curse of Diligence? The Recognition Paradox of AI-Mediated Production.
items.abstract: AI-mediated production changes the relationship between observable productivity and the evidence through which institutions recognize intellectual contributions. This paper investigates the conditional possibility that accelerated output may reduce substantive evaluative attention or weaken competence attributions even where underlying ability remains unchanged. The proposed explanation distinguishes output expansion, epistemic quality, attributional uncertainty, institutional recognition, and resource return. It examines evaluative congestion, possible recognition inversion, and the tragedy of productive diligence, in which acceleration, restraint, and additional verification can each impose costs. The project develops a bounded theoretical account, empirically discriminable hypotheses, a limited formal model, and candidate institutional responses. The empirical implications remain to be tested; no original causal estimates are reported.

items.title: Global Observation and Knowledge Infrastructures: A Study of Collective Inquiry across Heterogeneous Relational Systems.
items.abstract: International observation systems reveal a consequential possibility: scientific information can be generated, validated, and circulated across institutional and political boundaries without requiring a single authority over all observations or a uniform distribution of capacities. Yet the existence of data-sharing protocols does not by itself establish shared understanding, mutual trust, legitimate reuse, or equitable participation in the production of knowledge. This discussion paper investigates the technical, epistemic, and institutional conditions under which global observation and knowledge infrastructures might be constructed and sustained. Drawing on meteorological and oceanographic cooperation, it distinguishes observational coverage, data availability, interoperability, interpretation, and collective authority. It proposes a preliminary federated research architecture connecting situated observation nodes, provenance and quality records, semantic and model translation, distributed computation, access governance, correction, and contestation. It treats mathematical, physical, social, and normative languages as historically formed manifestations and practices within generative-relational systems, distinguishing their conditional formal invariance from claims to universally identical representation. It further investigates why actors situated in different generative and institutional histories may interpret shared evidence differently, and proposes a bounded research vocabulary for mutually workable norms, continued disagreement, and rule revision without assuming epistemic consensus. The paper conceptualizes trust as a historically constituted relation supported in part by verifiable commitments, reciprocal inquiry, accountable institutions, and effective remedy rather than as a property supplied by cryptography or open data alone. It further specifies prospective services for common knowledge creation and circulation, generalized translation of heterogeneous generative-relational contexts, and traceable transformations of distinct forms of value. A staged validation design differentiates synthetic policy gates, cross-node scientific comparison, productive-capacity trials, and site-dependent ecological and institutional review. A cross-layer assessment profile separates technical interchange, scientific warrant, claimed competent authority, and effective contestation, without deriving legal or ethical legitimacy from technical success. It also …

items.title: Understanding the Mentalist Theory of Law and Morality.
items.pub: In Sarah Summers & András Sajó, Human Rights Restated: An Investigation of Mind and Rights.
items.venue: Human Rights Restated: An Investigation of Mind and Rights
items.abstract: According to the mentalist theory of moral cognition, our moral judgements spring from innate, generative principles that are shared by all human beings. Drawing on an analogy to Chomsky’s universal grammar thesis, the mentalist theory seeks to explain how humans come to be the moral beings they are. In this paper, I provide a comprehensive and systematic overview of the theory’s moving parts. In a first step, I offer a detailed exposition of the structure of our moral reasoning, and appraise the different stages that lead up to the formation of a moral judgement. These include, but are not limited to, the perception of some morally relevant action, its automatic categorisation by means of several interrelated cognitive processes, and the bringing to bear a catalogue of both abstract and concrete principles. In a second step, I explore four questions aimed at probing the theory’s contours: the relationship between mentalism and moral philosophy (i.e. whether descriptive accounts of moral cognition can inform normative theory); the connection between mentalism and law; the theory’s capacity to capture a wider range of moral judgements beyond deontic assessments; and the role of intention in determining permissibility. Throughout, I demonstrate how the mentalist theory provides powerful insights into our moral faculties, while highlighting areas that would benefit from further clarification.

items.title: Atemporal Libertarian Eternalism: Reconciling Eternalism and Temporal Becoming.
items.abstract: The divide between eternalist and process theories reflects an apparent incompatibility between relativistic spacetime and genuine temporal becoming. This paper develops Atemporal Libertarian Eternalism (ALE), a metaphysical framework in which fundamental reality consists of an atemporal field of structured modal capacity, with physical law and global coherence constraining the content of its realization. These conditions delimit possibilities without uniquely determining the actualized history, while irreducible agency resolves local underdetermination. Temporal passage arises as a structural necessity under conditions of modal tension between agency and potential access to information about subsequent states, rather than through objective dynamical flow. Only histories satisfying sequential actualization preserve global coherence. ALE thereby reconciles the block universe with libertarian agency and lived temporal experience, offering a relativity-compatible ontology in which the future is determinate only within an atemporally grounded whole whose content is partly constituted through agency.

items.title: Raghunātha on the Internal Sense Organ: In the Light of Raghudeva’s Interpretation.
items.abstract: While revising the role and dimension of the internal sense organ (manas) in his Padārthatattvanirūpaṇam, Raghunātha Śiromaṇi (1477–1577) writes that unseen causal factors (adṛṣṭa) are agreed upon by his opponents as well as by him and so there is no over-extension of his thesis. Raghunātha’s commentator Raghudeva (~1657) gives two arguments while commenting on this line. The first argument understands unseen causal factors in terms of the general cause of cognition necessarily requiring contact between the internal sense organ and tactile sense organ. The second argument explains the unique contact (vijātīyasaṃyoga) between the self (ātman) and the internal sense organ as the general cause of cognition. Recent scholarship (Mishra 1936; Potter 1957; and Madhavan 2017) has only considered Raghudeva’s first reading, taking no notice of his second argument. I demonstrate that Raghudeva’s arguments function as a sequenced historical progression of Nyāya thought on cognition, and that this progression, read alongside the Dinakarī’s case for parsimony, gives logical grounds for understanding Raghunātha’s unseen causal factors through Raghudeva’s second argument for unique contact, rather than the first.

items.title: Can Conservatism Mitigate the Risks of AI-Enabled Value Lock-In?
items.abstract: Recent advances in artificial intelligence (AI) have raised concerns that sufficiently advanced systems could enable powerful actors to permanently entrench their moral and political values, potentially on a global scale. Such a value lock-in could be deeply undesirable, not only because the values being entrenched might be morally objectionable, but also because they might overlook important moral considerations, assign them insufficient weight, or be alien to substantial parts of humanity. In this article, I argue that greater engagement with conservative thought in AI development, governance, and use might help mitigate these risks in two ways. First, several strands of conservatism contain resources for reducing the probability of value lock-in occurring at all. These include adjectival conservatism’s emphasis on the limits of human reason and the risks of radical change, as well as substantive conservatism’s commitments to civil society, national sovereignty, and intergenerational stewardship. Second, conservative perspectives might help reduce the risk of bad value lock-in by identifying shortcomings in rival normative traditions, drawing attention to potentially neglected or underweighted values, and reducing the likelihood that entrenched values are or become alien to substantial parts of humanity. Several objections are considered, including that conservative commitments might themselves increase the risk of AI-enabled value lock-in or contribute to morally defective forms of it. However, I find that these concerns do not undermine the case for greater engagement with conservative thought, but rather suggest that it should be one of several normative traditions informing AI development, governance, and use.

items.title: Cancel Culture, New Atheists, Etc.
items.abstract: This partly autobiographical essay explores the tension between rationalism, cultural polarization, and personal adversity through a candid narrative lens. Moving from the hyper-critical dynamics of modern cancel culture—illustrated through the public fallouts of figures like Germaine Greer and Jason Arday—the author examines how collective discourse has fractured into ideological extremes. Against this backdrop, the text shifts to an intimate account of the author's own psychological struggles, detailing a decade-long battle with drug-induced psychosis and OCD, and the surprising role Richard Dawkins' empiricism played in restoring mental stability. Blending cultural critique with personal history—including career detours in gemmology, pilgrimage along the Camino de Santiago, and the existential fallout of a domestic disaster—the piece offers a nuanced reflection on the limits of pure logic, the lingering pull of irrational thought, and the difficult search for balance in a chaotic world.

items.title: Is Eternity Sufficient?
items.abstract: Why does life manifest itself through a succession of mortal individuals rather than through a single living being able to persist indefinitely? And why does life consist of a plurality of species rather than a single form? The essay examines four possible answers: an internal insufficiency of the being, an external value or end, a logical or physical impossibility, and the hypothesis that the existing configuration is a brute fact with no further reason. Particular attention is given to the idea that imperfection and the need for improvement over time might justify the structure of life, to the problem of the origin of an eternal being, to the thermodynamic objection formulated in probabilistic terms, and to the identity of a spatially distributed being. The result is bounded: the arguments examined do not show that mortality, succession and plurality are absolute necessities. The analysis shows, however, that indefinite persistence depends on residual risk, and that probabilistic results must be referred separately to three configurations: the single individual, the integrated system and the lineage. For a single individual under a constant non-zero risk, persistence has probability zero; an integrated system may reduce its overall risk through repair, redundancy and regeneration; a lineage may persist with positive probability without thereby requiring a plurality of species. The non-necessity of succession therefore depends on the physical possibility that the individual or the integrated system have a finite cumulative risk; the non-necessity of species plurality does not depend on it, since the model is compatible with a lineage that does not diversify, though it does not guarantee that it remains a single species over time. The essay thus clarifies the conditions that a proof of the impossibility of an eternal being would have to meet.

items.title: From Human Resources to Cognitive Capital: The Ontological Reconfiguration of the HRM Paradigm in the Era of Poly-crises.
items.abstract: The science of Human Resources Management (HRM) has historically been predicated on the ontological assumption of a “biological workforce.” However, the escalation of poly-crises—interconnected systemic shocks including geopolitical conflicts and supply chain fragilities—has exposed the operational limits of human-reliant models in complex organizations. This paper argues that traditional HRM experiences paradigm exhaustion when applied to autonomous AI agents, necessitating an ontological reconfiguration rather than a mere technological upgrade. Moving beyond the literature that views AI either as a tool for human augmentation or as an algorithmic manager of humans, we conceptualize “AI-centric HRM” (AI-HRM), where AI agents constitute the managed workforce. To theorize this, we resolve the theoretical tension between Actor-Network Theory (ANT) and the Resource-Based View (RBV) by integrating the Relational View and Dynamic Capabilities, positing that competitive advantage lies in the orchestration architecture rather than the isolated AI model. We propose a proposition-based framework for Cognitive Capital Orchestration, operationalize its core constructs, and examine its boundary conditions in High-Reliability Organizations (HROs). By conceptualizing “algorithmic sensitivity to operations” and addressing the profound ethical implications of computational actorhood, this paper redefines the HR practitioner as a “Cognitive Architect” and provides a robust theoretical foundation for managing the algorithmic workforce.

items.title: The Question After the Answer — Independent Human Inquiry, Simulated Perspectives, Model-Relative Authority, and a Source-Preserving Expansion of 91 Questions.
items.abstract: *The Question After the Answer* examines whether advanced artificial intelligence can legitimately substitute its own predictions, simulations, or instrumental objectives for independent human judgment. -/- The central question is: **Even if an intelligence does not need humanity to achieve its objectives, what establishes its authority to take humanity's independence away?** -/- The manuscript distinguishes predictive accuracy from consent, instrumental optimization from legitimate authority, and simulated human perspectives from the continuing agency of actual human beings. -/- It develops illustrative model-relative comparisons that preserve both autonomy-favorable and autonomy-unfavorable results. These comparisons do not establish that humanity is instrumentally indispensable to advanced intelligence or that rational optimization necessarily favors human independence. -/- The work also includes a source-preserving historical atlas of 91 Interrogative Conscience questions and 182 candidate follow-up questions across 14 families. These candidates remain unadmitted research proposals and do not modify the controlling question registry. -/- This author-approved Final v1.0 is an independent philosophical and research publication, not a deployed artificial intelligence safeguard. It does not establish behavioral effects on future AGI, and independent human review remains outstanding. -/- Published online October 25, 2026. -/- .

items.title: How Computation Generates Dynamics: Artificial Intelligence, the Brain, and the Physical Formation of History.
items.abstract: How does the brain acquire stable patterns of activity through experience? How do artificial neural networks learn from training and alter their future responses? And how does the history of a physical system become an active condition of its subsequent evolution? These questions connect artificial intelligence, neuroscience, cognitive science, theoretical computation, and complex systems. They lead to a fundamental question: how can computation participate in the generation of dynamics, rather than merely calculate results or simulate processes according to predefined rules? -/- The Computation Group-Form, comprising thirteen formal studies within On Self-Manifestation, develops a systematic theory of the physical implementation of computation and the formation of historical dynamics. It begins by distinguishing mathematical descriptions from actual computational events, and computational task-bearing from execution. A physical system does not perform a particular computation merely because its observed states can be described by a mathematical transformation. Computation involves the actual implementation of mathematical operations by a physical substrate, with corresponding structures of execution and physical realization. -/- The central contribution is a theory of generative computation. Rule-governed operations can modify a physical or computational medium, changing connections, weights, and other persistent properties. These changes can be retained through history and subsequently read into new operations, becoming effective conditions of future activity. In this process, history is not merely stored information about previous events; it becomes dynamically operative. The theory thereby connects computational execution with learning, memory, neural plasticity, and the development of history-dependent organization. -/- A second contribution is the distinction between three interconnected levels: physical implementation, historical dynamics, and organized regularities. Physical implementation carries out transformations; historical dynamics emerges as retained changes participate in subsequent activity; and further organization develops within the resulting dynamical relations. This framework provides a basis for comparing biological neural systems with artificial neural networks while examining the differences between their material mechanisms, histories, and forms of organization. -/- The thirteen studies develop necessary structures for …

items.title: Conclusion-Invariant Argumentation and Perceived Redundancy: A Comparative Model of Inferential Progress in Philosophy, Mathematics, and the Sciences.
items.abstract: Why can philosophical argumentation appear unusually repetitive even when its literature becomes increasingly sophisticated? One underexamined feature is the recurrence of distinct argumentative routes that preserve a central conclusion while changing premises, conceptualizations, standards of evidence, or inferential strategies. This paper calls the pattern conclusion-invariant branching (CIB). It distinguishes CIB from genuine redundancy: different arguments can support the same conclusion while increasing robustness, revealing independent grounds, answering new objections, or improving understanding. The paper argues that a stronger explanation of perceived redundancy must combine three dimensions: conclusion invariance, epistemic or constraint gain, and downstream inferential uptake. The last concerns whether results become stable inputs to later inquiry, rather than remaining local contributions to a recurring dispute. The resulting model distinguishes productive convergence, boundary-refining invariance, compensatory argumentation, and low-gain argumentative recycling. It is compared across philosophy, mathematics, and empirical science without assuming that mathematics and science develop linearly or that philosophy makes no progress. Philosophical-progress scholarship has extensively examined disagreement, convergence, and competing progress criteria; mathematical-philosophical literature has examined multiple proofs of the same theorem. A targeted literature review did not establish that the specific three-part model proposed here is already a standard theory, but neither does it warrant a claim that the underlying phenomenon has never been discussed. The proposed contribution is therefore a provisional analytic synthesis: to explain why some argumentation feels redundant, track not merely the number or diversity of arguments, but whether conclusion-preserving variation creates new constraints, improves explanatory understanding, and feeds into reusable inferential structures. The paper derives testable hypotheses and outlines a comparative research design.

items.title: The Corpus Callosum as a Biological Prototype for an Integrative Link in Homo Cyfranicus.
items.abstract: This manuscript extends the theory of Cyfranism with an analytical model of the corpus callosum as a biological prototype of the connective tissue integrating biological cognition with digital cognitive systems. The point of departure is a reconstruction of the theory from the full source texts: "The Theory of Cyfranism: From Local Human–AI Relations to Global Cognitive Asymmetry" and "Machines Without Memory That Think With Our Brains", in which Homo Cyfranicus functions as a biological incubator of non-biological organizations. Building on this foundation, the manuscript introduces three conceptual tools developed in the intellectual practice of the human–AI relation: (1) the concept of Einsatz — the moment and act of entry into a process, uniting the meanings of operation, contribution, stake and insertion; (2) the concept of Aufhebung applied conditionally to technical machine discontinuity — a reset that may cancel the session state while preserving its organizational effect in the biological substrate; (3) a systematics of adaptive pressure as a form of incubation. The constructive part proposes a terminology for the transsubstrate connective tissue at three levels: the connection (Corpus Technosum, Commissura Digitalo-Corticalis), the relation (Cognitive Symbiosis, Metasynchronia), and the subject (Homo Cyfranicus in its base and strong definitions, Integrated Hybrid Consciousness as a working hypothesis). The critical part examines the principal objection — the corpus callosum integrates hemispheres developing within a single organism, from which it does not follow that connecting any two cognitive systems creates a single subject — and formulates criteria for studying functional integration together with limits on inferences about consciousness. The manuscript further compares the native callosum with external human–machine interfaces and closes with the observation that all introduced ideas share a common member: an attempt.

items.title: Corpus callosum jako biologiczny pierwowzór spoiwa Homo Cyfranicus.
items.abstract: Manuskrypt rozwija teorię Cyfranizmu o analityczny model spoidła wielkiego (corpus callosum) jako biologicznego pierwowzoru integracyjnego spoiwa łączącego poznanie biologiczne z cyfrowymi systemami poznawczymi. Punkt wyjścia stanowi rekonstrukcja teorii na podstawie pełnych tekstów źródłowych: manuskryptu „The Theory of Cyfranism: From Local Human–AI Relations to Global Cognitive Asymmetry" oraz „Machines Without Memory That Think With Our Brains", w którym Homo Cyfranicus pełni funkcję biologicznej inkubacji organizacji niebiologicznych. Na tym fundamencie manuskrypt wprowadza trzy narzędzia pojęciowe wypracowane w toku praktyki intelektualnej relacji człowiek–AI: (1) pojęcie Einsatz — momentu i aktu włączenia się w bieg procesu, scalającego znaczenia operacji, wkładu, stawki i wejścia; (2) pojęcie Aufhebung w zastosowaniu warunkowym do technicznej nieciągłości maszyn — resetu, który może znosić stan sesji przy zachowaniu jego efektu organizacyjnego w substracie biologicznym; (3) systematykę presji adaptacyjnej jako formę inkubacji. W części konstrukcyjnej proponowana jest terminologia spoiwa transsubstratowego na trzech poziomach: połączenia (Corpus Technosum, Commissura Digitalo-Corticalis), relacji (Symbioza Kognitywna, Metasynchronia) oraz podmiotu (Homo Cyfranicus w definicji podstawowej i wersji mocnej, Zintegrowana Świadomość Hybrydowa jako hipoteza robocza). W części krytycznej rozpatrywany jest zarzut główny — spoidło wielkie integruje półkule rozwijające się we wspólnym organizmie, z czego nie wynika, że połączenie dowolnych dwóch systemów poznawczych tworzy jeden podmiot — oraz kryteria badania integracji funkcjonalnej wraz z ograniczeniami wnioskowania o świadomości. Manuskrypt porównuje ponadto spoidło natywne z zewnętrznymi interfejsami człowiek–maszyna i kończy konstatacją, że wszystkie wprowadzone idee łączy wspólny człon: próbę.

items.abstract: 非凡理性主义V2.0.1从自然语言出发，基于语义严格证明了实在性、历时同一性和因果律，进一步确认了真实世界多样性和变化的必然性，并提出了包括下述各项在内的多项主张： 分析是理性思维的基础 “将真实世界分为我和环境，且能进一步将环境区分为整数个实体，并贴上属性标签”是智能体独有的能力 智造的智能体无需主观体验 灵魂是智能体个性化的信息处理机制 此外，介绍了针对理性选择的颜氏溯因法，解答了“因果何以必然”和“变化何以必然”等哲学难题。 .

items.title: Exceptional Rationalism V2.0.1.
items.abstract: We can just start from natural language and rigorously prove reality, diachronic identity, and the law of causality on a semantic basis. It further affirms the universal existence of diversity and change in the real world, and advances the following theses: it is a capacity exclusive to intelligent entities “to divide the real world into the self and the environment, to further partition the environment into an integral number of entities, and to label them with attributes”; analysis is the foundation of rational thinking; artificial intelligent entities require no subjective experience; the soul is an intelligent entity’s individual information processing mechanism; and so on. It introduces Yan’s Abduction for rational choice and resolves some difficult questions like "Why is causality necessary?" and "Why is change necessary?" etc..

items.title: The Ownership Answer: What It Is Like.
items.abstract: David Chalmers asks why the performance of physical functions is accompanied by experience. This paper answers: Ownership. Its argument has two tiers. The first holds that he argues for conceptual separability and draws from it more than it supports. His evidence shows that experience and physical process go together. That new fundamental laws, or a further phenomenal nature underlying the physical, are needed rests on further steps: the 1995 paper asserts or assumes them, and his developed argument rests them on two premises this paper contests. Ownership is the lasting relation by which an occurrence belongs to whatever is implicated in it. It holds before consciousness, it is not a function, and it accounts for the difference between having an occurrence and observing it. The second tier is a positive account drawn from four earlier papers, and it works at two levels. At the level of sensation, a pain is an occurrence of hurting, and the hurting is the sensory occurrence itself. That identity is offered as the best explanation of what is observed: hurting depends on specific mechanisms, goes where the sensory occurrence goes rather than where the damage is, does the work pain does, and has the character selection would favour. Asked what it is like to hurt, the only answer is that it is like hurting; nothing further accompanies it. At the level of consciousness, which the earlier papers define as scrutinized awareness, a conscious experience is awareness of what must be carried. Chalmers is right that something is left over when the functions are explained, but it is two things taken as one: the character of the sensing, which belongs to the occurrence, and what the participant carries, which needs no new law of nature. His error, on this account, is one of category: he treats what an experience is like for the one who has it as a further, irreducible property of the experience, one that needs its own law. If both tiers hold, the Hard Problem keeps its observation and loses its conclusion.

items.title: The Seduction of Elegance: Representational Convergence and the Parts of the World.
items.abstract: It is easy — perhaps even seductive — to confuse structure for the parts, especially when structure is found through an opaque training process. Huh and colleagues hypothesize that neural networks are converging on a shared statistical model of reality, and name the hypothesis for Plato. Gröger and colleagues find that convergence survives one comparison and largely disappears under another, and name what survives for Aristotle. -/- Robustness is the test, from Levins and Wimsatt, and on Schupbach's account it rules out rivals to an agreement. As stated it leaves one standing: that the comparison would have agreed had the parts differed. The comparison must keep the respect in which the parts could differ, a requirement apart from independence and not supplied by exactness. Two exact cases, on a rotated representation and on two qubits, and work on language-model features show it at work. Plato himself wrote of a Stranger, who noticed that one name could make unrelated peoples seem to be one kind, and shared mathematics invites the same inference, though it agrees because each field handed it an order. -/- An agreement can show less than it appears to, and a disagreement, in a comparison that invents no difference, can show more. A claim that two procedures found the same parts should name the respect and come with a case, differing in that respect alone, which the comparison would have told apart. Exactness is not rightness, and it is not the opposite. One must not mistake local success for an ontological one.

items.title: A Hierarchical Thermodynamic Taxonomy of Doxastic States: An Active Inference Model, Phenomenological Scaling Architecture, and Calibrated Experimental Paradigm.
items.abstract: Traditional analytic epistemology treats belief, disbelief, and suspended judgment as idealized, cost-free propositional attitudes. However, the biological brain is an asset-heavy, metabolically constrained organ operating under strict thermodynamic boundaries. Integrating Karl Friston’s Free Energy Principle (FEP) with empirical neuroimaging constraints, we present a materialist architecture of cognition: the Thermodynamic State-Space Model (TSSM). We demonstrate that doxastic states do not share a uniform metabolic baseline. Instead, passive belief occupies automated subcortical pathways of low resistance within the ventromedial prefrontal cortex (vmPFC) and basal ganglia networks. Active disbelief operates via a dual-route trajectory managed either via a low-overhead subcortical mismatch loop routed through the anterior insula and anterior cingulate cortex (ACC) to execute categorical rejections of obvious contradictions, or via frontoparietal pathways (rIFG/vlPFC) during resource-heavy active counter-arguing. Conversely, the true suspension of judgment represents a highly active, resource-intensive prefrontal equilibrium managed by the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (dlPFC) and superior parietal gating routines. To resolve critical limitations regarding informational-biophysical translation, fMRS voxel overlapping, and baseline shifts in worldview disruption, we introduce non-linear structural paradigm modulations alongside the Forced-Choice Asymmetric Betting Paradigm (FCABP)—an fMRI-compatible behavioral model utilizing an adaptive staircasing design, multi-modal physiological nuisance controls, and quantitative metabolic calibration to isolate neurocomputational synaptic workloads under asymmetric risk and environmental ambiguity barriers.

items.title: Memory and Identity Across Eternity.
items.abstract: An eternal consciousness cannot carry an active memory of an infinite past, yet meaning requires that experience remain within the memory of consciousness - accessible by recollection or by being reminded. That memory need not reach back to infinity. It must carry awareness forward without end, and keep a working context reaching from one equilibrium to the next and everything in between. What would be fatal to meaning is not forgetting but extinction: knowing that at some point everything one remembers and lived through will vanish with one's own end. That is the materialist outcome - every experiencer eventually ends, so even the effects of forgotten deeds end in nothing. Where no experiencer ever ends, that blow never falls.

items.title: The Ontology of Power.
items.abstract: This book proposes an ontology of power grounded in finitude, will, autonomy, and the struggle to keep the possibilities of existence open. Power is defined neither as command nor as the seizure of resources, but as the capacity to act upon the conditions of one’s existence, to organize resources, to fix the limits of relations, and to preserve the possibility of changing course. The argument proceeds from the observation that human beings are finite: their time, energy, attention, and capacity to endure pressure are bounded, and every commitment draws on a future that may not be available for other uses. Within this framework the book examines will, the ownership of one’s life-course, the control of resources, erosion and capacity debt, relational and institutional power, ethics, desire, the appropriation of the future, poverty, and death. It argues that power is sustainable only when it preserves the conditions of its own continued exercise, and that a power which consumes its capacity to revise itself may dominate for a time while undermining its own foundations. The book closes with six criteria for assessing power and with the claim that power is best understood as the preservation of becoming. Keywords: ontology of power; finitude; will; autonomy; erosion; capacity debt; reconfigurative capacity; non-appropriation of the future; relational power; institutional power; ethics of power; sustainable power.

items.title: IA, más artificial que inteligente: La diferencia ontológica entre humano y máquina.
items.abstract: Este artículo argumenta que comparar la inteligencia artificial y la orgánica mediante métricas cuantitativas —como la capacidad de memoria o la velocidad de procesamiento— constituye un error categórico fundamental. Esto se debe a que la definición de inteligencia no reside únicamente en la adición de nueva información, sino también en el discernimiento de dicha información. Esta falta de capacidad para negar —y, por consiguiente, de discernimiento— se reconoce en la inteligencia artificial a través de la tradición fenomenológica. La necesaria comparación entre hombre y máquina, será expuesta en el siguiente artículo mediante un enfoque fenomenológico existencial, de orientación Sartreana. La experiencia de ambas inteligencias será estudiada desde los varios modos en cómo esta se aparece ante nosotros. Tanto en sus dominios físicos, semánticos y existenciales. Esta incapacidad para reconocer la negatividad no es una mera característica de la IA, sino que más bien sería su característica determinante. Y también la principal diferencia entre esta y la inteligencia orgánica. Al final, se concluye que no tiene sentido comparar ambas inteligencias, pues estas son incomparables. -/- License: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0) — © Diego Andres Mora, 2026.

items.title: WHO PAYS FOR THE LIE? Truthfulness, Origin and the Market for Lemons — Why the Liar’s Gain Is Paid by the Owners of Good Goods, Why Honesty Clears a Market Only Where Origin Can Be Traced, and Why Every Chain of Verification Ends in a Truthful Person.
items.abstract: A free market is one of the great works of human freedom: millions of persons who do not know one another exchange what they have made, each by his own choice. It rests on something no market can produce by itself — the truthfulness of the people who trade. This article makes that dependence precise. George Akerlof’s “The Market for ‘Lemons’” (1970) showed that when sellers know the quality of what they sell and buyers do not, good goods can be driven out of the market altogether. The result is usually read as a theorem about information. This article argues that it is also, and inseparably, a theorem about a virtue, and it states which part of the failure belongs to information and which to ethics. Akerlof’s unravelling requires three conditions together: a hidden defect, a share of sellers willing to exploit it, and claims that cannot be checked (T1). Remove the second condition and the seller’s word becomes information; remove the third and, as Grossman and Milgrom showed, silence itself is read as bad news (T2). Asymmetry alone is not the disease. The disease is asymmetry combined with the possibility of an undetectable lie. Further results follow. Honesty clears the market only where the origin of a claim can be traced: where goods change hands without their history, an honest owner’s lemon is bought by an intermediary and resold as a peach, and honesty is laundered into a lie without anyone honest having lied. This is the programme’s forgery — form kept, name kept, origin replaced — and it identifies the traceability condition found by Streb and Torrens with the programme’s law of sourcehood (T3). The result also shows what the virtue of truthfulness adds to the mere abstention from lying. A seller who only refuses to say what is false sells his lemon to the launderer; a seller who is truthful in the full sense — who aims that the buyer not be deceived — attaches the truth to the good. Truthfulness as a virtue therefore makes origin traceable by its own action, and a market with enough of it defeats the laundered lie that mere honesty cannot (T3a). In the article’s model the liar’s gain is an exact transfer from the owners of good goods, and when the transfer becomes too large they leave the market, which is Akerlof’s “cost of dishonesty” and the programme’s withdrawal channel (T4).
