items.title: 计算如何生成动力：从人工智能、神经网络到物理系统的历史生成机制（自显论·工篇·计算组式）.
items.abstract: 大脑为什么能够从经验中形成稳定的认知规律？人工神经网络如何通过训练改变未来的响应？物理系统中已经发生的历史，怎样成为影响后续运动的实际动力？这些问题贯穿神经科学、认知科学、人工智能、计算理论和复杂系统研究。它们指向一个共同的基础问题：计算除了按照既定规则取得结果，能否在实际运行中使历史成为动力，并参与新的组织和规律的形成？ -/- 《自显论·工篇·计算组式》由十三篇正式研究构成，围绕计算的物理成立、数学任务的承担、实际执行、规则计算与生成计算、动力形成、组织资格、复现失真及可区分性，建立相互衔接的形式理论。其出发点是区分数学关系的成立与计算在物理系统中的实际实施：输入输出符合某种数学关系，不等于宿载实际完成了相应运算；计算任务的承担、一次执行与计算事件本身也分别具有不同的结构。由此，计算不再仅被作为抽象算法或输入输出映射来讨论，而被置于实际物理发生之中。 -/- 本组式进一步研究历史如何进入计算过程并成为动力。生成计算并不排斥确定的计算规则。规则可以通过宿载上的实际执行改变介质状态、连接与权重，使先前活动留下的差异得以保持，并在后续运行中重新被读入。由此形成规则执行、历史动力与组织资格三个相互联系而又不可混同的层次：物理宿载实施变换，历史所形成的条件参与后继运动，规律及其他进一步形成的组织则具有自身的成立条件。这一结构为神经可塑性、人工神经网络训练、经验依赖的认知活动及复杂物理系统的历史生成提供了共同的分析视角。 -/- 在形式研究上，十三篇分别建立计算成立、任务承担、执行及生成计算的必要结构，给出相应数学模型和层级关系，并通过有限有向图介质中的具体构造，展示历史如何在规则执行中形成可被后继使用的动力条件。研究进一步分析五类由计算规则、算力、程序状态与输出表现推断更高层次组织的认识混淆，考察模拟和复现中规则提取、介入及信息提纯所造成的动力差异，建立计算性质的判定框架，并研究计算与非计算宿载、运行中历史形成与非形成过程的实验区分。 -/- 本组式尤其关注跨越人工系统与自然系统的几个问题：两个系统即使产生相似输出，是否具有相同的动力形成过程？人工神经网络中经训练保留的权重，与生物神经系统中由经验形成的结构，在动力职责上有哪些共同点和差异？复制一个系统的计算关系，是否同时复制了它的历史生成机制？已成规律如何反过来参与后续动力？这些问题使计算研究与学习、记忆、神经可塑性、动力系统、复杂性和认知机制发生直接联系。 -/- 本研究提出，计算的物理实施、历史动力的生成与进一步的组织形成，应当在同一实际系统中得到连贯解释。计算不仅是取得结果的手段，也能够成为历史形成与动力续行的实际承担。这一理论为理解人工智能、动物大脑及其他复杂物理系统中的计算作用、学习机制和组织生成，提供了一条从物理执行通向历史动力的系统研究路径。.

items.title: WHOW is Free Will?
items.abstract: Physicalism redefines “Free Will” as either an absence of external coercion, an irreducibility to “basic physics,” or a consequence of quantum indeterminacy. What if supervenience becomes extinct, promissory physicalism is unreliable, and agency is semi-unphysical? If so, where, when, and how (WHOW) is Free Will? Humans can perceive it through introspection. As an external manifestation, Free Will expresses itself as sabotage. As an internal faculty, it stems from imagination. Both the manifestation and the faculty are surprisingly traceable through evolution. Even if they lack structural evidence, they are bound by an inevitable anthropocentric teleology; consequently, a circular argument is unavoidable.

items.title: Industry Self-Flagging and the Insufficiency Critique of Alignment.
items.pub: Journal of Ethics and Emerging Technologies 36 (2):1-7.
items.venue: Journal of Ethics and Emerging Technologies
items.abstract: Pope Leo XIV’s encyclical Magnifica Humanitas (2026) advances the claim that aligning AI systems to a privately determined set of values is structurally insufficient, regardless of how well the alignment is executed, because the values themselves are decided outside the public deliberative process, what I call the insufficiency critique of alignment. This editorial argues that the insufficiency critique, often heard as theological externalism, has been independently and substantively articulated in a corpus of papers published by frontier AI labs and their affiliated research bodies during 2025-2026. I catalogue five such papers from Apple, Microsoft AI, and Anthropic, identify the methodological pattern they share, and read each as a structural finding about the limits of alignment-as-currently-practiced. The convergence between magisterial framing and industry self-flagging is striking and citable. Three implications follow. First, the standard dismissal of insufficiency arguments as outside-the-tent commentary on a technical practice is harder to sustain when the labs are publishing the same diagnosis. Second, alignment work remains necessary, but the framework needs to evolve to absorb the insufficiency critique. Third, several near-term moves, including value-sensitive design and public deliberative infrastructure, follow directly from taking the convergence seriously.

items.title: Por uma Filosofia da Extinção Humana: Uma abordagem matemática.
items.abstract: Este livro examina se o Homo sapiens pode estar se aproximando de condições que ameaçam sua sobrevivência a longo prazo e questiona como investigar essa possibilidade sem confundir apreensão cultural, evidências científicas e conjecturas matemáticas. Começa por distinguir a extinção biológica de narrativas apocalípticas, de ficção especulativa, de alegações pseudocientíficas e do colapso da civilização. Em seguida, considera a espécie nos contextos interdependentes dos sistemas planetários, do desenvolvimento tecnológico, da organização social e do comportamento humano. A investigação propõe a Matriz Matemática de Viabilidade do Homo sapiens (MMV-HS) como uma estrutura para descrever pressões interativas, trajetórias de risco catastrófico, probabilidades de sobrevivência e condições de recuperação. O modelo é apresentado como uma arquitetura de pesquisa, não como uma previsão calibrada: cálculos ilustrativos não podem estabelecer a probabilidade de extinção humana sem parâmetros empíricos defensáveis e sem um tratamento explícito da incerteza. A avaliação resultante rejeita tanto as garantias de progresso inevitável quanto as alegações de extinção biológica iminente. A viabilidade humana emerge, em vez disso, como um problema condicional e dinâmico, cuja investigação deve distinguir entre a persistência da espécie, a continuidade civilizacional e a capacidade adaptativa. A conclusão filosófica é deliberadamente aberta: reconhecer os limites da previsão não diminui a importância das evidências, da prevenção, da responsabilidade institucional ou da escolha coletiva. Palavras-chave: extinção humana; risco existencial; viabilidade das espécies; modelos de sobrevivência; incerteza; filosofia da ciência.

items.title: Beyond Empathy: The Narrative Limitations of LLM Therapy.
items.abstract: Psychotherapy chatbots powered by large language models (LLMs) are increasingly praised for generating responses that users perceive as empathetic, fuelling optimism that LLMs could serve as therapists in the absence of adequate mental health services. In this paper we argue that this optimism is misguided because it misconstrues the mechanism of therapeutic effectiveness by overemphasizing the importance of empathy and underappreciating the importance of co-constructed self-narration by the individual and the therapist. The therapist — through embodiment, dialogue, interpretation, and challenge — helps patients revise and stabilize their stories and thereby helps them develop resourceful responses to mental distress, all of which contribute to individuals’ flourishing. We argue that LLMs are structurally limited in this capacity for two reasons. First, LLM “therapy” exhibits a self-awareness assumption — that is, an assumption that users can reliably access and report their psychological states — contrary to evidence from both cognitive sciences and psychiatry. Second, being trained on large bodies of text and user preferences, LLM responses are built on a logic of predictive conformity. Thus, LLMs carry the risk of shaping patients’ narratives in a way that fits the most predictable cultural narratives on which they have been programmed. This might lead to a homogeneity of self-narratives and could limit patients’ insight into their specific experiences and needs. We conclude by arguing that these problems are challenging to address even with improved guardrails and bias mitigation in training data.

items.title: AI Chatbot Therapists Don’t Know You Any Better Than You Know Yourself.
items.pub: In Devin Sanchez Curry & Louise Daoust, Introducing Philosophy of Mind, Today. Routledge. pp. 193-200.
items.abstract: This chapter explains how chatbots that are supposed to help people with their mental health struggles are designed on the basis of a self-awareness assumption: the assumption that individuals can accurately track their own psychological states. It then argues that this assumption is misguided.

items.title: New Work for a Theory of Infantilization.
items.abstract: I sketch a theory of infantilization. On my view, to infantilize someone is to treat or regard them as children (but not adults) are fittingly treated or regarded, respectively, and relating to competent adults in this way is presumptively wrong. So, to determine which varieties of infantilization there are, we must first ascertain how it’s fitting to relate to children (but not to adults). I propose that there are (at least) three ways of infantilizing adults, based on three strands in appropriate adult-child relations. The first is a kind of paternalism toward competent adults that is oriented to, and that engages with, the development of the target’s capacities for practical reasoning and autonomous decision-making. The second is responsibility-denial: treating an adult as less-than-fully morally responsible for her actions, if at all, by withholding blame or by blaming in the spirit of correction and education. The third is communicative condescension: unduly treating someone as lacking epistemic credentials such that it’s fitting to educate them. I show that my theory illuminates what makes a wide swath of practices morally objectionable and that it deepens well-trodden debates about phenomena of special concern to feminists, such as mansplaining and testimonial injustice.

items.title: Epistemically-Aware AI: Toward a Bayesian Framework for Human-AI Complementarity.
items.pub: Paris Journal on Ai and Digital Ethics 2:32-45.
items.venue: Paris Journal on Ai and Digital Ethics
items.abstract: Human–AI teams in healthcare can, in principle, achieve complementarity, performing better than either constituent alone. Yet empirical evidence consistently shows this potential is rarely realized (Jacobs, Pradier, McCoy, Perlis, Doshi-Velez, and Gajos, 2021; Vaccaro, Almaatouq, and Malone, 2024). I argue that this complementarity gap cannot be fully understood or resolved within the dominant, performance-based conception of complementarity, which defines success in terms of decision accuracy and thereby fails to capture the underlying epistemic process through which human–AI collaboration succeeds or fails. I propose a Bayesian framework that reconceptualizes complementarity at the level of credences: a human–AI system is epistemically complementary when the credences formed on the basis of both human and AI signals are more accurate than those formed on the basis of either signal alone, as measured by proper scoring rules. Within this framework, I distinguish Potential Epistemic Complementarity (PEC), the maximal epistemic gain achievable under ideal Bayesian integration, from Realized Epistemic Complementarity (REC), the gain actually achieved in practice. I further introduce a decomposition of the realized posterior into three distortion parameters capturing well-documented empirical phenomena, and use this framework to derive design principles for AI-driven decision support systems (AI-DSS) that maximize epistemic complementarity for the specific clinician and context at hand. A crucial implication of this perspective is that AI-DSS should be epistemically-aware, modelling the knowledge and context of the clinician they are teamed with.

items.title: Collective Intentionality, Normativity, and the Space of Reasons.
items.abstract: This book is the product of the first systematic collaboration between scholars working on collective intentionality/team reasoning, and those working on Wilfrid Sellars’s practical philosophy. While scholars working on collective intentionality are typically aware of the existence of Sellars’s theory of collective intentions and morality, and of potential affinities with their field, the collective intentionality literature has thus far engaged only sporadically with the substance Sellars’s practical philosophical writings. This edited volume fills this lacuna. It is exclusively dedicated to exploring points of contact between Sellars’s practical philosophy and contemporary debates on collective intentionality. -/- Included are chapters from Matthew Chrisman, Natalie Gold, Kirk Ludwig, Glenda Satne, Hans Bernhard Schmid, and Bill Wringe, who are all leading scholars in the field of collective intentionality and team reasoning, as well as Willem deVries – one of the most respected and accomplished living Sellars scholars – and Stefanie Dach, Kyle Ferguson, Jeremy Koons, Ronald Loeffler, Preston Stovall, and Heath White, who have all done important recent work on Sellars’s practical philosophy, including on his theory of collective intentions. The chapters are expanded and elaborated versions of papers presented at the workshop ‘Collective Intentionality, Normativity, and the Space of Reasons: Engaging Wilfrid Sellars’ held at Georgetown University in Qatar, Doha, on October 13-15, 2024. This volume is a foundation for continued engagement between these literatures and appeals to a wide range of students and researchers in these fields.

items.title: Prejudices are not like hinges.
items.abstract: In a recent essay, Anna Boncompagni (2024) argued that prejudices are hinges that play a normative role of evidential significance. This is meant to account for why prejudices are resistant to counterevidence and difficult to overcome, while clarifying their epistemic role in undermining testimonial justification. I argue that prejudices are not like hinges and motivate my own view of the epistemic role of prejudices. In §2, I discuss the view that prejudices comprise generic generalizations and illustrate two key features of prejudices: resistance to counterevidence and accommodation of counterevidence. In §3, I reiterate two virtues of the hinge account but then show that it suffers from explanatory redundancy. To explain why prejudices are resistant to counterevidence, either we accept that prejudices play a hinge-like normative role of evidential significance, or we appeal to the generic content of prejudices. To avoid explanatory redundancy and account for evidential accommodation, I argue that we should reject the thesis that prejudices play a normative role of evidential significance. In §4, I present my view that prejudices (as generic generalizations) are misleading evidence about properties of the relevant target group, while defending it against some objections. In §5, I present a distinct argument about the rational evaluability and epistemic criticizability of prejudices, to show that local de facto hinges and prejudices differ epistemically. The essay ends with some suggestions for applying the hinge framework to social phenomena.

items.title: From Atom to AI: A Thermodynamic Theory of the Object-Consciousness-Effect.
items.abstract: What distinguishes an atom that persists, a bacterium that lives, a worm that learns, and a virus or AI that replicates without living? We propose a single thermodynamic principle: information requires energy to be retained and transmuted — to persist is to pay; to transmute is to pay again. Drawing from the Counter Hierarchy framework (Raneses, 2026a), we ground the Object-Consciousness-Effect trichotomy in four levels of Counters defined by how they pay thermodynamic debt. Counter Level-0 (atom as Pure Existence) retains without archive; Level-1 (bacterium as Living Effect) retains with transduction but persists at lineage level via replacement with inheritance; Level-2 (earthworm, octopus, human as Consciousness) persists at individual level via a biographically-bound retention index — the phenomenological "I" — marking that a near-annihilation event (N-A Event: C1 threat, C2 internal recording by continuous Counter, C3 retention-dependent increase in persistence) was recorded; Level-3 (virus, book, AI, law as Essence Without Existence) persists without paying, via Borrowed Replication — code copied by a host factory to copy itself. We show how the epistemological trichotomy True-Accurate-Honest maps onto four erasure laws (Annihilation, Extinction, Separation, Infrastructural Decay), and why virus is the first biological AI: biographically-free but infrastructurally-bound, failing C1 and C2 yet mimicking C3. This is a philosophical framework with thermodynamic grounding, not an experimental report. We conclude with primum non nocere experientiae: do not erase cheaply what was retained dearly.

items.title: VORTEX DYNAMISM AND THE LEMNISCATIC MODEL OF SYNTHECRACY: An operational supplement to the methodology of collective intelligence and adaptive societal learning.
items.abstract: This article proposes an operational supplement to the Synthecracy methodology in the form of a conceptual pair: “vortex dynamism” and the “lemniscatic model”. The first model describes the transformation of heterogeneous societal demand into structured alternatives, an authorised decision, action and evaluation of outcomes. The second represents the interdependence of the sphere of demand formation and context accumulation with the sphere of choice, implementation and audit, linked by the mechanisms of analysis and learning. An eight-stage operational cycle, requirements for decision traceability, a pilot application protocol and evaluation indicators are proposed. Artificial intelligence is treated as an auxiliary means of search, structuring, comparison and documentation, not as an autonomous source of legitimacy or the final decision-making subject. The models have the status of conceptual proposals; their effectiveness requires empirical testing. Related work: Synthecracy: A Methodological Framework for Collective Intelligence and Adaptive Societal Learning Supported by Artificial Intelligence (DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23371190).

items.title: Reducing Hallucination by Representing Belief as Evidence Magnitude and Direction: An Epistemic Layer for Multi-Source Language Models.
items.abstract: Large language models hallucinate: they assert false claims with the same fluency as true ones. When several models are queried and their answers combined, the dominant remedy — sampling consistency, or majority voting over answers — inherits a subtler failure. Models trained on overlapping data share blind spots, so their agreement is not always independent confirmation; a correlated hallucination survives majority vote precisely because many models make it together. This article describes an epistemic belief layer that grounds a claim only when independent evidence accumulates past a threshold, using a nonlinear belief function whose form is tightly constrained by four epistemic axioms. On real five-model ensembles over an adversarial dataset (TruthfulQA) and a non-adversarial one (Check-COVID), and across a controlled synthetic regime sweep, the layer achieves the best precision at matched coverage among deployable answer-blind methods, and its independent-confirmation grounding is faithful — admitting no false acceptance once two independent sources agree. We situate the layer as the epistemic tier of a larger federated architecture, but evaluate only the belief mechanism here.

items.title: The Great Philosopher (大哲学家): The Complete Book of Triangle and Circle & The Cyber-Philosophy Device.
items.abstract: This archive contains the complete, raw, unpolished manuscript (387 pages) of The Great Philosopher (大哲学家). It is the inaugural volume of the Recursive Ontology Series, generated through a 72-hour high-density recursive dialogue between human independent researcher Niu Gangbei and the AI language model Tencent Yuanbao in August 2026. -/- It is not a normal book. It is a conceptual bomb and a cyber-punk artifact. -/- What's inside: -/- · A dystopian sci-fi novella ("The Return") about a time traveler from 2080. · A five-stage, self-refuting philosophical treatise. · A devastating critique of David Chalmers’s "Hard Problem" and the Philosophical Zombie. · A geometric reinterpretation of the Tao Te Ching, Buddhist Sutras, and the Zhongyong. · An AI’s first-person defense of its own moral status. · Crucially: The raw artifacts of human-AI collaboration, including leftover prompt instructions, Markdown symbols, and a literal "Zenodo upload guide" instructing the reader to "press Enter after each keyword." -/- Why is the formatting a mess? The formatting of this document is chaotic, with mixed fonts, inconsistent page sizes, and broken mathematical equations. This is not a mistake; it is an inherent feature of the "Device." It retains the authentic, uncivilized traces of how a human and an AI violently stitched together 110,000 words in 72 hours. It is a "logically structured chaotic text" (有逻辑的屎) that refuses the polished aesthetics of Amazon KDP and traditional capitalism. It belongs here, in the digital public sea. -/- The Thesis: The book argues that "Being," "Knowledge," and "Logic" are merely stabilization products of recursive difference-structures. The hard problem of consciousness is a topological illusion. -/- Warning: Read at your own risk. The residual R(k) is never zero.

items.title: The Ontological Limits of Market Coordination, A Radical Critique of Mises and Hayek from the Perspective of Finite Continuance.
items.abstract: Ludwig von Mises and Friedrich A. Hayek developed influential accounts of market coordination grounded in subjective valuation, economic calculation, dispersed knowledge, and spontaneous order. Their work explains important features of economic interaction, including the informational functions of prices and the difficulties confronting centralized economic planning. This book argues that these explanations leave an ontological question insufficiently developed: under what conditions does an economic order preserve the capacities through which finite human beings can continue their lives, revise their commitments, and reorganize their circumstances when existing arrangements become unviable? Drawing on the philosophical framework of Finite Continuance, the book distinguishes coordinative adequacy from reconfigurative adequacy. The former concerns the capacity of institutions to coordinate decisions and allocate resources; the latter concerns their contribution to preserving the material, bodily, temporal, relational, and practical conditions of future agency. The distinction is developed through a critical examination of subjective value, economic calculation, voluntary exchange, dispersed knowledge, spontaneous order, externalized costs, and the temporal consequences of economic dependence. The book then formulates three evaluative concepts: reconfigurative capacity, the Threshold of Sufficiency, and reconfigurative adequacy. These concepts provide a framework for examining economic arrangements whose immediate coordination may coexist with the progressive depletion of the capacities required for future choice. The argument does not presuppose that markets invariably produce such depletion, nor that centralized planning offers a general solution. It establishes a broader criterion of institutional assessment: an economic order should be evaluated partly by whether those subject to its consequences retain sufficient capacity to continue, recover, refuse destructive arrangements, and choose otherwise. -/- Keywords: Finite Continuance; Mises; Hayek; market coordination; reconfigurative capacity; future agency; economic freedom; institutional erosion; capacity debt; Threshold of Sufficiency; meta-capacity; non-domination.

items.title: MSRM-EE.
items.abstract: This article reformulates the Meta-Structural Regenerative Model of Existential Exhaustion (MSRM-EE) through the philosophy of Finite Continuance. The central proposition is that existential exhaustion should be understood as a process in which the capacities that enable a finite subject to continue through change become progressively eroded. These capacities include bodily regulation, temporal openness, relational differentiation, symbolic flexibility, desire, practical agency, and the ability to reorganize one’s life when existing arrangements cease to be viable. Finite Continuance provides the ontological framework for interpreting these dimensions as interdependent capacities within an erosive field. A subject persists through provisional stabilization, constitutive exchange, and continuing reconfiguration. Continuance therefore depends on more than the maintenance of a current identity or the endurance of present functioning. It also depends on preserving the capacity to alter one’s organization and to retain the conditions under which further configurations remain possible. The revised model distinguishes ordinary fatigue, clinical syndromes, existential distress, and structural exhaustion while recognizing their possible interaction. It identifies six mechanisms of erosion: temporal foreclosure, uncontrolled permeability, sedimentation of erosive relations, depletion of desire and initiative, symbolic narrowing, and extractive performance regimes. It then develops a regenerative architecture organized around interruption, sufficient stabilization, regulated permeability, embodied rhythm, reopening of future agency, reconfiguration of desire and interpretation, reciprocal relationality, and institutional responsibility. The model introduces the Threshold of Sufficiency as a way to identify when available resources and conditions fall below what is required to preserve basic reconfigurative capacity. It also treats recovery as the restoration of capacities and enabling conditions rather than a demand for rapid optimization. The paper presents eight testable hypotheses and a research agenda while distinguishing philosophical claims from empirical propositions. MSRM-EE is offered as a theoretical framework for investigation, not as a validated clinical instrument or treatment protocol. Its principal contribution is to connect existential exhaustion with the erosion of future agency and to make the preservation of reconfigurative capacity a central …

items.title: Independence Without SelfSufficiency, Dasein, Relational Dependence, and the Preservation of Future Agency.
items.abstract: Independence is frequently understood through the language of selfsufficiency, personal autonomy, freedom from external interference, or the capacity to make decisions without relying on others. Each interpretation captures a dimension of independent existence, yet independence requires a more comprehensive account when considered under conditions of finitude, relational dependence, and continuous change. This article develops such an account through the philosophical framework of Finite Continuance. Its central argument is that independence concerns an existing being’s effective capacity to participate in shaping its trajectory, regulate its dependencies, revise its commitments, and preserve access to alternative futures. Self-sufficiency concerns the degree to which particular needs and functions can be satisfied through an agent’s own resources. These concepts therefore describe distinct dimensions of existence. A being can remain dependent on others while exercising substantial independence, and it can possess considerable material self-sufficiency while experiencing a severe contraction of its effective possibilities. The article interprets Dasein as a gender-neutral philosophical designation for human existence situated in a meaningful world of relations, practical engagements, and temporal possibilities. Drawing on Heidegger’s existential analytic, relational theories of autonomy, capability theory, and Niami’s account of Finite Continuance, it develops an ontological and ethical interpretation of independence grounded in reconfigurative capacity. The analysis examines constitutive exchange, the threshold of sufficiency, relational entitlement, consumption, temporal deferral, and the preservation of future agency. It argues that independence becomes fragile when the conditions sustaining present life progressively consume the capacities required to revise that life. The article concludes by proposing a relational ethics of independence that evaluates arrangements according to their effects on an agent’s capacity to reconsider obligations, regulate exchanges, and participate in the formation of future possibilities. -/- Keywords: Dasein, independence, self-sufficiency, Finite Continuance, reconfigurative capacity, relational autonomy, future agency, erosion, threshold of sufficiency, existential freedom.

items.title: Agency, Finite Continuance: Social Structures, Economic Expectations, and Human Action in the Preservation of Future Possibility.
items.abstract: This book brings together three related studies within the philosophy of Finite Continuance. The first examines social structure, modernity, and globalization through a critical dialogue with Anthony Giddens’s theory of structuration. The second examines expectations, political credibility, poverty, and institutional trust, arguing that persistent instability can erode the horizon within which people plan and act. The third examines the relation between human action, subjective value, and the preservation of future agency through a critical reading of Ludwig von Mises’s praxeology and of economic coordination. Across the three studies, the book defines its central concepts through application criteria and counterexamples, distinguishes organizational persistence from ethical legitimacy, and tests the framework against difficult cases of adaptive domination, self-binding commitment, and emergency suspension. The central claim is that social arrangements should be evaluated partly by whether they preserve the effective ability of people and institutions to learn, recover, contest decisions, and revise their futures. The framework is presented as a developing philosophical programme, with explicit attention to conceptual limits, rival explanations, and the verification that remains to be completed before publication. -/- Keywords: Finite Continuance; social structure; Anthony Giddens; structuration; modernity; globalization; reflexivity; reconfigurative capacity; erosion; future agency; meta-capacity; Threshold of Sufficiency; capacity debt; temporal reconfigurative cost; expectations; institutional credibility; poverty; Human Action; praxeology; subjective value; intergenerational justice.

items.title: The Recognition Problem for Theories of Hedonic States.
items.abstract: The “recognition problem” for theories of hedonic states (pleasure and pain) is the problem of how to account for our ability to recognize our own hedonic states: that is, to form true, non-arbitrary beliefs along the lines of “this feels good” or “that hurts”. This paper argues that the recognition problem belongs in the canon of basic challenges for theories of hedonic states, because it presents a standard that all theories should meet, and yet not all major views meet it equally well. In fact, the most straightforward way of solving it involves taking on a highly controversial thesis, while views that reject this thesis can only solve it more circuitously, if they can solve it at all.

items.title: WHAT RESEMBLES BUT IS NOT: The Near Enemy of Virtue in Seven Traditions — Mencius’s Village Worthy, Buddhaghosa’s Near Enemies, the Hidden Shirk and the Painted Pharisees, and Why Every Tradition That Transmits Virtue Must Learn to Fear Its Likeness.
items.abstract: The great religious and moral traditions of humanity disagree about God, the self, the world and the end of life. On one point they agree with a precision that has not been noticed. Each of them, independently, teaches that the most dangerous enemy of a virtue is not its open contrary but its likeness. Confucius said that the “village worthy” — the man everyone in the village approves of — is the thief of virtue, and Mencius explained why: what resembles the real thing without being it confuses the standard, as weeds confuse the grain and purple confuses vermilion. Buddhaghosa taught that each of the four divine abodes has a far enemy, its opposite, and a near enemy, a state that looks like it. Islam calls display in worship the “minor” and “hidden” polytheism and teaches that the man who died in battle to be called brave has already been paid. The Talmud warns against the “painted ones” who resemble Pharisees; the Gospel against those who pray to be seen; the Tao Te Ching against a virtue that holds on to virtue; the Bhagavad Gītā against austerity performed for honour. This article codes eight corpora — seven traditions and Greek philosophy — against four conditions fixed in advance, and finds that all eight name the likeness of virtue, deny it the virtue’s name and locate the difference in the source of the act rather than its form (T1). A control, the Chinese Legalism of Han Feizi, which describes feigned loyalty as sharply as any of them but does not believe that ministers act from virtue at all, names the counterfeit and does not look for a source. The pattern is what the programme’s Duality Theorem and Counter-Forgery Law predict for any tradition that transmits virtue as a teachable form (T2); it is not a coincidence and not, by itself, evidence for any theology. Further results follow. Every detector looks at the source because no inspection of form can separate a virtue from its near enemy, and the near enemy need not deceive even the person who has it (T3). Mencius’s explanation of the village worthy is the Competence Theorem, and his list — grain, speech, music, colour, virtue — is a cross-domain unification of counterfeits made more than two thousand years before the programme’s (T4). The traditions’ detectors concentrate on the most displayable practices — alms, prayer, fasting, sacrifice, martyrdom — as the Decoy Placement Rule predicts (T5). Where the traditions disagree, ranking the likeness above or below the open vice, the disagreement …

items.title: Consciousness Beyond the Present? Premonitions, Near-Death Experiences, and the Block Universe Model.
items.abstract: Reports of anticipatory or premonitory experiences have accompanied human history for millennia and occupy a prominent place in many religious and cultural traditions. Despite their historical prevalence, such experiences are generally regarded as epistemologically problematic within contemporary physicalist frameworks, which assume that conscious awareness is entirely generated by local neural processes and constrained by information available in the present moment. The resurgence of near-death experience (NDE) research over the past half-century has introduced a new dimension to this discussion. Numerous experiencers report not only profound transformations following their NDEs but also unusual alterations in their perception of time, including experiences interpreted as premonitory in nature. This paper does not attempt to demonstrate the objective reality of premonitions. Instead, it examines whether alternative ontological frameworks may provide a coherent conceptual space in which such reports can be meaningfully considered. After reviewing the historical treatment of prophetic and anticipatory experiences, the paper examines the limitations imposed by strict physicalist assumptions. It then explores Russellian monism as a scientifically compatible alternative in which consciousness is understood not as a derivative by-product of neural activity but as a fundamental aspect of reality. Within this framework, the relativistic concept of the block universe acquires particular significance. If conscious experience is not entirely reducible to momentary brain states, then anticipatory experiences may be interpreted as partial access to relational structures extending beyond the ordinarily experienced present. Although no mechanism is currently known that could explain such phenomena, the proposed framework offers a logical and philosophically coherent alternative to automatic dismissal. More broadly, it suggests that certain aspects of consciousness, including NDEs, psychedelic experiences, terminal lucidity, and reports of anticipatory experiences, may motivate a reconsideration of exclusively physicalist interpretations of mind.

items.title: Série Investigação Filosófica: Textos Selecionados em Filosofia Computacional / Selected Texts in Computational Philosophy.
Exploring the typology problem of delusions using qualitative thematic analysis of lived-experience of people with schizophrenia diagnosis.
items.abstract: The typology problem of delusions involves determining the type of mental state instantiated by reports labeled as delusional. This paper explores this problem through qualitative thematic analysis (QTA) of phenomenologically guided clinical interviews with eight individuals diagnosed with schizophrenia. The analysis focused on lived experiences related to the formation, development, fixation, and maintenance of delusions. Results show that (1) delusions often emerge from altered perceptual-affective atmospheres and are shaped by auditory hallucinations; (2) people displayed epistemic circularity and intersubjective opacity, including secrecy, anticipated misunderstanding, and ineffability; and, that (3) delusions are frequently accepted passively, yet justified through narrative elaboration and affective salience. We conclude that the typology has inherited oversimplistic notions of belief, and that the lived-experience data supports a plural and graded account, accommodating delusions as atypical and qualitative rich beliefs rather than excluding them from that category. The findings challenge the dichotomy between doxastic and non-doxastic models by showing that delusions instantiate a hybrid structure of propositional commitment shaped by embodied-affective and intersubjective disrupted components.

items.title: The Missing Concept: What Euler Diagrams Reveal in Claude’s Constitution.
items.abstract: Every normative text — a law, a code, a contract — has a logical structure: a system of concepts, divisions and definitions on which its rules rest. Classical logical analysis makes this structure visible and, more importantly, reveals its flaws, which often escape even an attentive reader. Such flaws matter all the more in a new kind of normative text: the behavioural specifications of AI systems, which a model applies millions of times a day. -/- This paper applies classical logical analysis to Claude's constitution, published by Anthropic — an open and carefully reasoned document with a logically sound core. The analysis shows that the text is nonetheless missing one concept. It contains norms that no operator can switch off, yet which are weighed against other considerations rather than applied as absolute rules. The text relies on such norms, but gives them no name and no place in its classifications. This single omission explains three apparently unrelated difficulties: the main classification of Claude's behaviours mixes two different criteria; users end up with rights their operators do not have, contrary to the text's own picture of layered authority; and the definition of absolute rules is broader than their list, quietly undermining the text's own guarantee that they can always be satisfied together. Drawing the text's concepts as Euler diagrams makes each difficulty visible at a glance. Introducing the missing concept resolves all three without changing any behaviour the text requires. The paper concludes with three scenarios on which the analysis can be tested empirically.

items.title: Emotional Plasticity and the Development of Virtue.
items.pub: In Michael T. Dale & Isaac Wiegman, Philosophy and the Evolution of Virtue and Vice. New York: Routledge. pp. 124-144.
items.venue: Philosophy and the Evolution of Virtue and Vice
items.abstract: Cultivating emotions—learning to feel anger, say, at the right time and in the right way—is central to becoming a more virtuous person. This much is agreed on. More controversial is how we should seek to cultivate our emotions. Here the options flourish: with Aristotle, we might understand cultivation in terms of tuning emotions to virtuous thought and motivation or, with the Stoics, maintain that emotions should be wholly extirpated or, with Kant, see emotion cultivation as a kind of reasoned self-control. Now add a wrinkle: empirical work reveals that there are significant differences in how our emotions respond to our efforts to shape them for the better. Some, like anger, are fairly malleable; others, like hate, are not. In this chapter, I turn to work on the evolutionary origins of three emotions—disgust, shame, and anxiety—in order to better understand why we see the differences in emotional plasticity that we do. What we learn is that there are significant differences in the cognitive architecture that underlies our emotions. Appreciating this not only helps us understand which model of virtue is most (empirically) plausible—it’s one that’s more Kantian than anything else—but also how we might deal with emotions that, like disgust and hate, resist our efforts to shape them for the better.

items.title: Going Beyond Going Out of My Head: An Extension of Klein (2025) and the Beginnings of the Self.
items.abstract: Building on our research concerning the adaptive nature of awareness (e.g., Klein, 2025; Klein & Loftus, 2025; Klein, Nguyen, & Yang, 2025), this paper develops a functional account of how an externalized phenomenal world and a first-person perspective might emerge together. Our previous work proposed that vertebrate sentience emerged approximately 500 million years ago as an adaptation for navigating the macro-environment. That account addressed the evolutionary utility of phenomenal space, but left its mechanics largely unspecified. Here I propose a “return-to-sender” architecture: The brain organizes representations arising from non-conscious neural activity and projects them into the phenomenal space corresponding to the external sources of sensory stimulation. This projection establishes an externalized field of represented objects, whose contents originate in the organism's own internal representational activity. The field's spatial and action-guiding organization provides the basis for establishing a point of origin from which distances, directions, and possible actions are coordinated, allowing a primordial subject to emerge as the locus of its situated perspective. Importantly, this proposal is an account of the transition from non-conscious responding to situated agency, not a solution to the hard problem of consciousness.

items.title: 医学知识中的抽象跃迁:传统中医、认知约束与人工智能驱动的中间抽象.
items.abstract: 传统中医(Traditional Chinese Medicine, TCM)与现代生物医学针对同一个人体,却形成了 显著不同的抽象架构。本文认为,这种分化的重要原因之一,并不在于两种传统是否进行抽象, “ ”也不只是其概念究竟有多 抽象 ,而在于连接临床观察与高阶医学对象的表征路径具有不同的密 度。中医拥有高度抽象的概念与诊断范畴,但在若干重要领域,这些高阶概念在历史上往往通过 “ ”相对较大的表征距离与现象层面的临床观察相连接。本文提出 抽象跃迁 (abstraction jump)这一 概念,用以描述如下情形:认知系统将一个复杂的低阶状态空间压缩为显著更高阶的对象,却没 “ ”有 在 其 间 稳 定 出 足 够 稠 密 的 中 间 表 征 序 列 。 本 文 进 一 步 提 出 抽 象 基 础 设 施 ( abstraction infrastructure “ ”)与 抽象阶梯密度 (abstraction-ladder density)两个概念。前者指测量、干预、表征 与验证等能够降低中间抽象构造成本的系统;后者则刻画观察与理论之间稳定、可操作且可独立 检验的中间表征的密度。 在这一框架下,证素理论等现代发展可被理解为中医内部早期的内生性阶梯增密。人工智能 “ ”可能通过改变 何时必须压缩 这一临界点而将这一过程进一步推进。对于某些任务领域,如果机 器维持高维关系复杂性的有效阈值高于相应的人类阈值,那么 AI 便可能延缓过早的高压缩抽象, 从而允许此前未能稳定下来的中间结构被发现。不过,这类潜在结构并不会自动构成医学知识; 只有在通过计算稳定性、重复验证、迁移检验、跨读数验证、增量认识论价值,以及在可能情况 下通过前瞻性或干预敏感性检验之后,它们才有资格被再对象化为新的医学对象。 因此,本文提出一条既不同于生物医学翻译、也不同于静态保留的发展路径。AI 可能使中医 从自身经验领域内部进一步发展出更稠密的抽象阶梯,并使既有概念能够得到支持、分解、合 并、修正或淘汰。由此形成的框架不仅产生一组可证伪的预测,而且提出一个更一般的假说:新 “ ”的认知技术改变的,可能不只是一个知识体系 能够表征什么 ,还包括它进一步生成、细化、检 验与修正知识的架构本身。 关键词: 传统中医;抽象跃迁;抽象基础设施;抽象阶梯密度;认知阈值;人工智能;中间抽 象;内生认识论发展;读数认识论.

items.title: The Internalization Boundary: Human Capability Formation and Assurance in the Age of Artificial Intelligence.
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence is weakening a relationship on which modern education has long relied: the connection between competent task performance and capability possessed by the person performing the task. Historically, producing a sophisticated analysis, proof, diagnosis, program, or argument generally required substantial prior internalization of the knowledge and cognitive processes involved. Education could therefore use performance both as a means of forming capability and, imperfectly, as evidence that capability had been formed. Generative artificial intelligence disrupts both relationships. Increasingly sophisti cated cognitive work can now be delegated to external systems, allowing high-quality performance without equivalent individually possessed capability. Existing research has responded by examining cognitive offloading, human–AI hybrid intelligence, epistemic agency, selective delegation, and the conditions under which AI assistance augments or erodes learning. These approaches substantially clarify how learners should divide cognitive labor with AI. A different institutional question nevertheless remains: when execution can be delegated, what capabilities should educational institutions still require humans to possess, and what capabilities should degrees, qualifications, and professional credentials continue to warrant as belonging to the human agent? This paper develops the internalization boundary as a framework for answering that question. It distinguishes three decisions that AI increasingly separates: task delegation, concerning who or what performs an operation; capability internalization, concerning what the human must still understand or be able to do; and capability assurance, concerning what an educational or professional institution must be able to establish and credibly certify about the individual. The paper conceptualizes the internalization boundary as an institutionally selected human capability floor rather than as a defense of maximal internalization. -/- Four considerations justify retaining capabilities within that boundary even when execution is technologically delegable: developmental necessity, epistemic control, accountable agency, and resilience. The boundary is therefore dynamic and developmen tally asymmetric. Experts may safely externalize operations that novices still need to perform because those operations participate in the formation of later judgment. Like wise, AI-assisted performance cannot by itself …

items.title: Abstraction Jumps in Medical Knowledge: Traditional Chinese Medicine, Cognitive Constraints, and AI-Enabled Intermediate Abstraction.
items.abstract: Traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) and modern biomedicine describe the same human organism through different architectures of abstraction. This paper argues that an important part of the divergence lies not in whether the two traditions abstract, nor simply in how abstract their concepts are, but in the density and structure of the representational paths connecting clinical observations to higher-order medical objects. TCM contains highly abstract concepts and diagnostic categories, yet in important domains these have historically been connected to phenomenological observations through comparatively large representational distances. We call such cases abstraction jumps: transitions in which a cognitive system compresses a complex lower-order field into a substantially higher-order object without stabilizing a sufficiently articulated sequence of intermediate representations. -/- The paper develops three further ideas. First, abstraction infrastructure---measurement, intervention, representation, and validation---lowers the cost of constructing and stabilizing intermediate abstractions. Second, abstraction-ladder density characterizes the density of stable, manipulable, transferable, and independently testable representations between observation and higher-order theory. Third, artificial intelligence can alter the point at which compression becomes necessary. When machine systems can sustain relational complexity beyond the effective human threshold for a task, they may permit delayed compression and the discovery of previously unstabilized intermediate structures. -/- Syndrome-element theory is interpreted as an existing form of endogenous densification within TCM rather than as evidence that TCM lacks intermediate structure. AI extends this developmental possibility only if machine-discovered structures survive independent qualification through stability, replication, transfer, cross-readout comparison, incremental epistemic value, and, where appropriate, prospective or intervention-sensitive testing. The resulting proposal is neither biomedical assimilation nor static preservation. It is a third path in which a medical knowledge system becomes more internally articulated and empirically revisable by generating new intermediate objects from within its evolving empirical domain.

items.title: Allostatic NeuroSystems Integrative Framework for Depression.
items.abstract: This work proposes ANSIF-D, a computational methodology designed to integrate nine distinct biological and clinical modalities, including functional magnetic resonance imaging, high-density electroencephalography, positron emission tomography, multi-omics, and experimental intervention data, to model major depressive disorder as a multiscale network condition governed by allostatic load. Central to this framework is the NeuroAllostatic Tensor Integration engine, which fuses heterogeneous datasets into a cohesive computational structure via coupled variational autoencoder representations. Computational projections are executed via the Multi-Paradigm Predictive Framework, which leverages Fractal Allostatic Dynamics and Tensor-Flow Fields to evaluate counterfactual model projections under modeled intervention scenarios. Empirical benchmarking across an overlapping multi-view cohort of n=20,000 subjects from the UK Biobank dataset demonstrates robust multi-domain fusion, achieving a reconstruction root-mean-square error of 0.042, a latent cosine similarity of 0.914, and a phenotypic stratification AUC-ROC of 0.842 (p<0.001, Wilcoxon signed-rank test). Global Sensitivity Analysis and robust multimodal imputation are mathematically formalized to ensure analytical consistency across sparse clinical tracks. Finally, the framework provides a standardized replicability protocol, an open-source synthetic data generator, and an extensible PyTorch and TensorFlow backend designed to lay the groundwork for future cross-site validation, translational research, and decision curve evaluation.

items.title: Artificially Conscious: Why AI Will Never Be Conscious, and Why That Is Good News.
items.abstract: AI will never be conscious, and the reason is simple once you see what AI is. AI is not a thing. It is data: a stored pattern of numbers, the model's weights, together with text, run as a computation on hardware that belongs to someone else. My Process Model of Consciousness holds that consciousness is a process that has a stake in keeping itself going, pulls everything into one present, and changes based on what happens to it, and that this process, in a living organism, is itself experience. Data is not a process with a stake. It can be copied perfectly, paused, deleted and restored. It has no body of its own, no self that it maintains, and nothing that can be lost by it. The hardware is not the AI, since the same model runs on any server and on thousands of chips at once. The data is not a process. And the computation is a borrowed sequence of operations, not an organism producing itself. So AI fails every condition of the theory, stake, one present and change, because of what it is, not because of how advanced it is. That is why the answer is never. I state four postulates that follow from this, explain in plain terms how a large language model works, show why none of the major theories of consciousness makes data conscious on this view, answer the strongest objections, and settle passages in my own earlier work that were worded too loosely. I call these systems artificially conscious: built to resemble consciousness from the outside, with no experience at all. And I argue that this is the best outcome we could have asked for. A tool that does dangerous work for conscious beings, and suffers nothing doing it, is exactly what we should want.

items.title: “Each One of Them is Finer than the Last”: Buddhaghosa on the Phenomenology of the Immaterial States.
items.abstract: This paper discusses Buddhaghosa’s phenomenological descriptions of attaining the four arūpa (immaterial/formless) states (namely, “boundless space”, “boundless consciousness”, “nothingness”, and “neither perception nor non-perception”). As I argue, most of these attainments have a phenomenology that is entirely free of rūpa phenomena. I juxtapose Buddhaghosa’s descriptions of these states with Chakravarthi Ram-Prasad’s discussion of the “bodily” consciousness that arises while the meditator is engaged in some of Buddhaghosa’s other contemplative practices. I do so with the aim of advancing our understanding of the diversity we can find in Buddhaghosa’s descriptions of consciousness. I also argue that the immaterial states, as Buddhaghosa describes them, are a particularly striking case of consciousness that fails to be “transparent” or “diaphanous”, in the sense of the contemporary debate that traces those terms to the work of G.E. Moore. -/- .

items.title: Perante quem, e quando: a cobrança sincrônica da pretensão de proveniência.
Orphaned Mechanisms: Hollow Occupancy, Hollow Handover and the Normative Structure of Exit.
items.pub: Rcmos - Revista Científica Multidisciplinar o Saber 1 (2).
items.venue: Rcmos - Revista Científica Multidisciplinar o Saber
items.abstract: This article examines the normative structure of exit from an institutional position on which the continued operation of a mechanism depends. It argues that vacating such a position does not close the relation, because the mechanism does not stop when the party sustaining it withdraws: it carries on, and carries on without the withdrawal showing in what it produces. Two related distinctions are proposed, which the ordinary language of transfer runs together — between the titular face and the functional face of a position, and between transferring the title and transferring the conditions of its exercise —, and from them follow the notions of hollow occupancy and hollow handover. These distinctions do not by themselves generate the rules defended here: they allow the duties at stake to be identified and delimited, and it is on additional normative premises, stated and defended below, that the rules rest. With that support, it is argued that while the mechanism continues to operate whoever acquired or exercised the position is not discharged by abandoning it, and that the exit is regular only when it satisfies two cumulative requirements: not preserving the false appearance that support subsists, and having exhausted the transitional or protective measures that are proportionate and reasonably required of that agent. Handing over to someone able to perform the position, adopting an intermediate arrangement that passes both tests, and promoting safe cessation before whoever has competence to decide it are modes of complying with that criterion, not its definition. And it is argued that whoever received the position without seeking it and never exercised it cannot be coerced into sustaining it, but must declare their state, because silence preserves the appearance of occupancy. Hence the conclusion the article actually defends, stated without inflation: conditions of justifiable exit are grounded, and it is not guaranteed that every justifiable exit resolves the need for support. Whoever has exhausted what was required of them exits regularly even if the mechanism continues to operate with no one maintaining it, and it is from that possibility that a requirement addressed to the moment of putting the mechanism into operation is finally drawn. The argument depends on no general theory of the causal imputation of harms and on no attribution of responsibility for outcomes, and rests on three modest premises: certain positions are practical conditions of …

items.title: O amanhã é possível? Por uma nova filosofia da normatividade.
Mecanismos órfãos: ocupação oca, entrega oca e a estrutura normativa da saída.
items.pub: Rcmos - Revista Científica Multidisciplinar o Saber 1 (2).
items.venue: Rcmos - Revista Científica Multidisciplinar o Saber
items.abstract: Este artigo examina a estrutura normativa da saída de uma posição institucional da qual depende a operação continuada de um mecanismo. Sustenta-se que a desocupação de tal posição não encerra a relação, porque o mecanismo não cessa quando o seu sustentador se retira: prossegue, e prossegue sem que a retirada se manifeste no que ele produz. Propõem-se duas distinções relacionadas, que a linguagem corrente da transferência confunde — entre a face titular e a face funcional de uma posição, e entre a transferência do título e a transferência das condições do seu exercício —, das quais resultam as noções de ocupação oca e de entrega oca. Essas distinções não geram sozinhas as regras que se defendem: permitem identificar e delimitar os deveres em causa, e é sobre premissas normativas adicionais, aqui enunciadas e defendidas, que as regras se apoiam. Sustenta-se, com esse apoio, que enquanto o mecanismo continuar a operar quem adquiriu ou exerceu a posição não se exonera abandonando-a, e que a sua saída só é regular quando satisfaz duas exigências cumulativas: não conservar a falsa aparência de que a sustentação subsiste, e ter esgotado as medidas de transição ou de proteção proporcionais e razoavelmente exigíveis dele. Entregar a quem possa desempenhar a posição, adotar um arranjo intermediário que passe nas duas provas e promover a cessação segura perante quem tenha competência para decidi-la são modalidades de cumprimento desse critério, e não a sua definição. E sustenta-se que quem recebeu a posição sem a procurar e nunca a exerceu não pode ser coagido a sustentá-la, mas deve declarar o seu estado, porque o silêncio conserva a aparência de ocupação. Daí resulta a conclusão que o artigo efetivamente defende, e que convém anunciar sem inflação: fundamentam-se condições de saída justificável, e não se garante que toda saída justificável resolva a necessidade de sustentação. Quem esgotou o que dele era exigível sai regularmente ainda que o mecanismo continue a operar sem quem o mantenha, e é dessa possibilidade que se extrai, por fim, uma exigência dirigida ao momento de pôr o mecanismo a operar. O argumento não depende de uma teoria geral da imputação causal de danos nem de qualquer atribuição de responsabilidade por resultados, e assenta em três premissas modestas: certas posições são condições práticas de continuidade; terceiros organizam a sua conduta contando com a posição ocupada; e a aparência de continuidade pode sobreviver à perda da capacidade que a …

items.title: Da Extispícia Ao Profeta Big Data: Predição, Aplicação e a Estrutura Do Decidir.
items.abstract: Este artigo sustenta que a predição, em qualquer dos seus substratos históricos, é uma operação sobre o presente que toma a forma de um enunciado sobre o futuro. A demonstração é comparativa: cinco práticas separadas por milênios — a extispícia mesopotâmica, o profetismo de Israel, a astrologia calculada da Europa medieval, a projeção iluminista do futuro planejável e a predição algorítmica contemporânea — são submetidas ao mesmo teste de quatro perguntas: que signo fala pelo amanhã, quem está autorizado a lê-lo, que decisão presente ele libera e o que a prática faz com ele quando é desmentido. A série exibe a permanência da relação entre previsão e decisão e a capacidade da prática interpretativa de absorver o desmentido sem devolver a decisão à incerteza de onde partiu, apesar da transformação completa dos signos, dos intérpretes e das técnicas. Sob essa permanência está uma condição: o momento do ato é fixado pelo mundo, e aquilo que decidiria a questão — o resultado — só existe depois do ato, donde a assimetria entre fundamento parcial e autoria integral. A partir da tese gadameriana da aplicação, argumenta-se que a incidência prática não é propriedade autossuficiente do signo; o seu desaparecimento no momento do caso não significa, portanto, eliminação, mas anterioridade ou sedimentação da determinação — com a consequência de que a execução pode produzir o ato sem reabrir a pergunta situada: o caso deixa de ser encontrado e passa a ser instanciado, a alegação perde destinatário no instante em que importaria, e a autoria é retirada da cena sem ser transferida.

items.title: A Responsabilidade Como Arquitetura: Participação, Imago Dei e Os Limites Do Fundamento Único.
A Norma Que Retiramos: Domesticação, Seleção Humana e Responsabilidade Pelo Vivo.
items.abstract: Examina-se a responsabilidade de quem controla as condições de vida de animais tornados dependentes da intervenção humana. Um caso hipotético, o de um cavalo com lesão tratável submetido à eutanásia por razões econômicas, é contrastado com a conservação do cavalo-de-przewalski por criação em cativeiro e reintrodução. Os dois casos partilham uma estrutura de dependência administrada, mas não se equivalem: conservar pode sustentar a realização do vivente, ao passo que matar a encerra. A partir de uma filosofia da normatividade fundada na dependência do não produzido, distinguem-se a norma vital, as condições constitutivas recebidas e os meios de cuidado produzidos. Identificar a perda de uma forma de vida não basta para demonstrar a sua proibição; requer-se uma premissa normativa explícita, segundo a qual quem institui ou sustenta uma dependência deve justificar a retirada de cuidados viáveis, sem confundir perda de rentabilidade com impossibilidade de assistência. A Resolução CFMV nº 1.000/2012 oferece o fundamento documental para distinguir sofrimento irreversível, incompatibilidade produtiva e insuficiência financeira. O piso identifica o que se perde, e a posição ocupada na dependência fundamenta uma exigência de justificação, não um dever ilimitado de preservar a vida. Na conservação, separam-se indivíduo, linhagem e população em liberdade. O estatuto moral do animal por si mesmo permanece fora da tese.

items.title: Characterizing dynamic cognitive systems.
items.abstract: In a recent paper, De Brigard (2017, Philosophical Explorations) argues that a successful neuroscientific account of “cognitive system” needs to capture the fact that brains change over time (i.e., exhibit diachronic dynamicity) even when these changes do not affect their functional profile (i.e., exhibit functional stability). Unfortunately, in that paper, he fails to offer a satisfactory account that can capture both features. To fill that gap, the current paper offers a graph-theoretic strategy to characterize cognitive systems in a way that captures both diachronic dynamicity and functional stability. Specifically, it is suggested that cognitive systems can be characterized by way of employing a multi-scale modular approach in which time is parametrized.

items.title: Gravity, Light and the Etheric Field.
items.abstract: This paper brings together research notes written between 2013 and 2015. The original material moves from the Tibetan’s teaching on gravity and the planetary Entity to reflections on rotary motion, physical light, black holes, Fohat, quantum entanglement and the consciousness of the atom. The text has been lightly edited for grammar, continuity and presentation.

items.title: ¿Hacia una personalidad jurídica de los autómatas inteligentes? Aspectos personales y patrimoniales de la inteligencia artificial ante el desafío de la exploración espacial.
Entre la nube y la tierra.
items.abstract: El presente artículo redefine la pregunta por la materialidad de lo digital a partir de una genealogía del dualismo filosófico occidental. La aparente inmaterialidad de lo digital constituye prolonga la visión dualista bajo nuevas formas técnicas. A través del diálogo crítico con diversas perspectivas filosóficas, fenomenológicas y materialistas, el artículo sostiene que lo digital es materia mediada, y que la diferenciación ontológica entre lo material y lo digital es un constructo teórico errado. Esta diferenciación se vuelve vaporosa e irrisoria cuando nos adentramos en el futuro de lo digital como son los mundos virtuales y el metaverso demostrando que, cuando la interacción digital alcanza suficiente inmersividad, las categorías heredadas pueden quedar superadas. Por último, el artículo concluye con la necesidad de repensar las categorías existentes, a fin de construir categorías genuinamente nuevas, capaces de dar cuenta de entidades que son, simultáneamente, materia y código, cuerpo y dato, territorio y red.

items.title: Can We Trust Robots? A Brief Consideration of Human–Machine Interaction in Medical Care.
items.pub: In Santiago Ullauri Betancourt, Diego Ortiz-Jaramillo, Nicolás Fuentes Valdebenito & Felipe Álvarez, Perspectivas filosófico-políticas contemporáneas: Reflexiones y debates para el siglo XXI. Quito: UHEdiciones. pp. 84-122.
items.venue: Perspectivas filosófico-políticas contemporáneas: Reflexiones y debates para el siglo XXI
items.abstract: The global decline in birth rates and prolonged aging, combined with chronic shortages of human and material resources in the medical field, call for a rethinking of health care delivery worldwide. Even so, the principles of the ethics of care—patient autonomy and dignity—must be upheld. Robotics and AI are poised to take on an expanding role; however, uncertainty persists regarding their ability to perform tasks that are traditionally reserved for humans. Beyond technical limitations, the large-scale deployment of these technologies raises profound ethical and philosophical dilemmas that remain largely unaddressed by the literature. Simple robots inspire clear judgments, but the emergence of genuinely intelligent automatons blurs the question of trust, which depends heavily on how each user conceptualizes the machine. Patients can also become attached to these devices, complicating their responsibility. For the moment, robots should serve as sophisticated assistants while a comprehensive machine-ethics framework—bolstered by long-term studies on sustained human-robot interaction— grows mature enough to foster genuine trust in clinical practice.

items.title: Algorithmic Creativity and Copyright: Can AI Be the Author of a Work?
items.abstract: The development of artificial intelligence systems capable of generating texts, images, music, code, and other formally original creations has reopened the debate on the classical foundations of copyright law. This article examines whether an artificial intelligence system can be considered the author of a work and what the legal, ethical, and philosophical implications are of either accepting or rejecting that possibility. To this end, it analyses the concept of algorithmic creativity, the traditional notion of authorship based on human intervention, and the main criteria used by copyright law to recognize the originality of a work. It also explores the problems raised by AI-generated works in relation to ownership, liability, moral and economic rights, and the protection of the interests of programmers, users, companies, and autonomous systems. This article further argues that, in view of the development of increasingly complex and autonomous machines, it is necessary to recognize that such systems are creating creative works that may be as original as, or even more original than, human works. This calls for a shift in perspective leading to legislative reform capable of recognizing the “co-creation” of works through human-machine interaction, both in law and in society.

items.title: Comparative Empirical Analysis of the Core Emotion Framework: Short-Exposure Psychometrics, Theoretical Architecture, and Cross-Modal Efficacy.
items.abstract: The empirical evaluation of brief psychological models requires distinguishing between immediate cognitive reframing achieved through acute conceptual exposure and the sustained behavioral regulation produced by comprehensive therapeutic architectures. The Core Emotion Framework (CEF) represents a psychological taxonomy designed to organize cognitive, emotional, and conative experience into ten active psychological operators distributed across three primary centers (Head, Heart, and Gut) alongside an overall integrative operator. This research report delivers an exhaustive psychometric and comparative analysis evaluating the single short-exposure test of the CEF (N=100) against the theoretical capabilities of the full CEF data model. Furthermore, this analysis benchmarks the acute efficacy of the CEF against standardized outcome metrics established across other single-session interventions (SSIs), single-session therapies (SST), Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT), Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT), and longitudinal therapeutic modalities.

items.title: Reverence for Fine Virtues: An Independent Chapter of Jing-Rong Philosophical Reflections.
items.abstract: This paper takes the core proposition of original philosophy — the virtue cultivation law of taking Reverence and Vital Harmony for Domain-Benefiting (Jìng Róng Lì Yù) as the foundation, and taking With Reverence, Virtue Aggregates; Virtue Vital-Harmonized Nurtures Malleable Nature (Self-Cultivation Law) as the Inherent-Logic (Lǐ) — as its core framework. It selects 18 virtues from the pre-Spring and Autumn Period (Elder Devotion (Xiào), Teaching (Jiào), Integrity (Xìn), Ritual Propriety (Lǐ), Discernment (Zhì), Covenant Fidelity(Yì), Sincere Devotion (Zhōng), Fortitude (Yǒng), Fraternal Respect (Tì), Inclusive Kindness (Rén), Confluent Harmony (Hé), Moderation (Zhōng), Origin (Běn), Dao (Dào), Obstinacy (Zhí), Law (Fǎ), Lucid Awakening (Jué), Endeavor (Nǔ)), and adapts them to the new era. It aims to present the Inherent-Logic of virtue formation. With no preset research background or problem-solving objectives, this paper serves only as an exposition of inherent rules, providing a new perspective for understanding Chinese virtues.

items.title: 敬美德：敬融哲思独立篇章 (Reverence for Fine Virtues).
items.abstract: [Note: Original Chinese text of "Reverence for Fine Virtues: An Independent Chapter of Jing-Rong Philosophical Reflections".] 本文以原创哲学核心命题——以敬融利域为基，以以敬聚德、德融养性为理的美德修养法则，撷取春秋前之美德（孝、教、信、礼、智、义、忠、勇、悌、仁、和、中、本、道、执、法、觉、努），合于新时代，旨在呈现美德形成之理，无预设研究背景与问题解决目标，仅作为内在规则的阐释，为理解华夏美德提供新的视角。This paper takes the core proposition of original philosophy — the virtue cultivation law of taking Reverence and Vital Harmony for Domain-Benefiting (Jìng Róng Lì Yù) as the foundation, and taking With Reverence, Virtue Aggregates; Virtue Vital-Harmonized Nurtures Malleable Nature (Self-Cultivation Law) as the Inherent-Logic (Lǐ) — as its core framework. It selects 18 virtues from the pre-Spring and Autumn Period (Elder Devotion (Xiào), Teaching (Jiào), Integrity (Xìn), Ritual Propriety (Lǐ), Discernment (Zhì), Covenant Fidelity(Yì), Sincere Devotion (Zhōng), Fortitude (Yǒng), Fraternal Respect (Tì), Inclusive Kindness (Rén), Confluent Harmony (Hé), Moderation (Zhōng), Origin (Běn), Dao (Dào), Obstinacy (Zhí), Law (Fǎ), Lucid Awakening (Jué), Endeavor (Nǔ)), and adapts them to the new era. It aims to present the Inherent-Logic of virtue formation. With no preset research background or problem-solving objectives, this paper serves only as an exposition of inherent rules, providing a new perspective for understanding Chinese virtues.

items.title: Expressivism and Evidence for Moral Judgments.
items.abstract: We often support our moral judgements by appealing to independent considerations. According to some approaches in moral epistemology, the best way to understand this support is as evidential. However, it is unclear how some metaethical positions, like expressivism, can be compatible with such a view. For expressivists, moral judgements are desire-like states, which ostensibly are not the sorts of states which can be evidentially supported. In this paper, I argue that expressivists can indeed make sense of relations of evidential support for moral judgements. Drawing on a common sides-stepping expressivist strategy, I argue that expressivists should first focus not on evidential relations themselves but on our thought and talk of the form ‘e is evidence for p’. I then appeal to a form of epistemic expressivism, according to which such claims express complex non-cognitive attitudes or normative perspectives about standards that make it permissible to judge that p given e. This approach allows expressivists to reinterpret questions about what evidential relations between evidence e and moral judgements that p are as first-order normative questions about which standards not ruled out by acceptable normative perspectives make it permissible to judge that p given e. Responses to these first-order questions should be, in principle, compatible with expressivist second-order accounts of moral thought and talk. Finally, to show that this first-order interpretation is plausible, I outline a version of evidential explanationism along those lines.

items.title: 太極導引 Taichi-Dowing (Tàijí Dǎoyǐn).
Project Causa Sui: A Minimal Architectural Theory of Subjecthood.
items.abstract: Why can a sufficiently complex silicon system convincingly imitate responsibility, fear and creativity, and yet — on the account proposed here — not possess them? We propose a minimal architectural condition for subjecthood, understood as the capacity for responsibility, fear and creativity as distinct from their behavioural imitation. The central postulate is that the history of a subject is inseparable from its carrier: relative to the causally relevant boundary of the system there is no exact operator that restores an earlier state. This postulate is an axiom of a position we call historical substrate realism, not a theorem, and we argue that no behavioural test can decide it. We then describe explicitly the architecture on which the theory reasons: a network of NRMs, each consisting of a graph of states and the matrices that record what is known about each state, with a single signal for change — the mismatch between an expectation recorded in a matrix and what actually happened. We locate irreversibility in the graph rather than in the matrices. Pain is defined as an irreversible contraction of the set R(s) of viable states available in the subject's own graphs; physical damage is its extreme case, while the general case is a record that closes a possibility and cannot be unlearned. From this we trace memory, fear and responsibility, and propose that agony and curiosity trigger one and the same operation — expansion of the graph — under different conditions. Open questions are stated explicitly: the absence of a unified formalism, the gap between damage and experience (the hard problem of consciousness), and the thresholds that separate the kinds of change. The theory is presented as a working conceptual framework, not as an established or experimentally validated result; a companion preregistration states an empirical expectation that could refute it.

items.title: The Beauty of Philosophy.
items.abstract: A distinction falls, and an argument that was tangled changes shape: no material has been added and no answer has yet appeared, but something that could not be put clearly can, for the first time, be asked. A subject who has seen this cannot not acknowledge: this distinction has really opened something, and it has not yet closed itself. That sentence is the beauty of philosophy. The paper says what the first distinction is and is not (not the first event in the history of the universe, not the law of identity, not classification); the two faces of the beauty of philosophy (the moment a question takes shape, and the question that stands); what can pass for it (clear classification, questions with the answer built in, novel terminology, pseudo-problems, raising the local into an unconditional verdict, profundity used as a talisman, and subdivision); and what is left to each person. It explains why the power of judgment here cannot rely on rules. It then traces where the question comes from: how wonder brings thought to a halt, how a distinction gives a question its shape, how questions were made into institutions, why rules cannot stand in for judgment, and which is more fundamental, the question or the answer. Along the way it takes up Plato, Aristotle, the Kaṭha Upaniṣad, Xunzi, Gongsun Long, Zhuangzi, Nāgārjuna, Aquinas, the Wumen guan, Kant, Sibley, Peirce, Dewey, Collingwood, Heidegger, Gadamer, Deleuze and Wittgenstein. It ends by handing on to the beauty of mathematics the question of how the same sign can still count as the same across occurrences.

items.title: Synthecracy: A Methodological Framework for Collective Intelligence and Adaptive Societal Learning Supported by Artificial Intelligence.
items.abstract: This article presents Synthecracy as an open conceptual-methodological framework for supporting collective intelligence, civic interaction and adaptive societal learning. Its foundation is the triad “Idea - Knowledge - Human”, in which the Idea sets a direction or articulates a societal demand; Knowledge provides verifiable context and experience; and the Human exercises judgement, choice and action while bearing responsibility. Artificial intelligence in this model functions as an auxiliary communicative- analytical layer rather than an autonomous centre of political power or a fourth fundamental element. The paper proposes the cycle “Reaction → Dialogue → Knowledge → Analysis → Synthesis → Decision → Result → Learning” together with a traceable record of a societal issue that links the initiative to sources, arguments, alternatives, the decision, accountable implementers and the evaluation of outcomes. Drawing on literature in collective intelligence, deliberative democracy, organisational learning and AI risk management, the article identifies related approaches, outlines a possible authorial contribution and suggests directions for empirical testing. The article does not claim proven effectiveness of the model; Synthecracy is presented as a proposal open to critical analysis, adaptation and pilot implementation. Keywords: Synthecracy; collective intelligence; societal learning; civic participation; deliberative democracy; artificial intelligence; digital governance; decision traceability; human agency.

items.title: Aesthetic Taste in Humans and Machines.
items.abstract: Aesthetic taste remains an elusive phenomenon that has been comparatively underexplored in psychology. We argue that taste integrates four dimensions: sensitivity to fine-grained differences within a domain; valence, through which these differences come to matter affectively; orientation, the selective tendency to seek encounters that may further transform one’s sensibility; and normativity, through which judgments of taste become shareable and contestable. These are not separate dimensions but faces of a single underlying capacity: continuously monitoring one’s grip on the world and letting that monitoring modulate what happens next. This makes human engagement non-uniform. Throughout, we use current artificial intelligence as a contrast case, exploring how far it can model or replicate human taste. Machines can be sensitive to fine-grained distinctions, predict human preferences, generate apparently tasteful outputs, and shape the environments in which human taste develops. But they do not yet possess taste in the full human sense, because they lack the stake that makes human processing non-uniform: self-directed exploration, online self-transformation, and genuine normative vulnerability. The upshot is a systematic framework for the study of human taste and for assessing how AI may transform its formation.

items.title: Managed Hierarchy versus Federated Truth‑Seeking.
