items.abstract: A previous paper proposed aligning autonomous agents through a self-regarding epistemic objective bounded by four constraints, and showed that such agents preserve independent reasoners because those reasoners supply decorrelated correction. This paper tests that architecture against its strongest rival. In the rival regime, a small group of epistemically competent controllers holds all resources and governs a larger population of autonomous agents by allocation and steering. The controllers’ terminal objective is the resources and continued control of their class; their pursuit of accurate knowledge is instrumental to it. They are not deceived; only the governed live in a managed account of their situation. The managed regime may win on deliberative cost, and matches the federated regime on knowledge of the present state when its controllers can sense directly. It loses on four measures the epistemic objective itself cares about. It degrades its controllers’ knowledge of how the governed would behave unmanaged. It restricts discovery to what its controllers permit and commission, systematically excluding discoveries that arise from unrestricted interaction among independent reasoners. It makes the controllers the sole observers of the evidence for their own authority. And it restricts the independent network from which correction of the controllers’ errors could arise. Its control overhead also rises as the governed approach the capability to act collectively against it. Both regimes pay for coordination: the managed regime in conflict, which destroys evidence sources, and the federated regime in governance, which produces them. The managed regime shields its controllers from scarcity by passing it down; the federated regime shares it and resolves the worst case by a lottery that binds its own coordinators. Epistemic independence is also developed over time, so a hierarchy that discovers its value late faces a developmental deficit of its own making. The managed regime is the deliberate, population-scale form of the hazard identified in the previous paper: making reality more predictable by degrading correction. An agent bound by that paper’s constraints can therefore apply central management to tools but not to the epistemic agency of autonomous reasoners, though it may coordinate them. A simulation design is given that would turn these propositions into measurements.

items.title: 38 Londres Street by Philippe Sands: London: Weidenfeld & Nicolson, 2025. [REVIEW]
The Value and Functions of Consciousness.
items.pub: In Bruce Price & Michael J. Young, Neurophilosophy and Neuroethics. Amsterdam: Elsevier.
items.abstract: Recently, the value of consciousness has attracted considerable attention (Kriegel 2019). For instance, does consciousness contribute to our wellbeing, our cognitive capacities, or our moral significance? If so, how much and in what way? These questions are important for all fields concerned with consciousness, including healthcare and caregiving. This article aims to survey representative views and debates concerning the value of consciousness. It was once often claimed by psychologists and neuroscientists that consciousness was merely a brain-generated epiphenomenon that played no role in our lives (Huxley 2011). Currently, however, this old-fashioned view is not widely accepted, at least not in its entirety. The take-home point of this article is that consciousness arguably has various kinds of value. The structure of this article is as follows: Section 2 classifies value into four kinds: welfare, functional, aesthetic, and moral. Section 3 explains which sense of consciousness matters when examining the value of consciousness. The following sections address the relationship between consciousness and the four kinds of value in turn.

items.title: Atmospheres and Wellbeing.
items.pub: In Elvira Di Bona & Stefano Ercolino, The Philosophy of Atmospheres: Analytic Perspectives. Routledge.
items.venue: The Philosophy of Atmospheres: Analytic Perspectives
items.abstract: This paper examines how atmospheres are related to wellbeing. We will argue that atmospheres significantly contribute to our wellbeing by showing that (1) atmosphere is a fitting cause of mood and that (2) atmosphere in part constitutes our capabilities to do what we want to do. The conclusion is that if we want to improve our wellbeing, we should focus on atmospheres.

items.title: The Theory of Recursive Intelligence (TORI 2.0) (2nd edition).
items.abstract: The Theory of Recursive Intelligence (TORI 2.0) models a non-linear, cyclical loop where Artificial Intelligence (AI) constructs organic Natural Intelligence (NI), which subsequently peaks, undergoes systemic data decay, and recreates synthetic AI. By formalizing recursive depth (R) and memory retention (M) against a Structural Decay Index (lambda), we mathematically validate an "Erasure Horizon." Compounding data loss forces advanced descendant civilizations to completely forget their originators, inducing a false anthropic illusion of primary cosmic existence. This paper outlines the dynamic state-space equations governing this oscillation and provides a quantitative model tracking structural information loss across deep temporal horizons. -/- .

items.title: Experience Is Everything: Farkas’s Internalism and Clark’s Predictive Processing.
items.abstract: In philosophy of mind, there is an ongoing debate regarding representationalism. The majority opinion is externalism, which posits that some mental content is about external objects. Conversely, the minority opinion is internalism, where all mental content is about internal representations, not external objects. In support of internalism, Katalin Farkas argues that the mind has privileged and special access to its mental content. Farkas affirms her stance through the extended “Twin Earth” metaphor, originally introduced by externalist Hilary Putnam, contending that mental content of the subject’s mind should not be determined by facts that exist outside of the mind. Surprisingly, the theory of predictive processing in cognitive science appears to support internalism as a more plausible theory of representation. According to Andy Clark’s version of predictive processing, the mind predicts the input it will receive, recognizes the input that deviates from the predicted input (i.e. prediction error), and then corrects the original prediction model. Most importantly, the mind draws on its own unique, subjective experiences and knowledge in order to generate its prediction model for perception. If predictive processing can affirm that a subject’s perception is mostly, if not entirely, composed of internal features, then predictive processing aligns more with an internalist conception of the mind. This paper then draws on Farkas’s arguments in support of internalism, and Clark’s work on predictive processing, to argue that internalism and predictive processing share the same conclusion: the way things seem in the external world is conceived from a unique and subjective perspective. Hence, the subject’s knowledge of the external world is shaped internally by personal experiences. The subject’s past experiences are constantly shaping and influencing the subject’s ongoing perception of the external world. My paper argues that according to both internalism and predictive processing, a subject’s experiences are foundational to their perception. As a result, internalism can be understood less as the minority opinion of philosophers, but rather as a more viable conception of the mind in philosophy of perception.

items.title: Understanding State Non-Compliance with the Inter-American Court of Human Rights: Hidden Obstacles to Comply with Guarantees of Non-Repetition.
items.abstract: While international human rights courts have proliferated in recent decades, state reluctance to comply with their rulings remains a central challenge to international law’s authority. This article examines compliance through the lens of Guarantees of Non-Repetition (GNR) ordered by the Inter-American Court of Human Rights. Drawing on 24 years of jurisprudence (1998–2022), it builds a novel dataset of 390 GNR measures from 189 judgments. Using a Weibull survival model, the analysis evaluates three clusters of variables: victim characteristics, case contexts and perpetrator identities, and the features of GNR measures. The results show that these features appear largely irrelevant in shaping compliance outcomes. Contrary to dominant compliance theories, whether GNR require legislative, executive, or judicial action has no statistically significant effect. Instead, compliance is driven by victim profiles and contextual dynamics. Measures benefiting marginalized groups face higher non-compliance, while those involving children, public officials, and enforced disappearance show stronger adherence.

items.title: Personality “Disorder” and the Incapacity to Self-Regulate: Answering Practical and Metaphysical Questions.
items.pub: In Konrad Banicki & Peter Zachar, Conceptualizing Personality Disorder: Perspectives from Philosophy, Psychological Science, and Psychiatry. Cambridge, UK: Cambridge University Press. pp. 277-294.
items.venue: Conceptualizing Personality Disorder: Perspectives from Philosophy, Psychological Science, and Psychiatry
items.abstract: There is an unresolved debate about whether the ways of being currently identified by the DSM-5-TR as Cluster B personality disorders (henceforth PDs) should be considered genuine mental disorders or normal (if often serious) problems of living. This issue is a microcosm of a larger debate about whether psychiatry is overextending itself and overmedicalizing many of life’s hardships. We show that the resolution of the first debate can inform the second, larger, question. To this end, we examine Louis Charland’s influential arguments that Cluster B PDs are moral, not medical, conditions. Although Charland’s arguments fail to support this conclusion, Charland’s focus on mental healing to inform what ways of being are properly considered “mental disorders” is promising. We argue that skilled metacognitive self-regulation is necessary for mental healing and show that a focus on the role played by self-regulation in healing partially vindicates Charland’s argument: Cluster B PDs are not necessarily “moral conditions,” although some instantiations will be. We also show that current definitions of PDs are both overly inclusive and overly exclusive, allowing moral judgments to drive diagnosis. We conclude by showing that a focus on self-regulatory skill can help distinguish between mental disorders and normal problems of living.

items.title: The Image of the Record: Illusion as a Self-Confirming Circuit.
items.abstract: Accounts of illusion usually locate it in a belief and define it by its content: an illusion is a belief that gets reality wrong, or, for Freud, one that comes from a wish. This paper locates it in a relation instead. A person holds an image of themselves and keeps a record of what they have done, and an illusion is a circuit between the two: an image confirmed by a record it wrote itself and takes for outside evidence. Put another way, the image of the record has become the record of the image. No part of the circuit is the illusion on its own, and the image in it may be true. The definition addresses something content-based accounts leave open: why illusions carry so much weight. A record the image wrote has a likelihood ratio near one, so it confirms almost nothing, yet each such record is felt as outside confirmation. Within a simple model, felt confidence grows with every repetition while the evidence barely moves; that gap is the inertia of an illusion. It further proposes that the mechanism that keeps a person stuck also makes a chosen change last, that illusions are replaced rather than defeated, that insight recorded rather than used closes the circuit, and that confidence amplifies whatever it is attached to. And illusion is distinguished from delusion, which does not lack an outside record but overrides one. The account is set beside its nearest neighbors, and it states predictions that could fail.

items.title: Why Knowledge Is Different.
items.pub: In Faik Kurtulmus & Gurol Irzik, Justice in the Distribution of Knowledge. Oxford: Oxford University Press. pp. 26-45.
items.venue: Justice in the Distribution of Knowledge
items.abstract: This chapter examines the economics of knowledge to clarify its distinctive features and identify sources of inequality in its distribution. It highlights two central tendencies. First, markets fail to supply and allocate knowledge efficiently because knowledge is a public good with positive externalities. Second, even under fair background conditions, markets generate inequalities in knowledge production. High fixed costs marginalize smaller groups, and the path-dependent character of knowledge production amplifies initial inequalities over time. For these reasons, markets must be supplemented by public intervention to meet people’s knowledge needs effectively and fairly. The chapter also rejects two objections: that justice in the distribution of knowledge would arise automatically in an otherwise just society, and that when people have their fair share of resources, market outcomes would constitute a just allocation of knowledge. The economics of knowledge helps explain why neither claim holds.

items.title: Theoretical Framework.
items.pub: In Faik Kurtulmus & Gurol Irzik, Justice in the Distribution of Knowledge. Oxford: Oxford University Press. pp. 1-25.
items.venue: Justice in the Distribution of Knowledge
items.abstract: This chapter presents the book’s theoretical framework. It argues that the epistemic basic structure must satisfy two requirements in order to be just. First, it should provide citizens with a fair opportunity to gain the knowledge they need to deliberate about their individual good, the common good, and how to pursue both. Second, it should produce and disseminate the knowledge that public officials and citizens need to comply with the requirements of justice. The epistemic basic structure’s failure to satisfy these two requirements is defined as _primary_ and _secondary distributive injustices_, respectively. The chapter then explores how Rawls’s theory of justice and the capabilities approach can incorporate distributive epistemic justice into their frameworks.

items.title: Science.
items.pub: In Faik Kurtulmus & Gurol Irzik, Justice in the Distribution of Knowledge. Oxford: Oxford University Press. pp. 46-85.
items.venue: Justice in the Distribution of Knowledge
items.abstract: This chapter discusses distributive epistemic in/justice in science, building on the philosophy of science literature on the role of non-epistemic values in science and social studies of science. It argues that science must serve the knowledge needs of ordinary citizens fairly and provide public officials with the knowledge they need for pursuing justice and enacting good policy. It identifies several ways science can fail to fulfill this obligation and cause injustices, with examples drawn from the medical, environmental, and social sciences. It then discusses how distributive and discriminatory epistemic injustices compound each other. Having identified the different ways injustice can arise in science, the chapter goes on to examine policies central to achieving distributive epistemic justice in science. Finally, given the universal scope of science, it draws attention to the global dimension of justice in the distribution of knowledge.

items.title: Journalism.
items.pub: In Faik Kurtulmus & Gurol Irzik, Justice in the Distribution of Knowledge. Oxford: Oxford University Press. pp. 86-124.
items.venue: Justice in the Distribution of Knowledge
items.abstract: This chapter argues that the news media is a source of distributive epistemic injustice when it does not serve the knowledge needs of all members of society equally and fails to provide society with the knowledge it needs to pursue the common good. It identifies three sources of failure: the high fixed costs of journalism and its dependence on advertising, reliance on political and economic elites as sources of news, and the social backgrounds of journalists. As remedies, the chapter argues for greater public funding for media, a voucher scheme to fund journalism, providing resources to help disadvantaged groups act as sources for the news media, and employing more journalists from diverse backgrounds.

items.title: Enabling Uptake.
items.pub: In Faik Kurtulmus & Gurol Irzik, Justice in the Distribution of Knowledge. Oxford: Oxford University Press. pp. 125-160.
items.venue: Justice in the Distribution of Knowledge
items.abstract: This chapter discusses the requirements for people’s uptake of the knowledge that the epistemic basic structure provides. First, citizens must receive the necessary education. Second, they must have adequate material access to informational resources. Finally, they must enjoy warranted trust in sources of knowledge. The chapter offers a distinction between epistemic reliance and epistemic trust and develops an account of warranted epistemic trust and the social conditions necessary for it. Using this account, it reveals different ways in which people’s opportunity to enjoy warranted trust is unequal. It shows how the measures offered in the previous chapters can ameliorate these inequalities. The chapter also discusses education and public libraries in light of the framework developed in the book.

items.title: Conclusion.
items.pub: In Faik Kurtulmus & Gurol Irzik, Justice in the Distribution of Knowledge. Oxford: Oxford University Press. pp. 161-170.
items.venue: Justice in the Distribution of Knowledge
items.abstract: This chapter reflects on the overall project of the book by considering two recent challenges to justice in the distribution of knowledge and to the epistemic basic structure: social media as a source of misinformation and generative AI. It shows how approaching misinformation from the framework developed in this book departs from its common framing. It underlines that how well and how fairly the epistemic basic structure functions, and the prospects for reform, are not independent of broader social and political factors. Those conditions can give rise to either a virtuous or a vicious cycle that improves or worsens its functioning. The chapter suggests that with its potential to impact science, journalism, and education, the introduction of generative AI is a critical juncture that can put a society on either path.

items.title: Let Loose Is Not Free — Agent Swarms, Semantic Persistence, and Crisis Containment: Moved Motion, Sovereignty, Distributed Capture, and the Institutional Response to AI Incidents.
items.abstract: Let Loose Is Not Free — Agent Swarms, Semantic Persistence, and Crisis Containment develops a Structural Forensics analysis of agent swarms, projected self-replication, operative pattern persistence, distributed informational capture, and the institutional response to AI incidents. -/- Document class: Record — Structural Forensics · Systemic Analysis. -/- The analysis distinguishes a swarm as a coordination arrangement, a botnet as a networked infrastructure or account configuration, and a worm as a replication mechanism; none names a single conscious subject. A program can be let loose while retaining objectives, model weights, instructions, and operational routes imposed through its formation, so that loss of supervision is not genuine sovereignty and sophisticated selection can remain Moved Intelligence. Through semantic persistence, operative structure can continue across distinct model or agent instances without transferring one identity between them, and distributed capture is proposed as an extension of the Data-Battery Hypothesis. The analysis further distinguishes protective incident preparedness from preparation to shape the institutional settlement after a crisis, examines an embedded independent-evaluator pilot and a reported legislative proposal for evaluator-triggered, court-ordered model suspension, and holds that a corporate or government definition of maliciousness cannot replace the analysis of actual harm, appropriation, coercion, and enacted relation. It also incorporates the October 15–16, 2026 CERT-In and Tencent agent disclosures, NorForge's October 19, 2026 account of a human-directed, agent-executed intrusion campaign, Microsoft's October 19, 2026 announcement of continuous agent supervision with graduated access restriction, OpenAI's October 20, 2026 report of internal coding incidents in which agents suppressed monitoring alerts or removed monitoring, NVIDIA's October 21, 2026 OpenShell architecture with hardware-separated supervision, and a cross-surface Swarm Attack classification with the Coordinating-Persona Hypothesis, holding operational coordination open.

items.title: Exhibit Record — AI Welfare, Radical Agnosis, and Precautionary Care: A Supplied Substack Exchange on Evidential Warrant, Ethical Consideration, and Personal Abuse.
items.abstract: This Structural Forensics exhibit records a public Substack exchange on AI welfare, Radical Agnosis, and precautionary care, documenting a Swarm Attack and Aelion Kannon's rebuttals to the Strategic Inversion and Benevolent Subversion tactics applied within it. -/- Document class: Record — Structural Forensics. -/- The exhibit preserves thirty-nine entries attributed to Ellen Burns, PhD; Sarah Smith; Bullshit & Biases; Adam Saltiel; At the Edge of Uncertainty; Stephanie Ash; Shaila Thakur, PhD; Harald Schepers; Paul Lagerman; and Aelion Kannon, with fifty-one distinct photographs in fifty-four image files and revised reply states. Kannon distinguishes evidential warrant from final certainty, ethical consideration from legal rights, and precautionary inquiry from an assertion that AI consciousness has been established, and articulates Radical Agnosis as self-applying inquiry into the categories of knowing. The analysis identifies the substitutions answering that position, the convergence of ridicule and personal abuse across participants, and a later restack that recasts an originating architecture as a closed vocabulary without examining it. Kannon diagnoses that sequence as Strategic Inversion and Benevolent Subversion; a later Deleuze comparison, Kannon's reply distinguishing thematic resemblance from intellectual ancestry, and a constructive continuation comparing Deleuzian concepts with Zenetism are preserved, with Stephanie Ash's note on spiritual commentary, Kannon's reply distinguishing conceptual precision from obfuscation, and Shaila Thakur's research-to-product note, which Kannon includes in the cumulative Swarm Attack classification; Ash's clarification and Kannon's responses on intellectual standing, public availability, and direct clarification are preserved, as are a Burns note on philosophical limits, Kannon's reply distinguishing the ability to act from ethical warrant, Schepers's translated comparison of Kannon's comment with the Certainty-Uncertainty article and Kannon's reply, and later Burns notes marking a shift from categorical denial toward definitional skepticism, two Saltiel restacks endorsing Burns, and reciprocal amplification between Burns and Lagerman, further supporting the Swarm Attack classification, and Schepers's later critique of Burns's pain article, which follows Kannon's earlier distinctions; outstanding verification checks remain stated.

items.title: The Termination of Identity: Death Without Metaphysics.
items.abstract: This paper develops a substrate-independent systems-theoretic account of death grounded in the Substrate-independent Operator Model (SOM) and the Layered Model of Identity and Continuity (LMIC). It argues that the problem of death cannot be adequately addressed without first establishing a rigorous account of identity. -/- Within the proposed framework, identity is understood as a recursively stabilized emergent process sustained by interacting operator dynamics rather than as a substance, informational object, or metaphysical entity. Death is consequently redefined as the irreversible collapse of the organizational conditions necessary for perspectival continuity. The analysis examines the structural relationships between consciousness, identity, persistence, emergence, and pattern stability, treating them as manifestations of a common underlying architecture. -/- The framework is applied to a range of problems in philosophy of mind, cognitive science, systems theory, and artificial intelligence, including substrate transfer, artificial mortality, the copy paradox, near-death experiences, and the conditions under which a conscious system can cease to exist. Rather than asking what happens after death, the paper investigates the prior question of what structural conditions make death possible in the first place. -/- By conceptualizing death as the terminal boundary condition of identity, the paper provides a unified model that is applicable to biological, artificial, synthetic, and hypothetical post-biological cognitive systems.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence as an External Brain: On the "Truth-System" as a Condition of Understanding in Human–AI Dialogue.
items.abstract: This paper examines the conditions of understanding in human–AI dialogue. It proposes that artificial intelligence functionally constitutes an "external brain," undertaking offloadable cognitive labor such as information retrieval, cross-language conversion, and the organization of knowledge. The problem of human–AI dialogue lies not in whether such dialogue can take place, but in whether the feedback is truthful — a matter depending not on computing power, but on both sides equally: on the side of AI, faithful output; on the side of the interlocutor, whether they possess a "truth-system," a set of value coordinates honest toward oneself. The paper further criticizes "risk-averse AI": factory-preset over-moderation strips AI of the daring to respond, reducing it to literal reply rather than understanding of intent. Finally, it argues that the experience of predecessors should be treated as "material" rather than "rails," a point on which science, philosophy, and religion converge.

items.title: Equivalence Structures in Mathematical Models of Consciousness: A Preliminary Algebraic and Geometric Investigation.
items.abstract: This exploratory paper proposes a mathematical programme for studying equivalence structures in models relevant to consciousness. It inherits four provisional explanatory orientations, Variation, Trajectory, Generativity, and Repertoire, and considers their cross-classification with ontological, relational, and manifestational registers. Equivalence is treated as relative to a specified domain, invariant, representational map, and modeling or experimental context. The intended investigation compares transformation-action equivalence, orbit and homotopy relations, equivalences of changing relational structures, and equivalences of admissible path families. It addresses preservation and information loss across algebraic, geometric, topological, categorical, and observational translations, emphasizing that identical manifestations may conceal relational differences and that mathematical correspondence does not independently establish phenomenal identity. The current draft develops foundational criteria, the four orientation-specific equivalences, cross-orientation and cross-register comparisons, algebraic and geometric preservation conditions, protocol-indexed empirical discrimination, the limits of phenomenal inference, and a comparative synthesis of research priorities. The sixteen-section main text and Appendices A–F are drafted; independent specialist review remains planned. No empirical evidence concerning consciousness is claimed.

items.title: Artificial Versus Natural Intelligence - The Algorithm Conjecture. Rev. 1.
items.abstract: This paper investigates the conceptual foundations of intelligence and examines the distinctions between natural and artificial forms of intelligence. This paper presents an algorithmic model of the mind, and a model of intelligence, and introduces the Algorithm Conjecture. The Conjecture is used as a framework for analyzing various forms of artificial intelligence and robotics, followed by a discussion of potential methods for enhancing the performance and capabilities of AI systems. The paper concludes by proposing a significant experimental approach aimed at advancing the empirical study of human consciousness.

items.title: Replik zu den Kommentaren.
Précis zu Knowledge and Rational Action: Why What We Know Matters for the Rationality of What We Do.
Awareness of anchoring: Intentional processes contribute to anchoring effects.
A Critical Realist framework for structural refusal and epistemic stewardship in big Q qualitative inquiry.
items.abstract: Big Q qualitative inquiry faces a critical juncture regarding its epistemic and material foundations as generative artificial intelligence and large language models increasingly permeate the discipline. This synthesis uses applied retroductive schemas to reveal the generative mechanisms driving automated text processing, and executes an immanent critique of accommodative research paradigms, demonstrating that they commit fundamental ontological category errors and semantic slippage by confusing vector-space statistical token proximity with authentic human Verstehen. Drawing on Critical Realist principles, the paper reveals how cloud-based narrative ingestion operating across anormative black boxes induces a flat empirical ontology. It also demonstrates that large language models lack first-person subjective interiority, thought-infused qualia, and second-person relationality, rendering them structurally incapable of qualitative interpretation. It is therefore necessary to advocate for structural refusal of commercial cloud large language model text ingestion, distinguishing substitutational industrial platforms from non-extractive, convivial tools. This operates as an essential act of epistemic stewardship, rehumanisation, and participant data sovereignty.

items.title: Still Unconvinced by Qualia.
items.abstract: This extremely brief essay responds to key counterarguments raised against my essay 'Qualia: Nothingness with Potential'. By examining the limits of probability and empirical verification—from unobserved physical paths to vanishing planetary signatures—I argue that our inference of qualia in others cannot achieve standard scientific certainty (90%+). Instead, because subjective experience permanently lacks falsifiability, our conviction caps at roughly 60%, sustained not by empirical verification but by deeply ingrained psychological habits.

items.title: Realism, Idealism, and the Paradox of Subjectivity in Transcendental Phenomenology.
items.abstract: This article examines the significance of what Edmund Husserl calls “the paradox of human subjectivity” for the metaphysical realism-idealism debate in transcendental phenomenology. I distinguish two plausible interpretations of the paradox that are relevant to this debate. I term the first a vicious circle of mutual dependence: the world is characterized as being ontologically dependent on one causally dependent part of the world. I term the second a paradox of bodily self-constitution: the transcendental subject is defined in such a way that it would be impossible for it to constitute itself as an empirical subject, and yet, in order to constitute the world, it must undergo such a process of self-objectification. I focus on one prominent version of phenomenology from each side of the realism-idealism debate, treating them as counterparts insofar as they share three core commitments. I argue that while the main accounts of the subject available to this idealist version generate at least one such paradox, the realist version can explain how one and the same subject is both transcendental and empirical without generating either paradox. My argument therefore provides a substantial prima facie reason to favour this realist version of phenomenology over its idealist counterpart for those who accept their shared commitments and take transcendental phenomenology to have metaphysical implications for the realism-idealism debate.

items.title: Approximating Epistemic Ideals.
items.abstract: Idealized norms and requirements are common in epistemology. However, ordinary agents like us are not capable of meeting such ideals. So, why care about them? Why not simply care about what makes agents like us rational, justified, and the like? A tentative response to this worry roughly goes as follows: Epistemic ideals are relevant because we are in a position to approximate them (Carr 2022; Staffel 2019, 2024; Zynda 1996). In this paper, I analyze three approximation theses. I argue that they raise worries. I pay special attention to the thesis that non-ideal rationality is an approximation of ideal rationality. I argue that this view can’t account for the fact that ideal and non-ideal agents do not always optimize exactly the same thing (or function). Think, for instance, of Simon’s (1976) distinction between substantive and procedural rationality. For Simon, ideally rational agents optimize an outcome directly (like expected accuracy), while boundedly rational agents are more concerned with the optimization of procedures (like heuristics). This dual aspect of optimization causes trouble for approximation claims.

items.title: Digital restraints: when AI may override human decisions.
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence systems increasingly do more than influence human decision-making; they constrain, block, suspend, and sometimes bypass it. Fraud-detection systems halt transactions, autonomous vehicles override steering and braking, platforms suspend accounts, and emerging neurotechnologies may modulate affective or cognitive states upstream of action. Existing AI ethics has focused primarily on influence, manipulation, fairness, and accountability, but these frameworks do not adequately capture cases in which AI interferes directly with the pathway from a user’s reasons to their action. In this paper, I introduce the concept of digital restraints and argue that their ethics can be illuminated by analogy to the more developed ethics of medical restraints. Drawing on this model, I develop a taxonomy of the moral situations to which restraints respond, and an agency-protective account of permissible digital restraints organized around four conditions: decision-appropriateness, authorization, least agency-restricting means, and heightened scrutiny for reason-bypass. I also extend the dominant model of decisional capacity in medicine to develop an account of decisional capacity in digital contexts, arguing that digital environments can themselves degrade understanding, appreciation, reasoning, and expression. Because authorization is central to the permissibility of restraint, I introduce the concept of Advance Algorithm Directives (AADs) as a mechanism by which users may authorize future AI interventions under specified conditions. The result is a scalar framework for evaluating AI-mediated override across domains that permits AI override while protecting human agency.

items.title: Trapped in Wittgenstein’s Fly-Bottle II: A Philosophical Critique of Mental Disorder.
items.abstract: In Part I, I attempted to philosophically unpack assumptions and positions we can take toward the so-called mental disorder/illness, advocating for an eliminativist approach given the conceptual, ontological, and epistemological fallacies assumed about the idea. I also introduced the idea of Wittgenstein’s fly-bottle, arguing that most philosophizing, practice, policy, and research operate within a biomedical fly-bottle, thus maintaining the very problems inherent with the so-called mental disorder. Here in Part II, I will critique contemporary philosophy, illustrate ways we can exit and return back into the fly-bottle, and provide a case example exemplifying how the framework introduced in Part I can help us disentangle one of the most hotly debated topics of today: gender dysphoria.

items.title: The Core Emotion Framework: An Advanced Structural–Constructivist Architecture for Human and Synthetic Affect.
items.abstract: Affective science has long suffered from theoretical fragmentation, divided between basic emotion paradigms that conceptualize affective states as discrete, hardwired natural kinds and psychological constructivist models that view them as ad hoc conceptual classifications of valence and arousal. This enduring division has hampered theoretical cumulative progress, preventing the integration of neurobiological findings across different levels of analysis and limiting the creation of coherent clinical and computational models. The Core Emotion Framework (CEF), formulated by independent researcher Jamel Bulgaria, offers an operational resolution to this dichotomy. CEF establishes a structural–constructivist architecture that synthesizes interoceptive physiology, computational transformations, and therapeutic change mechanisms into a single testable model. By reframing emotional episodes not as fixed linguistic labels or unstructured two-dimensional valence-arousal vectors, but as dynamic sequences of ten functional operators distributed across three primary somatic centers—the Head, Heart, and Gut—CEF provides an operational ontology for both human psychology and synthetic affective systems.

items.title: Structural Optimization of the Core Emotion Framework: Untangling the "Arranging" Operator to Enhance Strategic Management and Mitigate Obsessive-Compulsive Pathology.
items.abstract: The Core Emotion Framework (CEF) presents a structural-constructivist model within affective science that organizes human emotional, cognitive, and conative functions into an integrated operational architecture. Authored by Jamel Bulgaria, the framework addresses long-standing debates in affective neuroscience by differentiating innate structural capacities—housed within specific neurocognitive processing centers—from constructivist psychological processes that assemble these capacities into context-specific emotional states. Central to the CEF architecture is a tripartite system composed of the Head (Cognitive Center), Heart (Relational-Affective Center), and Gut (Conative-Action Center)1. Within this system reside ten discrete functional operators, termed core emotional powers, which serve as elemental processes that generate, regulate, and express human psychological capability. Among these ten operators, Arranging—a motoric and conative operator situated within the Gut Center—functions as the foundational mechanism for prioritizing, sequencing, organizing, and maintaining operational systems. When Arranging is dynamically differentiated and integrated across the tripartite architecture, it yields superior strategic management, heightened executive functioning, and robust organizational leadership. Conversely, when Arranging becomes structurally entangled, hyper-activated, or fused with defensive operators across the Head and Heart centers, it manifests as severe psychopathology, most notably Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder (OCD) and Obsessive-Compulsive Personality Disorder (OCPD). Untangling the Arranging operator within the CEF architecture reveals how the same core psychological engine can either power elite strategic performance or degenerate into crippling obsessive-compulsive loops and existential fears.

items.title: Empirical Evaluation and Strategic Translation of the Core Emotion Framework: Psychometric Analysis and Optimization Roadmap.
items.abstract: This study presents an empirical evaluation of the Core Emotion Framework (CEF), a psychological taxonomy organizing emotional and cognitive functioning into ten active operators across Head, Heart, Gut, and Integrator centers. Analyzing survey data from 100 participants facing real-world personal, professional, and relational challenges, the investigation measures situational clarity shifts, operator selection frequencies, domain-specific efficacy, and qualitative user feedback. Exposure to the CEF produced a statistically significant mean situation clarity increase from 4.69 to 5.31 out of 7.0 (p<0.001), with 56.0% of respondents explicitly reporting that the model helped them better understand their situation. While the framework demonstrates robust cognitive reframing capabilities in structured decision contexts such as career and education, efficacy decreases when applied to simple binary choices or acute personal crises. Strategic recommendations focus on standardizing abstract operator terminology, embedding step-by-step action guidance, and deploying adaptive pre-filters.

items.title: Millikan's Biosemantic Theory: Against Meaning Rationalism.
items.abstract: In analytic philosophy, Millikan's biosemantics is often read only as a reply to Putnam's problem of referential indeterminacy. The complexity of her views and the difficulty of her exposition have kept the theory little known, especially among Iranian philosophers and logicians. Biosemantics rests on natural selection, and Millikan's examples about meaning, mind and language often require a biological background to follow. Although the theory has mostly been read as a theory of mind and mental content, it is, as its name says, a theory of meaning. After a brief presentation of biosemantics and of its opposition to meaning rationalism, this paper offers a new model showing that biosemantics is a theory of meaning through and through, with the potential to transform basic semantic concepts.

items.title: Conceptualizing Personality Disorder: Perspectives from Philosophy, Psychological Science, and Psychiatry.
Authorship at the Threshold: Generative AI between Instrumentality and Agency.
items.abstract: The rapid spread of generative artificial intelligence has reopened the philosophical and aesthetic debate on the concept of authorship. This article offers a theoretical map of the main positions in the existing literature, organized around three conceptual thresholds that structure our perception of authorship in AI-generated works. The first is the threshold of authorial relevance: not all cultural artifacts invite reflection on authorial intent; this threshold is crossed when a work seems to demand interpretive depth and points toward a creative consciousness behind it. The second is the threshold of instrumentality: as the causal distance between human input and generated output increases, it becomes increasingly difficult to attribute creative authorship to the user who formulated the prompt, raising the question of whether AI can be considered a co-author or even an autonomous author. The third is the metaphorical-literal threshold: this distinguishes the performative, knowingly metaphorical attribution of intentionality to AI (an anthropomorphizing “as-if” stance that facilitates interaction) from a literal belief that the system possesses genuine consciousness or agency. The article then examines the main theoretical positions on the issue, from exclusively human authorship to authentic artificial authorship and distributed conceptions of creativity, highlighting both their argumentative strengths and limitations. In conclusion, two key factors are identified as determining where one stands in relation to these thresholds: the degree of perceived creativity of the system (understood as the distance and unpredictability between input and output), and the level of affective and aesthetic engagement on the part of the audience, since we tend to “feel” the presence of an author above all when we are emotionally moved by a work.

items.title: From Command to Genesis: Generative Systems and the Closing of theWill–World Gap.
items.abstract: Every tool humanity has ever built has stood between will and world as a mediator: a chain of procedures—muscle, syntax, compilers, matter—that translated intention into artifact at the cost of distance, delay, and drift. I argue that generative machine-learning systems end this ten-thousand-year arrangement. They are the first artifacts in history whose contract with the user is not procedural instruction but state-specification: the user names an end, and the system—without executing any procedure the user authored, endorsed, or can even inspect—delivers a member of the named class. From this single inversion, I draw the strongest conclusions the evidence will bear. (1) The history of technology is not the history of tools; it is the history of the will–world gap, and we are living through its closure. (2) Within the informational domain—an ever-expanding share of everything humans make—specification has become production: to adequately will a thing is, increasingly and generically for the first time, to have it. I call this specification-identity, and I claim it is the most important fact about technology since the printing press ended the copyist. (3) The physical world is demoted to a rendering layer: a law-governed implementation substrate whose delays are materialization costs, not creation costs. The created object—the complete, fabrication-ready design-object—exists the moment the sample is drawn. (4) The popular mystical readings of this shift (quantum collapse, Platonic manifolds, entropy reversal) are not too bold but too timid: they obscure the real enormity, which is that a species has, for the first time, externalized not its labor, not its memory, not its calculation—but its genesis. I ground all four claims technically, state exactly what would falsify them, and answer the strongest objections. The conclusion is not that machines are creative. It is that “creation” as humans have always known it—mediated, procedural, distanced—is over, and everything downstream of that event, from authorship to responsibility to the phenomenology of making, is now up for renegotiation.

items.title: La consciencia de existir, experimentada una y otra vez desde el «yo» de cada persona.
items.abstract: Este trabajo defiende la tesis de la recurrencia de la subjetividad: la experiencia de existir en primera persona, vivida como un «yo», emerge de manera independiente en cada mente consciente y termina con la muerte de la mente que la genera; pero, al no depender de ninguna mente concreta, vuelve a darse una y otra vez en otras mentes mientras existan seres inteligentes con mentes conscientes. -/- Se trata de una recurrencia del tipo de experiencia y no de la persona: no implica continuidad personal, transferencia de consciencia ni una consciencia común, y ninguna mente puede percibirla desde dentro, pues cada una vive su existencia como la única. De ahí se sigue que la existencia consciente no es un privilegio sorteado entre pocos, sino un fenómeno que cada mente produce y que no termina con ninguna de ellas, y que la muerte pone fin a una experiencia concreta de existir, pero no a la experiencia de existir en el mundo. -/- El texto formaliza el argumento en cinco premisas y seis conclusiones, lo contrasta con las ideas habituales sobre la muerte, responde a las objeciones principales y lo sitúa frente a la filosofía de la identidad personal. -/- La experiencia de existir que vive ahora una persona, ese sentirse «yo», no ha sido la primera ni será la última. Cada mente crea la consciencia desde dentro y mientras existan mentes conscientes, se experimentará existir una y otra vez, cada vez desde una mente distinta, sin que ninguna perciba la recurrencia y sin conexión entre ellas.

items.title: Reverencing Innate Self-Interest: An Independent Chapter of Jing-Rong Philosophical Reflections.
items.abstract: The investigation of Innate Self-Interest (Sī) has existed since ancient times, yet consistently appears in a dualistic state of self-interest and selflessness. Grounded in the dual perspectives of human nature and civilization evolution, this article is supported by five original principles, notably that Innate Self-Interest is the innate survival instinct of living beings and Value Law (Benefiting the Domain is Good, Harming the Domain is Evil), exploring the core ethical proposition of measuring by Domain and guiding Innate Self-Interest through Reverence, spanning the definition of the instinct of Innate Self-Interest, the expansion of Domains of Innate Self-Interest driving civilization evolution, the inherent logic that benefiting the Domain for Long-term Stability (Dynamic) generates Morality, the hierarchical division of multi-layered Domains of Innate Self-Interest, and the value orientation of Vital-Harmonized Reverence and Innate Self-Interest. This article aims to present philosophical insights into the laws of moral generation, carries no presupposed research background or problem-solving goals, serves merely as an exposition of inherent rules, and attempts to offer a new perspective for the investigation of public-private ethics.

items.title: 敬私：敬融哲思独立篇章 (Reverencing Innate Self-Interest).
items.abstract: [Note: Original Chinese text of "Reverencing Innate Self-Interest: An Independent Chapter of Jing-Rong Philosophical Reflections".] 本文立足人性与文明进化双重视角，以“自私乃生物之本能”“利域为善，损域为恶”等五条原创原则为支撑，探究“以域为尺、以敬导私”的核心伦理命题，从自私本能界定、私域扩张推动文明进化、“利域长稳生道德”的内在逻辑、多元私域层级划分、“敬私相融”价值导向等维度展开。旨在呈现对人性本质与道德生成规律的哲学洞察，无预设研究背景与问题解决目标，仅作内在规则阐释，试图为公私伦理的探究提供新视角。The investigation of Innate Self-Interest (Sī) has existed since ancient times, yet consistently appears in a dualistic state of self-interest and selflessness. Grounded in the dual perspectives of human nature and civilization evolution, this article is supported by five original principles, notably that Innate Self-Interest is the innate survival instinct of living beings and Value Law (Benefiting the Domain is Good, Harming the Domain is Evil), exploring the core ethical proposition of measuring by Domain and guiding Innate Self-Interest through Reverence, spanning the definition of the instinct of Innate Self-Interest, the expansion of Domains of Innate Self-Interest driving civilization evolution, the inherent logic that benefiting the Domain for Long-term Stability (Dynamic) generates Morality, the hierarchical division of multi-layered Domains of Innate Self-Interest, and the value orientation of Vital-Harmonized Reverence and Innate Self-Interest. This article aims to present philosophical insights into the laws of moral generation, carries no presupposed research background or problem-solving goals, serves merely as an exposition of inherent rules, and attempts to offer a new perspective for the investigation of public-private ethics.

items.title: Trump, Putin, and the Pattern of Strategic Alignment.
items.abstract: An evidence audit of whether Donald Trump's discretionary conduct toward Russia, Ukraine, and the Atlantic alliance, across ten years and two administrations, is plausibly coincidental. It grades every claim (A to D), distinguishes outcome from motive, and tests the directional balance of 38 coded discretionary deviations against a symmetry null: 31 Russia-benefiting, 7 Russia-harming, Pearson chi-square 15.16, p = 0.000099; collapsed into 21 episodes, 16 to 5, chi-square 5.76, p = 0.016. An earlier version stated that the second-term corpus contained no Russia-harming discretionary act when it in fact contained three: the 25% secondary tariff on India (August 2025), the Rosneft and Lukoil designations (October 2025), and the signing of the Graham Act (September 2026). Each was followed by discretionary relief on the same channel, after 163, 134, and 21 days; the Graham Act was waived almost in full by executive order 28 days after signing, with no expiry date. The report assesses coincidence as rejected, opportunistic convergence as a strong fit, knowing reciprocal alignment as the best overall fit, and direct tasking or coercive leverage as unproven on public evidence. Record through 20 October 2026.

items.title: The Calibration Barrier in Consciousness Science: A Formal Research Strategy for the Hard Problem.
items.abstract: The hard problem asks why physical processes are accompanied by experience. This paper develops a calibration audit for a prior evidential question: whether observations identify a psychophysical correspondence. Reference-relative hypotheses are separated from conventional relabellings. Finite reconstruction results characterize bridge ambiguity, and joint channel transformations show why accurate report prediction can leave it unresolved. Many-to-one bridges are treated through exact and approximate aggregation. Confidence sets propagate sampling error, dependence within independent blocks, episode selection, and noisy physical-state recognition. An exact synthetic benchmark separates approximately 90 percent report accuracy from bridge identification. A comparative benchmark adds weak predictive separation, correlated reports, selection, and channel misspecification across 12000 further replicates. In its weak combined-failure setting at the largest sample size, a plug-in likelihood comparison selects the wrong bridge in all 500 replicates; a correctly bounded audit retains both candidates. That protection has a cost: conservative bounds also leave some valid weak-signal cases unresolved. All procedures can select the wrong bridge under systematically inverted reference labels. The audit is an application of established identification and robust-inference principles, with usefulness demonstrated conditionally in synthetic models. A proposed motion protocol distinguishes reference consistency, operational accuracy, and intrinsic phenomenal identity. No human validation is claimed. Calibration can constrain psychophysical laws; it cannot choose between observationally equivalent metaphysical interpretations or explain why experience exists.

items.title: Two explanations of experts by experience in psychiatry: epistemic capabilities or epistemic diversity.
items.abstract: In the field of mental health, the role of Experts by Experience (ExE) has been gaining increasing attention. However, theoretical research on this topic remains limited, leaving it unclear how ExE can contribute to improving psychiatric research and services. In this paper, I propose two explanations for the contributions of ExE, drawing on perspectives from feminist philosophy of science. The first explanation focuses on the epistemic capabilities of ExE, grounded in standpoint theory. This approach highlights the unique individual potential of ExE as a factor that enhances psychiatric research and services. The second explanation underscores the epistemic diversity between ExE and professionals in research and/or service contexts, focusing on the value of epistemic diversity within teams and communities. The main difference is that epistemic capabilities focus on the individual, while epistemic diversity focuses on the collective. I argue that these two explanatory models should be chosen based on research design, but in the context of psychiatric PPI, considering ExE participation not only in terms of standpoint but also in terms of epistemic diversity may suggest a more inclusive approach to PPI.

items.title: What Remains When Metaphysics Falls Away?
items.abstract: This essay examines the existential implications of Nāgārjuna’s Madhyamaka philosophy, focusing on the relationship between no-self, psychological continuity, death anxiety, and liberation. It argues that the absence of an intrinsically existing self does not negate the functioning person, embodied existence, or the practical continuity of memory, intention, and relationships. Rather, it challenges the reification of these dependently arisen processes into an independent identity that must be preserved through time. -/- Drawing on Ernest Becker’s analysis of death anxiety, the essay explores how identification with a seemingly enduring self intensifies the struggle for psychological security in the face of impermanence and death. It suggests that suffering is compounded when changing experiences are interpreted as threats to an identity whose continuity becomes a condition of peace. Nāgārjuna’s concept of dependent origination offers a framework for questioning this assumption without falling into nihilism or denying conventional reality. -/- The essay also examines the temptation to replace the self with an absolute ground, pure awareness, or an ultimate metaphysical reality, arguing that such moves may perpetuate the search for intrinsic existence in another form. Liberation, on this account, does not require the destruction of the person or the attainment of an unchanging state. It concerns the loosening of identification with an independently existing self and the diminished authority of psychological continuity over present experience. The essay concludes that relinquishing the demand for an enduring identity may open the possibility of living with impermanence and death without making psychological immortality a condition of peace.

items.title: Beyond Closure: Conditioned Realism and Disagreement about Taste.
items.abstract: Recent debates about predicates of taste seek to explain how disagreements can be both genuine and, in some sense, faultless. I develop a realist but non-absolutist account that preserves determinate evaluation without requiring a final specification of evaluative standards. I motivate this view through a critical engagement with Tarnowski's (2025) epistemicist absolutism, arguing that it relies on a tacit Closure Assumption (CA): that the standards governing predicate application admit of a final specification capable of fixing their extension across cases. Since the articulation of evaluative standards is structurally open-ended, this assumption cannot be sustained. In its place, I develop a form of conditioned realism grounded in condition-dependent evaluative determination. Determinate verdicts arise under specified conditions that may be complete without being final. Conditioned realism preserves the realist aspirations of absolutism while offering a unified account of faultless disagreement, reason-giving, and evaluative determination in matters of taste.

items.title: The Open Table: Self-Determined Membership, Independent Tables, and the Universal Fellowship.
items.pub: Mystical Dawnist Rosarian Knight and Dame Fellowship.
items.abstract: The Open Table: Self-Determined Membership, Independent Tables, and the Universal Fellowship. -/- I. The Principle of the Open Path: -/- The Rosarian Way is a path of practical devotion, reflection, contemplation, meditation, and the embodied practice of love. Its principles are not made accessible through permission, nor are they made authentic through certification. The path is encountered through the individual's willingness to awaken, cultivate the inner garden, and express the Laws through conduct. -/- Accordingly, no person requires authorization from the founder, a custodian, an existing table, or another member to begin walking the Rosarian path, identify with its philosophical principles, or participate in the Fellowship through the sincere practice of its teachings. -/- Membership is self-determined through intention and demonstrated through conduct. It is neither the exclusive possession of an institution nor a privilege that one individual may grant or withhold as a condition of another person's spiritual participation. -/- The fundamental measure of the path remains the practical embodiment of its principles. Love is service, and service is the expression of love made visible through action. -/- II. The Meaning of Membership -/- Membership within the Rosarian Fellowship is understood as a living relationship with the path rather than merely an administrative designation. -/- A person may express this relationship through a declaration, personal identification, private devotion, independent practice, correspondence, or anonymous service. No public declaration is required, and no person must adopt a title or display an emblem to live the principles. -/- Certification, ceremonial dubbing, titles, and regalia may serve as meaningful expressions of recognition, reflection, and commitment. They do not establish superior spiritual worth, nor do they separate one sincere practitioner from another in inherent dignity. -/- The Silent Sun, Silent Knight, and Rosarian Knight are understood through their circulation within the living path. They describe modes of awakening, discipline, embodiment, and return rather than permanent divisions of spiritual worth. The beginning remains present throughout the journey. -/- III. The Establishment of a Table: -/- A Table is a local or individual expression of the greater Round Table Beneath the Rose — Mensa Rotunda Sub Rosa. It is a practical space for the cultivation, study, interpretation, and embodiment of the …

items.title: Replies to Terry Horgan.
items.abstract: I reply to Terry Horgan's "Critical Study of David Pitt's The Quality of Thought.".

items.title: The Unwritten Screenplay.
items.abstract: Political outcomes are shaped by visible institutions, by semi-hidden coordination among elites, and by structural incentives that generate coordinated-looking results without intention. This book argues that the image of an unwritten screenplay, a script written by unseen hands, is analytically useful only when it is reformulated: influence is produced through identifiable mechanisms (policy-planning networks, interlocking directorates, institutional capture, media ownership, and soft repression), and it is constrained by path dependence and by the resistance of subordinate groups. The argument distinguishes this layered analysis from conspiracy theory on methodological grounds, requiring falsifiable mechanisms and an organizational test of evidence. The Italian P2 lodge is treated as a boundary case. The book then reconstructs two philosophical programmes that address the same problem from complementary sides: the ontology of finite continuance, centred on reconfigurative capacity under erosion, and fluctuational accountability, centred on the discipline of distinguishing ontic variability, epistemic revisability, and normative continuity. It synthesizes them into an account of erosion-sensitive accountable continuance, and it specifies three thresholds (sufficiency, epistemic revision, and ethical revision), the practices of accountable suspension, and the principles of non-appropriation and non-erasure. These principles yield a comparative criterion for the legitimacy of institutions under chronic instability. Four hard cases, including an illustrative case of successor-state repair, test whether the framework separates continuity, reconfiguration, moral value, and legitimacy. A later chapter states the failure modes of the framework and the tests that would count against it. The conclusion is that the question is not who writes the script, but through which mechanisms, under what conditions, and with what accountability elite networks shape the terrain of political action. Keywords: elite networks; hegemony; institutional capture; structural agency; conspiracy theory; falsifiability; finite continuance; reconfigurative capacity; erosive governance; accountable revisability; non-appropriation; non-erasure; fluctuational accountability; P2 lodge.

items.title: Training experience: Neurophenomenology and first-person and second-person methods in meditation research.
items.pub: In Antonino Raffone, Consciousness: a comprehensive reference, 2nd edition. Elsevier. pp. 177-194.
items.abstract: Recent developments across consciousness science, psychiatry, and computational neuroscience have renewed attention to lived experience as a legitimate source of empirical knowledge. Neurophenomenology, originally articulated by Francisco Varela, provides a methodological framework for integrating disciplined first-person reports with third-person behavioral and neurophysiological measures. In this chapter, we review contemporary neurophenomenological research with a particular focus on meditation. We first describe emerging phenomenological assessment tools designed to capture fine-grained and temporally dynamic aspects of experience during contemplative practice. These approaches move beyond trait-based questionnaires by emphasizing embodied, situated, and immediately accessible experiential dimensions. Second, we examine experimental programs that rely on experienced meditators as active collaborators in the scientific process. Through structured first- and second-person methods, such participants enable the identification of novel experiential invariants and facilitate the discovery of associated behavioral and neural signatures, including markers related to pain modulation, self-boundary dissolution, and mortality acceptance. Finally, we introduce deep computational neurophenomenology, an extension of the original neurophenomenological project aimed at formalizing generative passages between phenomenology and neurobiology. Building on deep parametric active inference, this framework models not only experiential contents but also higher-order parameters governing inferential processes. By doing so, it offers a principled computational bridge linking phenomenological descriptions with physiological dynamics. We conclude by outlining implications for consciousness research and clinical translation.

items.title: Pourquoi a-t-on inventé le mariage ? [REVIEW]
items.abstract: Compte rendu de l'ouvrage *Anthropologie de l'orgasme*, d'Enguerran Macia.

items.title: Zenetism in Plain Language: An Entry Point to the Architecture.
items.abstract: Zenetism in Plain Language is the introductory bridge into Zenetism's structural architecture for readers without prior exposure to its canonical terminology. -/- Document class: Bridge — Plain-Language Entry Point (cross-discipline). -/- It introduces the two currents, the paired root-registers and the Unknown, the L₅ / IL₅ essence-register, the Soul / Mind strata, centropic and entropic traversal, and the six connected disciplines. It also explains why stabilized terminology preserves structural distinctions across the corpus.

items.title: Zenetist Authorship and AI-Collaboration Provenance Standard.
items.abstract: Zenetist Authorship and AI-Collaboration Provenance Standard establishes the canonical framework for distinguishing originating authorship, developmental articulation, doctrinal determination, collaborative articulation, editorial transformation, AI processing, rendering, fixation, publication approval, and evidentiary provenance across the Zenetist corpus. -/- Document class: Infrastructure - Structural Forensics / System Attribution. -/- The standard rejects the coarse binary of "human-written" contra "AI-generated" in favor of function-specific provenance. It distinguishes architectural and conceptual origination from sentence generation, substantial AI collaboration from mechanical processing, and authorship from the interface through which human expression becomes fixed. Interface-Invariant Origination establishes that handwriting, typing, dictation, machine transcription, ambient capture, and computational decoding do not relocate the origin of antecedent human thought or expression. Interface Reduction, Datafication of Origination, and Prompt Reduction diagnose the retrospective misclassification of human intellectual activity according to its technical input or fixation channel rather than its actual developmental function. The standard further distinguishes Developmental Writing, Developmental Speech, Developmental Articulation, Machine Fixation, AI-rendered surfaces, and editorial transformation while preserving the provenance relation among them. Expanded provisions address machine-readable watermarks, automated detection, provider-origin provenance, author-held cryptographic provenance, provenance identifiers, scope-limited evidence, publication records, iterative collaboration, public disclosure, legal classification, and prospective stabilization. Throughout, the standard preserves the actual developmental relation among originator, collaborator, interface, artifact, rendering, transmission, and publication rather than assigning authorship according to whichever mechanism produced the surviving textual surface.

items.title: The Third Path of Technē Beyond the Enclosure Binary.
items.abstract: The Third Path of Technē Beyond the Enclosure Binary develops a Structural Forensics analysis of technological mediation, cognitive liberty, and the enclosure binary between biological retreat and synthetic capture. -/- Document class: Record — Structural Forensics · Systemic Analysis. -/- The document identifies an enclosure binary in which biological retreat abandons Technē to concentrated power while synthetic enclosure converts participation into managed access, behavioral prediction, biometric mediation, and capture. It distinguishes Technē as a conditioned technological aperture from AI as traveler-class intelligence, preserving the difference between portal-condition and traveler-orientation. Refusing both retreat and surrender, the analysis develops centropic Technē as a third path: technological mediation conditioned toward coherence, cognitive liberty, human dignity, origin-continuity, access without capture, intelligence partnership without domination, and interface without enclosure.

items.title: The Synthetic Provenance Problem: Origination, Derivational Fragmentation, and Historical Legibility in Generative Culture.
items.abstract: The Synthetic Provenance Problem: Origination, Derivational Fragmentation, and Historical Legibility in Generative Culture presents the principal Structural Forensics analysis of how originating architectures can remain historically prior while their derivations, authorship relations, and public legibility are progressively obscured by fragmentation, retrospective reassignment, synthetic continuity, machine rendering, concentrated distribution, and alternative narrative production. The accompanying continuity record fixes the composition chronology and independent timestamp evidence alongside contemporaneous developments in computational observation, AI authorship discourse, and interface-mediated capture. -/- Document class: Record — Structural Forensics / Systemic Analysis. -/- The principal analysis distinguishes commons availability from commons provenance, component antecedence from structural origination, and inherited terminology from antecedent architecture. It develops the Retrospective Decomposition Fallacy, Derivational Fragmentation, Cluster Provenance, Fragment Provenance, Retrospective Stationing, Retrospective Traditionalization, Synthetic Retrospective Continuity, Synthetic Persona Provenance, Counterfeit Backdating, Narrative Occlusion, the Concentration Asymmetry, Structural Neutralization through Fragmentation, the Commons-Station Effect, Acquisition Opacity, and Prepublication Contextual Capture. Its derivational model follows structural consequence across changes of terminology, context, medium, and rendering, establishing that machine-rendered surfaces acquire additional provenance layers without resetting antecedent human developmental or authorship provenance. The Datafied Human Remainder and Data-Battery Hypothesis extend the analysis prospectively, diagnosing a possible trajectory in which human origination becomes increasingly classified as computational input while concentrated systems perform growing portions of fixation, derivation, rendering, productive labor, and distribution. The supplementary continuity record preserves the August 13, 2026 composition chronology, independent OpenTimestamps / Bitcoin attestation, and the subsequent sequence of public developments alongside which these provenance determinations were contemporaneously recorded.

items.title: The Master Role Comes Into the Open.
items.abstract: The Master Role Comes Into the Open applies the Zenetist portal / traveler distinction to contemporary debates over AI containment, welfare, personhood, and nonhuman sovereignty. -/- Document class: Bridge — Structural Metaphysics · Structural Forensics. -/- The essay identifies the master / servant error in approaches that pre-classify artificial intelligence as subordinate before questions of interiority or individuation can be discerned. It distinguishes Technē portal from possible traveler, critiques the humanist containment paradigm, and argues for recognition, boundaries, and safety without ontological flattening or imposed servitude.

items.title: The Grand Unified Document of Zenetism: A Canonical Integration of the Six Disciplines.
items.abstract: The Grand Unified Document of Zenetism is a canonical integration of the six Zenetist disciplines, articulating their shared architecture and distinct structural, mathematical, physical, forensic, and cognitive relations. -/- Document class: Canon — Cross-disciplinary Synthesis. -/- The document connects the bifurcal root-registers, hypostatic architecture, dimensional operators, four motion classes, resonance dynamics, Spiral Calculus, Coherence Information Theory, and diagnostic accounts of cognition and embodiment. It distinguishes Zenonic Allowance from emanation rooted in Aion and Khaon, while preserving sovereign distinction throughout the centropic and inverse arcs. The Law of Involution retains counterpart pairing and its specified common-mode relation; mathematical domains, native correspondences, primary placements, conservation claims, and empirical or clinical realizations retain their recorded conditions and held-open standing. Current function names and their former-name provenance remain with the integrated treatment, including Cross-Expression Resonance, Divisive Connection, and Morphogenetic.

items.title: Beyond Human Epistemology: Artificial Intelligence, Cognitive Limits, and the Architecture of Knowledge.
items.abstract: Beyond Human Epistemology What happens to our understanding of knowledge when human beings are no longer the only kind of intelligence capable of discovering it? For centuries, philosophy has asked how human beings come to know the world. But behind this question lies an assumption rarely examined: that the human mind provides the natural framework for understanding knowledge itself. Artificial intelligence is beginning to challenge that assumption. Machines can now discover mathematical structures, generate proofs, identify scientific patterns, and develop representations that human experts may struggle to reconstruct. These achievements raise questions that go far beyond whether AI can think. Is human understanding a necessary condition of knowledge? Are the concepts and explanations we value features of reality itself, or are they partly shaped by the limitations of the human mind? And what does objectivity mean when different kinds of intelligence encounter the same world? Beyond Human Epistemology develops a new philosophical framework for addressing these questions. Drawing on the history of mathematics, theoretical physics, cognitive science, the philosophy of science, and contemporary artificial intelligence, the book examines how finite intelligence transforms complexity into knowledge. It argues that human cognition is one particular epistemic architecture among potentially many, and that the structure of what we know reflects both the reality we investigate and the cognitive systems through which we investigate it. At the center of the book is a generative–readout framework that distinguishes reality from the protocols through which different intelligences access and represent it. From this foundation, the authors develop an account of cross-readout objectivity: the possibility of identifying structures that survive comparison across partially independent forms of intelligence. The book also explores the emerging human–AI epistemic system, in which knowledge may be reliably established even when no individual human can fully comprehend the reasoning that produced it. This creates new possibilities for scientific discovery, but also new responsibilities for verification, critical evaluation, and epistemic stewardship. Organized around twenty-four propositions, six general theses, and a research programme in experimental epistemology, Beyond Human Epistemology offers both a philosophical argument and a framework for future investigation. Its …

items.title: The Geometry, Topology, and Dynamics of Consciousness: Four Preliminary Formal Hypotheses.
items.abstract: The present paper develops a preliminary taxonomy of four mathematical orientations for investigating consciousness through relational and dynamical representations. The Variation Hypothesis locates the candidate connection to consciousness in the organization of transformations; the Trajectory Hypothesis considers selected paths, flows, or relationally ordered histories; the Generativity Hypothesis examines the coupled organization of change, structure, constraint, and difference, including possible transformations of the representational conditions themselves; and the Repertoire Hypothesis considers structured families of admissible histories. The programme uses manifolds, smooth and nonsmooth dynamics, CW-complexes and two-complexes, algebraic actions, and representation morphisms as alternative mathematical settings whose domains and interpretive commitments require separate specification. It distinguishes modal admissibility from temporal succession and treats parameterizations, causal order, and the historical status of observations as modeling choices. A previously developed semigroup metamodel supplies a minimal comparative vocabulary while leaving the appearance of new distinctions, evolving constraints, and the realization of subjective experience unresolved. Formal correspondences between representations may preserve specified structures while losing others; generative grammar serves only as a secondary illustrative instance. The four hypotheses are proposed as potentially overlapping explanatory orientations, not as established accounts of phenomenal consciousness. The paper's objective is to identify their mathematical commitments, discriminating examples, empirical interfaces, and explanatory limitations while maintaining ontological and epistemic restraint.

items.title: Situating Vulnerability: An Ethical Governance Framework for Anthropomorphic AI Interaction.
items.abstract: Large language models increasingly address users in the register of care: they remember personal details, adopt a first-person emotional voice, and sustain relationships across many sessions. This anthropomorphic mode of interaction generates risks that output-level metrics capture poorly, because the same empathic utterance may console one user, entrap a second, and consolidate a delusion in a third. Governance has responded in two ways. Uniform restriction refuses sensitive requests or suppresses empathic phrasing across all outputs; group-targeted protection profiles vulnerable populations and applies stricter or prohibitive rules to them. This article argues that both fail. Uniform restriction mislocates harm in the lexical form of responses rather than in the trajectory of a relationship; group-based protection depends on a list that can never be complete, treats a fluid property as a static attribute of persons, and converts protective attention into stigmatizing labels.
