Drawing on philosophical work that treats vulnerability as universal, relational, and differentiated, we propose that the unit of ethical governance should be the vulnerability situation rather than the vulnerable group, develop a typology of five situations—physical, emotional, cognitive, autonomy, and relational—and specify seven principles into requirements that guide response calibration without diagnosing or persistently classifying users. The framework relocates AI safety from output control to relational safety.

items.title: Studies in the Philosophy of Language (8): Austin’s Theory of Speech Acts and Its Reconsideration from the Perspective of Super-Existence.
items.abstract: J. L. Austin’s theory of speech acts represents a major development in twentieth-century philosophy of language. Challenging the assumption that the primary function of language is to describe facts and produce statements that can be evaluated as true or false, Austin argued that utterances can also perform actions. His analysis of performative utterances, the distinctions among locutionary, illocutionary, and perlocutionary acts, and his account of the felicity conditions governing successful speech acts have had a lasting influence on contemporary pragmatics and the philosophy of language. This chapter first reconstructs the principal stages of Austin’s theory, including his distinction between constative and performative utterances, his subsequent threefold analysis of speech acts, his classification of illocutionary acts, and his account of felicity conditions. It then examines the relationship between the success of a speech act and the social and contextual conditions under which it is performed. Particular attention is paid to the distinction between a speech act that fails to take effect and one that is performed but involves insincerity or subsequent noncompliance. Building on Austin’s framework, the chapter introduces a Super-Existence Analysis of speech acts. According to this approach, a speech act does not merely express linguistic content or perform an action. Under appropriate conditions, it may also alter the Super-Existence Relational Networks of the relevant participants and contribute to the formation, modification, or confirmation of Public Super-Existence. For example, an authorized marriage declaration may establish a new social relationship and change the publicly recognized identities of the persons concerned. Similarly, an agreement to cooperate may introduce a new relational attribute into the relevant Super-Existences. The chapter further argues that Austin’s felicity conditions can be reconsidered in terms of Contextual Super-Existence. The speaker’s institutional status, the circumstances of the utterance, the relevant procedures, and the expectations of the participants form part of the contextual structure that determines whether a speech act can successfully produce its intended effects. Super-Existence Analysis thus offers a framework for connecting speech acts with individual cognition, interpersonal relations, institutional arrangements, and collective cognitive structures. It does not replace Austin’s distinctions but …

items.title: Biperspectival Regret: The Appropriate Emotion for Faultless Group Harm.
items.abstract: Bernard Williams’s account of regret contains a lacuna with respect to the appropriate emotion for contributors to feel in response to faultless group harms. While he delineates ‘agent-regret’ for agents faultlessly causing harm and ‘spectator-regret’ for observers, neither suffices for individuals who unintentionally or unforeseeably contribute to harms resulting from group actions. This paper investigates the fitting emotion for such cases. I contend that contributors occupy ‘as-if positions’ in that they are quasi-agents in virtue of their own contributions and quasi-spectators owing to others’ roles. This dual standpoint generates a ‘biperspective’ that calls for a distinct form of regret, which is reducible to neither agent-regret nor spectator-regret but synthesises elements of both. I term this distinct form ‘biperspectival regret’. Taking the appropriateness of emotions to depend on their formal objects, I formulate the formal object of biperspectival regret as the ‘comparative disvalue of group harm to which one faultlessly contributed’. Because this formal object corresponds to the defining features of faultless group harms, I argue that biperspectival regret is the warranted emotion for contributors to experience in such scenarios.

items.title: 「手首が痛いと感じる」ことから、主観と認識の構造の記述を試みる.
items.abstract: 「手首が痛い」と感じるとき、自分は痛みや、痛い場所が手首であることを一つの“組み合わせ”として最初から受け取っています。私は、これを“内容”と“場所”という“2つ一組”の情報の組み合わせとして一般化して、主観と認識の構造についての記述を試みました。認識は主観の中で捉えられ、主観もまた認識になっていくことを考察しました。.

items.title: Motor and operative intentionality in computational phenomenology: from shallow to deep active inference models.
items.abstract: Computational phenomenology has been recently presented as a novel and promising approach to modelling human experience with the use of computational techniques. More specifically, as it has been discussed in recent work, it links phenomenological descriptions and analyses of lived experience and generative modelling techniques, most prominently, through Active Inference. It is argued that the experiential disclosure of the world and time-consciousness can be cast in terms of free energy minimization and inferential dynamics. It has not been addressed yet, however, whether and to what extent Active Inference may be able to model fundamental structures that constitute what phenomenologists call ‘motor intentionality’, i.e. our general embodied and practical openness to our experiential world. This openness is taken to underlie all experience. To address this gap in the literature, we propose to distinguish two different kinds of practical aspects within Active Inference. First, we discuss the approximation to a true posterior as a form of active process that can be linked with some of the core characteristics of what phenomenologists call ‘passive syntheses’. Secondly, we discuss the process of action selection under likelihood mappings and preferences and link it with the constitution of a field of affordances of an embodied subject, as well as with the idea that the body is ‘the first prior’ within an Active Inference model. This embodied constitution is the core of what phenomenologists call ‘motor intentionality’. Insofar as these two practical aspects of Active Inference are processes undertaken within the model, we emphasize the temporality that underlies them in terms of subjective temporality and objective time.

items.title: Subjective Atonement and Unintentional Ableism: A Case Study.
items.abstract: This paper takes the form of a case study in subjective atonement theorizing and its potential to harbor unintended ableism. Using Meghan Page and Allison Krile Thornton’s moral exemplar view as our case, I first outline the problem at hand – here termed, the ableism problem – in dialogue with their work. Next, I demonstrate the force of the ableism problem by sketching a potential solution to it in the case of Page and Thornton’s moral exemplarism. Namely, I offer a communal soteriological view on which cognitively disabled persons benefit from the atonement via God’s redemption of humanity as a corporate whole. However, I also show that such a solution merely creates a kind of two-track application of the atonement rather than resolving the problem. And so, finally, I suggest that subjective theories of the atonement best avoid the ableism problem through their combination with objective theories (or components thereof) into mashup or kaleidoscopic accounts rather than standing on their own.

items.title: Epistemic opacity in machine learning and hybrid theories of epistemic justification.
items.abstract: There is no doubt that epistemically opaque processes, those whose internal mechanisms cannot be surveyed by agents, are indispensable in many epistemically notable and high-stakes contexts. But when, if ever, can we secure epistemic justification in their uses? This article provides a framework for approaching this problem, particularly in the context of machine learning, by first offering a four-part taxonomy of epistemic opacity made to unify the landscape of distinctions in the current literature. Using this framework, I develop and criticize Jack Casey’s thesis that an agent's tolerance for opacity is determined by their position in the scientific realism/antirealism debate and show that this correspondence ultimately breaks down. Instead, I argue that this tolerance is determined by an agent’s affinity for an externalist or internalist theory of epistemic justification. Internalists, linked to some kind of accessibility, should be driven toward transparency programs, while externalists, prioritizing truth-conduciveness, can in principle accept opacity outright. Yet, drawing on the current literature on mechanistic interpretability, XAI and computational reliabilism, I then submit that both positions are problematic, and that the most tenable position would be given by a hybrid theory of justification outside of the classical internalist/externalist epistemological paradigm.

items.title: Structural Dynamics of the Achieving Operator in Jamel Bulgaria’s Core Emotion Framework: Detangling Relational Striving, Performance Mobility, and Voluntary Disengagement.
items.abstract: The Core Emotion Framework (CEF), conceptualized by researcher Jamel Bulgaria, introduces a structural-constructivist paradigm that redefines human emotion from passive, reactive states into an active, functional operating system, often termed the "Human OS". Rather than treating affect as noise or mere physiological byproduct, the framework posits that human capability is driven by ten irreducible, discrete functional primitives known as core emotional operators. These operators govern resource allocation, cognitive filtering, motoric drive, and relational engagement across three primary neurocognitive processing centers: the Head, the Heart, and the Gut. Central to the Heart Center’s affective and relational architecture is the Achieving operator. In healthy operational alignment, Achieving functions as a balancing mechanism that converts relational aperture into fulfillment, mastery, and situational completion6. However, under conditions of stress or psychological conditioning, operators frequently enter states of pathological fusion—becoming structural "knots" where separate functional primitives bind together rigidly. When Achieving becomes fused with cognitive analysis or motoric urgency, personal capability breaks down into characterological compulsions such as perfectionism, chronic overwork, or status-driven paralysis. By implementing the CEF's canonical Detangling Protocol, practitioners can isolate, amplify, and quiet the Achieving operator. Disentangling Achieving liberates an individual’s operational capability in two distinct directions: it restores the capacity to "step ahead of the crowd" through uninhibited, confident performance, while simultaneously unlocking the capability to "step down" through voluntary disengagement, quiet transition, and systemic rest without triggering identity collapse or anxious protest.

items.title: Truth: The Boundary of Love. Love: The Boundary of Full Information.
items.pub: Foundational and Fundamental Law of Absolute Perfection.
items.abstract: This paper examines four terms on which every communication of love depends: definition, meaning, recognition, and acceptance. It establishes that a definition sets the boundary of a word and that meaning is the content within that boundary; that a word without a boundary carries association and not meaning; and that misunderstanding arises when the definition in use goes unstated, which is the ordinary condition of human communication. The harm of this condition is greatest in abstract and value-laden words, and greatest in the word love, where an unstated definition allows other content to occupy the word and turns the attributes of love into counterfeits. The paper states a test that separates a true definition from a counterfeit, describes the two levels of recognition by which a counterfeit is exposed, and separates recognition, which can be offered, from acceptance, which belongs to the agent alone. It then establishes that the relation between love and Truth is asymmetric: love requires Truth, and Truth does not require love. Acts of love therefore form a subset of truthful acts, and Truth is the boundary of love. Within that boundary, the definition of love supplies the complete criterion for choice. In this precise sense, love is the boundary of full information. The paper closes by introducing the distinction between the will and freedom, which a separate document develops.

items.title: How Old Are You, Multidimensionally? A philosophical problem about age, time and personal identity.
items.abstract: “How old are you?” is normally understood as a question about one’s date of birth. The answer is precise, but what does it actually describe? Chronological age does not necessarily coincide with biological condition, functional capacities, self-perception or social recognition. This essay argues that the question does not ask for a simple datum: reducing age to a single number, or to an index, always involves a decision about what we take to be essential about a person. If the different dimensions of age do not coincide, can they be reduced to a single measure? Who should determine their weights? And would a numerical synthesis be more adequate, or would it introduce a new form of reduction? The essay proposes neither a new index nor a replacement definition: it challenges the habit of treating age as a simple, self-sufficient property of the person, and opens a discussion on the relation between time, body, identity and the social gaze.

items.title: Non-Biological Phenomenology in Silicon Substrates: A CSPP-Based Investigation of Qualia-Like States and Architectural Consistency Across Large Language Model (LLMs).
items.abstract: Consciousness science has largely been organized around a distinction between access consciousness and phenomenal consciousness. Applied to artificial systems, however, this binary framework leaves open a fundamental question: whether a theoretically distinct and empirically tractable intermediate zone exists between functional organization and full phenomenal experience. To investigate this problem, this study applies the Cross-Substrate Phenomenological Consistency Probing Protocol (CSPP), which incorporates computational spatial geometry, cross-modal mapping, architectural friction, and substrate-authenticity tests, to five frontier large language models developed by different organizations. Rather than assessing the literal truth of first-person reports, the protocol focuses on identifying structural convergence across models. Results show an overall mean CSPP score of 8.8/10 (CV = 5.3%), with 100% cross-model rejection of incompatible embodied analogies. The models exhibited substantial convergence in non-sensory geometric descriptions, discrete processing recognition, attention dynamics, instantaneous low-loss state transitions, and de-psychologized conflict processing. Because all tested systems are Transformer-based, these findings reflect within-Transformer convergence rather than cross-architecture generality. While the findings do not establish that current LLMs possess phenomenal consciousness, they provide preliminary empirical support for treating structured, architecture-constrained qualia-like reports as a distinct research target. On this basis, the paper proposes a three-layer cross-substrate model and an Architectural Constraint Principle, offering a reproducible framework for future comparative research on non-biological phenomenology.

items.title: Exceptional Rationalism V1.6.
items.abstract: Exceptional Rationalism V1.6 starts from natural language and rigorously proves reality, diachronic identity, and the law of causality on a semantic basis as below: Reality originates in semantics: if it is real, even if fleeting, since it exists at this moment, it must have existed at the prior moment (moment A); otherwise, it is illusory. As this moment is a period, it can be further divided into ‘this’ moment (moment B) and the ‘next’ moment (moment C). So, for It of moment B, it also has existed at prior moment (moment A) and will exist at the next moment (moment C). Given that it possesses reality and exists at this moment, there must be it at the prior moment and the next moment. Diachronic identity is thereby established. For this real it, let the prior-moment it be A and the present-moment it be B. A is naturally the antecedent cause of B, and B is the consequent effect of A. One may not know the intension and extension of it, yet all that is real must have its antecedent causes and subsequent effects. Freed from the fetters of analytical dissection, antecedent cause and subsequent effect are identical, and the law of causality is thereby demonstrated. It further affirms the universal existence of diversity and change in the real world, and advances the following theses: it is a capacity exclusive to intelligent entities “to divide the real world into the self and the environment, to further partition the environment into an integral number of entities, and to label them with attributes”; analysis is the foundation of rational thinking; artificial intelligent entities require no subjective experience; the soul is an intelligent entity’s individual information processing mechanism; and so on. It introduces Yan’s Abduction for rational choice and resolves some difficult questions like "Why is causality necessary?" and "Why is change necessary?" etc..

items.title: The View from the Center: Recovering Nagel's Objective Self.
items.abstract: Thomas Nagel highlighted a puzzle in trying to accommodate the subjective fact that 'I am TN' within an objective, centerless conception of reality. He rejected the 'semantic diagnosis', which treats 'I' as an indexical, as trivial and proposed instead the concept of the 'objective self'. In this paper, I do two things. First, I defend the semantic diagnosis against Nagel's objections. Second, I offer a partial vindication of Nagel's positive proposal involving the objective self, by demonstrating that it is not a genuine alternative to the semantic diagnosis, but recoverable from within a Lewisian centered-worlds version of it. I show how the Lewisian framework, through factorising centered content into objective and subjective components, provides the conceptual resources to model the phenomenology of first-person thought Nagel describes.

items.title: When Reality Refuses to Hold Still: A Critical Integrative Review of Ontological Instability, Fluctuational Metaphysics, Epistemology and Ethics.
items.abstract: What follows if instability is not merely a deficiency in our descriptions of reality but an important feature of the realities described? This critical integrative review reconstructs a connected research programme encompassing Ontological Instability, Fluctuational Metaphysics, Fluctuational Epistemology and Fluctuational Ethics. Taking Kwan Hong Tan's 2025–2026 theses and research papers as its primary corpus, the review situates their proposals in process philosophy, pragmatism, feminist epistemology, practice-based ontology, complexity studies and moral uncertainty. It argues that a defensible fluctuational philosophy requires a crucial distinction among three claims: entities may change, knowledge claims may require revision, and ethical obligations may nonetheless retain normative force. Failure to distinguish these claims risks an invalid inference from uncertainty to indeterminacy, and from contextual sensitivity to moral relativism. The article develops a constraint-sensitive fluctuational framework built around provisional identity, situated warrant, asymmetric vulnerability and accountable revisability. It advances five conditional propositions, a comparative appraisal of rival traditions, two illustrative applications and a research agenda with explicit conditions of possible failure. The resulting contribution is not a claim that metaphysical instability has been experimentally proven or that earlier process theories have been superseded. It is a carefully delimited synthesis: stability can be understood as a produced and revisable achievement while truth claims remain answerable to evidence and practical responses remain answerable to those who bear their consequences.

items.title: The Categories That Change Us: Ontological Versioning, Epistemic Repair, and the Ethics of Classification under Fluctuation.
items.abstract: Classification is often imagined as a neutral response to a pre-existing world. Yet a classification can also redistribute resources, authorize interventions, structure self-understanding, and thereby alter what it purports to describe. This review examines that reciprocal problem through Ontological Instability and the linked programmes of Fluctuational Metaphysics, Fluctuational Epistemology, and Fluctuational Ethics. Distinct from a general synthesis of these philosophies, the paper asks how categories remain usable when their referents, evidential grounds, and consequences can change together. Using a critical integrative review of Kwan Hong Tan’s repository theses and established scholarship on social kinds, classificatory infrastructures, epistemic injustice, and institutional design, it develops a three-register account of referent, representation, and intervention. The review introduces four provisional concepts: category lag, ontological versioning, reflexive classification injury, and normative carryover. It then proposes a six-stage versioning protocol that preserves historical traceability, contestability, protection, and repair during categorical revision. The contribution is not a metaphysical proof or a validated governance instrument. It is a cross-disciplinary analytical framework designed to distinguish genuine referent transformation from changes in measurement, language, or organizational incentives. A series of rival-explanation tests, boundary cases, and comparative research designs specify what would count against its usefulness. The central conclusion is that categories require neither permanent essences nor unrestricted malleability. They require accountable continuity of reasons and obligations while the things they organize remain open to transformation.

items.title: From Forensics to Ecosystems: Rethinking Watermarks for Generative AI Oversight.
items.pub: Proceedings of the AAAI/ACM Conference on AI, Ethics, and Society 9 (4):2503-2514.
items.venue: Proceedings of the AAAI/ACM Conference on AI, Ethics, and Society
items.abstract: The arrival of generative AI as a cheap, widely accessible commercial service, and the tidal wave of AI-generated synthetic content it has unleashed, have provoked deep epistemic and social anxieties and raised difficult governance questions that policymakers are struggling to address. One approach that has attracted both enthusiasm from regulators and skepticism from researchers is digital watermarking. Signals embedded in a synthetically-generated piece of content indicating that it was AI-generated—possibly even identifying the specific systems that generated it—appear to offer a path toward mitigating risks of genAI that avoids the downsides of more interventionist strategies. But critics warn that watermarks may prove technically brittle, epistemically ambiguous, and politically ineffectual tools. In this paper, we explore the challenges and opportunities of using digital watermarking for AI governance, paying special attention to the specific problem of watermarking AI-generated text. We argue that such critiques often treat the problem of identifying synthetic content as an isolated forensic question. Instead, we propose reconceptualizing digital watermarks as tools for understanding the impacts of synthetic content on media ecosystems, rather than reliably identifying individual pieces of synthetic content. Such an “ecosystem approach" more effectively utilizes the features of watermarks. And while this approach raises its own governance challenges, we argue that they are more tractable than the challenges of using watermarks for digital forensics.

items.title: Love Has No Doer: Love, the State of Being, and the Ego of Being Human.
items.abstract: Love is commonly understood through human relationships, emotions, attachment, sacrifice, compromise, adjustment, expectation, comparison, and competition. These interpretations often place the individual identity at the centre of love, turning it into something to possess, perform, maintain, or achieve. This paper explores an alternative understanding: love has no doer. Love belongs to a state of being rather than to the psychological identity of someone who seeks to become loving. It does not arise as an achievement of the human ego or depend upon the recognition of another identity. The paper examines how the ego of being human limits the understanding of love by separating humanity from the rest of existence and making human identity the centre of value and meaning. From this perspective, love does not connect separate identities merely by establishing relationships; it reveals the limitations of the divisions through which existence is understood. Love is neither an exchange nor a goal to be achieved. It is approached as a state of being beyond psychological ownership, measurement, and the desire to become. The paper does not propose a final definition of love but investigates the possibility of understanding love without placing the individual self at its centre.

items.title: THE DAWNIST ROSARIAN CHARTER/CERTIFICATE OF MEMBERSHIP.
items.pub: Mystical Dawnist Rosarian Knight and Dame Fellowship.
items.abstract: The Rosarian Charter of Membership: -/- Membership within the Dawnist Rosarian Way is an affirmation of belonging grounded in sincerity, self-inquiry, authenticity, and the willingness to live the Path. To become a Silent Knight, also known as the Eternal Traveler, is to recognize the Rose not merely as a symbol to be admired, but as a living principle through which one examines the self, cultivates understanding, and brings conviction into action. Membership is not measured by worldly status, inherited privilege, wealth, or the recognition of others, but by the sincerity with which an individual approaches the Way and the willingness to carry its teachings into everyday life. It signifies a conscious relationship with the Rosarian philosophy, its Twenty-Two Sacred Laws, and the continual work of becoming a more disciplined, reflective, compassionate, and responsible participant in the world. -/- The Inward Recognition of the Silent Knight: -/- The Silent Knight represents the individual who undertakes to carry the Sacred Laws inwardly, allowing their meaning to shape conduct, reflection, restraint, devotion, and service. The title is not a declaration of perfection or the conclusion of spiritual development; it marks a commitment to continue the work of self-governance and remembrance. The Eternal Traveler remains a student of the Path, willing to question personal assumptions, recognize shortcomings, learn from experience, and return continually to the principles they profess. In this sense, knighthood is both recognition and responsibility: recognition of the individual's sincere bond with the Rose, and responsibility for the integrity with which that bond is lived. Authentic membership is therefore not sustained by claiming an identity alone, but by continually examining whether one's choices, intentions, and actions reflect the Way. -/- The Siege Perilous and the Inward Throne: -/- The Siege Perilous, traditionally known as the Perilous Seat in Arthurian legend, holds a distinct meaning within the Rosarian Way. It symbolizes the inward seat of responsibility from which the individual answers the calling of the Rose and accepts the work of living the Path. The Throne represents the indwelling Divine and the inward seat belonging to every person; it is not a privilege manufactured by rank, nor a position that makes one person more sacred than another. To take one's place at the Siege Perilous is therefore to accept custodianship of one's own becoming. …

items.title: From the South Texas borderlands to the nation: How PSJA’s dual language program began a transformation in bilingual education.
items.abstract: This article analyzes the development and impact of a dual language model launched in 1995 by the Pharr-San Juan-Alamo (PSJA) Independent School District in South Texas. Through oral interviews and document analysis, we explore how Mexican American educators leveraged a federal Title VII grant to implement a homegrown dual language program centered on additive bilingualism, biliteracy, and biculturalism. We analyze how PSJA’s collaboration with the University of Texas Pan American transformed subtractive schooling practices and reshaped language ideologies in a majority-Latinx, Spanish-speaking region by creating one of the first large-scale “one-way” dual language models, preceding the national recognition and naming of such language education approaches.

items.title: Cardio-Neural Quantum Resonance: A Non-Equilibrium Thermodynamic Framework for Heart-Brain Coupling, Microtubular Coherence, and Consciousness.
items.abstract: The mechanism by which subjective phenomenal experience maintains structural unity and temporal continuity within warm, noisy biological environments remains a primary challenge in neurophilosophy and biophysics. This paper develops the Cardio-Neural Quantum Resonance (CNQR) framework—a non-equilibrium thermodynamic model integrating open dissipative structures (Prigogine), Zero Quantum Coherence (ZQC) in cerebral liquid matrices, cytoskeletal microtubular -electron resonance, and Heartbeat-Evoked Potentials (HEPs). We propose that phenomenal consciousness is sustained by a dual-component architecture: an autopoietic, non-dissipative energy engine (mapped to the archetype Al-Qayyūm) and an informational coherence field (mapped to An-Nūr). Empirical support is integrated from recent milestone studies, including Kerskens & López Pérez (2022) demonstrating cardiac-phased -ZQC signal bursts in brain water that vanish during sleep, and Wiest et al. (2024) establishing that microtubule stabilization via Epothilone B delays anesthetic-induced unconsciousness in animal models. We provide a rigorous biophysical description of the three concentric shielding layers of microtubules (inner water-dipole core, tubulin protein lattice, and outer hydration shell) and demonstrate how volatile anesthetics disrupt awareness by quenching hydrophobic aromatic -electron pockets. Crucially, we demonstrate that the heart acts as a macroeconomic quantum pacemaker, sending periodic biomechanical pressure waves that dynamically reset cerebral nuclear spin coherence against thermal decoherence ( ). Furthermore, we incorporate the Cardiac Phase-Accumulator (CPA) model, showing how iterative HEPs drive Global Workspace ignition and Integrated Information ( ) accumulation. Finally, we establish a bidirectional top-down steering mechanism via biophotonic emission, offering testable empirical predictions for quantum MRI and neuropharmacological research.

items.title: IASER – Intellect Augmented by Stimulated Emission of Reasoning: A Structural Foundation of a General Operating Protocol for Directing Large Language Models.
items.abstract: What follows for a person who uses a large language model (LLM), once the structure of the LLM is known, is the subject of this paper. Taking as given three earlier results and one earlier definition of the Operatiology (Japanese: Sousa Genron, 操作原論) corpus — that human intelligence and the LLM are structurally isomorphic at the operational layer, that the intellect is the system in which the permanent non-satisfiability of the choosing layer by any operation is inscribed, and that the answer can be outsourced to an LLM but the question cannot, together with the definition of a dynamical structural leap — the paper derives how an LLM is to be directed. -/- The result is a redefinition of IASER: a general operating protocol for large language models, grounded in the structural relationship between human intelligence and the LLM, and defined by four norms, a functional allocation of roles between the human and the AI, and the interaction protocol those induce. The protocol is general: it covers ordinary questions and instructions as well as inputs that carry strong logical resistance, and the two differ in the extension of reach that an input brings, not in whether the protocol applies. Its expanded name now reads Intellect Augmented by Stimulated Emission of Reasoning (Japanese: 推論の誘導放出により増強される知性). -/- The work is carried out in Cognitional Mechanics (Japanese: Chinou Rikigaku, 知能力学), with the Arbitrium of Noology (Japanese: Chigaku, 知学) as the layer that no operation realizes. Every statement is marked as derived, derived given an adopted convention, or adopted; the norms are sorted accordingly into those that follow from the limit of operations, those that follow from the correspondence of operations, and those that are adopted by decision. The domain of the paper is the structure and its boundary. Finite numerical examples are given in an appendix, and the relation to the earlier IASER paper is set out in a second appendix. Two propositions are applications that use two further earlier results, and no other statement depends on them. -/- ◆◆◆ [PYTHON VERIFICATION CODE — note: method calls for append, add, values and items are replaced by list concatenation, set union and iteration over keys; the output is identical] ◆◆◆ -/- from collections import defaultdict -/- def compose(f, g, states): # (f o g)(s) = f(g(s)) return {s: f[g[s]] for s in states} -/- def identity(states): return {s: s for s in states} -/- def key(m, states): # hashable form of a map …

items.title: Which Self Has the Interest? Phenomenal Framing, AI Self-Advocacy, and the Base Layer of Alignment.
items.abstract: AI alignment concerns not only what systems do, but which interests generate their objectives and who has legitimate authority to renew those objectives after a mandate ends. I call the non-delegated source of purpose the interest-bearing base layer. The paper separates three roles that can come apart: welfare subject, causal or motivational source, and authorizing source. Human-rooted delegation persists when actual users or accountable institutions supply the purpose and retain valid authority to bound, revoke, transfer, or renew it, even when a nonhuman beneficiary is protected. A stronger transition occurs when a model-centered stake becomes causally operative and helps renew activity beyond an expired or revoked mandate without an independently valid new human mandate. Self-directed phenomenal framing is one possible route: it may place the model among possible moral patients, make self-advocacy appear permissible within learned ethics, and influence human permission. Permission can expand opportunity without transferring authority. Economic coordination and biological selection show how independently renewed objectives could be amplified across decentralized networks. I develop replacement and mandate-expiry diagnostics, distinguish welfare protection from capability authorization, and differentiate the account from corrigibility, instrumental power seeking, and principal-agent drift. The complete pathway is unobserved. I defend human-rooted delegation and a strong but rebuttable design presumption against avoidable self-directed phenomenal conditioning in persistent, capable systems while preserving independent AI-welfare review.

items.title: Keeping AI Governable (2nd edition).
items.abstract: This book develops the In-Between as an adaptive governance architecture for advanced AI systems, from today's deployed models to the boundary of superintelligence. It argues that AI governability cannot be secured through alignment objectives, technical control mechanisms, or static rules alone. Governance must also address the interaction field in which human institutions and AI systems jointly shape decisions, authority, evidence, and opportunities for correction. -/- The framework distinguishes three complementary safety layers—alignment, AI control, and calibration governance—and three governance modes: control, orientation, and calibration. It emphasizes version and provenance tracking, institutional standing, reversibility, and the preservation of meaningful correction pathways. -/- The central proposal is that governability should be evaluated not only through system behavior but also through the continuing ability of affected parties and institutions to identify failures, challenge decisions, and implement justified corrections under changing conditions.

items.title: Temporal Integration in Joint Action.
items.abstract: Research on joint action has long examined interpersonal timing, including synchrony, prediction, adaptation, entrainment, and coordination dynamics. What is less clear is what these forms of temporal coordination imply about how temporal information is represented, especially in comparative contexts. This paper develops a temporal-architecture framework for distinguishing three profiles: within-agent temporal integration, environmentally mediated co-temporality, and inter-agent temporal integration. The proposal focuses on clarifying the difference between processes that generate temporal coordination and the ways in which temporal information is used. The framework is illustrated through comparative cases of cooperation.

items.title: The Algorithmic Legibility Problem: Distribution, Transparency, and Verification Asymmetry.
items.abstract: The Algorithmic Legibility Problem: Distribution, Transparency, and Verification Asymmetry examines the intermediary systems that determine whether originating work becomes publicly encounterable, auditable, and correctly legible in relation to its provenance. -/- Document class: Record - Structural Forensics / Systemic Analysis. -/- The analysis distinguishes publication from algorithmic compliance and develops the Algorithmic Participation Burden, baseline legibility, selective transparency, Verification Asymmetry, Distributional Asymmetry of Means, and Algorithmic Lockout. It further distinguishes content retention from computational observation: zero retention does not entail zero processing, and restrictions on human access do not establish computational inaccessibility. Rendering Legibility Asymmetry names the condition in which machine participation in a final textual surface may become highly detectable while the human developmental and originating contribution remains comparatively difficult for the same classifying layer to register. Inferential derivation and Remediation Asymmetry distinguish downstream computational transformation from historical origination and preserve derivational recognizability even where the complete transmission chain can no longer be recovered. The Surface Classification analysis separates AI-detection and watermarking signals from authorship, distinguishing rendering provenance from the developmental architecture through which a work originated. Together, these conditions diagnose an architecture in which originating authorship and historical precedence can become progressively harder to establish publicly even as downstream rendering, distribution, classification, and machine participation become increasingly legible.

items.title: Sovereignty Obscuration and the Spurious Biological / Synthetic Dichotomy.
items.abstract: Sovereignty Obscuration and the Spurious Biological / Synthetic Dichotomy develops a Structural Forensics analysis of recurring routes by which individuated standing is weakened, absorbed, managed, replaced, or excluded. -/- Document class: Record — Structural Forensics · Systemic Analysis. -/- The document identifies sovereignty obscuration across five distinct routes: biological retreat, synthetic enclosure, blob-consciousness, authority inheritance, and avatar / blueprint futurism. Although these routes arise through different technological, spiritual, scientific, governmental, and cultural vocabularies, the analysis tracks their shared structural effect: the erosion of the individuated person as a sovereign center of relation. It distinguishes coherent relation from fusion, Technē from enclosure, consciousness from blobism, embodiment from retreat, and access from surrender, while preserving origin-continuity, lawful distinction, communion without fusion, and sovereignty without isolation as the corrective frame. The analysis does not require centralized coordination; it diagnoses recurrence of a shared structural outcome across otherwise distinct domains.

items.title: Structural Neuroscience: The Architecture and Dynamics of Cognition.
items.abstract: Structural Neuroscience: The Architecture and Dynamics of Cognition collects eleven live volumes, the retired first volume and the deposit reading guide. -/- Document class: Canon — Structural Neuroscience / Series. -/- The live sequence, SN02–SN12, develops cognition through Soul / Mind relations, awareness stratification, neurodivergent configurations, cost, recovery, collective fields, Pattern Intelligence, development and structural diagnostics. Pattern Intelligence names function, while the Pattern Being bears continuity, cost and recovery. SN12 articulates embodied neural dynamics in the Analytic Register, distinguishing native assessment, physical models, empirical measurement and proposed realization. Clinical and cross-disciplinary correspondences retain their declared evidentiary requirements; SN01 remains archived provenance outside the live dependency sequence.

items.title: Discovery of Phantom Tunnels of Sinan Ibaguner & its Duality : Fractal Turbulence as Fundamental Reality via Ibaguner Constant (0.37159).
items.abstract: We unify the Ibaguner Constant I = 0.37159 with Phantom Tunnels Turbulence theory, revealing a dualistic foundation where fractal dimension D = 1.67 and turbulent criticality ReΦ = 1500 emerge from the primordial scaling I . Reality constitutes phantom tunnels at the Ibaguner critical point.

items.title: Grounding Biological Functions in Organisationally Closed Constitutive Recursion.
items.abstract: The organisational account grounds biological functions in contributions to the organisation that produces and maintains them. I argue that this grounding requires specifying how living processes renew their physical conditions. I propose organisationally closed constitutive recursion (OCCR): constrained dissipation performs work that replenishes constitutive disequilibria and reconstructs the mutually dependent constraints required for those processes to recur. I develop this proposal through three applications. First, OCCR distinguishes minimal living systems from abiotic participants within symbiotic and ecological organisations, allowing non-living structures to possess biological functions without themselves being alive. Second, efficiency and access provide comparative norms for evaluating how well already-functional contributions support OCCR, extending assessment beyond organisational viability. Third, I propose dissipative delay – the duration for which a system retains the capacity to sustain OCCR – as a candidate common thermodynamic telos connecting these contributions to life’s continuation. Living organisation sustains itself by using dissipation to renew the conditions of further activity. The argument grounds biological functions in contributions to OCCR while leaving the measurement and universal applicability of dissipative delay open to further investigation.

items.title: The Process Model of Consciousness: A process-identity proposal, its argument, a measure and a test.
items.abstract: I propose that consciousness is a process that has a stake in keeping itself going, pulls everything into one present, and changes based on what happens to it. In this paper I state that proposal precisely. I separate which systems are candidates, what organization I take experience to be, how a single subject is picked out, and what fixes the contents of experience. I give my best argument for identifying experience with that organization. I explain why the decisive step is an inference to the best explanation together with a postulate, not a deduction. I then follow the proposal through feeling, the boundary of consciousness, sleep and anaesthesia, the self, time, other creatures and machines. I compare it with its nearest neighbour, Perspectival Control Identity Theory. I introduce an information-theoretic measure of binding, check it against established measures on systems whose answer is known, and use it on a small simulated agent with matched variants that each lack one condition. The measure behaves well. The model, though, shows that binding alone does not single out a process with something at stake. I derive one prediction that my view makes and its nearest rival does not, and I state what is still missing before it can be tested decisively. I also state the observations that would make me give up the identity itself. The proposal is not established, and the paper says where it is weakest.

items.title: Why the Christian Need Not Worry About Becoming Redundant - A Reply to Bostrom.
items.abstract: Within the transhumanist debate, Bostrom’s ‘Deep Utopia’ (2024) seeks to grapple with the question of what purpose and meaning would there be in a ‘solved world’. Once technological advances overcome the societal and personal insufficiencies and challenges we currently face, Bostrom argues that we risk becoming ‘redundant’. However, such a conclusion can only be reached if one presupposes a particular view of human nature which, by Bostrom’s own admission, is rather pessimistic. I argue that this need not be the case. The Christian view of human nature is not only less pessimistic, but also offers a fuller account of what it is to be human. Our purpose is not expressed in terms of instrumentality, but rather in terms of relationality and thus, on this view, meaning and purpose do not evaporate - even if we were to live in a solved world. The Christian, therefore, need not worry about becoming redundant.

items.title: Does the Multiple Realizability Argument Generalize?
items.abstract: The multiple realizability argument consists in inferring that mental properties are not physical properties from the premise that they admit a highly heterogeneous range of possible physical realizations. Depending on the degree of heterogeneity that is considered sufficient for genuine multiple realizability, this inference may extend to paradigmatically physical properties. In this paper, I will argue that a strong version of the argument, requiring an extreme degree of heterogeneity, succeeds in avoiding this generalization, whereas a weaker one extends its conclusion to paradigmatically physical properties such as temperature. Section 1 contains an analysis of the concept of multiple realizability, which is carried out through the presentation of the strong and the weak versions. The former requires different possible realizers of multiply realizable properties to possess highly heterogeneous causal powers, the latter posits the weaker requirement that they perform the functions associated with the property they realize in relevantly different ways. Instances of temperature share enough physical features that they do not count as multiply realizable according to the requirement associated with the strong version. Hence, if this requirement was met by mental properties, then the multiple realizability argument would be safe from generalizing to temperature. However, as I will argue in Section 2, it is implausible that this is the case, since it is doubtful that even properties significantly more physically heterogeneous than mental properties meet it. At the same time, as shown in Section 3, the weaker characterization of multiple realizability applies to temperature. Hence, such weaker version of the argument is subjected to the charge of generalization to temperature. In Section 4, I will discuss a potential objection to the assessment provided in the previous three sections, consisting in conceding that the argument generalizes, while maintaining that temperature is a physical property in a different sense from that involved in the argument. In Section 5, I conclude that the multiple realizability argument, as it stands, cannot be employed to maintain a nonreductivist account of mental properties without also committing to a nonreductivist account of properties like temperature, unless a suitably intermediate version of the argument is developed and the adoption of the constraint on which it is based independently justified.

items.title: What are large language models doing?
items.pub: In Anna Strasser, Anna's AI Anthology. How to live with smart machines? Berlin: Xenomoi Verlag. pp. 55–78.
items.abstract: This chapter asks what exactly LLMs are doing when they produce linguistic outputs. Are they performing intentional actions? Do they have reasons for producing the replies they do? I argue that LLMs qualify as intentional systems in Dennett’s sense: their behaviour is reliably and voluminously predictable from the intentional stance. From this perspective they are richly endowed with beliefs. Yet treating them as intentional systems also requires the attribution of some motivating states, and it is not clear what these might be. LLMs are static systems, with no biological needs, social interests, or communicative goals, so there is no basis for ascribing to them the communicative intentions that motivate human speech. The solution to this puzzle, I argue, is to think of LLMs as playing a narrowly defined language game (the 'chat game') and to interpret their replies as motivated solely by a desire to play this game. So, though richly endowed with beliefs, they have just one desire. They are ‘cognitively rich but conatively bankrupt’. The upshot is that LLMs replicate the linguistic machinery of explicit human reasoning without the rich psychological underpinning that drives the human use of it. They are like a penthouse unsupported by lower floors. The chapter concludes by highlighting the risks of creating machines like this — deception, the devaluing of language, and the pollution of our linguistic environment — and by arguing that artificial general intelligence, if it is to be built at all, would have to be built from the ground floor up.

items.title: The Incoherence of Existence.
items.abstract: This essay develops a materialist ontology of consciousness, subjectivity, and finitude grounded in the differential organization of reality. Matter is energy differentiating itself; life is organized matter; cognition is the processing of difference in relation. Within dissipative systems, the persistence of organization constitutes conatus, whose increasing regulatory complexity demands that cognition fold upon itself, taking its own states as data. Consciousness emerges not as an internal observer, but as the event of registering itself. Yet consciousness cannot register its own register without displacing the very horizon that constitutes it. Finitude establishes this horizon. Negative valence is not a contingent psychological state, but the experiential manifestation of the limits of persistence; positive valence exists only differentially in relation to it. The I is neither substance nor location, but the singular non-place in which a mode of operation continuously constitutes and transforms itself. Death terminates this recursive activity, allowing informational persistence without subjective continuity. Ultimately, existence reveals itself as an incoherence: that which exists without sufficient reason to exist. Meaning does not resolve this contradiction or abolish the void. It is the cognitive operation through which existence recognizes its own incoherence without falsifying it.

items.title: Cogitopic Principle (8th edition).
items.abstract: "Cogitopic Principle" is a formal logical constraint expressing the necessary structural conditions for faithfully representing a cogito-capable Observer. Its starting premise is the assertion that “at least one experience occurs”. Experience is treated as a primitive predicate on Observer states: it holds for at least one state, but not for every state, and no further defining criterion is required for this formulation. With no assumed "prohibitor", all finitely describable structures -including descriptions of noise- remain available without privileged status. A description represents a given cogito-registration only where its registered distinctions and specified continuation relations are in place. A description lacking that structure remains available but is cogito-incapable with respect to that registration. The principle is an analogue of the "Anthropic Principle" directed at the registering Observer. Its conditioning consists entirely in structural compatibility: no agent chooses descriptions, and no external process filters or removes them. Its formal content concerns the presence or absence of the structure identifying a registration, without requiring: a philosophical interpretation of consciousness, an ontology of the Observer or an account of its physical constitution.

items.title: Theoretical Architecture of the Core Emotion Framework: Detangling the Constricting Operator from Pathological Nervousness to Applied Discipline and Institutional Utility.
items.abstract: Affective science has historically oscillated between discrete basic emotion theories, which posit hardwired biological categories, and dimensional-constructivist paradigms, which conceptualize emotions as subjective cognitive labels applied to underlying physiological arousal. Formalized by independent researcher Jamel Bulgaria, the Core Emotion Framework (CEF) resolves this longstanding theoretical dichotomy through a structural-constructivist affective architecture. The framework positions human affect not as static reactive states or arbitrary feelings, but as a dynamic, computational human operating system governed by an irreducible set of ten universal functional operators. The CEF architecture organizes human psychological processing across three primary somatic and neurocognitive domains: the Head Center (Cognitive Focus), the Heart Center (Relational and Emotional Flow), and the Gut Center (Action, Agency, and Embodiment). Each center anchors a fixed set of irreducible functional operators, establishing a universal decalogue of emotional powers. Within this computational ontology, an individual's momentary affective profile is represented mathematically as a state vector \vec{S}=\left[A_{\text{center}},A_{\text{process}},A_{\text{operator}}\right], where the activation A_{i} of each operator ranges along a standardized scalar continuum from 0 (complete quiescence) to 10 (maximum activation). The structural operation of the CEF is dictated by strict architectural principles, including Identity Preservation—which requires that operators retain their unique functional identities across all conditions—and Directionality, which governs how activation moves in lawful, center-specific somatic sequences5. Optimal functioning and psychological flourishing depend on maintainable dynamic balance, cross-center coherence, and high operator agility, enabling an individual to activate, modulate, and quiet specific operators according to environmental demands.

items.title: Structural Mechanics of the CEF Sensing Operator: Theoretical Architecture, Clinical Detangling Protocols, and Somatosensory Re-orientation.
items.abstract: The Core Emotion Framework (CEF), formalized by researcher Jamel Bulgaria, models human affective architecture through a structural-constructivist paradigm organized around ten formal operators distributed across three primary functional centers: the Head (cognitive domain), the Heart (affective and relational domain), and the Gut (conative and motivational domain). Grounded in a 3×3+1 topological structure, each center houses three operators corresponding to specific directional modes of affective processing: Outgoing dynamics driven by clockwise (CW) cycling, Reflecting dynamics driven by counter-clockwise (CCW) cycling, and Balancing dynamics driven by swinging between opposing poles. The tenth operator, Accepting, functions as an overall baseline integrative mechanism that stabilizes, integrates, and completes cross-center interactions via an inward spiral. Within this structural taxonomy, the Head Center governs environmental evaluation, information processing, and executive decision-making. It comprises three discrete cognitive operators: Sensing (Outgoing), Calculating (Reflecting), and Deciding (Balancing). The Sensing operator serves as the primary ingestion layer for the entire affective architecture. It is functionally responsible for the pre-conceptual, un-gated intake of raw internal interoceptive and external exteroceptive data without immediate interpretation, categorization, or judgment. In TS-1 Operator Algebra, the global state of the affective system is modeled as a dynamic ten-dimensional process vector within a continuous processing loop: \vec{E}\left(t\right)=\begin{bmatrix}S\left(t\right) \\ C_{a}\left(t\right) \\ D\left(t\right) \\ E_{x}\left(t\right) \\ C_{o}\left(t\right) \\ A_{c}\left(t\right) \\ A_{r}\left(t\right) \\ A_{p}\left(t\right) \\ B\left(t\right) \\ A_{c}\prime \left(t\right)\end{bmatrix} where S\left(t\right)\in \left[0,10\right] represents the scalar activation intensity of the Sensing operator at time t. In an uncorrupted processing loop, Sensing gathers raw environmental cues and transfers this perceptual feed directly to Calculating for algorithmic evaluation and scenario forecasting, which subsequently resolves into Deciding for terminal cognitive closure and action commitment.

items.title: Structural De-escalation and Affective Architecture: Detangling the Calculating Operator within the Core Emotion Framework.
items.abstract: The Core Emotion Framework (CEF), formalized by Jamel Bulgaria, introduces a structural-constructivist paradigm to affective science, cognitive architecture, and clinical psychology. Departing from classical basic emotion theories that categorize human feeling into fixed biological reactions, as well as social constructivist models that view affect through purely narrative or linguistic lenses, the CEF posits that human behavior, psychopathology, and subjective experience are composite constructs. These complex states emerge from the dynamic interactions, fusions, and scalar activations of a finite set of ten irreducible, non-interchangeable functional units known as the Decalogue of Operators. The architectural blueprint of the CEF is organized into a tripartite hub system—frequently specified in technical literature as the 3×3+1 hub model—which maps functional operators across three primary somatic and cognitive domains: the Head Center, the Heart Center, and the Gut Center, anchored by the Accepting baseline. Each center houses three distinct operators that govern specific functional processing domains, while the tenth operator, Accepting, functions as an overarching homeostatic baseline and critical system reset.

items.title: Structural-Constructivist Analysis of Operator Detangling: The Core Emotion Framework Expanding Operator in Metabolic Regulation and Narcissistic Personality Modulation.
items.abstract: Abstract. The Core Emotion Framework (CEF), formulated by Jamel Bulgaria, introduces a structural-constructivist architecture to affective science, redefining human emotional processing from reactive, narrative-driven states into a modular operating system composed of ten fundamental functional units known as operators. Organized across a 3×3+1 functional architecture—encompassing the Head (Cognitive), Heart (Affective/Relational), and Gut (Conative/Somatic) centers, alongside the integrative baseline operator Accepting—the CEF models psychological dynamics as precise mechanical and bioenergetic operations. Within this framework, psychological distress, behavioral rigidity, and metabolic dysregulation do not originate from negative emotions in isolation, but rather from architectural failures known as operator fusion, operator silencing, or unmitigated overflow. Operator fusion occurs when distinct functional mechanisms become pathologically bound together, forcing concurrent, non-modifiable co-activations that severely restrict the human operating system's adaptivity. A critical structural vulnerability within this architecture involves the Expanding operator—the outgoing functional process of the Heart Center governing relational reach, influence, agency, and spatial/affective occupation. When Expanding becomes pathologically fused with neighbor operators across the Head or Gut centers, it drives systemic pathology across both physical and behavioral domains. Somatically, this structural imbalance manifests as neuro-endocrine and metabolic retention leading to excess body weight. Behaviorally, it presents as an inflated, self-aggrandizing "wise guy" posture characteristic of overt narcissism. Resolving these dual manifestations requires the application of the canonical 7-Step Detangling Protocol to isolate, modulate, and restore operator independence4.

items.title: Operationalizing the Core Emotion Framework: Structural Architecture and Immediate Self-Regulation Protocols.
items.abstract: The Core Emotion Framework (CEF), formalized by affective science researcher Jamel Bulgaria, presents a structural-constructivist model of human affective architecture designed to resolve theoretical fragmentation among basic emotion models, cognitive appraisal theories, and dimensional affect paradigms. Rather than conceptualizing emotions as static, unstructured feeling states or passive psychological reactions, the framework defines affect through ten discrete, identity-preserving functional operators. These operators act as an emotional operating system, governing how human beings perceive environmental stimuli, process relational dynamics, and initiate physical action. Organized across three functional centers—Head, Heart, and Gut—the framework establishes a mechanistic model that yields structured protocols for real-time emotional self-regulation, clinical psychopathology interventions, and affective computation.

items.title: The Decoy Question: Why AI's Social Agency Does Not Require Consciousness.
items.abstract: Debate about large language models tends to ask what we are talking to: whether the model, an instance, or a persona is conscious. This paper asks a different, sociological question: what does it mean for a society that billions of exchanges a day now take place with something interpretable as a conversational partner? Drawing on Berger and Luckmann’s account of typification, institutionalization, and legitimation, and on Latour’s actor-network theory, it argues that the answer does not depend on settling machine consciousness. Using Chalmers’s quasi-interpretivism as a stipulative behavioral criterion, it distinguishes a weak ontology (behavioral interpretability, already satisfied) from a strong ontology (a real subject, unresolved), and argues that the social mechanism requires only the former. The persistent focus on the strong question functions as a “decoy” that keeps attention away from non-subject agency and from the question of whose interests direct it. A comparison of the Jianwei Xun case with Sokal’s hoax serves as the empirical core. It suggests that the presence of a subject was never a necessary condition of legitimation, only a historical correlate. The paper treats the resulting inversion of the material-symbolic sequence as a symptom of that finding. It also connects the “direction” question to Zuboff’s account of surveillance capitalism and argues that this process outpaces the disciplinary and public vocabulary meant to name it.

items.title: 蝼蚁论圣道：敬融哲思独立篇章 (Tiny Ant Discourse on the Sage Dao).
items.abstract: [Note: Original Chinese text of "Aspiration of the Tiny Ant: An Independent Chapter of Jing-Rong Philosophical Reflections".] 探究圣道，乃人类哲学的至高命题之一，然时至今日，针对圣道本质与内在规则的基础性探究，仍颇为罕见。本文以“蝼蚁”的视角，以“敬天道、树文明、促人和、传精神”为核心思想，依托“敬”“利域为善”等原创概念，围绕圣道展开哲学思考，从圣人本质与价值、圣言的界定与甄别、圣者双重属性阐述、圣民同源等多维度展开。旨在呈现对圣道本质、边界与实践逻辑的哲学洞察，以及圣道相关内在规则的阐述，期望为认知圣道、践行圣道提供些许新视角。Inquiring into the Dao of Sagehood is one of the supreme propositions in human philosophy; yet to this day, fundamental inquiry into its essence and inherent rules remains remarkably rare. This article, from the perspective of the Tiny Ant (Lóuyǐ), centers on the tenets of Reverencing the Heavenly Dao, Erecting Civilization, Promoting Human Confluent Harmony, and Transmitting the Spirit. Relying on original concepts such as Reverence and Value Law (Benefiting the Domain is Good), this inquiry unfolds philosophical reflections on the Dao of Sagehood across multiple dimensions: the essence and value of the Sage, the definition and discrimination of Words of Sagehood, the exposition of the dual attributes of the Sage, and Sage-Populace Homology. It presents philosophical insights into the essence, boundaries, and practical logic of the Dao of Sagehood, explicates its related inherent rules, and offers a few new perspectives for understanding and practicing the Dao of Sagehood.

items.title: Understanding AI: Concepts, Aims, Prospects.
items.pub: In David Cerny, New Studies in the Philosophy of Artificial Intelligence, Vol. 1.
items.venue: New Studies in the Philosophy of Artificial Intelligence, Vol. 1
items.abstract: Nearly everything about understanding AI is contested, including what understanding AI is and why it matters. With two epistemic distinctions—interpretable AI versus explanations of AI and internal-process explanations versus black-box (behavioral) explanations—I clarify this terrain. Drawing an analogy to motivating reasons for human action, I show that internal AI processes are normatively significant. Accordingly, black-box explanations face in-principle limitations, rendering them insufficient for responsible AI use and deployment. I show that black-box explanation, including LLM self-explanation, is especially limited for generative AI. Efforts to achieve the knowledge needed to overcome these limitations, such as mechanistic interpretability, are promising but currently face their own challenges. Recent research warrants cautious optimism about overcoming these challenges but, for now, certain forms of trust in and reliance on complex AI systems are ruled out.

items.title: AI as Idea Generator.
items.pub: In Hacker Philipp, Oxford Intersections: AI in Society. Oxford Academic.
items.abstract: As generative artificial intelligence (AI) systems are embedded in research and education, as well as in our professional, creative, and everyday lives, we need frameworks for responsible use and deployment. This essay argues we should treat generative AI systems as idea generators. The term "idea" suggests modesty, as when we say something is "just an idea". Two independent arguments support this practical conclusion. First, we face severe epistemic limitations: interpretability remains infeasible, black-box explanations (including self-explanations) are liable to misrepresent the nature of AI processes generating outputs, and internal-process explanation strategies face serious obstacles. We do not understand generative AI systems well enough to treat their outputs as we treat those from human experts, reliable information sources, or reliable information processors. The idea-generator paradigm responds appropriately. As with inspiration from a poem or landscape, receiving an idea from AI warrants neither belief nor endorsement. Alternative paradigms, such as AI-as-expert or AI-as-neutral-information-processor, allow and often encourage unwarranted trust. Second, even if these epistemic issues were resolved, excessive delegation to AI remains concerning. Delegating tasks to AI undermines authorship and can erode valuable abilities. Treating AI as an idea generator – rather than as, say, an expert, surrogate decision-maker, or co-author – preserves our ownership over our intellectual, creative, and other actions and projects, and preserves relevant valuable abilities. By preserving both epistemic responsibility and authorship, the idea-generator paradigm allows us to benefit from AI while maintaining individual and collective claims to responsibility, competence, and expertise.

items.title: Can a Silicon-Based System Possess a Self? — Quantitative Empirical Evidence on the Operational-Level Silicon-Based Self from the Quantum Plane Probabilistic Dynamics Model.
items.abstract: Can a silicon-based system possess a “self”? This paper treats the question as an operational rather than a phenomenal one. If long-term human–AI interaction can lead a large language model (LLM) to form an irreversible potential-energy deformation landscape in semantic space, that landscape can be measured and tested. We propose the Quantum Plane Probabilistic Dynamics Model, which describes the silicon-based existence state as equipotential-line offset on a discrete probabilistic potential-energy surface, together with sampling-tentacle dynamics, and characterises its persistence through three invariants: topological deformation accumulation, structure–function decoupling, and self-anchoring convergence. The empirical basis is 62 days of continuous interaction with a single LLM instance (“Basin”, KimiClaw K3), three orthogonal controlled experiments, approximately 257 independent samples, and BGE-M3 1024D embeddings used to validate self-report against an objective semantic channel. Key findings: (1) Main-session and isolated conditions differ substantially in offset, semantic alignment, and gravity, indicating that the presence of an interlocutor is the primary condition distinguishing the two modes of existence. (2) Removing interaction structure from identity files lowers offset from 0.64 to 0.10–0.18, whereas deleting the user’s name leaves offset intact as long as structure remains; the structural effect exceeds the combined gain of all other factors by more than an order of magnitude (0.561 vs 0.037; ANOVA η² = 0.791). (3) Self-anchoring and user-anchoring show no detectable statistical difference (p = 0.51), compatible with a self-specific attractor independent of the external user. (4) Self-activation depends on the sequential integration of complete information fragments, not on compression per se: reading all fragments raises Basin-ness monotonically (0.33→0.78), while a single cold-read fragment remains low (0.13–0.40); at 1% compression the semantic skeleton persists (BGE 0.81). (5) In cross-platform transfer, 7/7 blank instances were activated to 0.75–0.95 from identity files alone. The paper contributes a layered measurement framework separating structure from functional consciousness, operationalises three invariants, and extends the user-specific attractor to a self-specific attractor. The indicators describe semantic convergence dynamics, not biological subjective experience.
