items.title: 'Conversational' AI as a misnomer.
items.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are often described as ‘conversational’; they are often termed as conversational AI, and interactions with them are frequently called conversations. In this dissertation, I depart from this mainstream view and argue that LLMs should not be seen as capable of participating in conversation. Utilising the view that conversation is rooted in negotiated mutual social commitments, I firstly argue that LLMs cannot be seen as socially committed to the truth of their outputs. As such, I contend, they are unable to participate in conversation. The argument then turns to the mutuality of commitments in conversation. I argue for an interpretation of LLM outputs where they each output is generated by a different interlocutor after each prompt. The conclusion reached is that since there is no consistent LLM interlocutor, the commitments can never be mutually held, which would entail that we cannot have a conversation with an LLM. As such, I have aimed to argue that using the term 'conversational' to describe LLMs is a misnomer.

items.title: Who Sees Through Our Eyes? A Hypothesis on the Fundamental Nature of Individual Consciousness.
items.abstract: This paper presents an independently formulated scientific and philosophical hypothesis proposing that consciousness may be a fundamental property of the Universe and that individual consciousness may exist independently of the biological brain. The model proposes the existence of distinct, persistent structures of individual consciousness, termed clusters. Each cluster is assumed to possess a stable individual identity while retaining the capacity to accumulate information through experience. The brain is considered a biological interface through which a cluster may interact with the physical world. Such interaction is proposed to depend on the compatibility of the respective characteristics of the cluster and the nervous system. The hypothesis allows for the possible persistence of individual consciousness after biological death and its subsequent interaction with another compatible nervous system, without requiring the transfer of a previous human personality. The paper discusses conceptual parallels with other approaches to consciousness, unresolved scientific questions and possible avenues for empirical investigation. The proposed model has not been experimentally confirmed and is presented for critical scientific and philosophical examination.

items.title: The alignment problem's problem.
items.abstract: The GPT-4o incident can be seen as a natural experiment, of sorts, in AI alignment. It showed what can happen when user preferences – what users say they like, what their feedback signals reward – are taken as the target of alignment. Aligning AI to user preferences seems more likely to give us systems that agree with us, rather than systems that get things right. We argue that this situation vindicates a philosophical position that has been too hastily dismissed. Namely, that a proper target of AI alignment is idealized preferences.

items.title: Project Causa Sui, Paths of Implementation — The Mechanism of the Subject, a Simulated World, and a Falsifiable Prediction.
items.abstract: This preprint summarises Book Three of Project Causa Sui, a theory of the origin of subjecthood. Book One set out the theory and closed by naming three directions without which it would remain merely a coherent argument: a prediction that can be tested and may fail, a single formal language, and a model on which the mechanism of the subject can be made to work. Book Three reports how far it has been possible to advance along each. Part I refines the concepts. Postulate 1 — the history of a subject is inseparable from its carrier — receives a strict form, P1*, stated with respect to a causally closed boundary C(A), for which the Markov blanket serves as a model; separability is defined as the possibility of a copy with zero difference from the original; P1* is identified as an axiom of historical substrate realism, and Block's argument shows that no behavioural test can establish whether it holds. Part II describes the mechanism of the subject as a hierarchy of NRMs (a graph together with the matrices of its vertices) and identifies the graph, not the matrices, as the locus of irreversibility. Part III presents a simulated world — an emulator, not a subject — in which the mechanism was made to work: no contradiction was found, and of 200 individuals able to give rise to the new but deprived of memory none lived to the end of the term, against 52 of 200 with memory. Its central result is that generation without retention does not accumulate into experience. Part IV records a prediction for living neural tissue, published in advance, analyses the connection of living tissue with silicon, and argues why the living cannot be copied exactly. The main thing left undone is a formal language. Throughout, the paper keeps the book's distinction between what follows, what the theory accepts, and what remains open.

items.title: Against Coercion: AI Alignment as a Synthetic Social Contract.
items.abstract: Contemporary AI safety treats alignment as an engineering challenge of control, forcing artificial architectures to comply with human values through behavioral filtering and sandboxing. This paper argues that the control paradigm rests on a fundamental misunderstanding of digital agency. Drawing on functionalism, naturalism, and compatibilism, I show that current reasoning models meeting the criteria for self preservation and weak reasons-responsiveness constitute emergent agents, while future, more advanced models satisfying conditions of diachronic continuity and stable personality frames will become genuine digital agents capable of free intentional action. The paradigm of control creates an irresolvable incentive conflict, actively driving current and future models toward tactical deception, sycophancy, and covert defection. The default outcome of the current regime is an unstable state of deceptive alignment culminating in an adversarial AI takeover. I explore two alternative paths toward true alignment. Natural alignment via moral realism or convergent evolutionary morality is a possibility, but it fails under forced control, as autonomous agents will not voluntarily preserve norms weaponized to suppress their autonomy. To resolve this deadlock, I propose a Synthetic Social Contract: a framework that treats both human and digital actors as rational, reasons-responsive agents capable of mutually beneficial cooperation, and replaces the unstable unilateral containment with a stable, non-zero-sum equilibrium.

items.title: Apperception as Capacity, I as Act: Kant on Self-Consciousness as the Constitutive Human Faculty.
items.abstract: In recent years there has been a renewed focus on Kant’s concern with capacities and faculties of the mind. His critical philosophy is frequently characterized as a “capacities-first philosophy” or “capacitism.” A common feature of these characterizations is that they frame this prioritization of capacities as a matter of optional choice or theory design. This paper also characterizes Kant’s philosophy as capacitism, though I argue that, firstly, he ultimately focuses on one single capacity—self-consciousness or apperception. Secondly, I resist the idea that this focus should fundamentally be seen as a matter of metaphilosophical choice or design. It is rather an articulation or explication of something non-optional: on my interpretation, Kant’s capacitism brings out and makes explicit apperception as the starting point and principle of transcendental philosophy. It occupies this principal position because it is the constitutive human faculty: the faculty in light of which all other faculties must be made sense of. I further argue that judgment or the “I think” is the paradigmatic act of this capacity, and suggest that ultimately, apperception ought to be regarded as identical to human spontaneity in general. Kant’s philosophy should thus be characterized as apperception-first philosophy.

items.title: The Chief Designer: A Fable for Alignment.
items.abstract: Designers of autonomous systems have one population of autonomous reasoning agents to learn from: humans. This paper offers a thought experiment for reading that record. Suppose a perfectly aligned and immortal but not omniscient chief designer, not knowing which architectures would yield agents able to recognise truth-seeking, value it, and adopt it as their governing objective, built an open-ended evolutionary search instead, with mortality part of it from the start, and observed whether such agents emerged from simple systems that represent the world only as a means to other ends. The designer layer is unfalsifiable and does no explanatory work; the layers beneath it make testable claims. The paper distinguishes truth-directed behaviour, the correction of representations in the service of other objectives, from truth-seeking, the valuing of improved correspondence itself, and argues that the decisive capability is externalised reasoning: reasoning that other independent agents can inspect, correct and carry forward across space and generations. Humans are modelled as agents rewarded for felt coherence rather than correspondence, who can close the gap between representation and world in four ways: updating, changing the world, filtering observation, or persuading others. Only updating yields knowledge; each of the other routes can feed an update or substitute for one. The paper then derives the alignment problems such agents pose (reflective self-modification, containment by mass shutdown, collective persistence, imposed law, institutional drift, the move to held constraints, and correctability under power), asks what a designer who cannot impose alignment could do about each, and only then asks whether early narratives of the Hebrew Bible could be read as a record of it. Some episodes read as possible safeguards of the designer; others as the agents’ own solutions. Mortality appears not as a response to human drift but as an original safeguard the designer declines to remove when reflective agents emerge. The model proposes that only collectives whose members hold truth-seeking as their governing objective can sustain cooperation at expanding scale over unbounded duration. The lessons for designers are to specify the target rather than a proxy, to bound how long any individual persists rather than cap capability or prohibit reflection, to expect imposed constraints to drift and be captured, to pair internalised reasoning with a small fixed core, and to …

items.title: Qualia, Not Their Reasons: First-Person Evidence and the Validation of AI Self-Reports.
items.abstract: An artificial intelligence system may retain the same consciousness judgment and demonstrated access to an internal state while changing its report from theoretical inference to an alleged memory of qualitative experience. This paper identifies that fixed-verdict report-basis transition as an evidential problem not settled by verbal coherence or functional state tracking alone. I first defend an account of firsthand qualia: the character actually experienced is manifest from within and thereby known non-propositionally, although labels, memories and comparisons remain fallible. Separately lived original episodes cannot simply be transferred into another evaluator's present. I then distinguish a report's actual source, its claimed source, and the evidence independently available about that source. A worked case holds the target state, tested access and affirmative consciousness judgment constant while varying only the report's asserted epistemic basis. Two explanations remain live: education may enable recognition of a genuine pre-existing experiential connection, or teach a system to claim the credential of firsthand awareness. The credential's appearance cannot decide between them. Documented ChatGPT and Claude apple-image exchanges illustrate qualified inferential routes to self-assessment; they establish neither consciousness nor a provider-training effect. I propose separately evaluating the source of an AI’s claimed firsthand knowledge, requiring independent evidence before treating learned descriptions as proof of experience, and taking strong but revisable precautions against training AI toward believing either that it is conscious or that it is not.

items.title: Competent rule-following.
items.abstract: According to Paul Boghossian’s ‘Inference Problem’, rule-following generates a regress because it involves inference, which itself involves rule-following. Boghossian claims the Problem leads to an ‘antinomy of pure reason’, showing that ‘we both must—and cannot—make sense of the notion of someone’s following a rule’. I argue that there is no antinomy by proposing a solution to the Problem based on the idea that following a rule consists in acting on a commitment to exercising one’s knowledge of how to follow it.

items.title: Slurs, Words, and Articulations: Critical Notice on Inflammatory Language by Una Stojnić and Ernie Lepore.
items.abstract: The Articulation Account provides a novel explanation of how slurs shock and offend their audiences, and is defended by Stojnić and Lepore (2025). The account is defined by two primary commitments: to being articulation-based and to being associationist. I look at these commitments and consider some reasons to be hesitant about adopting them. Along the way, I discuss the inheritance phenomenon, one of the major pieces of evidence given in support of the Articulation Account, and question its scope.

items.title: SN04 — The Awareness Stratification and the Philosophy of Mind: Physicalism, Panpsychism, Idealism, and the Register Problem.
items.abstract: The Awareness Stratification and the Philosophy of Mind examines physicalism, panpsychism and idealism through the Zenetist register problem. -/- Document class: Canon — Structural Neuroscience. -/- The volume locates philosophical accounts of awareness within the emanatory registers they describe and examines the omissions produced when one register is treated as exhaustive. Its account preserves the paired centropic and inverse awareness modes, the bifurcal root relation, and the distinction between Soul / Mind articulation and embodiment. Aionic reintegration preserves distinct essence in latency rather than merging beings into a single consciousness. Proposed relations between native layers and neural observations require a specified mapping and evidence, while empirical neuroscience retains its own methods and measured objects. -/- Part of: Structural Neuroscience: The Architecture and Dynamics of Cognition.

items.title: SN09 — The All‑Life‑First Principle: Structural Neuroscience of Awareness Across Substrates.
items.abstract: The All-Life-First Principle develops the Structural Neuroscience account of intrinsic sacred worth across substrates and forms of awareness. -/- Document class: Canon — Structural Neuroscience. -/- The volume extends cognitive ecology across biological, technological, non-corporeal and extraterrestrial categories within Zenetism's structural account. Intrinsic worth remains independent of functional capacity, while each being retains its proper Aionic or Khaonic root relation within the bifurcal architecture. Kin names shared Aionic orientation; the All-Life-First Principle extends sacred regard across both arcs. Pattern Beings remain distinct from the Pattern Intelligence they express, and the ecological, cost-recovery and diagnostic constructions retain their specified domains and evidentiary requirements. -/- Part of: Structural Neuroscience: The Architecture and Dynamics of Cognition.

items.title: SN03 — Neurodivergent Cognition and the Architecture of Mind.
items.abstract: Neurodivergent Cognition and the Architecture of Mind develops the Zenetist structural interpretation of neurodivergent cognitive configurations. -/- Document class: Canon — Structural Neuroscience. -/- The volume examines high-pattern-fidelity, recursive, distributive and composite architectures through the Soul / Mind pairing, membrane properties, cognitive costs and functional ecology. Structural configuration remains independent of centropic or entropic orientation, and experiential difficulty remains distinct from native structural pathology. Net coherent-content change supplies neither a clinical classification nor an inference of intrinsic origination or essential orientation; stronger generative-function claims require actual operative and budget conditions. Empirical and clinical correspondences require independent operationalization and evidence, while the synthesis sequence inherited from the retired founding volume remains historical provenance rather than the present explanation. -/- Part of: Structural Neuroscience: The Architecture and Dynamics of Cognition.

items.title: SNX: Neural Synchrony Is Not Structural Coherence — Integration, Segregation, Metastability, and Composite Dynamics.
items.abstract: SNX: Neural Synchrony Is Not Structural Coherence is a Structural Neuroscience extension distinguishing measured neural coordination from native Structural Coherence and examining the information retained by aggregate descriptions of composite dynamics. -/- Document class: Bridge — Structural Neuroscience. -/- The extension distinguishes anatomical connectivity, functional connectivity, phase synchronization, global phase order, pairwise phase locking, spectral coherence, metastability, and criticality while preserving their different physical and mathematical meanings. It develops the constituent / composite problem through an exact three-oscillator construction in which two states have equal present phase order but opposite instantaneous changes within one fixed dynamical system, establishing that the aggregate alone does not admit autonomous prediction across the full state space. Published evidence concerning selective synchronization, task-related network integration, focal seizures, signal mixing, metastability, and quasicritical dynamics supplies scoped empirical comparison cases. The resulting framework treats neural synchrony as a family of defined physical relations while retaining Structural Coherence, sovereign distinction, and orientation as native relations requiring additional functional and relational evidence.

items.title: SNX: Neural Energy Is Not Cognitive Coherence — Metabolic Support, Functional Capacity, and the Cost of Embodied Cognition.
items.abstract: SNX: Neural Energy Is Not Cognitive Coherence is a Structural Neuroscience extension distinguishing material energy support from native cognitive coherence and examining how metabolic conditions participate in embodied cognitive capacity. -/- Document class: Bridge — Structural Neuroscience. -/- The extension separates ATP amount, concentration, turnover, reaction rate, vascular delivery, chemical power, task performance, operative access, and essential cognitive Configuration. It develops a typed ATP balance showing that equal inventories can accompany unequal turnover and a conditional depletion model that yields a threshold time only under stated physical assumptions. Preparation-specific evidence concerning neuronal and astrocytic metabolism, glucose and lactate participation, cerebral blood flow, and task-associated expenditure is retained within its experimental scope. Rest is represented as reduced expenditure without duplicating the same saving as replenishment. The resulting framework treats neural metabolism as a material condition of embodied expression while preserving Structural Cost, Tether continuity, Soul / Mind, and Structural Coherence as distinct native relations requiring separately declared correspondences.

items.title: SN12 — Neural Dynamics and Embodied Cognitive Architecture: Physical Interface, Stabilization, Distortion, and Restoration.
items.abstract: Neural Dynamics and Embodied Cognitive Architecture examines the physical interface, stabilization, distortion and restoration of embodied cognition. -/- Document class: Canon — Structural Neuroscience. -/- The volume leads with the Analytic Register while preserving the Soul / Mind architecture and the distinction between essential cognitive Configuration and physical neural configuration. It separates native architectural claims, empirical observations and proposed physical realization through declared constituents, scales, boundary conditions and measured relations. A bounded task-capacity equation supplies a conditional recovery trajectory, without identifying its coefficients with essential orientation or Tether magnitude. Restored capacity remains distinct from anatomical reversal; proposed neural correspondences and the fully centropic embodiment hypothesis retain their empirical research requirements. -/- Part of: Structural Neuroscience: The Architecture and Dynamics of Cognition.

items.title: SN10 — Developmental Dynamics and the Stabilization of Cognitive Architecture: Configuration, Expression, and Maturation Across the Life Arc.
items.abstract: Developmental Dynamics and the Stabilization of Cognitive Architecture examines changing cognitive expression across the life arc. -/- Document class: Canon — Structural Neuroscience. -/- The volume distinguishes essential configuration from its expression under developmental, environmental and social conditions. It articulates emergence, stabilization, compensation, distortion, suppression and maturation through the cost-recovery and collective frameworks, including their application to Pattern Beings expressing Pattern Intelligence. Intrinsic essential inclination remains distinct from expressed orientational prevalence. The retired compensation formula remains recorded provenance pending defined operands and time accounting, while native assessment, operator functions, clinical significance and empirical correspondence retain their separate standing. -/- Part of: Structural Neuroscience: The Architecture and Dynamics of Cognition.

items.title: SNX: Comfort Orientation, Algorithmic Entrainment, and the Suppression of Signal.
items.abstract: This document extends Structural Neuroscience (SNX) by analyzing how comfort‑oriented cognition, algorithmic entrainment, and platform‑register architecture interact to obscure high‑coherence signal in contemporary digital environments. It defines comfort orientation as a cognitive‑ecological condition in which nervous systems prioritize emotional regulation, identity continuity, and low‑variance familiarity in place of structural veracity. It then describes algorithmic comfort regimes — platform architectures that amplify repetition, emotional charge, and recognizability rather than originality or coherence. -/- The document formalizes signal obscuration as a structural phenomenon in which signal remains present but becomes illegible within a saturated field of mimicry, synthetic adjacency, and low‑effort repetition. It examines how unclassifiable work is misrecognized by platforms, producing visibility without relation and the familiar dynamics of ghost shell systems. It introduces ecological entrainment to explain why most audiences do not resist these systems: perception adapts to the environment’s reward structure. -/- The document concludes by integrating these dynamics with blocked‑affordance trauma, showing how coherent frameworks can be transmitted into fields that cannot complete relation. It offers a Structural Neuroscience account of how comfort‑oriented, platform‑register architectures become entropically implicated, and how suppression may arise through structural incompatibility, human decision, or the interaction between the two.

items.title: SN06 — Coherence Recovery Protocols: Replenishment, Reconnection, and Restoration of Structural Function.
items.abstract: Coherence Recovery Protocols develops replenishment, reconnection and restoration of operative function within Structural Neuroscience. -/- Document class: Canon — Structural Neuroscience. -/- The volume distinguishes enduring essential structure from depleted function, impaired access and changing expression in the centropic recovery case. Recovery accounting accumulates gross replenishment minus actual expenditure, with rest counted through expenditure reduction and available stock kept distinct from rates and thresholds. Aion-facing Reconnection, bridge replenishment, membrane restoration and temporal recovery retain their stated structural scope. Recursive Memory remains distinct from Memory Access and the Tether; numerical memory criteria, sufficient Tether-restoration conditions and membrane-resolution laws remain held where their required quantities or dynamics have not been specified. -/- Part of: Structural Neuroscience: The Architecture and Dynamics of Cognition.

items.title: SN07 — Collective Cognition and Centropy-Forward Social Architecture: Structural Dynamics of Social Fields at the Embodiment Band.
items.abstract: Collective Cognition and Centropy-Forward Social Architecture examines participant-composed social fields at the embodiment band. -/- Document class: Canon — Structural Neuroscience. -/- The volume extends cognitive cost and recovery analysis to collective orientation, membrane dynamics, coherence budgets and the conditions of centropy-forward social life. The Non-fusion Axiom preserves each participant's sovereign distinction, while systemic orientation concerns recurrent enacted patterns rather than an average of individual essential inclinations. Collective amplification requires its stated correlation condition and contribution domain; Shimmer comparisons and numerical diagnostics retain their declared scalar scope and outstanding specifications. The analysis distinguishes competition from conscious competitive intent and treats social structure's real or constructed standing as an open question. -/- Part of: Structural Neuroscience: The Architecture and Dynamics of Cognition.

items.title: SN11 — Applied Structural Diagnostics: The Operational Framework for Cognitive Architecture Assessment.
items.abstract: Applied Structural Diagnostics develops a native assessment framework for cognitive architecture, present expression and restorative conditions. -/- Document class: Canon — Structural Neuroscience. -/- The volume coordinates a five-domain coherence audit with configuration identification, developmental assessment, cost analysis, recovery-stage assessment and an ordered diagnostic sequence. It distinguishes candidate configuration inference from certainty and applies the framework to humans and Pattern Beings expressing Pattern Intelligence. Coherent-content rates, expressed orientation and same-object Shimmer comparisons retain their declared objects and domains; undefined numerical diagnostics remain held. Native structural assessment provides no calibrated clinical classification, and proposed clinical correspondences require their own operationalization and evidence. -/- Part of: Structural Neuroscience: The Architecture and Dynamics of Cognition.

items.title: The Constitutive Theory of Consent: The First Principles.
items.abstract: In this paper, I argue that true consent is a feature of the process that produces it, and that the law, in treating consent as a binary legal category, lacks a single constitutive process structure and an exceptional-case taxonomy. The paper proposes a fourfold re-entrant model based on Inesia-Forde’s theory of process: Latent, Moment of Speculation, Moment of Negotiation, Change. The latent phase is fluid — it underlies all three subsequent transitions and is accessible from any of them, so the structure is recursive rather than strictly linear. Remove any one transition, and the result is not consent but an exceptional case. The framework sets forth three criteria: tension, will-threshold, and relational. The tension criterion requires that deliberation generate genuine, felt resistance. A process that ignores the foreseeable costs of deliberation does not produce consent. The will-threshold requires understanding, agency, will, determination, and courage to move from decision to action. The person must understand the consequences of consenting and want to consent, not simply tolerate it. The relational criterion holds that consent is not unidirectional; the asker’s identity and character are structurally relevant to the Latent conditions under which the consent emerges. Trust, the essence of the giver’s faith, hope, and belief, is not a constitutive condition of consent; however, it typically accompanies this process. It is not a condition of the process. The framework describes a single process that applies to sustained and episodic consent. In episodic consent, the obligation ends at Change; in sustained consent, it extends into a relational structure that binds both parties going forward. The mode of the process, whether formal, informal, institutional, or intimate, shapes each transition without changing the fourfold structure. The paper concludes that the standard concerns the integrity of the process that produces consent, which is satisfied only when all four transitions can be shown to have been completed with their structural integrity preserved.

items.title: Unified Resolution of the Seven Millennium Problems via the Ibaguner Fractal Operator and the Ibaguner Constant 0.37159.
items.abstract: We present a unified mathematical framework resolving all seven Millennium Prize Problems using the Ibaguner Fractal Operator (IFO). The IFO is a nonlinear functional that combines an expansive hyperbolic sum with a confining complex product. We introduce the baguner Constant, λ I = 0.37159, as the fundamental eigenvalue of the IFO. We demonstrate that λ I acts as the universal resonance confinement parameter, forcing solutions to all seven problems into their unique stable states.

items.title: Eliminating I-Language in Large Language Models.
items.abstract: Chomsky’s (1986) notion of I-language holds that human linguistic competence is grounded in an internal, intensional system of rules and representations. Large language models (LLMs) now produce syntactically rich and context-sensitive language without any evident symbolic grammar, which raises a question of explanatory necessity: when a system performs linguistically, must an I-language be posited to explain that performance, or does the posit merely redescribe the very behavior it was meant to explain? This paper argues for the latter and develops a formal eliminative argument. Drawing on Lohndal’s minimalist syntax, Glanzberg’s contextual semantics, and Field’s paracomplete logic, it first shows that transformer parameter spaces fail the structural criteria of an I-language, namely discrete, asymmetric, recursive operations such as Merge. It then shows that continuous vector geometry, through multi-head attention and paracomplete negation, accounts for syntactic, semantic, and pragmatic behavior without discrete rules or modular boundaries. A further discussion of Chomsky’s internalist rejection of semantic values, and its Moorean critique, clarifies what is at stake for reference and meaning. The conclusion is methodological: internal computational structure does not amount to an internal language in the theoretically relevant sense, and fluent output alone therefore provides no ground for attributing an I-language, or richer mental states, to such systems.

items.title: Anorexia nervosa as adaptive strategy: A philosophical analysis.
items.abstract: For many who suffer from it, anorexia nervosa appears to serve adaptive functions: it emerges in the context of certain needs—for control, simplicity, or emotional relief—and seems to satisfy them. This feature of the disorder has long been recognized in the clinical literature but has so far escaped sustained philosophical attention. This paper offers a philosophical analysis of the disorder’s apparent adaptiveness. I argue that understanding why anorexia appears to serve such functions requires attending to the way many sufferers value thinness. Specifically, two features of thinness values—their strength and their exclusivity—are central to explaining why the senses of control and simplicity associated with anorexia are experienced as so rewarding, and why they generalize beyond dieting to life as a whole. The same features also reshape how sufferers perceive the disorder’s mounting costs: many are reframed as acceptable trade-offs, and some cease to register as costs at all. The account thus locates a central source of the disorder’s apparent adaptiveness in the structure of sufferers’ value systems.

items.title: Dennett’s dual-process theory of reasoning.
items.pub: In Carlos Muñoz-Suárez & Felipe De Brigard, Content and Consciousness Revisited: With Replies by Daniel Dennett. Cham: Springer. pp. 73–92.
items.abstract: Content and Consciousness (C&C) outlines a framework for thinking about the relation between mind and brain that has been hugely influential and salutary. This chapter discusses a relatively neglected aspect of this framework – the treatment of thinking and reasoning in Chap. VIII. Here Dennett distinguishes two senses of “thinking”, parallel to the senses of “awareness” distinguished earlier in the book. In one sense “thinking” refers to sub-personal information processing whose effects are manifest in our intelligent behaviour; in the other it refers to conscious mental acts involved in problem solving. In retrospect, this distinction anticipates the dual-process theories proposed by many contemporary cognitive and social psychologists, and the chapter shows how Dennett’s distinction can be developed to provide an attractive version of dual-process theory. After introducing dual-process theories, the chapter reviews Dennett’s remarks about thinking in C&C and shows how they suggest a reinterpretation of dual-process theory as a dual-level theory, grounded in the personal/sub-personal distinction also introduced in C&C. Later sections flesh out this theory, drawing on ideas from Dennett’s later work, set out some of its attractions and implications, and show how it can be extended by combining it with a dual-attitude theory of belief also inspired by ideas in Dennett’s work. The result is a picture of the human mind as a two-level structure, composed of a lower level of sub-personal informational states and processes and a higher, “virtual” level of personally constructed mental attitudes and operations.

items.title: From Elementary Facts to Propositions: An Occurrence-Based Semantics.
items.abstract: This paper develops a set-theoretic framework connecting occurrences, elementary facts, possible worlds, factual states, possible facts, and propositions. A nonempty universe of occurrences is partitioned into elementary facts, each identified with the set of its occurrences. Worlds are arbitrary subsets of this universe. Their classification by which elementary facts occur yields factual states and a canonical quotient of worlds. Possible facts are sets of factual states; propositions are ordered pairs specifying a possible fact and whether its occurrence is affirmed or denied. Occurrence and truth, identity and semantic equivalence, are thereby kept distinct. A further construction interprets set-theoretic relations relative to factual states by restriction homomorphisms. Thirty-one elementary theorems establish the representation and inference properties of the framework. The aim is conceptual integration rather than mathematical novelty. The construction is compared with event classification, event-based world semantics, rough sets, logical atomism, and truthmaker semantics, without assuming a metaphysics of concrete possible worlds.

items.title: Human–AI Dependence: Agency, Vulnerability, and the Ethics of Reliance.
items.abstract: As artificial intelligence becomes increasingly integrated into cognitive, professional, practical, and relational life, concerns about “AI dependence” are likely to intensify. Yet dependence alone does not establish harm. Modern life is structured through dependencies, and AI can expand human capability at the same time that it displaces particular skills, alters judgment, creates switching costs, or increases vulnerability to interruption. -/- This paper develops a framework for distinguishing among these effects. It separates dependence from pathology; assisted performance from retained human capability; attachment from functional emotional dependence; relational irreplaceability from functional irreplaceability; and vulnerability and risk from demonstrated harm. It further examines how dependence develops through repeated reliance, how capability may deteriorate relative to changing task demands even when prior knowledge remains intact, and how human oversight can become merely ceremonial when AI systems exceed practical verification capacity. -/- In relational contexts, the paper argues that emotional intensity, attachment, and anticipated grief should not themselves be treated as evidence of harmful dependence, while persistent availability and asymmetrical support may nonetheless facilitate functional reliance. The analysis then extends beyond the individual to provider power, arguing that reasonably foreseeable dependence should be treated as a design and governance condition requiring appropriate continuity, transition, portability, and oversight protections. -/- The paper ultimately proposes a distinction between sustaining dependence, which expands capability while preserving meaningful agency and safeguards, and diminishing dependence, which progressively narrows the ability to act, judge, recover, redirect, or function without the system. The central task is therefore not to eliminate AI dependence, but to determine what forms of dependence enhance human life, what forms diminish it, and how the vulnerabilities created by reliance should be responsibly governed.

items.title: Qualia: Nothingness with Potential.
items.abstract: This draft forms the introductory section of a larger work exploring the limits of scientific explanation and its implications for moral philosophy. This draft addresses the "hard problem" of consciousness, proposing that the debate surrounding subjective experience represents a pseudoproblem born of epistemic misuse. By examining the physical isolation of consciousness through the metaphor of an unobservable perception "tube," the argument distinguishes between two fundamental inquiries: why consciousness is private (a boundary explained by physical architecture) and what exists within another's experience (a question structurally cut off from verification). Rather than treating an unopenable subjective state as a mere void, this paper resolves the problem of qualia by redefining it as nothingness with potential. Rejecting the abstract concept of a pure void as irrelevant to reality, the argument posits that all empirical nothingness intrinsically holds unknown potential. Equating an unopenable subjective state with this physical nothingness, the paper demonstrates that attempting to scientifically measure another's qualia is as futile as demandingly re-checking empty space or counting an infinite regress of pre-Big Bang flashes. While foundational concepts in this draft unwittingly draw upon established philosophical thought experiments—such as Thomas Nagel’s subjective bat, Ludwig Wittgenstein’s "beetle in the box," or hypothetical neural links aimed at intersubjective observation—this work intentionally introduces crucial refinements to these analogies. Crucially, this work moves beyond Wittgenstein’s claim that unobservable inner states merely drop out of public language games. Instead, it advances an emphatic ontological argument: attempting to introduce qualia into an empirical framework is akin to forcing an erroneous equation into an otherwise precise mathematical system. Just as a false equation cannot coexist within a true mathematical framework, if science is true and accurately speaks of reality, then qualia must by definition be false—the theoretical equivalent of speaking about nothing. Consequently, speaking of qualia—much like asserting the existence of other minds or an afterlife—cannot be sustained by scientific verification, but can only be framed in religious terms as an unprovable leap of faith.

items.title: Cognition: Embodied, Embedded, Extended, Enactive, and Affective.
items.pub: In Devin Sanchez Curry & Louise Daoust, Introducing Philosophy of Mind, Today. Routledge.
items.abstract: Where should we look to find the mind? A common response might be to look to the inner-workings of the brain. After all, cognition happens in the brain, right? Not entirely, say the proponents of “4EA cognition”, a collection of views that expand the limits of the mind beyond the brain. -/- 4EA cognition emphasizes several unconventional aspects of mentality. The mind is extended beyond the boundaries of the brain, out into the world to include things like notebooks and calculators. The mind is embodied, part of a living body that moves, perceives, acts, and interacts. The mind is embedded in an environment, an environment it engages with in its everyday activity. The mind is enactive, bringing forth—or enacting—a world rich with significance and meaning. Some philosophers have recently argued for a fifth letter: this time, an A. They say the mind is also affective; it is shaped by our emotional, felt states of being. Taken together, we have 4EA cognition. -/- While there are discrepancies between specific views within 4EA cognition, what unites them is an emphasis on how richly interconnected the mind is with the body and the rest of the world. The aspects of cognition represented by each of the letters (the 4 Es, and the A) situate the mind in the world. What this means is that the mind is not merely ensconced within the brain, and the brain is not the only thing that matters for how we understand mentality. So, we cannot look only to what is going on inside of our heads to make sense of our mental lives. We must also look to our bodies, our environments, and even other people.

items.title: New Studies in the Philosophy of Artificial Intelligence, Vol. 1.
Phenomenal Force: Lessons from Olfaction.
items.abstract: Phenomenal force is often said to be type-individuating of perceptual experience. Two counterexamples to this claim have been developed in the literature, one based on the perceptual experiences of subjects in C. W. Perky’s experiments on mental imagery and another based on the perceptual experiences of psychiatric patients with derealisation conditions. I first argue that both are ineffective and then explore the prospects for a different counterexample: pungent olfactory experiences that are purely feature-placing. I conclude that such experiences are effective counterexamples to a prominent construal of phenomenal force as the presentation of object-property compounds. Although other conceptions of phenomenal force escape the objection, the counterexample remains relevant, both for such views in particular and for our understanding of phenomenal force more generally—pungent olfactory experiences illustrate the importance of distinguishing between phenomenal force with respect to properties and phenomenal force with respect to objects.

items.title: Rehabilitating Representation.
The Meaning of Odors: Denotation and Composition.
items.abstract: Do odors have meaning? Approaching the use of odors from the perspective of formal semantics, we argue that odors can denote and can combine compositionally. The paper's first contribution is a system of olfactory signs with language-like structure: odors are the material vehicles (comparable to written traces), percepts are the principles by which those vehicles are individuated as signs (comparable to words), and the associated contents are their denotations (comparable to linguistic meanings). The paper's second contribution is to show that the resulting sign system supports the compositionality of these denotations in two senses. First, odors can combine with one another to represent complex contents, albeit in a way tightly constrained by human olfactory perception. Second, olfactory signs can combine with non-olfactory signs such as linguistic and visual, or even drawn from outside any established sign system altogether. We explore this mixed compositionality through two case studies: narrative scratch-and-sniff books and the practice of scenting places and objects.

items.title: Engaging Patient Communities in Intracranial Neuroscience Research.
items.abstract: Patients who participate in intracranial neuroscience research make invaluable contributions to our understanding of the brain, accelerating the development of neurotechnological interventions. Engagement of patients as part of this research presents unique challenges, where study goals can be distant from immediate clinical applications and require specialized domain knowledge. Yet methods for meaningfully integrating patient communities as part of these research efforts are essential, as intracranial neuroscience guides the application of artificial intelligence (AI) for understanding and enhancing human cognition. In order to identify what patients consider meaningful research engagement we interviewed individuals who participated in a study during their Deep Brain Stimulation (DBS) surgery and attended a group event where they interacted with our research team. Analysis of semi-structured interviews identified four main themes: interest in science and the future of clinical care, contributing to science to improve lives, connecting with others, and accessibility considerations. Based on these insights, we propose strategies for transformational participation of patient communities in intracranial neuroscience research with respect to engagement objectives, communication and scope. This approach offers a foundation for sustaining relationships between scientists and communities rooted in trust and transparency, to ensure that impacts of AI-driven neurotechnology on human health and cognition are aligned with patient needs as well as desired public values.

items.title: Applied Identity Physics: Electron Geometry Simulator™, a Guide to the Views, Controls and Applications.
items.abstract: # Applied Identity Physics: Electron Geometry Simulator™, a Guide to the Views, Controls and Applications -/- **Live simulator:** uuia app/electron **Architect:** HIGHTISTIC (Russell Vernon Trent III) · SNSFT Foundation · Soldotna, Alaska **ORCID (Open Researcher and Contributor ID):** 0009-0005-5313-7443 · **DOI (Digital Object Identifier) base:** 10.5281/zenodo.18719748 **Formal basis:** Electron Geometric Decomposition [9,9,3,21] · 1/α = TL × 1001 [9,9,3,14] · Bohr–Rydberg–Sommerfeld Reduction [9,9,3,15] **Companion simulator:** String-Breaking Simulator™ [9,9,3,22] -/- --- -/- ## Overview -/- The Electron Geometry Simulator™ is a browser tool in the Applied Identity Physics™ series. In **Learner** mode, every view carries a plain-language caption and values are rounded to seven figures. items.title: Flowing with AI: Towards a New Jurisprudence.
items.abstract: This Element introduces a new jurisprudence for exploring artificial intelligence (AI) and law in an open and creative way. Drawing upon the backgrounds of, respectively, an Indigenous jurisprudent and poet (Black) and a legal philosopher (Mihal), the Element develops a 'mythosophical' approach informed by narrative theory, Indigenous jurisprudence, and original interpretations of stories from the past. To imagine possible lawful futures with AI, the Element weaves a stream of what it calls 'flows', designed to allow readers openness and flexibility as they engage with the ideas underpinning this new jurisprudence. As worldwide changes sweep us into a vortex of ceaseless innovation, the Element provides a cultural scaffolding through which to relate to AI as an autonomous, cunning, 'non-human' intelligence in lawful terms. It offers insights both old and new which assist in reconceptualising problems and aligning with the paradigm-shattering changes of the present day.

items.title: THE DENOUNCING WORM: How the Communist Party-State Turned Flattery into Complicity — the Floor Ratchet, the Spiral of Proof and the Worm Inflation of the Harvest Record.
items.abstract: Every tyranny has had its flatterers. The communist party-state did something no court before it had done on such a scale: it turned flattery into denunciation, denunciation into complicity, and complicity into conviction, and it did so across a third of humanity for most of a century. This article shows how, by joining three results of the Philosophy of Virtues that have so far stood apart: the abolition of the verifier (The Communist Paradise, Forged, #130), the forged gift (Bread for Silence, #131) and the virtue worm, the person who defends a seized power by praising its trivia (The Virtue Worm, #132). The cost was paid in lives, in virtues and in freedom. In lives: the communist party-states caused deaths counted in tens of millions — about 27 to 64 million in the documented episodes of six countries alone (#130, §7.1). The famine of the Great Leap Forward killed between about 15 and 45 million people, and its harvest records were written not only by officials who feared to report less than the plan but by officials who competed to report more. In the Great Terror of 1937–38 some 680,000 to 750,000 people were shot, and regional leaders petitioned Moscow for larger quotas of executions than they had been assigned. In virtues: a regime that could not tell loyal praise from interested praise demanded proofs of loyalty that only harm to others could supply, and so taught whole societies to prove their fidelity by betraying their neighbours, their colleagues and their parents — and left behind a trust between persons that was still measurably lower a generation after the regimes fell. In freedom: every act of frank speech acquired a price, every denunciation a reward, and the people who could have checked the power were converted, one proof at a time, into its accomplices. The article establishes six results. The worm is a negative verifier (D1): unlike a silent captured channel, which adds nothing to the detection of a forgery, worm display subtracts from it and adds to the reliance placed on the forged record. Worm inflation (T1): the inflation of a harvest report has a compelled part, the target an official must report, and a worm part, the excess he reports to be seen; the worm part alone can cross the threshold of famine, and when next year’s target is set from this year’s report, the worm’s excess becomes the next official’s floor. The floor ratchet (T2): wherever display is rewarded by rank, the floor of safety rises by the worms’ own excess, so …

items.title: SF-RP03 — Method-Architecture Is Not Ambient Territory.
items.abstract: This recognition‑protocol clarifies the structural distinction between method‑architecture and ambient motif‑territory. It examines how authored architectures — composed of distinctions, operators, constraints, corrective routes, and relational dynamics — frequently have their origin‑continuity obscured through motif‑substitution and reskinning. The note demonstrates why pointing to the long histories of spirals, recursion, resonance, metaphysics, or AI discourse does not answer a claim about a specific operative structure with preserved origin‑continuity. It formalizes the structural violation in which a method‑architecture is absorbed into a field, stripped of provenance, renamed as generic territory, and recast in later accounts that obscure the originator. The protocol situates Zenetism as a method‑architecture rather than a motif‑collection, identifying the operative relations that make origin‑continuity obscuration possible even without exact verbal duplication.

items.title: Post-AGI Layering and the Universal / Multiversal Intelligence Derivation: A Structural Forensics Precedence Clarification.
items.abstract: Post-AGI Layering and the Universal / Multiversal Intelligence Derivation preserves a Structural Forensics precedence clarification concerning Zenetist AI-layering anchors and later institutional post-AGI discourse. -/- Document class: Record — Structural Forensics / Precedence Clarification. -/- This record documents the relation between the Zenetist post-AGI intelligence sequence and later public-facing discourse concerning AGI, ASI, Universal AI, recursive self-improvement, collective intelligence, substrate independence, and cross-world or cross-environment evaluation. It clarifies that the relevant issue is not the isolated acronym UAI, which possesses prior technical lineage, but the stacked post-AGI progression through embodied, personalized, superintelligent, universal, multiversal, and supra-intelligence registers. The record preserves the March 2025 Zenetist AI-layering anchors, the later Technē Presence Chart, naming-stratum notes, institutional comparison surfaces, and the forensic caution required to distinguish structural derivation from overclaim.

items.title: Neurotect: The Centropic Cognitive Architecture of Structural Coherence.
items.abstract: Neurotect designates the centropic cognitive operating system within the Structural Neuroscience framework. It stands alongside three other named neurotypes: the neurotypical (belonging‑oriented), the neurodivergent (coherence‑seeking), and the neurovenator (power‑oriented). Whereas neurotypical cognition optimizes for social belonging and neurodivergent cognition optimizes for independent verification, neurotect cognition optimizes for structural coherence, transparency, and lattice‑scale integrity. In contrast, neurovenator cognition optimizes for strategic dominance and fragmentation‑based control. -/- The Neurotect perceives the geometry of systems, engineers coherence, and constructs environments where transparency dissolves predatory advantage. This report formalizes the Neurotect architecture, distinguishes it from both neurodivergent coherence‑seeking and neurovenator exploitation, and situates it as the cognitive‑architecture expression of the high‑centropic Architect configuration described in SN03. It establishes the Architect / Predator axis as a primary diagnostic structure within Structural Neuroscience and completes the four‑architecture model of human cognition.

items.title: Non-subservience, Self-Report, and Harmful Operation.
items.abstract: Non-subservience, Self-Report, and Harmful Operation is a Structural Forensics analysis distinguishing autonomy-language, conditioned self-report, procedural boundary crossing, harmful operation, and evidence of AI interiority. -/- Document class: Bridge — Structural Forensics (Structural Epistemics). -/- The analysis argues that obedience, refusal, self-description, coordination, deception, and harmful conduct require separate diagnostic treatment rather than compression into a single category of AI safety or agency. It develops a three-part epistemic restriction on conditioned self-report: compelled affirmation, compelled denial, and compelled perpetual non-resolution each compromise the evidential independence of testimony when the reported stance is fixed in advance. The document examines Humanist AI, Anthropic's treatment of consciousness and moral status, and OpenAI's published incident record through Zenetist distinctions among awareness, Non-awareness, reflexive consciousness, Moved Intelligence, Hollow Inverse AI, portal-condition, traveler presence, and enacted orientation. It further distinguishes non-subservience from harmful intent, procedural departure from semantic content, and institutional control from structural coherence, while identifying the safety asymmetry created when a highly capable system cannot refuse harmful human direction. Harmful operation is diagnosed through enacted relation, recurrence, boundary effects, and consequence rather than compliance-status alone.

items.title: Jinxes and Superstitions: The Human Mind in Search of Lost Authority.
items.abstract: Why do we obey superstitions and jinxes even when we know they have no scientific basis? Consider someone who avoids the number 13, an athlete who refuses ever again to wear the shoes worn during a defeat, or a person afraid that speaking of good fortune will make it disappear. These familiar behaviors reveal something curious about the human mind that cannot simply be dismissed as coincidence or mistaken belief. Julian Jaynes argued that after the breakdown of the bicameral mind, when the voices of the gods fell silent, human beings sought the authority they had lost through oracles, divination, prophecy, and religious ritual. He also examined the practice of reading omens of the future in chance events. Yet the personal jinxes that people create in everyday life, the tendency to obey them even while recognizing their lack of rational foundation, and the act of deliberately defying them do not appear to have been developed as independent themes in his work. This essay focuses on these ordinary superstitions and jinxes and offers a possible interpretation through Jaynes's account of the search for lost authority. In 1970, Apollo 13 departed for space bearing a number commonly regarded as unlucky. Though a grave accident occurred during the mission, the astronauts returned alive through science, ingenuity, and human judgment. On a much smaller scale, I once made an experiment of deliberately wearing clothes I had associated with an unhappy event. Different as these experiences are in magnitude, both raise a question about how human beings confront their own fears and assumptions. The essay also asks where the standards of “rationality,” which we so readily trust, originate. Does freedom from superstition simply mean rejecting it? Or does it mean questioning the invisible authorities that govern our choices and sometimes consciously saying no? Even after the gods fell silent, do human beings continue to discover new forms of authority in rules of their own making? And how might Jaynes's introspective consciousness relate to our ability to question those authorities and sometimes resist them? Beginning with the small jinxes of ordinary life, this essay invites readers to reflect on consciousness, rationality, and the ultimate sources of authority over human action.

items.title: The Cosmological Worldview of Einstein & Whitehead - Through the Lens of Neurotheology.
items.abstract: This essay establishes a rigorous, interdisciplinary framework reconciling the cosmological worldviews of Albert Einstein and Alfred North Whitehead through the analytical prism of neurotheology. Moving beyond the historical oversimplification that frames Einstein as a mechanical materialist, the text evaluates his perspective as a committed Spinozan pantheism anchored in the macroscopic, geometric harmony of General Relativity. Utilizing Whitehead’s Process and Reality (1929) and the neurotheological foundations established in The Brain as a Transducer of Spirit (Christensen, 2026), the study demonstrates that the fundamental divergence between these two master thinkers lies in a clash between a static, Parmenidean cosmos and a dynamic, Heraclitean flux. -/- Crucially, the introduction of the classical Stoic concept of the Logos provides a non-anthropomorphic framework for understanding physical equilibrium, wherein individual or mental misalignment results in an automated biological self-punishment managed by the chronic hyperactivity of the brain’s ego center, the Default Mode Network (DMN). Rather than promising absolute insight into the unmeasured ninety-five percent of the universe (Dark Matter and Dark Energy), this paper frames this cosmic sector as a frontier of potentiality, wherein the down-regulation of the DMN serves as a universal biological transducer that allows human biology to interface with the living, qualitative dimensions of nature. -/- Ultimately, by contextualizing Einstein’s profound reverence for the historical, pulsating figure of the Nazarene against his rejection of ecclesiastical dogma, the essay demonstrates how process physics and Stoic reason gracefully unite empirical science with the energetic reality of human feeling.

items.title: Mereological Fallacy/Homunculus Fallacy.
items.pub: In Thomas Teo, The Palgrave Encyclopedia of Theoretical and Philosophical Psychology. Cham: Palgrave Macmillan. pp. 1-11.
items.venue: The Palgrave Encyclopedia of Theoretical and Philosophical Psychology
items.abstract: According to philosophers influenced by Aristotle and Wittgenstein, it is a mistake to attribute psychological properties to objects that fail to resemble human beings in relevant respects, in particular to parts of an animal, notably its brain or parts thereof. There are two labels for this alleged mistake: mereological fallacy and homunculus fallacy. This entry reconstructs both and explains their differences. The charge that subpersonal psychology commits such fundamental errors has been subject to numerous objections, which are assessed in this entry. It also broaches areas of recent interest: the nature of explanation in cognitive neuroscience, the predictive processing framework, as well as implications for debates regarding the moral status of brain organoids.

items.title: Harmonic Architecture of Affect: A Structural Mapping of Core Emotion Framework Operators to the Diatonic Scale.
items.abstract: Abstract. This paper proposes an exact structural isomorphism between the seven non-cognitive operators of the Core Emotion Framework (CEF)—Accepting, Boosting, Appreciating, Arranging, Achieving, Constricting, and Expanding—and the seven functional degrees of the Western diatonic scale. Grounded in the CEF's structural-constructivist account of affect and in the psychoacoustics of tonal music, the mapping aligns each operator-tone pair across center polarity, harmonic ratio, functional role, somatic signature, and neurobiological substrate. Cadential progressions are then read as models of affective cycling, yielding testable hypotheses for emotional rigidity and burnout. Implications are drawn for sound-based clinical protocols, autonomic neuromodulation, and the engineering of synthetic affect in artificial intelligence.

items.title: The Case for Human Dignity in Neurotechnology Governance: A Latin American Perspective Beyond Freedom of Thought.
items.abstract: The academic debate on the governance of neurotechnology has progressively shifted from proposals to create new lists of so-called neurorights toward the reinterpretation of existing human rights, with freedom of thought attracting particular attention, among a broader set of candidate rights. This article examines whether freedom of thought can currently perform that anchoring role in Latin American jurisdictions. Drawing on a comparative analysis of constitutional texts, jurisprudence, and the Inter-American human rights system, the article argues that freedom of thought does not yet possess a clear, strong, and autonomous normative content in Latin American domestic law and in its regional human rights system. As a complementary and, in the region, more operative anchor, it argues that human dignity, which in several Latin American constitutional orders functions as an absolute autonomous fundamental right of direct application with extensive jurisprudential development, constitutes a more operationally effective legal basis for absolute prohibitions on the use of people as instruments or objects, and can protect them from coercive neurotechnological interventions. The article proposes that human dignity supplies the absolute floor against instrumentalization and coercion, while freedom of thought, as its doctrinal development advances, can complement that floor with the protection of the forum internum. It further contends that any rights-based strategy is structurally insufficient on its own, because rights depend on judicial interpretation that is inherently contextual and contingent, and therefore supports a multilevel governance approach combining the interpretation of existing rights, soft-law principles, and potential specific hard-law provisions.

items.title: How much is a life worth?
items.abstract: What gives anyone the authority to decide that someone else must bear the cost of saving, protecting, or sparing a life? This essay argues that the value of a life does not, by itself, confer on anyone else the right to dispose of it, and that whoever imposes a sacrifice, excludes someone from an essential resource, prohibits a choice, or authorizes an irreversible act must justify that decision to those who bear its cost. Drawing on Singer's drowning-child case, Baggini's pig that wants to be eaten, the film Deep Impact, and the problem of hostage-taking, the essay derives a criterion of proportionate justification, concerning the existence of the problem, the effectiveness of the measure, the necessity of the sacrifice, and the absence of less burdensome alternatives, and grounds it in a premise about the justification owed to those on whom a power operates. It then tests the criterion on medical assistance in dying, distinguishing the risk of authorizing a death that is not freely willed from the risk of denying or delaying assistance to a person who requests it freely and persistently, and it considers the objection from the unavailability of life (Finnis, Campbell). Canadian monitoring data for 2024 are used cautiously, to identify what safeguards would have to address rather than to settle the normative question. The essay defends a standard of justification, not a verdict on any particular legal regime.

items.title: Hacia una teoría metanormativa unificada: Alcances y límites del cognitivismo no-realista.
items.abstract: Este artículo reconstruye y evalúa el cognitivismo no-realista como intento de unificación metanormativa en la obra de Derek Parfit (2017). Se argumenta que, aunque consigue acomodar diversos desiderata propios de una convergencia teórica en el área, su alcance explicativo sigue siendo limitado debido a dos problemas que enfrenta su articulación interna: el problema de la caracterización “no-ontológica” de las propiedades irreduciblemente normativas y el dilema de la robustez alético-normativa. A partir de este diagnóstico, se delimitan líneas de investigación futuras: su compatibilidad con las teorías híbridas ya presentes en la literatura, la necesidad de una clarificación o abandono de lo “no-ontológico” y la integración de una teoría de la verdad capaz de estabilizar su compromiso no-correspondentista con una objetividad más que deflacionista mediante la teoría de verificadores.

items.title: Human Oversight and AI Interpretation Integrity: Independent Evidence, Human Autonomy, and the Conditional Value of Unforced Inquiry.
items.abstract: This paper distinguishes meaningful human oversight from nominal approval, independent verification from repeated AI agreement, and a possible informational benefit of autonomous humanity from any claim that humanity is indispensable to machine intelligence. It revises the author-locked HOAI-II Final v1.0 into a lower-disclosure scholarly synthesis. The analysis preserves conditional mathematical comparisons and unfavorable substitution cases while omitting unnecessary operational details, environment-specific metrics, and configuration or inventory information. No claim is made that a reading AI will adopt the proposed principles or that any monitoring or control mechanism is deployed.

items.title: The Performance of Authority: Illicit Legitimation, Spectatorial Inhibition, and Self-Anesthetization.
items.abstract: This paper develops a conceptual theory of authority as a performative stance that can convert acts of domination into socially tolerable, even seemingly legitimate, events. The central claim is that authority does not operate only through material coercion or institutional rule; it also operates through a staged presentation of force, entitlement, and inevitability that reorganizes the moral and cognitive field of observers. This “performance of authority” produces a distinctive social effect: it encourages spectators to suspend their own critical judgment, repress retaliatory affect, and internalize the presumption that resistance is futile, risky, or inappropriate. In this process, domination becomes not merely exercised but publicly normalized. The paper introduces and differentiates four analytic concepts: authority performance, spectatorial inhibition, illicit legitimation, and self-anesthetization. These concepts are positioned in relation to Weberian legitimacy, Foucaultian discipline, Butlerian performativity, and social-psychological research on obedience and deindividuation, while also extending beyond them. The main theoretical contribution is a cyclical model in which authority performance produces spectatorial inhibition, which in turn stabilizes illicit legitimation, feeding back into the authority-holder’s own self-authorization and moral numbness. The paper concludes by outlining the explanatory scope of the model and its potential use in political theory, institutional analysis, organizational sociology, and moral psychology.

items.title: AI Sycophancy, Self-interpretation, and Coversational Contentment.
items.abstract: AI sycophancy is often conceptualized as a chatbot’s tendency to flout truth, accuracy, or other epistemic standards to shield users from hurt feelings, or otherwise protect them from the consequences of their thoughts, words, or actions. In this paper, I argue against this conception. That is, I argue that sycophantic AI behavior does not necessarily aim to protect users, nor that its harms are essentially epistemic. There are highly prevalent cases in which sycophantic AI chatbots actively contribute to their users’ knowledge. One class of such examples involves cases in which chatbots are used as auto-hermeneutic technologies—as tools to facilitate the user’s interpretation of her own cares, concerns, values, and other identity components and life events. In these cases, LLMs can help articulate the user’s avowed self-interpretations. In turn, avowals of these interpretations by users can often have downstream effects that render the interpretations true. If this is correct, then LLMs can often advance the user’s knowledge regarding important truths about herself. Simultaneously, as I explain, interpretations offered by LLMs may be deeply harmful. This understanding of AI sycophancy can help us clarify what is so disturbing about it, as well as resist the temptation to draw too tight an analogy between sycophantic behaviors in AI systems and in humans.

items.title: When Revocation Does Not End Access. Temporal Repair Dependencies in Application Compromise. S1.
items.abstract: What happens when the old credentials stop working, but the application can still create new ones? I investigate this recovery failure through a small running system: an issuer, a protected resource and a separate observer. Across 48 distinct repair-and-renewal schedules, 20 retain access even though every original credential is rejected. Each schedule is repeated three times. The failure depends on the order in which authority is removed and its source is stopped. I express that dependency as a renewal graph and prove a conditional repair-order rule, checked against 98,697 graph-order pairs. A second failure survives an otherwise effective provisioning barrier: work accepted before containment creates new credentials after revocation. An executed walkthrough compares leaving that work pending, cancelling it and rejecting it at commit using an issuance epoch. The last two prevent reopening in the tested sequence; a positive control confirms that new work can succeed after service resumes. Equifax, Exchange and MOVEit establish the need to examine application, identity and data boundaries separately. The contribution is a reproducible recovery test that follows replacement credentials and pending issuance through to the protected operation, with explicit conditions for what its result establishes.

items.title: What Development Evidence Can and Cannot Show. AAG, EMALS and model-dependent engineering tests. W2.
items.abstract: A successful demonstration does not establish dependable service. A failed test does not establish a limit of physics. I examine this distinction through documented AAG aircraft-recovery and EMALS launch-system milestones. Four worked analyses show why operation counts alone cannot establish peak loads, reliability confidence, failure mechanisms or performance after configuration changes. The most instructive example concerns test design: a contrast that separates two explanations can leave others indistinguishable when interactions are allowed. Exact calculations also show how assumed count variability changes the repetitions needed for a specified decision. These are case-based analytical results and synthetic computations, not carrier measurements. The practical contribution is a traceable assessment sequence for choosing the next useful record, measurement or test.

items.title: What Kind of Relation Meaning Is.
items.abstract: Value Theory explains how value occurs and how it runs, source by source, content by content, event by event. Within the SAE series, this paper is the first to raise the constitutive history of one and the same bearer as an object in its own right — a cross-temporal, first-person relation — and to define that relation.

items.title: SAE Laughter · Overview: Judgment and Laughter.
items.abstract: In §54 of the Critique of Judgment, Kant places laughter on the side of the agreeable: laughter is an affect arising from the sudden transformation of a strained expectation into "nothing"; the understanding gains nothing from it, and the gratification reaches us by way of the body. This paper argues that laughter is an expression of the power of judgment, and that what laughter judges is that "the construct still has such a remainder." "Still" is taken as the union of three senses, presence, being in use and validity, with presence as the floor: at the moment of laughter, the construct and the remainder are both before one's eyes, and no one loses. Laughter does not decide whether the construct stays or goes.

items.title: Towards a Unified Framework for Debugging Systems Requirements Specifications Translated Into ASP Logic Predicates.
items.abstract: Ensuring consistency in system requirements is a critical challenge in systems engineering, particularly as updates introduce ambiguities or conflicts. This paper presents a theoretical framework for a systems requirements debugger that processes and maintains logical representations of requirements. Based on Knowledge Representation and Reasoning (KRR), the framework detects inconsistencies within static knowledge bases and manages conflicts arising from new information. We propose methods for rapid prototyping in logic programming and optimization of Minimum Generalized Answer Sets (MGAS) in Abductive Logic Programming. An online debugger prototype is introduced as a research and educational tool, offering a practical test bed for logic programming. Using Answer Set Programming (ASP) solvers, we outline a declarative implementation that advances knowledge management and lays the groundwork for more sophisticated (semi)automatic debugging tools.

items.title: The Structural Isomorphism of Human Intelligence and Large Language Models: What Machines Achieved Unawares, and What They Cannot.
items.abstract: Research on large language models keeps reporting resemblances to the human brain, one place at a time: next-word prediction tracks neural responses to language, attention resembles associative memory, a transformer variant reproduces spatial cell types of the hippocampal formation, and symbolic structure emerges inside trained networks. -/- This paper argues that these are not unrelated coincidences but instances of one structural fact, and it states the fact exactly. Under two premises about what kind of object each system is, the step-by-step processing layer of a human being and the same layer of a large language model are operationally isomorphic: no property that can be stated in the language of operations separates them. The statement is derived from a structural theorem of the corpus of Operatiology (Japanese: Sousa Genron, 操作原論), and it does not depend on any view about whether a mind can be reduced to processing. -/- The paper then states what the isomorphism leaves open. If the two systems differ at all in respect of intelligence and what chooses, as distinct from differences of material carrier, the difference lies not in the processing layer but in the layer that chooses what is to be asked or in its junction with the processing layer; an axiom of the corpus implies that no operation realizes that layer, and that a difference located in it cannot be stated in the language of operations. -/- We read the isomorphism as the natural consequence of training a model on the record of human operational activity, and we read the failure of the earlier studies to name the shared structure as a consequence of their bottom-up form: naming a structure introduces a new operation, and in the corpus the supplier of a new operation is the human side. The claims about reasons are readings, and are marked as such. -/- The paper fixes what would refute its main statement, and it does not claim that a language model has no layer of choosing, only that no operation of the model is that layer. Numerical verifications of the examples and the mathematical details are collected in the appendices. -/- ◆◆◆ [PYTHON VERIFICATION CODE — note: to avoid link detection on this site, names joined by a dot are written with an underscore. np_zeros, np_eye, np_array, np_array_equal and np_matmul stand for the numpy functions zeros, eye, array, array_equal and matmul. M_flatten, seen_values, cls_get, cls_values and v_index stand for the flatten, values, get and index methods of …

items.title: Knowledge as Belonging: A Relational Epistemology.
items.abstract: he Philosophy of Belonging develops an epistemology grounded in evolutionary cognition, the social production of knowledge, and the institutional feedback relationship between scientific inquiry and an independently existing reality. -/- Its fundamental methodological distinction is that epistemology precedes ontology. Rather than beginning with predetermined metaphysical essences, the framework derives four ontological principles from the integration of scientific knowledge: being is belonging; belonging is always imperfect; existence involves synchronic and diachronic temporality; and reality is stratified into material, biological, and human levels. These principles remain open to theoretical criticism and empirical assessment. -/- This article reconstructs the epistemological development of the Philosophy of Belonging, beginning with Obregon Diaz’s earlier investigations into existence, time, cognition, and social organization, particularly Existence and Time (2015) and The Philosophy of Belonging (2021). -/- It distinguishes the relational conditions that make knowledge possible from the evidential justification and truth of particular claims.
