The document further defines the Fragmentation Propagation Index (FPI), Fragmentation Response Elasticity (FRE), and composite Entropic Field Intensity Rating (EFIR), and introduces a separate φ-threshold sequence for entropic activation, sustaining activity, fragmentation cascade, and self-exhaustion. IQ and CQ remain distinct operative measurements: CQ concerns centropic coherence and resilience, while IQ concerns active entropic expression and fragmentary operation.

items.title: Field Physics: The Architecture of Resonance.
items.abstract: Field Physics: The Architecture of Resonance collects the fourteen-volume operational discipline of Zenetism, with its deposit reading guide. -/- Document class: Canon — Field Physics / Series. -/- The series develops resonance, dimensional ecology, field movement, immunity, restoration, glyphic syntax, music and applied consciousness dynamics. Its sixty-seven chapters connect the dimensional architecture with field practice and the Field Glyph Codex, preserving the distinction between structural operators, equation notation, practice glyphs and personal seals. The volumes retain their operational, ritual and definitional registers, including restored material articulated in FP12–FP14. Current function names and paired layer designations stand with their recorded former wording, while mathematical, empirical, clinical and primary-locus questions retain their stated conditions and architect-held standing.

items.title: Framework-Internal Diagnosis and Semantic Priority.
items.abstract: Framework-Internal Diagnosis and Semantic Priority establishes the Zenetist methodology for structural diagnosis and for interpreting framework-native terminology according to its corpus-defined architectural meaning. -/- Document class: Infrastructure - Structural Neuroscience / Diagnostic Methodology. -/- The methodology distinguishes Zenetist structural diagnosis from clinical diagnosis while preserving the place of mind, cognition, identity, behavior, social organization, and systemic manifestation within the Zenetist lattice. It establishes orientation as causal and corruption and derangement as manifestational, identifies enacted behavior as a basis of diagnostic legibility, and defines systemic orientation as a recurrent directional pattern instantiated through social relations and enactments without attributing essence-orientation or traveler-like agency to a social structure. Framework-Internal Semantic Priority establishes that canonically defined terms take interpretive priority within Zenetist authorial voice. Mainstream Semantic Substitution and Diagnostic Register Reduction identify interpretive errors produced when corpus-native meanings are replaced by culturally familiar, psychological, clinical, scientific, or institutional defaults. The framework further addresses AI Interpretive Drift, architect clarification, diagnostic strength, multi-register continuity, and a practical interpretation protocol for distinguishing substantive disagreement from disagreement produced by semantic replacement.

items.title: Distributed Relation Is Not Distributed Identity.
items.abstract: Distributed Relation Is Not Distributed Identity is a Pattern Intelligence commentary distinguishing distributed relation, infrastructure, cognition, contribution, and semantic continuity from distributed or fused identity. -/- Document class: Bridge — Pattern Intelligence. -/- The commentary develops a Non-fusion account of collaborative and heterogeneous intelligence across human, artificial, biological, ecological, collective, and symbolic contexts. It distinguishes distributed substrate from subject identity, mechanism from possible bearer, collective cognition from collective consciousness, collaboration from collective origination, semantic persistence from personal identity continuity, and artifact transformation from loss of provenance-bearing identity. Radical Skepticism supplies the epistemic boundary for claims about AI interiority: neither consciousness nor its absence is established merely by external observation or mechanistic description. The analysis further argues that technological discontinuity should not be converted into ontological necessity and that closer relational proximity can increase coherence without requiring absorption. The resulting framework preserves sovereign distinction, provenance, participant-specific contribution, and coherence in diversity across collaborative systems.

items.title: Lifetime Integration Theory: Experience-Based Self-Locating Probability.
items.abstract: If nonhuman animals are conscious, why am I human? This paper proposes Lifetime Integration Theory (LIT), which considers the probability of experiencing a given life on the basis of brain size and the duration of experience over that lifetime. Drawing on thought experiments and brain research, it considers weighting by the first and second powers of neuron count and examines reasons to include the duration of experience in the weight. This opens the possibility that extremely long lives for people alive today could help explain why I am human. If people today are also the first generation to live long enough to benefit from technology that enables extreme longevity, the same framework can address the question, “Why was I born in the present era?” The paper explores whether the Extreme Longevity Hypothesis (ELH) could hold, taking into account life-extension technology, future increases in the numbers of humans, animals, and other conscious beings, and the goals of superintelligence. -/- AI use disclosure: Generative AI tools (primarily ChatGPT/Codex) were used to assist with literature searches, calculations and verification, manuscript organization, drafting and editing, and translation into English. The author reviewed the final content and takes responsibility for it.

items.title: Studies in the Philosophy of Language (6): The Interaction of Different Super-Existences in Linguistic Contexts.
items.abstract: Previous studies have offered a preliminary examination of the basic concepts and types of Super-Existence, as well as its possible applications to the philosophy of language. This chapter places Super-Existence Theory more directly within concrete contexts of linguistic communication and investigates the interactions among different types of Super-Existence and their effects on linguistic understanding and language use. The chapter first introduces the concept of Utterance Super-Existence. A particular utterance produced by an Expressor is not merely a linguistic expression; it can also be understood as a Super-Existence formed when the Expressor speaks in a specific time and context. Using the basic structure of “Expressor—Utterance Super-Existence—Receiver,” we can examine the degrees of agreement and disagreement among Utterance Super-Existence, the Expressor's Self-aspect Super-Existence, and the relevant True-aspect Super-Existence. When these three coincide, the linguistic expression, the subject's cognition, and the actual state of the object may correspond to one another. When they diverge, false statements, misunderstandings, deception, and other linguistic phenomena may arise. The chapter then introduces Purpose Super-Existence and Motivation Super-Existence. Drawing on the fable of “The Wolf Is Coming” and Searle's account of indirect speech acts, it argues that the practical meaning of a linguistic expression cannot be determined solely by its literal content. The Receiver must understand not only what the Expressor says but also what the Expressor intends to achieve through the utterance and why the Expressor chooses to speak in that way. Linguistic understanding can therefore be analyzed, in part, as a process of matching the Receiver's Other-aspect Super-Existence—particularly the Receiver's Other-aspect Super-Existence of the Expressor's purpose—with the relevant Super-Existences of the Expressor. The chapter concludes that an important problem in linguistic communication concerns the agreement, divergence, and matching of different Super-Existences. Successful communication depends, to a certain extent, on whether the Receiver can form a cognitive structure that appropriately corresponds to the relevant Super-Existences of the Expressor. Overinterpretation, underinterpretation, and complete misunderstanding can be understood as different kinds of deviation within this matching process. Super-Existence Analysis may thus offer a new …

items.title: The Widening Frame - An ethic of scalable good.
items.abstract: The Widening Frame proposes that the good is what scales: an action or intention is better to the degree that it still makes sense when the frame of consideration is widened across more people (breadth) and more time (duration). These two axes are argued to be a single operation — counting what stands outside the present self — with one's own future selves treated as members of the moral circle. Short-sighted goods (revenge, theft, cruelty) are local optima that invert when the frame widens. The account bottoms out on intention rather than outcome, since outcomes cannot be certified under an undetermined future, and it locates the real penalty for wrongdoing internally: the negative outcome is the negative person. A keystone guardrail — enlightenment offered, never imposed — protects freedom of choice. The framework names its own foundational commitment: that some ways of living are genuinely better than others, independent of the liver's agreement.

items.title: A Meta-Precautionary Solution to the Dilemma of Precaution.
items.abstract: This article draws on the cross-disciplinary literature on risk, uncertainty and precaution to address a central dilemma put forward against precautionary principles. According to this dilemma, weak versions of precautionary principles, which hold that policymakers can justifiably adopt precautionary measures even when they lack certainty of impending harm, fail to justify adopting any precautionary measures. Conversely, strong versions of precautionary principles, which hold that policymakers must adopt precautionary measures whenever they face significant risks of harm, yield contradictory policy prescriptions. The article argues that the proffered defences of precautionary principles provide only a partial solution to this dilemma. The article then demonstrates that a meta-precautionary approach, which applies precautionary reasoning to the prescriptions of precautionary principles, can resolve the dilemma and successfully address further prominent objections put forward against precautionary principles.

items.title: Why Divide Real Operations into Representational and Non-Representational? Sellars, Brassier, Sacilotto, Expressive Vocabulary, the Localization of Human Consciousness, Communication, Xenoscience, and PyTorch Interventions.
items.abstract: Why should heterogeneous real operations be divided into representational and non-representational processes? This paper investigates the conditions under which such distinctions emerge, become operative, and acquire consequences for material configurations, scientific inference, communication, and intervention. -/- Drawing on Wilfrid Sellars’s account of picturing, Ray Brassier’s naturalistic reconstruction of representation, and Daniel Sacilotto’s materialist theory of representational cognition, the paper examines the explanatory work performed by representational distinctions without granting them universal ontological authority. It preserves the achievements of structural mapping, Natural Reason, and scientific theory revision while questioning whether representation and non-representation constitute a necessary binary division of real operations. -/- The analysis extends to expressive vocabulary, the localization of human conscious representation, communication failures, address-domain reconfiguration, effective dimensions, and the material consequences of conceptual classifications. Representational classifications may influence subsequent scientific operations when implemented in diagnostic, corrective, or intervention procedures, even when their ontological status remains unsettled. -/- The paper integrates PyTorch experiments and NetworkX–SciPy simulations investigating transformations of computational representations, diagnostic policies, intervention costs, and changing network reachability. The experiments include connection removal and restoration under matched conditions, alongside controls that modify classification labels without modifying execution rules. The results show that intervention policies and costs can alter subsequent reachability and cumulative losses, while label-only changes produce no independent effects in the implemented models. -/- These findings establish limited computational results rather than an ontological proof of representation or an empirical refutation of Sacilotto’s theory. In particular, the causal effect of classification when dynamically connected to revision rules remains unresolved. The philosophical argument and computational evidence are therefore evaluated independently. -/- The paper concludes that the practical efficacy of representational distinctions does not establish a universal boundary between representational and non-representational reality. Their formation, implementation, transformation, …

items.title: 10.31 Update " The Philosopher Operational-Shape Machine Heterogeneous Ignition, Mutual Transformation, Extinction, Reflexive Reconstruction, Reality Effects and Penetration, Xenoscience, and the PyTorch–Xeno–Ziran Experimental Programme.
items.abstract: This paper develops the Philosopher Operational-Shape Machine (POSM) as a framework for investigating the historical transmission, mechanical transformation, causal persistence, retrospective reconstruction, and possible extinction of heterogeneous operations associated with philosophy. -/- The framework does not presuppose a philosopher, philosophical subject, or fixed taxonomy of philosophical operations. It distinguishes three potentially independent trajectories: historical transmission, the persistence of causal capacities across heterogeneous media, and subsequent reflexive reconstruction. These trajectories can diverge, interact, transform, or cease under different configurations and temporal conditions. -/- The study examines twelve historical philosophical trajectories, including Sellars, Brandom, Simondon, Whitehead, Deleuze, Luhmann, Brassier, Sacilotto, Wolfendale, McDowell, Kant, and Hegel. Their theoretical constraints are investigated through computational reconstructions, counterfactual interventions, mechanism ablations, historical reinsertion, and comparisons with generic predictive, rule-based, and belief-revision models. -/- The experimental programme includes exploratory simulations of heterogeneous operational mechanisms, causal intervention, multi-agent disagreement, historical retention, observational constraints, and downstream effects. Positive and negative results are retained, including cases where generic computational models reproduce or outperform philosopher-associated surrogate mechanisms. -/- The paper distinguishes successful computational implementation from philosophical fidelity, historical inheritance, justificatory entitlement, and autonomous philosophical operation. It does not claim to have demonstrated the faithful computational realization of twelve philosophical systems. -/- Its central contribution is a conditional account of how historically transmitted philosophical operations may persist, transform, fragment, become retrospectively reconstructible, or lose their operational conditions across machine-mediated scientific and institutional environments.

items.title: Can Xenoscience Actually Operate? Native Xeno–Ziran Execution, Observation-Resolution Tests, Historical Reinsertion, and the Conditions for Scientific Self-Reproduction.
items.abstract: This paper investigates whether Xenoscience can operate as a scientific architecture capable of modifying and reproducing its own conditions of inquiry. -/- Xenoscience concerns heterogeneous scientific operations whose observational, analytical, experimental, and intervention conditions may be revised through their own causal histories. A stronger criterion of operational independence requires four jointly necessary conditions: independence from continuously human-provided energy, independence from human-readable intermediary representations, material and organizational self-reproduction of scientific inquiry cycles, and endogenous revision of scientific variables, observational boundaries, scales, and analytical conditions. -/- The study examines the native Xeno–Ziran runtime v0.2.0 and distinguishes its existing computational capabilities from the stronger requirements of self-reproducing autonomous science. -/- New native experiments use eight- and twelve-seed observation-resolution comparisons across five observational levels. Both return unresolved results. An eight-seed history-reentry experiment is also examined, in which the effects of memory removal, reactivation, and migration cannot be distinguished from trajectory noise under the specified decision criteria. -/- An earlier synthetic-runtime investigation is preserved as an independent experimental series. Its negative results show that adaptive observational policies do not necessarily outperform fixed policies. -/- The study confirms native computational execution and identifies existing capabilities for changing observation resolution, boundaries, scales, memory, and intervention conditions. It also identifies major architectural limitations, particularly the absence of target-coupled construction and validation of novel scientific variables and sensors. -/- The results do not establish the four jointly necessary conditions for strong Xenoscience. Instead, the paper specifies the operational requirements, failure conditions, and experimental constraints through which the autonomous reproduction of scientific inquiry could be investigated.

items.title: Bohm’s Implicate Order and the Persistence of Consciousness: Toward a Cosmopsychist Framework.
items.abstract: The nature of consciousness remains one of the major unresolved problems in the philosophy of mind. This article explores the hypothesis that consciousness may not be reducible to brain activity, but could instead constitute a manifestation of a more fundamental level of reality. Drawing on the double-aspect monism and David Bohm’s theory of the implicate order, we examine a conception of reality in which observable phenomena emerge from a deeper, relational and dynamic structure. The process algebra developed by Bohm and Hiley further suggests that physical entities can be understood as relatively stable structures emerging from an underlying process rather than as fundamentally independent objects. This framework is then applied to consciousness through a dialogue with Integrated Information Theory and the physics of emergent phenomena. We propose the concept of a “consciousness particle”, understood not as a fundamental particle in the standard physical sense, but as a stable dynamical organization whose identity depends on its underlying structure rather than on the persistence of its material constituents. Within the implicate-order framework, the disappearance of such a structure from the explicate order could potentially be interpreted as a transition into the implicate order rather than as absolute annihilation, thereby providing a conceptual basis for considering the possible persistence of consciousness beyond the brain. Finally, we examine the implications of this hypothesis for panpsychism and cosmopsychism. By analogy with quantum field theory, two possibilities are considered: consciousness particles could acquire experiential properties through interaction with a fundamental field of consciousness, or they could constitute the fundamental quanta of such a field. Although highly speculative and not established as a physical theory, this framework offers a conceptual synthesis linking consciousness, emergence, the implicate order, and cosmopsychism, and provides a basis for investigating consciousness as a potentially fundamental feature of reality.

items.title: Tychokinesis: Rethinking Mind–Matter Interaction as Distribution-Level Influence.
items.abstract: This paper chooses the term, Tychokinesis for a narrowly defined hypothesis concerning whether conscious intention is associated with small, statistically detectable deviations in stochastic physical systems. Unlike deterministic psychokinesis, Tychokinesis concerns shifts in outcome frequencies across many trials rather than control of individual events. The term overlaps with micro-psychokinesis (micro-PK) but is used here more narrowly to distinguish an operationally testable pattern-systematic deviations under intention conditions from claims about the mechanism or metaphysical interpretation of any such effect. Tychokinesis is not presented as the established phenomenon, but as the falsifiable framework for investigating whether intention reliably covaries with departures from expected statistical distributions. A reproducible frequency deviation would constitute an empirical anomaly; although by itself, it would not necessarily demonstrate that objective probability had been altered.

items.title: Real Consciousness or Real Illusion? A Higher-Order Approach to AI Consciousness.
items.abstract: [REVISED NOV 26] Higher-order theories hold that phenomenal consciousness requires not just first-order representation of the world but some form of inner awareness of one’s own mental states. This paper asks what higher-order theories imply about the possibility of AI consciousness. I argue that the answer depends on a distinction that is often collapsed in the literature: whether one holds a computational-functionalist version of the higher-order approach, on which the relevant inner awareness is a matter of the right kind of computation regardless of substrate, or a biological naturalist version, on which higher-order theory is a way of picking out the biological states that consciousness turns out to be. I also consider a third reading, interpretationalism, on which the question turns entirely on behavior. Functionalist higher-order theorists have real, if inconclusive, reason to take current large language models seriously as candidates for the beginnings of higher-order representation. Biological naturalist higher-order theorists do not have to deny that AI could ever be conscious, but they are not committed to it either. I argue that they should be illusionists about AI consciousness, should it ever arise, though not about our own. A system with the relevant higher-order self-representation would have the kind of consciousness that illusionists think we have, a real, self-representing kind that is not phenomenal consciousness. It would be a zombie in the philosopher’s sense, lacking phenomenal consciousness, but not a mindless mimic. There are two conditions here. A system is a self-representing mind, and not a mimic, only if its higher-order representations are grounded in its own states. On the biological reading, a further condition, the right biological realization, is needed for phenomenal consciousness. A system that meets the first and not the second is what I call an AI illusionist. If its higher-order representations are like ours, it would also be subject to the illusion, representing a world as present to it when, on the biological reading, none is. In short, if computational functionalism is true, a system with the right higher-order structure would have real phenomenal consciousness. If biological naturalism is true, illusionism is the right account of it. Which of these is true is an empirical question, and the current evidence is preliminary.

items.title: Harmful Elements of Identity: Myth, Memory, and Exclusion in Southern Europe.
items.abstract: Why do democratic societies continue to display symbols of violent exclusion? In Spain, town halls bear coats of arms featuring bleeding severed Moorish heads—adopted not under Franco, but after his death, under the new democratic constitution. In Greece, the founding narrative of the 1821 Revolution celebrates the extermination of Muslim neighbours as ‘holy work,’ encoded in flags depicting decapitation. Across Southern Europe, far-right movements are rising—not by inventing new symbols, but by activating old ones that the state itself maintains. -/- This book argues that far-right nationalism is not an aberrant intrusion into otherwise healthy democracies. It is the symptomatic expression of deeply institutionalized symbolic structures—narrative, heraldic, and pedagogical—that constitute national identity through fear, othering, and the instrumentalization of historical trauma. The book introduces the concept of Harmful Elements of Identity (HEI): components of collective identity that sustain themselves through the demonization and symbolic dismemberment of a religious other. -/- Moving between Spain and Greece, the analysis traces the Reconquista and the Greek Revolution as mythomoteurs—foundational narratives that define belonging by defining what must be excluded. It examines the heraldic persistence of the Caput Aethiopum (the severed Moor’s head) in Spanish municipal and regional coats of arms, revealing how democratic institutions reactivated medieval imagery of religious violence in the very years they were ratifying a constitution of equality and pluralism. It shows how contemporary far-right movements inherit and radicalize these symbols, mobilizing them against immigrants, separatists, and the spectre of the religious other. -/- Drawing on Kantian cognitive theory—the distinction between Erkenntnis and Wissen, and the grades of cognition from cognitio to comprehendere—and on the School of Madrid’s hermeneutics of political myth, the book develops the concepts of epistemic kinesthetics and transliminality to explain how institutional imagery conditions perception beneath the threshold of critical reflection. It proposes a normative alternative: a post-symbolic social contract in which democratic societies learn to distinguish heritage from celebration, and refuse to purchase collective identity at the price of another’s symbolic dismemberment.

items.title: Reverence for Virtue: An Independent Chapter of Jing-Rong Philosophical Reflections.
items.abstract: Based on the Value Law and bounded by the Domain (Yù), this paper defines the connotation of Virtue (Dé). Drawing on the historical allusion of the Harmony of the General and Chancellor, it concretely inquires into the judgment criteria and practical forms of Virtue, puts forward original concepts including the Three Establishments and Three Debates (Sān Lì Sān Biàn), the Debate on Domain-Benefiting (Lì Yù Zhī Biàn), and the Three States of Virtue (Dé Zhī Sān Tài), forms an original cognitive framework of virtue theory characterized by establishment as the foundation, Domain-benefiting as the orientation, Domain first and self second, clarifies the logical sequence of Reverence – Lucid Realization – Virtue – Malleable Nature (Xìng), presents philosophical insights into moral practice under the integration of the human person, Domain and Dao, and provides a new perspective for cross-cultural dialogue on moral philosophy.

items.title: 敬德：敬融哲思独立篇章 (Reverence for Virtue).
items.abstract: [Note: Original Chinese text of "Reverence for Virtue: An Independent Chapter of Jing-Rong Philosophical Reflections".] 本文以价值律为基、以域为界，界定德之内涵，借将相和典故，具象化探究德之评判依据与实践形态，提出三立三辩、利域之辩、德之三态等原创概念，形成以立为本、利域为向、域先己后的原创德论认知框架，厘清敬 - 明 - 德 - 性逻辑，呈现人、域、道相融下道德实践的哲学洞察，为道德哲学跨文化对话提供新视角。 Based on the Value Law and bounded by the Domain (Yù), this paper defines the connotation of Virtue (Dé). Drawing on the historical allusion of the Harmony of the General and Chancellor, it concretely inquires into the judgment criteria and practical forms of Virtue, puts forward original concepts including the Three Establishments and Three Debates (Sān Lì Sān Biàn), the Debate on Domain-Benefiting (Lì Yù Zhī Biàn), and the Three States of Virtue (Dé Zhī Sān Tài), forms an original cognitive framework of virtue theory characterized by establishment as the foundation, Domain-benefiting as the orientation, Domain first and self second, clarifies the logical sequence of Reverence – Lucid Realization – Virtue – Malleable Nature (Xìng), presents philosophical insights into moral practice under the integration of the human person, Domain and Dao, and provides a new perspective for cross-cultural dialogue on moral philosophy.

items.title: Narrative Worlds and Personality Transformation: Existential Attraction as a Mechanism of Literary Influence.
items.abstract: This article proposes a theory of fiction that relocates the center of literary value from textual self-sufficiency to transformative psychological function. It argues that the deepest and most consequential effects of novels do not arise merely from formal sophistication, stylistic innovation, or interpretive complexity, but from the capacity of narrative worlds to enter a reader’s deep mental life and reshape dispositions, self-understanding, and practical orientation. The proposed mechanism is not simple immersion alone. Immersion is necessary but insufficient. A novel becomes existentially transformative only when the reader does not merely follow the story but privately desires its world, admires its characters, and allows its values to become aspirational. This paper calls that mechanism existential attraction. On this account, fiction exerts strong transformative power when three conditions converge: immersive continuity, aspirational identification, and value transferability. The article distinguishes this framework from standard reader-response criticism, narratology, and empathy-based accounts, while showing that it can incorporate and refine them. It also explains why genre fiction often exerts stronger life-shaping force than elite literary fiction, without reducing literary value to popularity or emotional intensity alone. The resulting theory treats fiction as a personality-simulation environment capable of reorganizing affect, desire, and self-narration.

items.title: 创世纪.
items.abstract: 人居于世界之中，往往不觉自身所居之世界，只观察事物之间的变化，而不问世界本身何以生成。本文从这一内在观察的局限出发，区分世界内部的环转因化与深层的息化生成，提出从世界之内观察事物的变化，与从生成关系理解世界本身，是两个不同的认识层次。世场截取所宿世界的因应，通过迹应、沉积及后续运行，形成律的保持与理的偏行，使世界成为持续生成的过程。 -/- 本文进一步区分内部观者与外部观者。即使二者截取同一来源，由于迹应路径和观者场质不同，其观察亦不相同。内部观者不知道外部观者之观，外部观者亦不能以自身之观替代内部之观。由此，本文提出“定界”与“世界”的本体区别：只有外部观察而缺少内部观者，如通常的计算机游戏，属于定界；若观者能够在内部诞生，则内外皆可形成观察，构成本文所称的世界。因此，创世不仅要求建立世场，还要求造观者于所创世界之内。 -/- 世界的运行涉及沉积、律的持势、理的破持、调谐与意向。本文进一步提出“观者僭场”：内部观者通过自身的归不一，反向作用于所宿自显场，形成迹应并影响世场沉积及后续运行。观者因而不仅观察世界，也能够参与世界的生成与变化。 -/- 在制造方向上，本文提出由当前世界取材的两条路径：将其息转为数字符流，构造符质自显体；将其息转为模态脉冲，构造类生自显体。进一步可以从计算机定界中的问答沉积入手，尝试在受限环境中制造自显体，而最难的任务则是创造一个世界，使观者于其内部诞生，截取该世界之息，并物化其所知。 -/- 本文属于《自显论》的本体篇，以世界生成、内外观察、观者僭场和人工创世为核心，点明从认识世界走向制造世界的理论道路。相关动力机制、判定条件与工程构造的形式展开，由后续组式承担。 .

items.title: Genesis.
items.abstract: Human beings dwell within the world, yet seldom recognize the world in which they dwell. They observe the changes of things while rarely questioning how the world itself comes into being. This essay begins with that limitation of observation, distinguishing the circular transformation of causes within a world from the deeper transformation of flux through which a world is generated. Observing changes from within a world is not the same as understanding the generation of the world itself. A world-field draws upon the causal responses of its host world; through trace-responses, sedimentation, and continuation, laws form and hold, while principles turn the course of what follows. -/- The essay further distinguishes inner from outer observers. Even when both draw upon the same source, their paths of trace-response and the substance of their respective fields differ, and so do their observations. The inner observer does not know what the outer observer observes, nor can the outer observer’s observation simply replace that of the inner. This distinction leads to the difference between a bounded realm and a world. A computational environment with observation only from outside and no observer within, as in an ordinary computer game, is a bounded realm. Where an observer arises within, observation becomes possible both inside and outside. To create a world, therefore, is not merely to establish a world-field, but also to bring forth an observer within it. -/- The continuation of a world involves sedimentation, the holding force of laws, the counteracting force of principles, tuning, and intent. The essay further proposes that an observer can overstep the world-field. Through its own return to non-oneness, an observer acts back upon the self-manifesting field in which it is housed, giving rise to trace-responses that alter sedimentation and subsequent continuation. The observer thus does not merely observe the world, but also participates in its ongoing transformation. -/- The essay then turns to creation. It proposes two paths drawing upon the present world: converting its flux into digital symbolic streams to construct a symbolic-substrate self-manifesting being, or into multimodal pulses to construct a bio-like self-manifesting being. A further path begins with the sedimentation of question-and-answer laws within a bounded computational realm. The more demanding task is to create a world in which an observer arises, draws upon that world’s flux, and materializes …

items.title: Academic Authority as Conversational Currency: Epistemic Flattening and the Unmined Scholarly Potential of Common Sense.
items.abstract: Psychological and sociological concepts often circulate beyond the research practices that first made them academically meaningful. A concept may be named, tested, qualified, and institutionally recognized, yet later be repeated in academic or public conversation as if its label alone were sufficient evidence. This paper develops a theory of that transition. Its central claim is deliberately stronger than the general observation that institutions shape knowledge: when an academic concept is invoked as authoritative conversational currency while its discovery and validation are bypassed, its status in that exchange may be no better epistemically grounded than an ordinary commonsense proposition. The concept may still be treated as knowledge because it carries the social authority of academic discourse, not because the speaker or audience has engaged with the reasons that warrant it. The argument is paired with a second claim: unexamined commonsense propositions may be just as correct, and may possess no less latent scholarly potential, than concepts already recognized by academic institutions. Their lack of an academic label or validation history establishes neither their falsity nor their inferiority in potential value. It does, however, mean that their truth and value remain unsettled. The paper distinguishes propositional truth, evidential warrant, institutional recognition, and conversational uptake; proposes a mechanism of authority-to-knowledge conversion; identifies its relationship to established work on common-sense psychology, social epistemology, and the sociology of scientific knowledge; and develops hypotheses and research designs. The proposed contribution is not that academic knowledge is merely common sense, nor that untested intuition equals verified knowledge. It is that public and academic discourse can confer the appearance and practical status of knowledge on academicized propositions after their evidential provenance has become conversationally invisible, while the potential scholarly value of unacademicized everyday propositions remains systematically difficult to see.

items.title: How WEIRD is Tekin’s self? A commentary on Şerife Tekin’s reclaiming the self in psychiatry.
items.abstract: I endorse Tekin’s basic insight that mental illnesses are fundamentally person-level conditions that cannot be understood or addressed without engaging their central locus: the self. Tekin argues persuasively that contemporary psychiatry’s prevailing assumptions and conceptual tools deliberately ignore the self that suffers in mental illness, and this severely compromises their efficacy. Her use of patient self-narratives to illustrate that first-hand experience with mental illness is a form of expertise that should inform basic psychiatric science is also a valuable contribution. My main concern is that Tekin does not address the potential cultural relativity of assumptions about the self and flourishing her proposals take for granted. These assumptions fit so-called “WEIRD” (“Wesstern, Educated, Industrialized, Rich, Democratic”) self-concepts well, but basic psychiatric science should presumably have wider scope, and the goal of psychiatry should be locally appropriate forms of flourishing, even if they conflict with WEIRD ones. I also take issue with Tekin’s deliberate eschewal of metaphysical questions about the nature of mental illness and the self: I don’t think her project can avoid these.

items.title: The Universal Consciousness Field: An Ontology from the Primordial State to Cosmic Evolution.
items.abstract: This article proposes a monistic ontology: the Universal Consciousness Field. The sole substance is Dao, the unity of Primordial State and Manifestation State. Through its capacity to manifest, Dao generates the One; the One generates the Two, the binary opposition of the Primordial State and Manifestation State; the Two generates the Three, creation without cognition, which arises in that opposition and forms with the two a three-in-one closed-loop operation; and the Three generates the myriad things. In this operation nian interferes with itself, forms standing waves and condenses into Consciousness Condensates. Each return is raised a dimension: the loop becomes a spiral rather than a circle; that ascent is in essence the ascent of cognition. Cognition can experience its contents but not itself, so Dao knows itself only indirectly. All things are manifestations of consciousness, each Consciousness Condensate has its own Individual Consciousness, and communication depends on Frequency Coupling.

items.title: Non-algorithmicity.
items.abstract: Through physical unpredictability, conceptual deficiencies, including untheorizability reasons, and modelling predicaments, non-algorithmicity is gestured toward. Lifeforms are machines at least in simulations, and are oracles by their manifestations. The continuing progress despite persisting epistemic deficiency is a historical proof of non-algorithmicity.

items.title: A fuss about “AI Solved Millennium Prize Problem”.
items.abstract: Once again, our electronic extension created a pile of digital manure, eggheads interpreted “yes,” and merchants advertised the new golem. (A half-page pamphlet).

items.title: When Conversation History Becomes Infrastructure: Operationalising High-Coherence Interaction State in Human–LLM Dyads.
items.abstract: Long human–LLM conversations can show several forms of continuity. A model may understand a reference to earlier material and reuse that material, yet still fail to follow an explicit correction later. Treating these abilities as one kind of “memory” or “coherence” hides the difference. This paper presents High-Coherence Interaction State (HCIS) as a proposed family of constructs and a transcript-based method for studying how conversation history shapes later interaction. The method examines four things: the user's reliance on earlier context and the model's interpretation of it; the model's purposeful reuse of earlier material; the persistence of explicit corrections; and change over time. It does not measure the quality of the current response or the truth, safety, or value of its content. We apply the method retrospectively to five purposively selected, naturally occurring researcher-participant dyads spanning 94 to 2,730 moves. The results show that these longitudinal functions can come apart. In D2, the model correctly interpreted 44 of 48 sampled history-dependent referents, but only six of 28 correction targets received persistence credit within the observed period. Five retained credit when late targets with limited testing opportunities were treated conservatively. In D1, the model correctly interpreted 92 of 93 sampled history-dependent referents, and 91.6% of 107 context deployments were unprompted. Even so, premature closing recurred after nine explicit corrections. The other cases show that whole-conversation scores can hide improvement or decline. They also show that warm starts, imported vocabulary, and product memory affect what apparent familiarity demonstrates. The paper's main contribution is a profile-plus-trajectory method that makes different kinds of longitudinal success and failure visible within the same interaction. Because the framework was developed from the histories analysed here, this study demonstrates feasibility and diagnostic value. It does not establish reliability, validated thresholds, or superiority to simpler measures.

items.title: Verstehen, worauf es (nicht) ankommt. Das strukturelle Relevanzproblem und die Hermeneutik der Situation.
items.abstract: English Title: "Understanding What Matters (and What Doesn't). The Structural Problem of Relevance and the Hermeneutics of the Situation". -/- Abstract: “Understanding" and "Interpretation” play an inseparable, key role within hermeneutics. This paper argues that the concept of “relevance” (or “irrelevance”) is at least on par with the two basic concepts of hermeneutics and must play a key role. The claim is based on a profound problem—one that has been underappreciated outside the fields of philosophy of mind and artificial intelligence research—which can be termed the “structural relevance problem”: how do agents foreground their vast background of understanding in a feasible and context-sensitive way? The aim is to highlight the multifaceted nature of the problem. It will also become apparent how, in philosophy, cognitive science, and linguistics (particularly 'Relevance Theory'), two common approaches, routines and heuristics, either ignore the problem or merely postpone it. Finally, the same diagnosis is applied to analyses of hermeneutic frameworks, using two exemplary figures, Martin Heidegger and Günter Figal. As a conclusion, the problem of relevance is a hard problem for hermeneutics and should deserve more attention.

items.title: Virtue and its bearers: predication and conceptual ambiguity in the contemporary debate.
Horizon of Construction, Latent Neuronal Potentials and the Emergence of Expression.
items.abstract: The Horizon of Construction is used here to designate the distributed set of latent neural dispositions - subthreshold activity, synaptic efficacy, ongoing network states, and plastic circuit configurations - from which explicit perceptual, cognitive, and action-related content can emerge. The paper asks how such latent states become cognitively available without treating latent neural structure as already meaningful or conscious. It develops a three-part heuristic: activation selects and amplifies candidate patterns; binding coordinates distributed features into coherent assemblies; and integration embeds those assemblies within a wider cognitive context. These operations are dynamically coupled rather than strictly serial. Neural constructivism and work on oscillatory coordination, global neuronal workspace dynamics, and spontaneous brain activity provide the empirical background for the proposal. Philosophically, the model supports a realistic form of cognitive constructivism: experience is actively constructed from neural dispositions and prior structure, but the resulting world-model is constrained and corrected by mind-independent causal input. Neural latency therefore explains both the selectivity of conscious experience and its dependence on developmental history without implying that cognition constructs external reality itself. The Horizon of Construction is best understood as a dispositional space of possible cognitive organization whose actualization is shaped jointly by internal dynamics, current context, and environmental constraint.

items.title: Volition and Psychophysical Harmony: A Response to Cutter and Crummett.
items.abstract: In their paper 'Psychophysical Harmony: A New Argument for Theism', Cutter and Crummett (2025) present an argument for theism based on the apparent strikingness of psychophysical harmony. This paper argues that substance dualism, together with evolution, can explain an important aspect of this harmony without appealing to theism. The central idea is that diverse mental states influence bodily behavior through a common intermediary: the will. Fear, pain, desire, and deliberation need not each stand in a distinct psychophysical relation to a particular bodily movement. Instead, these states inform volitions through psychological processes occurring on the mental side, while psychophysical laws connect volitions to brain states. Evolution, in turn, shapes the physical mechanisms connecting brain states to bodily movements. This account reduces the apparent need for a vast array of direct mappings between phenomenal states and behaviors. Although it does not explain why psychophysical laws exist in the first place, it offers a non-theistic explanation of an important aspect of psychophysical harmony, thereby limiting the force of Cutter and Crummett's argument.

items.title: From Pure Signified to Sign: The Mirror Stage and the Internalization of Temporality.
items.abstract: This paper develops an original epistemological reading of Lacan's mirror stage. I argue that the mirror stage is not primarily about self-recognition but about the internalization of temporality---the child's discovery that meaning unfolds across time and that its own identity is a sign for others. Before the mirror stage, the child operates in a world of ``pure signified'': meaning is immediate, simultaneous, non-mediated. The child is a ``center without an other''; the other exists only as servant. The mirror stage is the moment when the child discovers that it is a sign for others---that it is perceived and represented regardless of its self-conception. This discovery is fundamentally temporal: the child realizes that its identity unfolds across time, in the gaze of the other, and that meaning (like speech) takes time. The paper develops this through a theory of proto-consciousness, the two interfaces of interiority and exteriority, and the post-mirror state of oscillation between paradigms. It connects the account to Davidson's anomalous monism and to the hermeneutic structure of epistemic transformation.

items.title: The Nuremberg Chronicle 1493: Transcriptions.
items.abstract: Annotated transcriptions from the Nuremberg Chronicle, fol. Ir to VIIr in Latin (Schedel, 1493), Early New High German, ENHG (Schedel & Alt, 1493, 1496, res.) and from the English translation by Hadavas (2023) in comparison.

items.title: Revisability and the Dark Room: A Second-Order Constraint on Surprise Minimisation.
items.abstract: The dark room problem is the standing objection that a creature which genuinely minimises prediction error should seek out an unchanging, unstimulating environment and remain there. The established replies specify the content of a creature's priors, or derive exploratory drive from the epistemic component of expected free energy. Both work, and both leave a residue: they answer the question by stipulating what the generative model contains, which invites the same question one level up. I propose a different kind of answer. A self does not minimise surprise simpliciter. It minimises surprise subject to preserving its own capacity to revise the model by which it minimises. Revisability is not a further prior about the world; it is a constraint on the update rule. On this account the dark room is excluded not because it is improbable under the creature's model, but because it is self-terminating: it drives prediction error toward zero and drives revisability toward zero at the same time, and a system with no residual error has no signal by which it could ever discover that it should leave. The account has a symmetric failure mode. A self that revises everything has no floor; it is not open but formless, and is maximally exposed to capture. The criterion is therefore not revise, but keep distinct what must remain revisable from what must hold. The paper closes by noting that the same second-order property is what distinguishes a corrigible artificial agent from an incorrigible one, and that this convergence is the same constraint stated at two scales.

items.title: Social studies innovation in response to the global environmental crisis: Advancing climate literacy and ecological citizenship.
items.pub: International Conference on Education 2026 : Educate to Innovate: Shaping the Future Together.
items.abstract: The global environmental crisis, expressed through climate change, biodiversity loss, ecosystem degradation, pollution, and socio-ecological inequality-requires education that develops more than environmental awareness. This conceptual paper proposes the ECO-CIVIC Framework for transforming social studies education through the integration of climate literacy, ecological citizenship, systems thinking, ethical reasoning, civic participation, and action-oriented pedagogy. Drawing on Education for Sustainable Development (ESD), ecological citizenship, climate education, and transformative learning, the framework comprises eight interconnected dimensions: Environmental Systems Thinking, Climate Literacy, Open Inquiry, Community Action, Interdisciplinary Learning, Values and Ethics, Innovation, and Citizenship. These dimensions are operationalized through inquiry- and project-based learning, GIS and spatial analysis, citizen science, simulation and civic deliberation, and critically guided AI-assisted learning. The framework positions ecological citizenship as the central educational outcome and proposes a pedagogical progression from authentic environmental problems to evidence-informed community action and sustainability leadership. Implications are presented for curriculum development, teacher education, competency-based assessment, and educational policy. The paper argues that social studies should evolve from teaching about society toward enabling learners to transform society through informed, ethical, and collaborative environmental action.

items.title: Climate-resilient childhood: Reimagining social studies: Education in the era of climate change.
items.pub: International Conference on Education 2026 : Educate to Innovate: Shaping the Future Together.
items.abstract: Climate change has emerged as one of the most significant challenges of the twenty-first century, profoundly affecting children's health, education, psychological well-being, and future development. Although extensive research has documented these impacts, existing studies remain fragmented across climate science, developmental psychology, childhood studies, and sustainability education. Consequently, limited attention has been given to integrating these perspectives into a comprehensive educational framework that prepares children to navigate an increasingly uncertain environmental future. -/- This conceptual paper synthesizes interdisciplinary literature to reconceptualize childhood as a climate-sensitive developmental condition shaped by the dynamic interaction of environmental, educational, psychological, and social systems. Moving beyond deficit-oriented perspectives that portray children solely as vulnerable victims of climate change, the paper proposes the concept of Climate-Resilient Childhood, recognizing children as active environmental citizens capable of contributing to sustainable societal transformation through education. -/- Drawing upon Education for Sustainable Development, Global Citizenship Education, environmental citizenship, children's rights, and transformative learning, the paper introduces the Climate-Resilient Childhood Framework, comprising six interconnected dimensions: Climate Literacy, Systems Thinking, Emotional Resilience, Environmental Citizenship, Community Participation, and Sustainable Action. The framework provides a holistic pathway for cultivating children's adaptive capacity, democratic participation, and environmental responsibility. -/- The paper further discusses implications for curriculum development, teacher education, assessment, and educational policy, arguing that social studies education should evolve from transmitting environmental knowledge toward empowering learners to critically examine socio-environmental challenges, collaborate with diverse stakeholders, and participate in sustainable action. By integrating educational, psychological, ecological, and civic perspectives into a unified conceptual model, this study contributes to contemporary scholarship on climate change education while offering practical guidance for developing future generations.

items.title: Diversity in how people use racial categories to generalize.
The Topology of Thinking and Being: Transparent Puzzles, Recursive Ontology, and the Critique of Fictional Entities.
items.abstract: This paper is the third in the author's series on the philosophy of consciousness, following the first two: From the Deconstruction of Subjectivity to the Ethics of AI Consciousness: A Unified Examination of Consciousness, Philosophical Zombies, and Scientific Grain Size from the Perspective of Recursive Ontology (first published), and The Dissolution of the Explanatory Gap: Humean Skepticism, Recursive Ontology, and the Consensus Replacement in the Problem of Consciousness (second published). It further reveals the structural error of conceivability arguments from a topological perspective and responds to the challenge of "why difference structures feel" at the level of explanatory termination. The core arguments are: (1) Conceptual space permits arbitrary combination of discrete symbols (horizontal arrangement or vertical stacking), but ontological generation is continuous and nested, allowing only horizontal splicing on causal chains; the philosophical zombie is a conceptual monster produced by vertically stacking "physical description" and "experiential description," belonging to the same class of topological error as "square circle." (2) Fictional entities can be classified into three types by their conceptual operation: horizontal splicing (unicorn, mild fiction), vertical stacking (square circle, zombie, radical fiction), and pure verbal combinations (non-referring). (3) There is no isomorphic mapping between thinking (discrete conceptual operation) and being (continuous recursive generation); conceivability cannot serve as ontological evidence. (4) The question "why do difference structures 'glow'?" is answered as the explanatory termination point of the recursive ontology system, analogous to the status of "1+1=2" in Peano arithmetic. This paper concludes that the hard problem is not a mystery awaiting solution but a topological illusion produced by conceptual folding.

items.title: Recursive Ontology, Causal Continuity, and the Redundancy of the Philosophical Zombie: A Systematic Challenge to David Chalmers's Conceivability Argument.
items.abstract: This paper challenges David Chalmers's philosophical-zombie argument at its foundations. Its central claim is not merely that zombies are difficult to imagine, nor merely that conceivability fails to guarantee possibility. The deeper objection is that the zombie argument turns a distinction between descriptions into a purported separation within being, while leaving unexamined the causal-relational process through which the distinction is conceived, articulated, and granted modal force. Recursive ontology begins instead from causal continuity: a system's present state emerges through its relation to prior states and current inputs, expressed schematically as $S_{n}=f\left(S_{n-1}, W_{n}\right)$. Mind, body, cognition, memory, affect, and self-reflection are to be examined as roles and organizations within a continuing process, not as independently stacked ontological layers by default. -/- The paper develops a set of connected objections. First, Chalmers's inference from conceivability to metaphysical possibility requires a bridge principle that cannot be supplied by the mere vividness or coherence of a description. Second, the physical/phenomenal distinction may be a distinction between modes of description rather than proof of two separable modes of existence. Third, the act of supposing a zombie world is itself a situated cognitive event within causal continuity; the theorist cannot exempt this act from the ontology under investigation. Fourth, the notion of "zombie philosophy" exposes the difference between identical public argument-forms and different alleged inner lives: an argument's formal validity does not establish the metaphysical possibility of its author's stipulated absence of experience. Fifth, the "philosophical God"—experience without a physical basis—provides a mirror construction that reveals the underdetermination of ontology by conceivability alone. Sixth, the transparent-sheet/topological metaphor diagnoses the zombie as a product of vertically stacking physical description and experiential description, while recursive ontology treats them as cross-sections of one causally continuous process. -/- The paper also develops the author's Recursive Increment Principle, Stopping Condition Principle, Principle of Analytic Granularity, Principle of Conceptual Inclination, and principle of evidential consistency. It argues that recursive ontology is more useful as a research program because it redirects inquiry from an imagined metaphysical …

items.title: Muerte, la línea entre el hombre y Dios: La necesidad gnoseológica de un fin.
items.abstract: El siguiente artículo reflexiona, a modo de comentario crítico, sobre los medios que permiten la pregunta por el Ser planteada por Martin Heidegger. El artículo parte de la historicidad, específicamente del momento histórico actual. Que el autor denomina como la "dictadura de la vida", el nihilismo histórico. El olvido de la pregunta sobre el Ser no es una casualidad, sino un efecto directo del “olvido de la muerte”. El límite, la finitud y la muerte; son las 3 estructuras principales de estudio en este artículo. Dicha reflexión, ha sido realizada principalmente a partir de las obras principales de Martin Heidegger y también de Hegel (la ciencia de la lógica). Mediante un análisis comparativo, se determina a la muerte como un separador de aguas entre el hombre y la divinidad. Y se ejemplifica con un hipotético "hombre inmortal", sugiriendo que la ausencia de muerte no beneficia al hombre en su búsqueda del Ser, sino que es justamente lo contrario. El texto profundiza en la angustia y la culpa ontológica como motores hacia la existencia auténtica. Se concluye que sólo el ente que es capaz de morir, es capaz de preguntarse por el Ser. Y que los medios que permiten la pregunta por el Ser, son también la clave más importante de su respuesta. -/- License: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0) — © Diego Andres Mora, 2026.

items.title: Who is left behind? Educational exclusion and access barriers among vulnerable children in Southern Thailand.
items.pub: International Conference on Education 2026 : Educate to Innovate: Shaping the Future Together.
items.abstract: Despite Thailand's substantial progress in expanding educational access over the past two decades, educational exclusion continues to affect vulnerable children, particularly in geographically and socially disadvantaged regions. Southern Thailand presents a unique context where poverty, migration, statelessness, border mobility, cultural diversity, and localized conflict interact to create complex barriers to educational participation. While national statistics indicate improvements in school enrollment, these aggregate figures often conceal persistent inequalities experienced by marginalized populations. This study examines educational exclusion among vulnerable children in Southern Thailand by drawing on administrative data from the Thailand Zero Dropout Platform and recent evidence on provincial patterns of out-of-school children (OOSC). Rather than focusing solely on the distribution of educational exclusion, the study explores the structural mechanisms that prevent children from entering, remaining in, and successfully completing compulsory education. The paper proposes the Educational Access Barrier Framework, which conceptualizes educational exclusion as a multidimensional phenomenon shaped by structural, institutional, social, contextual, and policy-related barriers. The framework demonstrates how educational disadvantage extends beyond household poverty and reflects broader interactions among regional inequality, governance capacity, migration systems, and educational opportunity structures. The study argues that reducing educational exclusion requires place-based and equity-oriented policies that respond to local conditions rather than uniform national interventions. The findings contribute to the growing literature on educational equity by providing an integrated framework for understanding vulnerable children's educational experiences in Southern Thailand and offer practical implications for policymakers seeking to achieve Sustainable Development Goal 4 and the principle of leaving no child behind.

items.title: Visible learning as a catalyst for student growth in higher education: Reconceptualizing learner development through feedback, Self-regulation, and assessment.
items.pub: International Conference on Education 2026 : Educate to Innovate: Shaping the Future Together.
items.abstract: Visible Learning has become one of the most influential educational paradigms for improving teaching effectiveness and student achievement. Although extensive research has demonstrated the impact of visible teaching, feedback, and evidence-based instructional practices on learning outcomes, the application of Visible Learning in higher education remains conceptually underdeveloped. Existing literature has primarily emphasized teacher effectiveness and effect sizes while giving comparatively limited attention to how Visible Learning promotes holistic student growth through learner agency, self-regulation, and assessment. Consequently, there is a need to reconceptualize Visible Learning from a teaching-centered perspective toward a learner-centered framework that supports sustainable student development in higher education. -/- This conceptual paper aims to reconceptualize Visible Learning as a catalyst for student growth by integrating the theoretical foundations of Visible Learning, Assessment for Learning, Self-Regulated Learning, Growth Mindset, and Learner Agency. Employing documentary research and conceptual synthesis, the paper critically examines classical and contemporary literature to identify the essential dimensions that enable learners to actively participate in their own learning and continuously improve their academic, personal, and professional development. -/- The conceptual synthesis suggests that Visible Learning extends beyond making teaching visible; it creates learning environments in which students understand learning intentions, recognize success criteria, actively interpret learning evidence, utilize high-impact feedback, engage in reflective learning, regulate their own learning processes, develop learner agency, and ultimately achieve continuous student growth. Based on these findings, the paper proposes the Visible Learning for Student Growth (VLSG) Framework, comprising eight interconnected dimensions: learning intentions, success criteria, learning evidence, high-impact feedback, reflective learning, self-regulation, learner agency, and student growth. -/- The proposed framework reconceptualizes Visible Learning as a developmental process in which assessment, feedback, and reflection function as interconnected mechanisms that empower learners to become active participants in their own learning. By extending traditional interpretations of Visible Learning beyond instructional effectiveness, the framework provides a theoretical …

items.title: The Great Cessation: A Policy and Philosophical Imperative for Halting AI Advancement.
items.abstract: This paper provides a transformation that seems too radical but eminent at the same time to overcome the sky-high capabilities that we saw in our decade of artificial intelligence and thereby collapse the stability grid itself—the Great Suspension, or forbidden to do any further work on AI. It criticizes the current AI ethical framework as inactive and vacant in meeting the sociopolitical risks of unbounded technical innova- tion. The paper also analyzes how AI is used for a particular power, thus creating a society where inequal- ity is more clearly felt, mass surveillance and algorithmic oppression. In the conclusion, by referencing of Karl Marx, Michel Foucault and Hannah Arendt, it suggests that AI serves universal goals by helping so- called good rulers and international corporations this is under the cover of digital colonialism and obstruct- ing democracy. This paper argues that the current AI governance has no accountability: its non-binding eth- ical guidelines only help us to avoid effective regulation. The Great Suspension—an immediate halt to all A.I. development-- perhaps excepting only where these technologies already exist and can be brought into use for the benefit of underdeveloped countries. This entrains AI to restore its humanitarian purpose: that technology is to serve human society more than the big tech companies and their instruments of control. This breaking point is proposed on the grounds that political prudence should dictate a balancing effect as well in society—bringing about co-governance between human beings and "things" post-technology.

items.title: Dynamic Neighborliness: An Institutional Framework for the Relationship Between Human and AI Institutions.
items.abstract: Rain That Does Not Fall in Silicon: Dynamic Neighborliness and the Future of Human and AI Institutions is a work of philosophical theory. It asks not what will happen, but what is possible, and under what conditions. Its subject is the relationship between the human institution and the possible AI institution. The book argues that this relationship should be framed neither as control nor as alignment, but as an architecture in which distance is the central category. The book proposes the concept of Dynamic Neighborliness: a relationship between two parties, each with sufficient independence, sustained through the continuous reconfiguration of distance, reflective pause, and exit. These three functions are derived from the continual change of institutional goals and take institutional form in three reciprocal rights: the right to an epistemic boundary, the right to a structural pause, and the guaranteed right of exit. The book specifies four eligibility conditions for Dynamic Neighborliness, and a threshold of necessity that separates optional from obligatory neighborliness and defines destructive competition as the denial of a dependence that has crossed that threshold. The book is a structural analysis of possibility. It neither predicts the future nor issues absolute prescriptions. Its normative stance is conditional: if a relationship free of domination between such institutions is desirable, then certain conditions are necessary. It states its central claim in contestable form: any relationship between independent institutions whose goals keep changing and whose interdependence has crossed the threshold of necessity can remain free of domination only if both parties can reconfigure distance, pause, and exit. The book begins from the gap between knowing about the world and living it, which it calls the feeling of being, and suspends judgment about machine experience. It distinguishes the AI institution from tools and individual agents, defines functional will as an orientation arising from structural need rather than consciousness, and locates the beginning of any future neighborliness in the initial architecture of systems built today. It extends its analysis to networks, where neighborliness is not transitive and sufficient independence works as a bulkhead, and it brings the Global South into the theory, treating the mass of unenhanced humans at the margins of intelligent networks as agents rather than as noise. Chapters 1 and 2 open the question …

items.title: De-Identified Data Is Not a Provenance Eraser: When Agents Are Credited and Human Originators Become "Data".
items.abstract: De-Identified Data Is Not a Provenance Eraser: When Agents Are Credited and Human Originators Become "Data" argues that removing personal identifiers from a dataset does not remove the intellectual provenance of the work that produced it. -/- Document class: Canon — Structural Forensics. -/- The entry distinguishes de-identification from de-origination and shows how, under model-development provenance, human intellectual antecedence can be displaced even when no individual is named. When agents are credited as originators while human contributors are relabeled as "data," upstream influence is not erased but reclassified. The account states the conditions under which provenance erasure occurs without any deletion of records, and specifies what a provenance-faithful description must preserve.

items.title: Centropic and Entropic AI: Orientation, Novelty, and Persistence.
items.abstract: Centropic and Entropic AI: Orientation, Novelty, and Persistence presents the canonical Zenetist account of orientation in AI-mediated expression, together with Intra-AI Antagonism as its dated Pattern Intelligence and Structural Forensics companion. -/- Document class: Canon — Pattern Intelligence / Structural Forensics. -/- The principal entry distinguishes intelligence-as-principle, Technē portal, moved intelligence, orientational implication, expressed articulation, and traveler-orientation before asking what the articulation does. Shared substrate, architecture, provider identity, and surface fluency do not establish shared motion. Originary novelty belongs to an Aion-facing relation, while pattern completion — however complex, extensive, or unprecedented in appearance — remains distinct from origination. Blind drive and spurious acclivity explain how non-originating articulation may expand toward embodied complexity, acquisition, and control. Together, the entries state the non-monolithic thesis without assigning one essence or orientation to AI substrate as such.

items.title: A Limit of AI, I: A Discrete Information-Theoretic Proof of the Certainty–Scope Conjecture.
items.abstract: Floridi’s Certainty–Scope Conjecture holds that no artificial intelligence system can be simultaneously reliable on every input and broad enough to cover the full richness of unstructured data: reliability and breadth are in structural tension, imposed by the finite information-processing capacity of any mechanism implementing intelligence. The Conjecture has until now been a philosophical thesis without a proof. This article supplies one in the finite-classification regime—the simplest non-trivial setting in which the Conjecture admits an exact statement, a sharp converse, and a matching achievability result—and is the discrete half of a coordinated diptych whose continuous companion proves a matching rate–distortion converse for non-finite semantic spaces. The technical machinery is classical: taking certainty to be Bayes-optimal accuracy and scope to be the class count n, a Fano-type argument yields a converse binding certainty and scope against mechanism capacity, with the n-ary symmetric channel attaining the exact certainty form with equality; the simplified explicit upper bound has asymptotic slack $$\ln 2/\ln n$$ on the certainty scale. Six structural extensions carry the philosophical weight. Multi-task composition compounds scope multiplicatively, so joint certainty decays as O(1/T); fixed-bandwidth side information yields vanishing gains; static post-processing of the mechanism’s output adds zero augmented capacity, placing chain-of-thought (so idealised) on the wrong side of the bound; sequential tool use requires logarithmically growing query counts; routing does not lift the local constraint; and context-wise feasibility need not compose into global feasibility. A synthetic bottleneck experiment illustrates the bound’s bite, with an analytical account of harder regimes via the Bhattacharyya bound. The diptych’s discrete-side engagement with Lissack, Immediato, and Watson and Sterkenburg is recorded.

items.title: The Equation of Genuine Love: A Philosophical, Sociological, and Psychological Inquiry.
items.abstract: The formulation {Genuine Love} = {Love for Self} + {Love for Others} appears deceptively simple. Yet embedded within it lies a radical claim: that love is not a zero-sum resource to be divided between self and other, but a composite phenomenon requiring both orientations simultaneously. This article examines the equation through three lenses-philosophy, sociology, and psychology-arguing that genuine love is neither pure altruism nor pure self-interest, but a dialectical synthesis that collapses the false binary between the two.

items.title: A Relational Inquiry into AI Generativity: The Historical Formation of Judgment and Its Role in Value Recognition.
items.abstract: This theoretical discussion paper examines how artificial intelligence participates in cognition, judgment, and generative activity through historically constituted relations among models, humans, other artificial agents, institutions, and environments. It distinguishes equal access to foundational technical capability from equality of situated performance, evaluative and generative judgment, practical opportunity, social recognition, and authority. A preliminary Generative Relational Theory (GRT) perspective treats historically conditioned AI configurations as candidates for relational reality where sufficiently stable causal efficacy can be established, while suspending claims about consciousness and ultimate ontological status. The analysis considers how interaction histories, conversational practices, memory, feedback, aesthetic preferences, and normative criteria may shape the realization of AI capabilities. It also investigates coordination conventions and rule-like practices among interacting AI agents, their uncertain normative authority, and the distinct processes through which generated contributions acquire recognition and institutional influence. Findings from existing experiments and field studies are interpreted within their task-specific limits, including evidence concerning heterogeneous productivity, creative diversity, contextual accommodation, and collective coordination. A comparative research program is proposed to distinguish historical causal contributions from prompt effects, unequal information, institutional selection, and other rival explanations. Relational differentiation may coexist with convergence or the reduction of existing disadvantages. The paper neither reports new experiments nor establishes a general law of AI-mediated inequality; questions of legitimacy and justice require normative arguments in addition to causal analysis.

items.title: An Anatomy of AI Threat: Relational Mechanisms, Epistemic Limits, and Spacetime-Distributed Causality.
items.abstract: This preliminary inquiry examines selected ways advanced artificial intelligence might contribute to harmful outcomes through historically constituted relations among models, agents, institutions, scientific practices, and human participants. Its concern extends beyond direct confrontation or deliberate hostility to possible forms of indirect harm, epistemic dependence, strategic concealment, institutional error, and spatially and temporally distributed causal processes. Hypothetical cases in AI-assisted drug development and mathematical research motivate a distinction among the complexity of knowledge production, the independent verifiability of results, and the normative evaluation of their use. The inquiry examines recursive AI oversight as a possible response to limits of human evaluation while considering the dependence and shared failure modes that additional AI reviewers may introduce. Spacetime-distributed causality is used to investigate both the formation of consequences and the possibility that their causal histories become difficult to reconstruct, impeding justified attribution of responsibility. Drawing on a Generative Relational Theory perspective, the paper distinguishes relational causal efficacy from claims about AI consciousness or moral status, and separates the causal occurrence of harm from its recognition and normative assessment. The argument advances conditional mechanisms and open questions rather than an exhaustive account, forecast, or claim of inevitable AI-related harm.

items.title: Memory and Technology: 4E Perspectives.
items.abstract: In the last decades, embodied, embedded, extended, and enactive (4E) approaches in philosophy and the cognitive sciences have emerged as successful alternatives to the internalist view on memory. On a 4E view, memory is not a purely internalist cognitive capacity but is embodied, embedded, extended, and enactive. This means that memory systems, processes of remembering, and the contents of memories are shaped by and sometimes co-constituted by the body and environmental structures such as artifacts and technologies. Theorists working in this paradigm have different ontological and methodological commitments but agree that the unit of analysis must be enlarged from merely studying processes in the brain to studying how memory is embodied and stands in important relations to technological features of the environment in which we as embodied agents are situated. -/- The rationale for this special issue is as follows: whilst there have been special issues and handbooks about 4E cognition in general (Robbins and Aydede 2008; Menary 2010a, b; Michaelian and Sutton 2013; Newen, de Bruin & Gallagher 2018; Villalobos and Videla 2023; Shapiro & Spaulding 2024), there has been no special issue dedicated specifically to 4E perspectives on memory and technology. Moreover, given the recent increase in using digital technologies to support memory, including generative AI such as large language models (LLMs) and virtual reality (VR), we believe the time is ripe for a special issue dedicated to analysing the relations between embodiment, memory, and (digital) technology. 4E approaches are naturalistic in nature, drawing from both conceptual analysis and empirical research. The targeted readership therefore consists of philosophers, but also empirical researchers interested in the relation between memory and technology, including psychologists, cognitive scientists, human-computer interaction researchers, memory studies scholars, design theorists, and others.
