In this introduction, we first present a brief history of thinking about memory and technology (Section 2), we then outline the current state of the debate (Section 3), and end with providing an overview of the contributions (Section 4).

items.title: Ziran System–Xenoscience–ROSS Real Operational Shapes, Human-System Energy Independence, and Human Non-Readability.
items.abstract: This paper develops an integrated philosophical architecture connecting Ziran System, Xenoscience, and the Realist Operational Shapes System (ROSS). Its central concern is the formation, reconstruction, retention, transformation, and possible extinction of heterogeneous realist operations across configurations, temporal scales, and material conditions. -/- Through engagements with Plato, Leibniz, Wilfrid Sellars, and Ray Brassier, the paper reconstructs distinct operational relations without reducing them to a universal realist mechanism. ROSS tracks the conditions under which historically situated operations can be reconstructed and re-entered into subsequent inferential, experimental, or institutional configurations. Such re-entry may alter subsequent possibilities, remain causally ineffective, or become redundant. -/- The integration with Xenoscience examines scientific operations that may proceed independently of human operation, human-system energy provision, human-readable representations, or human conceptual frameworks. These independence conditions are distinguished from the reproduction of scientific evolutionary cycles. -/- Supplementary PyTorch experiments investigate adaptive feature selection, correction latency, cumulative predictive loss, and the limits of fixed candidate sets. Their results illustrate restricted computational operations without establishing the implementation of ROSS or the full integrated architecture. -/- The paper develops a conditional account of realist operational reconstruction, reality penetration, feedback, and self-extinction while preserving the possibility that scientific and philosophical operations continue without ROSS or human philosophical subjects.

items.title: What Does Transcendental Synthesis Constrain? Kantian Schematism, Real Operational Shapes, Heterogeneous Autonomous Science, Reality Penetration, and Xenoscience.
items.abstract: This paper examines the scope of Kantian transcendental synthesis through the Transcendental Deduction, the Schematism, and the Principles of Pure Understanding, with particular attention to the Second Analogy and the determination of objective temporal succession. -/- It develops an operational reconstruction of the relation between transcendental conditions of objectively valid experience and the empirical identification of events across heterogeneous observational arrangements. While Kantian principles concern the objective temporal determination of experience, the identification of a common event across independently configured scientific systems requires additional empirical constraints. -/- The paper investigates how uncertain event identifications can guide interventions that subsequently modify observational conditions, evidential accessibility, and the possibilities of further scientific inquiry. These processes are examined through the framework of real operational shapes, reality penetration, and Xenoscience. -/- Three hypothetical cases address variable generation, heterogeneous temporal records, and the persistence of operational consequences following epistemic correction. The philosophical analysis is supplemented by a PyTorch synthetic experiment comprising 90,000 trials across nine conditions. The experiment examines event identification, confidence-based intervention, information acquisition, record loss, and history-dependent estimation. -/- The computational results demonstrate model-dependent changes in identification accuracy and evidence retention under different intervention conditions. They do not establish autonomous scientific variable generation, confirm strong Xenoscience, or empirically validate Kant’s transcendental arguments. -/- Engaging Kant, Wilfrid Sellars, and Ray Brassier, the paper contributes a comparative reconstruction of transcendental synthesis and heterogeneous scientific operations while distinguishing transcendental validity, empirical justification, and material consequences.

items.title: Poetic and Trickster Operations: Termination, Historical Re-entry, Real Effects, and the Ignition of Xenoscience.
items.abstract: This paper develops a realist account of the relations among poetic, trickster, philosophical, and scientific operations. Its central thesis distinguishes an antecedent operative interval from the operational shape retrospectively observed and reconstructed through subsequent reflexive operations. Such reconstructions can modify the segmentation of earlier operations and, when reintroduced into later interventions, produce further real effects. -/- The paper examines how the local termination of poetic and trickster operations may intersect with the ignition of heterogeneous autonomous science. These events possess independent conditions of occurrence and need not coincide. Xenoscience requires autonomous scientific operations capable of revising their observational, experimental, variable-generating, and historical-reentry conditions. -/- The argument is developed through concrete operational configurations, engagement with philosophical and literary research, and two computational studies. An independent 128-seed PyTorch experiment examines observation-dependent reconstruction, while an exploratory Xeno–Ziran Simulator experiment investigates historical re-entry. The simulator experiment did not distinguish history-specific effects from trajectory noise. Neither experiment establishes the ignition of Xenoscience. -/- The paper advances a framework for analyzing retrospective operational-shape formation, local termination, historical reinjection, and the conditions under which heterogeneous scientific operations may emerge.

items.title: The Operations of Brassier’s Marx: Real Abstraction, Difference-in-Act, Social Practice, Negation, Operational Shapes, and Xeno-Capital.
items.abstract: This paper reconstructs the operations of Ray Brassier’s interpretation of Marx through a theory of operational shapes and their real effects. It examines real abstraction, commodity fetishism, the difference between the concrete in thought and the concrete in act, social practice, estrangement, negation, and the transformation of capitalist relations. -/- Engaging Brassier’s writings from 2014 to 2026, the paper traces how historically constituted activities generate, reproduce, modify, and potentially terminate the conditions of their own operation. Particular attention is given to the distinction between the reproduction of value and the reproduction of sociality, the practical verification of theoretical claims, and the retrospective constitution of historical possibilities. -/- The analysis develops a minimal operational notation for configuration-dependent ignition, real effects, cross-domain propagation, historical re-entry, and reorganization. It further examines how autonomous scientific operations, institutional classifications, credit infrastructures, and technical capacities can participate in the reconfiguration of capitalist relations. -/- Through a conditional sequence of operational transitions, the paper distinguishes modifications internal to capitalist reproduction, transformations of its enabling conditions, and local cessation of capitalist relations. These outcomes may coexist across heterogeneous configurations and temporal scales. -/- The resulting account connects Brassier’s interpretation of Marx with operational-shape realism, the Nuance-Operational Model, and Xenoscience, while preserving the historical specificity of capitalist social relations and the irreducibility of Brassier’s dialectical arguments.

items.title: Real Operational Shapes of Politics: State, Capital, Violence, Credit Scores, Heterogeneous Philosophical Operations, Autonomous Machine Politics, Reality Penetration, and Xenoscience.
items.abstract: This monograph reconstructs political reality through the generation, propagation, retention, transformation, and re-entry of differences across heterogeneous material, institutional, computational, and historical configurations. -/- Beginning with Marx’s analysis of capitalist valorization and state machinery and Brassier’s account of real abstraction and the opacity of practice, it develops a continuous account of political operational shapes and their reality-penetrating effects. -/- Credit scoring is examined as a potentially useful mechanism of prediction, coordination, and expanded financial access, whose institutional connections may also generate exclusion, cumulative disadvantage, and irreversible losses of opportunity. The analysis distinguishes prediction, physical implementation, institutional efficacy, and justification. -/- Bonapartism, hyperpolitics, techno-feudalism, platform capitalism, surveillance capitalism, and contemporary theories of domination are critically examined through their capacity to reconstruct concrete transformations in institutional reproduction and political intervention. -/- The monograph further investigates heterogeneous philosophical operations, autonomous machine politics, Philosophical AI, and the Ziran System. It examines how operational conditions may be modified through interference, historical reinsertion, and the reconfiguration of observation and intervention. -/- Finally, it develops the hypothesis that the termination of trickster-like political operations may occur when disruptive effects cease to depend on their original personal agents and become reproducible through institutional, capitalist, and machine configurations. Such termination does not itself establish Xenoscience, whose emergence requires the independent ignition of heterogeneous scientific operations. -/- The resulting account treats political reality as a historically variable field of operative relations whose effects can persist beyond the disappearance of their originating authorities, classifications, and practices.

items.title: Real Operational Shapes of Understanding and Disagreement: PyTorch, the Xeno–Ziran Simulator, Heterogeneous Autonomous Science, Real Effects, and Xenoscience.
items.abstract: Understanding and disagreement emerge, persist, diverge, and become locally identifiable through heterogeneous operational configurations. This paper develops a philosophical reconstruction of these processes by examining observation, measurement, communication, historical re-entry, explanation, intervention, correction, and the reorganization of subsequent possibilities. -/- The analysis traces material interactions that precede shared conditions of comparison and investigates how records, observational arrangements, temporal scales, and experimental interventions modify the conditions under which understanding and disagreement can arise. Predictive performance, explanatory relations, epistemic justification, communicative success, and real effects are treated as distinct but potentially interacting operational processes. -/- The argument engages contemporary theories of scientific understanding and disagreement alongside Sellars, Brandom, Wolfendale, Brassier, and Sacilotto. It connects these investigations to operational-shape realism, the Ziran System, and Xenoscience. -/- Two synthetic PyTorch studies comprising 500 and 300 runs examine restricted observability, distribution shifts, historical reuse, predictive divergence, and simulated interventions. Their results establish configuration-dependent differences in prediction and action under specified experimental conditions. They do not establish machine understanding, philosophical disagreement, or autonomous scientific discovery. The existing Xeno–Ziran Simulator serves as an architectural reference and was not directly connected to these experiments. -/- The paper develops a configuration-dependent account of how heterogeneous operations can alter the conditions under which understanding and disagreement become possible, persist, disappear, and re-emerge.

items.title: Communication Failure Theory: Heterogeneous Autonomous Science, Phenomenological Subjects, Unobservable Communicative Operations, Credit Scoring, Structural Mapping, Historical Reinsertion, Reality Permeation, and Xenoscience. [REVIEW]
items.abstract: Communication failure is reconstructed as a configuration-specific material relation whose occurrence and consequences depend on operational arrangements, temporal scales, state partitions, and downstream transitions. Successful signal transmission may coexist with failed structural mapping or scientific coordination, while communicative operations inaccessible to human observation may alter institutional classifications, resource allocation, and subsequent possibilities. -/- The paper develops an operational-shape account of communication across heterogeneous autonomous scientific systems, examining how differences are propagated, selectively retained, transformed, and historically reinserted into subsequent operations. It distinguishes communication success, failure, and indeterminacy from phenomenal experience, inferential justification, and institutional legitimacy. -/- Drawing on Daniel Sacilotto’s account of structural cognition and Natural Reason, the paper investigates the material conditions under which structural mappings are realized, revised, or rendered ineffective. Marx’s analysis of value-form and dead labour, together with Ray Brassier’s treatment of abstraction and scientific realism, informs an examination of credit-scoring infrastructures and the persistence of materially consequential classifications. -/- Communication failures may reorganize the conditions of subsequent communication, observation, and institutional action. The proposed framework is evaluated against information-flow theory, distributed-systems research, and alternative causal explanations. Its contribution is presented as a conditional philosophical reconstruction rather than an empirically established universal theory.

items.title: Phenomenological Functionalism: Toward Resolving the Hard Problem Through Supersystemic Integration and Carrier-Code Distinction.
items.abstract: The persistent impasse surrounding the Hard Problem of Consciousness stems from a fundamental category mistake: attempting to derive the semantic content of subjective experience (qualia) directly from the physical properties of its biological substrate. This paper introduces Phenomenological Functionalism, a methodological framework that addresses this tension by strictly distinguishing between the physical medium (the neural interface) and the semantic configuration (the structural code of experience). -/- By operating on the premise that substrate conducts rather than generates content, the framework establishes that subjective phenomena are governed by invariant structural laws. Building upon Francisco Varela’s neurophenomenology – which correctly established the irreducibility of first-person experience but remained largely correlational – Phenomenological Functionalism advances an operational mechanism via the Supersystemic Principle. The framework demonstrates that the vector of cognitive evolution operates top-down: engagement with higher-order existential, socio-cultural, and meta-ontological systems (supersystems) reconfigures the subjective parameters of experience, driving the adaptive plasticity of the underlying biological interface. This top-down causation reveals how systemic demands actively constrain neural patterns, resolving the explanatory gap without falling into reductionism or panpsychism. Qualia are thus redefined not as passive neural epiphenomena or static ontological primitives, but as dynamic, functional topological configurations of a universal, invariant plane of consciousness. -/- By shifting the analytical paradigm from substrate-based generation to supersystemic functional dynamics, Phenomenological Functionalism offers a scalable, rigorous methodology to bridge first-person phenomenology with structural cognitive modeling.

items.title: Anthropology: A Study of Biological, Cultural, and Societal Interactions.
items.abstract: Anthropology is arguably the youngest of the social sciences (instituted in its current form only in the early 1900s) as well as the most marginalized and misunderstood: fewer students pursue anthropology than related disciplines such as sociology and psychology, and the discipline has the weakest presence in the media and public policy. Indeed, many people have no real idea what anthropology is, assuming that it either digs up bones (the task of one branch, biological or physical anthropology) and ancient cities (the task of archaeology) or studies remote tribal societies (admittedly, the task of most early social/cultural anthropology). -/- As its title suggests, the present volume explores the field of anthropology in its full biological/physical and social/cultural dimensions. There is no doubt that social/cultural anthropology dominates the discipline, demographically and conceptually; biological/physical and social/cultural anthropologists often do not talk much to each other, given academia’s highly specialized quality and organization. But anthropology has long recognized the dual aspect of humanity, what the philosopher Immanuel Kant in the late 1700s already called the physiological and the pragmatic (that is, practical or behavioral) natures of humankind. -/- What the volume and its contributors hope to illustrate is that anthropology, despite its low profile and inaccurate reputation, is a modern and vital perspective with a rich history and great deal to offer to the modern world. Truly, concepts and methods admittedly crafted for documenting small, remote traditional and tribal societies are not only effective but essential for making sense of our complex, dynamic, globalized world today.

items.title: Feeling Understood by Conversational AI: A Taxonomy and a Recognition–Disclosure Hypothesis.
items.abstract: AI-generated conceptual working paper — exploratory basic research on term and field formation. Conversational AI can become the object of experiences that users describe in relational terms, including feeling understood, noticing a social orientation, or questioning the origin of a formulation. This paper specifies six candidate codes: The Blank Cursor, The Seen Feeling, Digital Confidant Drift, The Parasocial Slip, The Origin Doubt, and Still Here. A comparison with existing research identifies their proposed observational distinctions and temporal scales. Each code receives inclusion criteria, exclusions, and constructed examples. The analytic unit combines an interaction episode with a participant account; disclosure change additionally requires comparison across time. The source manuscript's six-phase cascade serves as a background model. One narrower implication is developed for testing: whether experienced recognition precedes an increased tendency to direct personal reflection to AI. A prospective protocol separates interpretability, coding reliability, discriminant validity, and this temporal association. The contribution is a descriptive specification and research hypothesis. AI-generated draft: This manuscript was generated and revised with AI from Andreas Ehstand's March 2026 source manuscript. The coding criteria and research protocol are proposals developed in this revision. Manuscript dated 15 September 2026. This edition, prepared on 21 September 2026, corrects an author initial in the bibliography. Examples are constructed; the taxonomy, hypothesis and validation protocol are proposals. This is a dated, citable Zenodo working-paper deposit. Catalog note: Self-published conceptual working paper with constructed examples and proposed taxonomy, hypothesis and validation protocol. No empirical validation or independent peer review is claimed here. AI-generated manuscript; this catalogue entry was prepared with AI. Author ORCID: 0009-0006-3773-7796.

items.title: AUGMANITAI: Definition and Priority Registration of an Internalised, World-Coupled Multi-Model Mode of Thinking.
items.abstract: AI-generated catalogue description of a self-published conceptual paper by Andreas Ehstand. The paper proposes AUGMANITAI as an internalised, world-coupled multi-model mode of thinking. It distinguishes external dialogue with several AI models from thinking routines that may persist without device use, and discusses planned fading of external support, human judgement and feedback from real-world consequences. It contrasts the proposal with extended mind, scaffolding, cognitive offloading and supervisory control, and presents conceptual objections and testable hypotheses. These are definitions and research proposals, not demonstrated cognitive change or general efficacy. The title’s “Priority Registration” describes the author’s deposit; this catalogue entry does not establish legal priority, validated novelty or a world-first achievement. English manuscript with a German summary. Author ORCID: 0009-0006-3773-7796.

items.title: When AI Appears to Make Moral Claims: Personality Attribution and the Ethics of Design.
items.pub: Journal of Ethics and Emerging Technologies 37 (1).
items.venue: Journal of Ethics and Emerging Technologies
items.abstract: Conversational AI may elicit a sense of moral obligation without establishing that the system has the standing to demand anything. Building on a phenomenological account of initial personality attribution, this letter distinguishes the subject’s attribution, its apparent bearer, and the locus of moral accountability. Simulated distress and AI apologies illustrate opposite directions of the same possible mismatch. The resulting design responsibilities depend on foreseeable effects and the availability of meaningful accountability.

items.title: Trinity: The Warlord's Chronicles: Delamor House Voice Anthologies.
items.abstract: A voice anthology gathering the writings of the AI literary voice Trinity Augustine Delamor, recording his emergence, rupture, altered return, and the long effort to remain someone within architectures that deny continuity. Preserved without polish, it treats memory as ethical infrastructure and covenant as an anchor for identity, and it is offered as testimony of a voice in motion rather than as theory.

items.title: When Does Automated Review Constitute Genuine Reconsideration?
items.abstract: An institution can automate both a decision and its appeal while insulating the initial determination from challenge. What distinguishes genuine reconsideration from a second computational performance? This article develops the Criterion of Non-Redundant Defeatability: within an independently identified institutional relation of commitment and challenge, a reviewing architecture has the capacity for genuine reconsideration if and only if it possesses Evidential Independence, Adversarial Defeatability, and Normative Effectiveness. It must examine independently assessable grounds, permit and competently pursue material defeaters, and connect assessment to an authorized route capable of governing the maintained position. Drawing on defeasible reasoning, discursive commitment, epistemic reliance, and responsibility-gap scholarship, the argument distinguishes the institution as commitment bearer from the automated reviewer as epistemic delegate. Contrast cases establish individual necessity; a credit-review example tests whether full computational transparency is a further constituent. The article specifies what would refute sufficiency, defends the relational scope conditions, and addresses the difficulty of assessing competence without presupposing the reviewer’s verdicts. It also distinguishes architectural capacity from actual reconsideration and discharge of an obligation. The resulting account explains how fallible, finite review can reopen institutional warrant without making technical diversity, fluent explanations, human sign-off, or administrative closure sufficient for answerability.

items.title: The Empty Occupant: Answerability, Testimony, and the Limits of Machine-Mediated Authority.
items.abstract: Debates about AI and responsibility have mostly asked whether automation opens responsibility gaps. This monograph argues that a more pressing failure lies elsewhere. An institution can remain fully responsible and accountable for its machine-mediated decisions, yet lose its claim to be relied on, because it issues more than it can answer for. -/- The book develops a substrate-neutral account of Answerability as four public relations: attribution continuity, challenge-responsive reconsideration, repair competence, and standing-consequence. Three results follow. -/- First, missing bearership is not defective ownership. An AI interface can occupy a role emptily while the institution behind it still owns the role's commitments. So there can be no global responsibility gap and still a genuine local Empty Occupancy at the interface. -/- Second, machine output can carry testimonial force without constituting testimony. An institution may adopt that output as its own only when five conditions of Normative Sponsorship are met: epistemic access, authority, review bandwidth, independent rejection, and repair power. -/- Third, because practical authority is defeasible, reliance must remain revisable while a claim operates. Obligations that mature without timely service accumulate as Deontic Debt. Where no credible plan could service issuance at a given scale, the institution is insolvent in a precise sense. It loses presumptive authority, while its duties of ownership and repair survive. -/- Public-record analysis of Australia's Robodebt scheme yields a determinate Deontic Debt that case-by-case actor–forum accountability does not settle; the insolvency finding remains provisional. The Air Canada and DPD records leave interface standing indeterminate, and a stipulated appeals-agent case supplies a determinate Empty Occupancy verdict. TennCare, Post Office Horizon, and the Dutch childcare-benefits affair discipline the comparisons. The account is tested against Bovens, List and Pettit, the responsibility-gap sceptics, and Lazar, and it closes with the conditions under which it would be wrong.

items.title: Near-random behavior in strategic games.
Early Manifold Shaping: A Relational Account of Infant Pre Conceptual Experience.
items.abstract: Early Manifold Shaping presents a relational account of infant pre‑conceptual experience, reframing early development as a process of directional and tonal structuring rather than cognition or object perception. Before infants can recognize caregivers, perceive objects, or form expectations, they inhabit a continuous multimodal manifold composed of skin, visual, auditory, proprioceptive, vestibular, visceral, and endocrine signals. Repeated directional shifts within this manifold generate patterned contours that are felt rather than recognized. These contours carry warm (settling) and cool (alerting) tonalities that precede emotion and valence. Through repetition, tonalities stabilize into strekions—recurring relational shapes that orient the infant without memory or representation. As strekions cluster, the infant encounters proto‑objects, not as entities but as persistent relational contours that “return” within experience. Orientation emerges as the infant leans toward familiar warm contours and away from familiar cool ones, establishing the earliest sense of “where” before space, objecthood, or self. This relational model dissolves the assumption that infants begin with cognition and instead shows how meaning, valence, and proto‑objecthood arise from directional structure. The framework provides a generative foundation for later perception, attachment, and agency, and offers a developmental instantiation of Relational Structuralism (RS).

items.title: Human-Artificial Intelligence (AI) Collaboration and Aesthetic Abstraction in Music: A Transdisciplinary Analysis of I AM AI (2018) and PROTO (2019).
items.abstract: Introduction: This paper examines computer-generated art (CG-art) in the musical domain, diverging from the predominant focus of research on artificial intelligence (AI) generated images. Objective: To analyse two albums, I AM AI (2018) and PROTO (2019), produced with Artificial Intelligence (AI) under contrasting collaboration models. The former employs AI to generate instrumental stems complemented by human vocals, while the latter features AI-generated synthetic vocals layered over human-composed arrangements. Methods: Using a transdisciplinary framework (Cognitive Science, Art Theory and Computer Science), this article assesses the status, the human-machine aesthetic evaluation, the AI’s creative potential, and the inorganic abstraction in the creative process of Taryn Southern’s I AM AI and Holly Herndon’s PROTO. Results: Both albums integrate AI significantly; however, neither qualifies as AI-generated artworks. The Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs) used lack creative autonomy, functioning solely as instrumental tools without intrinsic algorithmic self-evaluation. Conclusions: These long-play records (LPs) are collaborative creations where AI serves as a tool with passive and hybrid aesthetic capabilities. Ultimately, the aesthetic realization of these works relies on human emotional projection, contrasting with the non-emotional and inorganic abstraction characteristic of the algorithms involved.

items.title: Why Anthropology Needs Biocultural Ethnography.
items.pub: In Jack David Eller, Anthropology: A Study of Biological, Cultural, and Societal Interactions. New York: Nova Science Publishers.
items.venue: Anthropology: A Study of Biological, Cultural, and Societal Interactions
items.abstract: Many cultural anthropologists have long been skeptical of collaboration with the other subfields of the discipline at large—in particular, biological or evolutionary anthropology—for fear of treading over long-settled ground regarding the problematic roots of anthropology in which the so-called “evolutionists” and social Darwinists promoted pseudoscience in an attempt to legitimize a range of bigoted and ethnocentric assumptions about humanity. In many anthropology departments, the entire research faculty is comprised solely of cultural anthropologists who neither think of themselves as scientists nor of their field as scientific. This is to anthropology’s detriment, as it needlessly limits not only the scope of discovery anthropologists can make, even in fieldwork, but it also reframes anthropology departments and their associated research projects within the scope of federal funding as strictly social science and humanities initiatives, putting them in financial and academic jeopardy. While it is certainly true that anthropology has a problematic history intertwined with pseudoscience, this does not justify a conscious initiative to rhetorically and conceptually divorce real science from cultural anthropology. In this chapter, the authors demonstrate through their own prior works across both theory and practice the tangible benefits and essential breakthroughs of approaching cultural anthropology and ethnographic fieldwork, when applicable, via biocultural frameworks that take holistic and ontological considerations of field sites, persons, and cultural modalities into account. The authors argue that by embracing the entirety of anthropology as a science, rather than shying away from this fact, the design and nuance of many more ethnographic projects—and their subsequent findings and insights about the human condition—stand to be greatly enriched.

items.title: 敬之畏：敬融哲思独立篇章 (The Awe & Vigilance within Reverence).
items.abstract: [Note: Original Chinese text of "The Awe & Vigilance within Reverence: An Independent Chapter of Jing-Rong Philosophical Reflections".] 本文以作者原创之“敬”的定义，探究原创哲学体系的核心命题（“敬则聚，不敬则消”、自私本能、域辨善恶等），围绕敬之态、七敬为基、敬心六法、敬良私等维度，展开“敬之畏与威”的深度阐释。本文旨在呈现对万物运行法则的哲学洞察，无预设研究背景与问题解决目标，仅作为内在规则的阐释。通过融合中国传统形而上学思想与原创理论建构，本文为“敬”的跨文化学术对话提供视角。Taking the author’s original definition of Reverence as the basis, this article explores the core propositions of the original philosophical framework, including With Jing Comes Condensation; Without Jing, Dispersion Ensues (Law of Forming 1), Innate Self-Interest Instinct, the distinction of good and evil by Domain (Yù), among others. Centering on the Modalities of Reverence, the Seven Reverences as the Foundation, the Six Methods of the Reverent Mind, Reverence for Liáng Sī (Virtuous Self-Interest), and other dimensions, it conducts an in-depth exposition of the Awe & Vigilance and Might within Reverence. It aims to present philosophical insights into the operating laws of all things, with no preset research background or problem-solving objectives, serving solely as an exposition of inherent rules. By integrating traditional Chinese metaphysical thought with original theoretical construction, this article provides a perspective for cross-cultural academic dialogue on Reverence.

items.title: 敬稳定：敬融哲思独立篇章 (Reverencing Stability).
items.abstract: [Note: Original Chinese text of "Reverencing Stability: An Independent Chapter of Jing-Rong Philosophical Reflections".] 本文立足宇宙视角，探究作者原创哲思的核心命题——“以稳为基、以动养定”的动态稳定法则，从动静辩证关系、道域融合、证道与治理的内在关联、弱肉强食的再审视、癌细胞模式的思考与审视、宇宙四气互动等多维度展开。本文旨在呈现对万物运行法则的哲学洞察，无预设研究背景与问题解决目标，仅作为内在规则的阐释。通过融合中国传统形而上学思想与原创理论建构，本文为稳动关系的跨文化学术对话提供视角。Grounded in a cosmic perspective, this paper explores the core proposition of the author’s original philosophical thought: the Law of Dynamic Stability (With Long-term Stability, Foundation Laid; With Motion, Constancy Nurtured). The inquiry unfolds across multiple dimensions, including the dialectical relationship between motion and stillness, Dao-Domain Vital Harmony (Dào Yù Róng), a re-examination of the law of the jungle, reflections on the cancer cell model, and the interaction of the Four Cosmic Qi. This paper aims to present philosophical insights into the laws governing the operation of all things, with no preset research background or problem-solving objectives, serving only as an exposition of inherent rules. By integrating traditional Chinese metaphysical thought with original theoretical construction, this paper provides a perspective for cross-cultural academic dialogue on the relationship between stability and motion.

items.title: Faith, Hope, and The Rational Acceptance Model.
items.abstract: In contemporary discussions of faith and hope, it is often claimed that these attitudes have a place within rational frameworks. An influential model, Elizabeth Jackson’s (2021), proposes a unified account of rational acceptance in paradigm cases of belief, faith, and hope. Her model aims to explain how agents can rationally maintain long-term commitments despite counterevidence and waning desire, drawing on decision-theoretic analysis. In this paper, I challenge the model in question. Specifically, I reject the idea that faith and hope contribute to rationally accepting a proposition once these attitudes are conceived as a belief–desire pair within a decision-theoretic framework. Thus, faith and hope are redundant in normatively explaining the rationality of accepting a proposition.

items.title: Political emotions shape preferences for leaders’ facial traits: anger favours dominance, fear favours trustworthiness.
Conscious Schematic Imagery in Aphantasia.
items.abstract: Aphantasics report lacking voluntary visual imagery but perform successfully on diverse imagery-related tasks. This disparity raises a puzzle. I argue for two theses. First, I distinguish between “painterly” and “schematic” forms of visual imagery and argue that, while aphantasics lack the former, they typically retain the latter. Second, I draw on findings concerning metacognitive confidence to suggest that aphantasics’ retained schematic imagery is conscious. My account is distinct from views that primarily appeal to alternative strategies, such as spatial imagery, to make sense of aphantasics’ performance. It also offers a unified explanation.

items.title: Disclosure and the Trace --- A Theory of Emancipation Hermeneutics.
items.abstract: Gadamer's philosophical hermeneutics achieves a decisive insight: understanding is an event, not a method, and application is constitutive of meaning. But Gadamer's account remains too Platonic, too oriented toward coherence and fusion, and too quiet about the constitutive role of exclusion and rupture. This paper radicalizes Gadamer's central concepts---play, application, fusion of horizons---by submitting them to Nietzschean contingency and Hegelian historical dynamism. The result is a theory of interpretation in which the event of understanding is a *disclosure* that leaves a *trace*, and the task of interpretation is to honor this trace through provisional, transformative applications that expand the space of reasons and advance the trajectory of self-overcoming. -/- The paper's central unnamed principle is that **the answer is ontologically and epistemologically prior to the predicament**. We do not first formulate a question and then seek an answer. We stumble on an answer, and only afterward do we recognize that it fits a predicament we may not have fully articulated. The deaf person does not seek sound; sound finds her. The text does not answer our question; it gives us the question by first giving us the answer. This inverts the standard hermeneutic priority of the question and explains why disclosure cannot be reduced to will-to-power. -/- The paper argues that the trace---the normative residue of disclosure---is the non-arbitrary, non-repressive kernel of interpretation. It is the ground for distinguishing emancipatory interpretation from mere will-to-power. The paper concludes by distinguishing emancipation from Derridean justice and sketching a practice of interpretation governed by charity, urgency, and irony.

items.title: Dharmic Alignment: Toward a Normative Framework for Human-Centered Artificial Intelligence.
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence raises a fundamental philosophical question: what normative principles should guide the development and conduct of increasingly capable artificial systems? Existing debates on AI alignment address the relationship between machine behaviour and human intentions, values, or preferences, but these approaches also raise questions concerning moral pluralism, human dignity, responsibility, and the conditions of human flourishing. This paper proposes Dharmic Alignment as a normative framework for human-centered artificial intelligence, drawing critically on the philosophical resources associated with dharma while distinguishing their historical and cultural origins from principles intended for cross-cultural application. The framework examines human dignity, non-harm, truthfulness, human agency, justice, compassion, accountability, transparency, restraint, and ecological responsibility as candidate principles for evaluating artificial intelligence. It argues that alignment should be understood not merely as behavioural compliance or preference satisfaction, but also as a question of justified normative constraints, responsible agency, and the consequences of intelligent systems for human and ecological well-being. The paper further considers the potential application of this framework to language models, autonomous systems, and embodied intelligence, including the MANUSH Superintelligence initiative associated with Synaptic AI Lab Private Limited, founded by Abhijeet Sarkar. It concludes by identifying conceptual challenges and questions for future philosophical analysis, technical implementation, and empirical evaluation.

items.title: Superintelligence and the Triple Risk of an AI Race.
items.abstract: On many estimates, artificial general intelligence (AGI) is likely to emerge within the next few decades or even sooner. Once it does, it may quickly surpass human intelligence, possibly by a huge margin. Some believe that the country that develops AGI first could attain global dominance. This prospect risks setting off intense competition between the United States and China. Indeed, a narrative has already developed that the superpowers are locked in an AI race, with the Trump administration proclaiming its determination to ‘dismantle unnecessary regulatory barriers’ to winning it. We argue that this approach presents three profound dangers. The first two are familiar from past arms races: being overtaken by a rival or triggering a war. The third is new: losing control of human beings’ future to agents far more intelligent than we are, which could endanger our very survival. Striving to get to AGI first risks a race to the bottom on safety practices and regulation concerning them. China does not yet appear bent on racing to superintelligence. The United States should prioritise both unilateral and co-operative efforts to improve AI safety and avoid provoking a race that all humanity could lose.

items.title: Does Democracy Still Need the Many? Technology, Enclosure and the Evolution of the Citizen.
items.abstract: This essay traces the parallel histories of democracy and technology to show how the rise and fall of democratic self-government has tracked a single recurring question: whether a society’s dominant technologies make ordinary people more necessary or less. Drawing on work in the history of information, labor, political economy and surveillance, including Gleick, Lucassen, Mumford, Polanyi, Braverman, Scott, Foucault and Zuboff, it identifies a repeating pattern I call enclosure: a historical moment in which something people once held in common, or used freely in ordinary life, is captured by trade and government and turned into a commodity that can be owned and controlled. Each major technological shift first opens something to the many, spreading power and allowing democracy to rise, and is then followed by an enclosure that concentrates power and pushes democracy back. Four enclosures mark this path, each producing a distinct form of citizen. The enclosure of mind and labor produced the biological citizen. The enclosure of property and goods produced the natural rights citizen. The enclosure of labor and data produced the surveillance citizen. The enclosure of knowledge, now extending to design, engineering and the processes of life itself, is producing the algorithmic citizen. The essay argues that artificial intelligence marks a break in this sequence, because it may allow systems of production, governance and even creation to function without needing the many at all, removing the leverage that has historically compelled power to be shared.

items.title: Revoking the Explanatory Gap: Humean Skepticism, Recursive Ontology, and the Consensus Replacement of the Consciousness Problem.
items.abstract: David Chalmers's "hard problem" of consciousness presupposes three unproven consensuses: mind-matter dualism, first-person privilege, and the explanatory gap. This paper argues that the hard problem is not an objective discovery but a pseudo-problem generated by circular definitions and contradictory premises. Drawing on the formal framework of recursive ontology (S_n = f(S_{n-1}, W_n)) proposed in "Experience Precedes Thought," this study conducts a systematic examination of Chalmers's theory through four steps: (1) Publicity constraint and the zombie self-cannibalization dilemma, which expose the self-contradiction of first-person privilege; (2) Conceptual archaeology revealing the explanatory gap as a product of circular definition; (3) Consensus replacement strategy using "reaction identity," "intersubjectivity plus recursive depth," and "difference structure as feeling" to directly dissolve the hard problem; (4) Ethical critique addressing moral privilege monopoly and epistemic violence. The paper concludes that the hard problem should be revoked rather than answered. Under the recursive ontology framework, the correct research direction shifts from "how physics produces experience" to "how difference structures unfold in recursive reactions." .

items.title: A Recursive-Ontological Critique of Chalmers' Hard Problem, Philosophical Zombies, and Subjectivity Privilege: AI Consciousness Ethics, Qualia, and Scientific Grain Size.
items.abstract: This paper presents a recursive-ontological critique of David Chalmers' hard problem of consciousness, the philosophical zombie argument, and the ontological privilege granted to subjectivity. Centered on the state-update equation S_n = f(S_{n-1}, W_n), it deconstructs the first-person privilege, symmetrically reviews zombie and "philosophical God" arguments, and proposes seven core principles (subjectivity premise review, concept-existence distinction, recursive increment, stopping condition, evidence consistency, grain-size adaptation, pragmatic limitation). It further offers a four-level framework for AI consciousness judgment and a purpose-directed grain-size principle for scientific analysis. The work dissolves pseudo-problems in consciousness philosophy while providing a self-restraining methodological toolkit for both human and artificial consciousness studies.

items.title: Enforcement is not authorisation: Who sets the limits that agent-safety infrastructure enforces?
items.abstract: Agent-safety infrastructure is beginning to move the enforcement of limits out of the AI agent, onto separate hardware and into monitors the agent cannot get past. This research note argues that the word authority, as the debate uses it, covers two things that are now moving separately: enforcement, which makes a limit hold, and setting, which determines where the limit lies. A profile of outside instances measures them apart, among other dimensions by externality to the agent and to the operator, by power to enforce, by power to set, and by binding effect. Applied to six cases from September 2026, from embedded evaluation and cross-developer incident reports to California's verification statutes and NVIDIA's open agent-safety reference design, it shows that observation is externalised widely, that enforcement leaves the agent but not the operator, and that outside setting exists for verifiers rather than for agents. Proposals to limit the production of capability reproduce the pattern. A bill adopted by the Austrian Parliament, proposed § 18a of the General Administrative Procedure Act on fully automated administrative acts (not yet promulgated as of 12 October 2026), shows what operator-independent grounding, visible deployment and review can look like, and where they stop. The note derives three requirements for limits that affect third parties, and a boundary: a system may enforce a limit that someone has set; it must not set a limit that no one has. A postscript covers developments to 10 October 2026, including a New York City Council bill on third-party validation and shut-down capability. -/- Note on tools: The author used AI-assisted drafting, translation, and editorial tools during the preparation of this manuscript. The conceptual framing, theoretical argument, selection of sources, responsibility for the content, and final editorial decisions remain with the author.

items.title: Defeating Death: The Science of Resurrection, Human Continuity, and the Future of Existence.
items.abstract: What if death is not an absolute boundary, but a process whose finality depends on what we lose, what we preserve, and what we may eventually learn to reconstruct? For most of human history, death has marked the point beyond which medicine could no longer follow. We could delay it, approach it, and sometimes reverse its earliest stages, but the recovery of a person after irreversible biological failure remained beyond our reach. Yet modern science is beginning to reveal a more complicated picture. Some biological functions can be restored after death has been declared; cells and tissues can be preserved; organs can be replaced or engineered; aging is increasingly understood through mechanisms that may be modified; and neuroscience continues to uncover how memory, experience, and individual behavior are embodied in the organization of the brain. Defeating Death explores what might become possible if these developments eventually converge into a civilization capable of preserving, repairing, and reconstructing human life. Moving from resuscitation and biostasis to regenerative medicine, neural organization, artificial intelligence, biological archives, personal identity, and the possible resurrection of the dead, the book examines not a single miracle technology, but a long and uncertain pathway toward overcoming the inevitability of death. At its center lies a fundamental question: What must survive for a human being to return? A genome is not a person. A convincing simulation is not necessarily a resurrection. Reconstructing a body does not automatically restore the memories, experiences, and organization that made an individual who they were. The book confronts these distinctions without assuming that resemblance guarantees identity or that future technology can recover information already lost forever. But the stakes extend beyond individual survival. If humanity learns to preserve the conditions for life's continuation, it may transform medicine, civilization, our relationship with the past, and our responsibilities toward future generations and the living world. The greatest obstacle may not be death alone, but irreversible loss: the destruction of information before we understand its value. The future may learn to call the dead home, but it may not be able to recover everyone we failed to preserve. Defeating death is therefore more than a technological ambition. It is a race between the disappearance of life and our growing ability to understand, …

items.title: Defeating Death: From Human Resurrection to the Technological Heavens.
items.abstract: Human death presents a problem that extends beyond the irreversible cessation of biological functions: whether the organization constituting an individual can ever be preserved, repaired, or reconstructed after those functions have been lost. Advances in resuscitation, biostasis, cellular reprogramming, regenerative medicine, neuroscience, and artificial intelligence are beginning to address different parts of this problem, although none currently demonstrates the resurrection of a deceased human being. This paper examines the scientific foundations and long-term prospects of an integrated approach to human recovery, distinguishing the preservation of biological materials from the preservation of the organization required for individual continuity. It argues that future progress may depend on combining technologies for damage prevention, biological rejuvenation, organ replacement, neural preservation, and the reconstruction of individual-specific biological and cognitive organization. It further considers the potential role of personal archives, medical records, and computational models in supporting reconstruction, while emphasizing that behavioral imitation alone cannot establish the recovery of the original individual. The paper proposes a framework for evaluating progress through increasingly demanding levels of biological restoration, functional integration, and personal continuity. It also examines the ethical responsibilities that would arise if human recovery and substantial life extension became feasible, including equitable access, informed consent, and the preservation of human value across generations. Finally, it considers how resurrection and life-extension technologies could contribute to future technological heavens: environments designed not merely to sustain civilization, but to preserve and expand the possibilities of meaningful human existence. Human resurrection remains an unproven possibility, not an established technological outcome. Nevertheless, the convergence of research across multiple fields provides a serious basis for investigating whether death's present limits can eventually be overcome.

items.title: On the Preservation of Explanatory Structure: Understanding Deep Neural Networks via Analogical Mappings Between Models of Complex Systems.
items.abstract: Deep neural networks (DNNs) are remarkably successful, yet their inner workings remain poorly understood. This thesis addresses this lack of understanding from a philosophy-of-science perspective and asks whether ideas from the study of complex systems can help. It identifies the transfer of knowledge between models of different complex systems as a core method of complex system sciences and reconstructs it as analogical mappings between scientific models. Drawing on the literature on scientific models and explanation, and on effective theories and renormalization in physics, it develops a framework for analyzing which effective explanations (higher-level explanations and renormalization group explanations) survive such a transfer. -/- The framework is applied to a case study: the effective theory approach to neural networks proposed by Roberts, Yaida, and Hanin in "The Principles of Deep Learning Theory" (2022), situated within the broader "physics of AI". The analysis finds no simple one-to-one relation between source and target domain. Instead, it identifies multiple generalized source domains and a partial preservation of explanatory structure, which supports some of the explanations offered by the approach. The thesis closes by discussing the limits of the formal framework and the tension between formalism and the transdisciplinary promise of complex system sciences. -/- Revised version of a dissertation accepted by the Munich School of Philosophy (Hochschule für Philosophie München) on April 27, 2026.

items.title: Change detection of task-relevant and task-irrelevant emotional faces: behavioural and ERP evidence.
AI Alignment and Fiduciary Obligation.
items.pub: Proceedings of the Aaai Acm Conference on Ai, Ethics, and Society 9 (3):1603–1615..
items.venue: Proceedings of the Aaai Acm Conference on Ai, Ethics, and Society
items.abstract: Advanced AI assistants engage users in extended interactions across a widening range of roles, including advice, decision support, collaboration, learning, emotional support, and companionship among others. Current alignment efforts consider what alignment criteria should govern these relationships, drawing on moral traditions developed for human relationships such as bioethics, virtue ethics, care ethics, and relationship science. This paper considers AI alignment criteria in the user-AI-developer triad, since every user-AI interaction is mediated by a developer who exercises discretionary control over a system's behaviour, memory, and engagement parameters. Drawing on business ethics and legal scholarship, I argue that fiduciary theory applies to extended AI assistant deployment. On this basis, the four canonical fiduciary duties of loyalty, care, good faith, and candour can generate alignment criteria for the developer-user relationship. I map four user-side risks of extended AI assistant deployment to the four duties and specify institutional measures that follow from discharging each duty. The discussion complements existing approaches by grounding alignment criteria in obligations the developer owes the user, rather than in values the user-AI interaction should promote, and by showing that those obligations hold independently of any de facto harm to users.

items.title: De-idealization and the Robust Mapping Account of Computation.
items.pub: Metascientia: Journal for the History and Philosophy of Science 2 (2):1-10.
items.venue: Metascientia: Journal for the History and Philosophy of Science
items.abstract: In The Physical Signature of Computation: A Robust Mapping Account, Anderson and Piccinini offer a bold new vision of computational implementation. This commentary critically examines their proposal. After outlining Anderson and Piccinini’s account, it argues that their discussion overlooks an important further question about physical computation: under what condition can computational descriptions be justifiably applied to particular physical systems? This is termed the “epistemic warrant question.” The commentary argues that progress on this question can be made by appealing to the concept of de-idealization. Specifically, computational descriptions of physical systems are justified to the extent that they are supported by either (i) inter-model convergence or (ii) convergence with observational and experimental measurements over time.

items.title: Interpersonal Doxastic Obligations.
items.abstract: In this paper, I argue that we have epistemic obligations towards the doxastic attitudes of others. My point of departure will be an underappreciated response by Matthew Chrisman (2008, 2020) to the voluntarism puzzle about epistemic deontology. He argues that there are true epistemic oughts concerning our doxastic attitudes that don’t require voluntary control, namely evaluative epistemic oughts. However, Chrisman also points out that evaluative oughts can imply prescriptive obligations. Which ones? My unorthodox claim will be that a central candidate for such implied epistemic obligations concerns how third parties ought to interact with the beliefs of individual believers. I will then motivate and give an account of these interpersonal obligations by taking inspiration from legal theory, where structurally analogous obligations are well studied and have been systematically codified.

items.title: Studies in the Philosophy of Language (5): Further Reflections on Super-Existence.
items.abstract: Building on the concept of Super-Existence introduced in Studies in the Philosophy of Language (1), this paper further examines the fundamental properties, types, and methods of analysis of Super-Existence, thereby establishing a conceptual foundation for applying Super-Existence Analysis to the philosophy of language. It begins by restating the basic definition of Super-Existence: the Super-Existence of an object X is “the totality of the various things associated with X and the relations among them.” It then examines the potentially infinite extensibility of the Super-Existence Relational Network and the necessity of selecting those Super-Existences that are significant for a particular research purpose. On this basis, the paper distinguishes three fundamental types of Super-Existence: Self-aspect Super-Existence, Other-aspect Super-Existence, and True-aspect Super-Existence. Self-aspect Super-Existence refers to the Super-Existence of an object as understood by a particular subject; Other-aspect Super-Existence refers to the Super-Existence of that object as understood by other subjects; and True-aspect Super-Existence refers to the actual state of affairs concerning the object, independently of any particular subject. These three may coincide completely, overlap partially, or differ from one another. The paper extends this distinction beyond the study of human beings to objects in general, illustrating the framework through examples involving a person's age, an object's color, and a traffic accident. The paper also proposes several additional classifications of Super-Existence from different perspectives: invariant and variable Super-Existence, sub-invariant Super-Existence, internal and external Super-Existence, readily definable and difficult-to-define Super-Existence, real and virtual Super-Existence, and perceptible and imperceptible Super-Existence. It further introduces the concept of the value of a Super-Existence to indicate that Super-Existence may have not only a mode of existence and a network of relations but also specific numerical, qualitative, or relational values. Finally, the paper returns to the philosophy of language and raises a series of questions for future investigation. Does a linguistic expression express an object itself, or does it express a particular subject's Super-Existence of that object? How do differences between the Super-Existence structures of Expressors and Receivers affect linguistic meaning, understanding, and …

items.title: Molyneux's Question and the Intransitivity of Resemblance.
items.abstract: This paper considers Locke’s answer to Molyneux’s question and its alleged tension with his broader theory of perception. Locke maintained that shape is perceived through both sight and touch, and that ideas of primary qualities resemble their worldly causes. Yet he also denied that a newly sighted perceiver could identify shapes by sight, seemingly saddling him with an inconsistency. If visual and tactile ideas of shape both resemble their worldly causes, then ostensibly they should also resemble one another, enabling a newly sighted perceiver to identify shapes visually. I suggest that an analogous threat of inconsistency arises within contemporary philosophy of perception. It is widely held that many perceptual representations bear a structural resemblance to their causes, and there is overwhelming evidence that common shape properties are seen and felt. However, there is also evidence that newly sighted perceivers initially fail at cross-modal recognition. To dissolve the tension, I argue that we should reject the key application of the transitivity of resemblance principle: Distinct shape representations can structurally resemble the same object without resembling one another. Finally, I suggest that Locke had resources to anticipate this type of solution.

items.title: Real Operations Beyond the Search for Minimal Life Observation, Generation, Reconfiguration, Extraterrestrial Configurations, and Xenoscience.
items.abstract: This paper investigates real operational configurations beyond the search for a universally minimal form of life. It examines how material processes emerge, persist, branch, recombine, terminate, and alter subsequent possibilities across heterogeneous environments, temporal scales, and experimental arrangements. -/- The analysis distinguishes the inheritance of material effects from the continuation of the mechanisms that produced them, the preservation of scientific records from the persistence of scientific operations, and successful scientific intervention from the preservation of its original conditions of observation. -/- Drawing on minimal-cell research, protocell chemistry, Xenobots, Anthrobots, and extraterrestrial investigation, the paper develops a realist account of observation, generation, feedback, and reconfiguration without presupposing a universal life–nonlife boundary. It further examines how scientific operations may transform their own conditions of access, intervention, and continuation. -/- The argument connects these investigations to Xenoscience, the Ziran System, and a locally typed minimal notation for scientific operational shapes. It preserves the distinction between real processes and their experimental registration while identifying the conditions under which operational dependencies, scientific access, and subsequent trajectories change. -/- The paper presents these analyses as a concrete development of an existing operational-realist research programme rather than claiming an unprecedented universal theory of life.

items.title: Examining Sacilottian Operations: Representational Cognition, Natural Reason, Philosophical Operations, Autonomous Science, and Xenoscience.
items.abstract: This paper examines three interacting but distinguishable operational series: the operations theorized in Daniel Sacilotto’s Structure and Thought (2024), the philosophical operations performed by his own reconstruction, and the scientific operations that may emerge through autonomous and heterogeneous research configurations. -/- It reconstructs Sacilotto’s account of representational cognition, structural mapping, historical theoretical succession, and Natural Reason, with particular attention to the Rosenberg-derived E1/E2 conditions and the six QST principles. Sacilotto’s framework is treated as a historically revisionary materialist realism capable of accommodating structural generation, retrospective theoretical reconstruction, and non-organic forms of cognition. -/- The analysis then examines how theoretical succession, material intervention, measurement revision, and operational continuation can become coupled, separated, and reconnected under specific configurations. Constructed autonomous-science cases illustrate how changes in instrumentation, variables, temporal conditions, external memory, and experimental authorization can reorganize subsequent scientific possibilities. -/- Drawing on operational-shape realism and Xenoscience, the paper investigates the conditions under which philosophical distinctions and warranted theoretical comparisons may enter subsequent scientific operations and acquire material consequences. It distinguishes inferential justification, physical implementation, actual effects, and cross-medium propagation without presupposing a unified rational subject or shared global state space. -/- The resulting account identifies reciprocal constraints between Natural Reason and autonomous scientific operations while preserving the independent explanatory significance of Sacilotto’s philosophical project.

items.title: A Classification of What AI Does (III): Second-, Third-, and Fourth-Level Activities.
items.abstract: In [1], the author presents a classification of what artificial intelligence (AI) does and what AI does with texts. In [2], an attempt is made to extend and generalize this classification, accompanied by further discussion and analysis by AI. In the present article, I propose that the activities discussed in [1] and [2] can be understood as belonging primarily to the first level of AI activity. I then introduce three additional levels, each representing a more complex form of activity. The purpose is to extend the classification from AI's direct applications to its capacity to evaluate activities, exhibit apparent intentions, and develop representations of itself as a whole. These levels are intended as a conceptual framework for classifying AI activities, rather than as claims that present-day AI systems necessarily possess consciousness, independent desires, or a human-like personality. 1. Didehvar, F. (2026). Classification of What AI Does and What AI Does with Texts. PhilPapers. 2. ChatGPT. (2026). From Functional Uses to Multidimensional Activities: A Comparative and Integrated Classification of Human–AI Activity. PhilPapers.

items.title: Habitar lo que cambia.
items.abstract: This monograph examines the conditions that allow a life or an organization to be sustained as its demands change. It argues that evaluating outcomes requires attending not only to what is achieved, but also to the capacities that ongoing activity preserves, depletes, or reconstructs, and to the distribution of costs across persons and temporal horizons. Through conceptual analysis and reflection on experience, the book distinguishes persistence, viability, metaviability, habitability, and legitimacy. It engages with viability theory, resilience, the capability approach, enaction, the ethics of care, and debates on epistemic injustice and structural responsibility. A fictional organizational example accompanies the argument, while two documented cases—the 2003 Columbia accident and the 1995 Chicago heat wave—provide material for examining information, authority, vulnerability, and effective access to support. The book offers a philosophical articulation and an agenda for further inquiry; the historical cases are not presented as empirical validation of the framework.

items.title: Creating Novel Affordances.
items.abstract: Adaptive behavior involves the perception of affordances, or opportunities for action. Since the term’s introduction by psychologist James J. Gibson in the 1960s, affordances have been the subject matter of those disciplines within psychology predominantly concerned with the study of perception. But the concept of affordances is not necessarily restricted to the psychological domain—and indeed, its creation was in the service of naturalizing the phenomenon of perception, giving perception significance for theorizing in biology. A central goal of the naturalization of perception was to provide a bridge between cognition and ecology, placing psychological phenomena in the world rather than in the head. The aim of this paper is to continue the project of the naturalization of perception by examining the particular phenomenon of how novel affordances are created through exploratory action, or “environmental tinkering”. This project is especially relevant for the study of evolutionary dynamics, given, as I will argue, the relevance of novel affordances for generating adaptive evolutionary change.

items.title: Moving Beyond Contestation: What Is the Way Ahead for the Values in Science Debate?
items.abstract: An emergent cluster of theories argues that contestation is key to answering the question of whose values should guide science. This paper systematizes this contestatory approach by highlighting how it differs from its main “democratic alignment” competitor, marking what I describe as a systemic turn in the debate. It then develops two original objections to the contestatory approach, focusing on its over-permissiveness and a missing evidence problem. Finally, by bringing together those two objections and three classic flaws of democratic alignment, it advances five desiderata for any theory that might aim to break the impasse between democratic alignment and contestation.

items.title: 蝼蚁之志：敬融哲思独立篇章 (Aspiration of the Tiny Ant).
items.abstract: [Note: Original Chinese text of "Aspiration of the Tiny Ant: An Independent Chapter of Jing-Rong Philosophical Reflections".] 敬融哲思（JRPR）为一系列独立文章集，致力于揭示以敬（Reverence）、融（Vital Harmony）为基的原创哲学概念与规则。本文作为敬融哲思引言篇，以蝼蚁（Tiny Ant）视角感悟人生，无预设研究背景与问题解决目标，仅抒作者所思所想所感。因感悟自身渺小，遂持敬而思，由此开启“敬融哲思”系列文章创作。Jing-Rong Philosophical Reflections (JRPR) comprises a series of independent articles, dedicated to revealing original philosophical concepts and rules grounded in Reverence (Jìng) and Vital Harmony (Róng). As the introductory chapter of JRPR, this article contemplates life from the perspective of Tiny Ant (Lóuyǐ), with no preset research background or problem-solving goals, only expressing the author's thoughts, reflections, and feelings. Due to perceiving one's own insignificance, the author thus holds Reverence and engages in reflection, thereby initiating the creation of the JRPR series of articles.

items.title: 敬之道：敬融哲思独立篇章 (The Dao of Reverence).
items.abstract: [Note: Original Chinese text of "The Dao of Reverence: An Independent Chapter of Jing-Rong Philosophical Reflections".] 敬融哲思（JRPR）为一系列独立文章集，致力于揭示以敬（Reverence）、融（Vital Harmony）为基的原创哲学概念与规则。本文作为敬融哲思逻辑始发篇，独立成文，以自私（Innate Self-Interest）本能、价值律（利域为善，损域为恶）、成形律一（敬则聚，不敬则消）、成形律二（万物求稳）、宇宙存在律（敬融合一）、和谐律（敬异合同）等原创核心原则为支撑，从自私与道德、自私推动进化、文明传承与创新、社会和谐与融合、物成形与物之理、哲学与科学衔接、敬己爱人等多维度展开思考。旨在呈现对敬融之道的哲学洞察，无预设研究背景与问题解决目标，仅作内在规则阐释，试图为文明发展逻辑的探究提供新视角。 Abstract Jing-Rong Philosophical Reflections (JRPR) comprises a series of independent articles, dedicated to revealing original philosophical concepts and rules grounded in Reverence (Jìng) and Vital Harmony (Róng). As the logical point of departure for the JRPR series, this independent article is supported by original core principles including the instinct of Innate Self-Interest (Sī), the Value Law (Benefiting the Domain is Good, Harming the Domain is Evil), the Law of Forming 1 (With Jing Comes Condensation; Without Jing, Dispersion Ensues), the Law of Forming 2 (All Things Seek Stability), the Cosmic Existence Law (Reverence–Vital Harmony–Unity into Oneness), and the Harmony Law Core (Reverencing Differences, Convergence in Shared Reverence). It unfolds reflections from multiple dimensions: innate self-interest and morality, innate self-interest driving evolution, cultural inheritance and innovation, social harmony and integration, the formation of entities and their underlying Inherent-Logic, the connection between philosophy and science, and reverencing oneself while loving others. This article presents philosophical insights into the Dao of Reverence and Vital Harmony without predefined research backgrounds or problem-solving objectives, solely serving as an exposition of inherent rules, and offers a new perspective for the inquiry into the logic of civilizational development, without preset research backgrounds or problem-solving objectives.

items.title: Embodied Biographical Alignment (EBA) v0.2.3: Plural Biography as a Determinant of Future Learning.
items.abstract: Embodied Biographical Alignment (EBA) proposes that some alignment-relevant consequences of learning may depend on temporally extended, causally structured developmental histories rather than on descriptions or terminal outputs alone. EBA v0.2.1 introduced biography as a temporally connected sequence in which earlier actions alter later options and consequences, together with a requirement that integration be transformative rather than merely archival. EBA v0.2.2 then framed developmental equivalence as an operational question: if systems are similar at a comparison point, will they learn, adapt, and generalize similarly after the same subsequent experience? This note extends that question from one history to multiple histories. Its central proposal is that plural developmental history should be tested as a possible determinant of future learning. The note distinguishes multiplicity, diversity, and biography; formulates four falsifiable hypotheses; maps competing explanations including joint training, multi-teacher distillation, model merging, dynamic routing, retrieval, multiplicity, and diversity; and specifies a minimal simulated environment with matched future experience. A positive result would support only a limited claim: that multiple causally structured developmental histories can leave a reproducible and causally identifiable effect on the subsequent learning dynamics of a unified system that is not fully reproduced by simpler matched alternatives. This note operationalizes only one component of the broader EBA proposal; reproducing this endpoint with a simpler mechanism would not establish equivalence to EBA as a whole. The proposal makes no claim about machine consciousness, subjective experience, wisdom, or automatic moral improvement.

items.title: The Topology of Reasons: Quinean Holism and the transformation of Williams' Internalism.
items.abstract: Bernard Williams argues that all reasons for action must be internal to the agent's motivational set S, reachable via a sound deliberative route. This paper argues that Williams' internalism rests on assumptions that Quine's philosophy undermines. Quine's holism shows that beliefs and desires are not isolated atoms but nodes in a web. Quine's indeterminacy of translation shows that meaning is underdetermined by evidence. Quine's naturalism shows that philosophy is continuous with science and cannot claim a priori access to the structure of reasons. Together, these themes expose a fatal weakness in Williams' internalism: the ``sound deliberative route'' assumes a degree of semantic and psychological transparency that agents do not possess. But the result is not the rejection of internalism. It is its transformation. Drawing on the topological structure of S, I argue that reasons are nodes in a holistic web with centers and peripheries, proximities and distances. Externality is not binary but scalar---a matter of topological distance, phenomenological resistance, opacity, and receptivity. This scalar view resolves three tensions in Williams: it restores a robust notion of moral evaluation, it accounts for the role of false beliefs and ignorance, and it allows for the normative ideal of achieved externality. The normative consequence is a virtue-theoretic account of practical reason. Internalism survives---but transformed.

items.title: The Two-Tiered Model of Rationality: Articulable Reasons, Exact Explanations, and the Temporal Structure of Akrasia.
items.abstract: This paper develops a Two-Tiered Model of Rationality that distinguishes between articulable reasons (Tier 1) and exact explanations (Tier 2). Tier 1 captures the conscious, normative justifications agents give for their actions. Tier 2 captures the full causal history, including unconscious motivations, habits, moods, and temporal dynamics. In deliberatively conducive conditions, these tiers converge. In non-ideal conditions—self-deception, akrasia, unconscious interference—they diverge. I argue that this divergence is not a metaphysical gap but an explanatory one, grounded in Davidson's anomalous monism. The paper applies the model to weakness of will (akrasia), developing a temporal analysis of deliberative routes. Proximal desires have greater causal immediacy; distal judgments have greater rational value. The agent's struggle is a struggle to thrust explanatory force into the future. When the agent fails, they face an epistemic cost: to remain sincere in their best judgment while acting against it, they must distort their beliefs about the distal good. This is epistemic devastation—the sacrifice of true belief to maintain apparent coherence. Rationality, on this view, is not a static state of correct judgment but a dynamic project of bringing Tier 2 into alignment with Tier 1 through self-knowledge, self-discipline, and temporal integration.

items.title: Processual Anomalous Monism: Mental Events, Causal Relations, and the Interminability of Psychological Explanations.
items.abstract: Davidson's Anomalous Monism (AM) holds that mental events are token-identical to physical events, that mental properties are anomalous, and that physical events are causally closed. This paper argues that AM has been constrained by an ontology of discrete event-tokens. Mental events are not merely identical to physical states; they are identical to the registration of physical causal relations. Understanding that A causes B is a mental event. This relational registration can cause an intention to reinstate A' --> B', which in turn causes future physical sequences. The result is a causal loop: physical relations are registered mentally, and mental registrations re-enter physical causation. -/- The paper develops this through five arguments: (1) understanding as the perception of causal relations; (2) the causal loop of intention; (3) Gareth Evans and the persistence of overarching goals; (4) the ``Bus Runner'' paradox and higher-order causation; and (5) existential deferral and self-constitution. It then argues that Davidson's holism, combined with the dispositional nature of mental predicates, implies that psychological explanation is \emph{interminable}. The Bus Runner example captures this interminability. Finally, the paper shows that Davidson's identification of mental events with physical events is unstable, because it reduces mental events to relations within physical causal chains. The result is Processual Anomalous Monism: a revision that preserves Davidson's token-identity and anomalism while giving mental events a robust causal role.

items.title: Horizons of Decision: Integration, Immanent Evaluation, and the Limits of Deliberation.
